### The reader gate fired NOT DISTINGUISHABLE, and it cost twenty minutes instead of the sweep

`Qwen/Qwen3-8B`, bf16, on the 57 image-annotated studies, scored by `core.data.labels.reader_upgrade`:

```
177 pairs the lexicon left blank; the candidate speaks on 81 (45.8%)
blank-pair accuracy 0.840 against a majority-class 0.840
the lexicon's own 463 answered pairs: candidate accuracy 0.812
blank-pair accuracy interval [0.737, 0.911] over studies
```

**Read the first number before the third.** The reader DOES speak where the lexicon abstained — 45.8% of
the blank pairs, which is the coverage the whole lane was arguing for. It is the second number that closes
it: 0.840 against a majority class of 0.840, to three decimals, with an interval [0.737, 0.911] that
brackets the baseline rather than clearing it. On the blank cells the prevalence is 13.6% (24 positives in
177), so "absent everywhere" scores 0.864 on the FULL blank set and 0.840 on the subset this reader chose
to speak on. It has matched that and added nothing.

**And it does not hold the ground the lexicon already had**: 0.812 on the 463 answered pairs, below the
lexicon's own 0.8705 macro against the same annotations. So the trade on offer is coverage that carries no
information bought with a regression where supervision already worked.

**What this refutes and what it does not.** It refutes an 8B reader as a source of supervision on the
blank cells, on this prompt, against this truth. It does NOT refute `knee-fuhq`'s finding that label noise
outranks architecture — that finding rests on our labels reading 0.8705 while a published coatnet reads
0.9167 on the same studies, and this arm did not touch it. The lane's real blocker is unchanged and is not
a result: BOTH cached 35B readers fail to load under transformers 5.15 (gptqmodel imports the removed
`no_init_weights`; the NVFP4 twin declares `modelopt`, absent from `AUTO_QUANTIZER_MAPPING`), and vLLM is
Linux-only here. A 35B is a different reader, not a bigger version of this one.

**The gate is the deliverable, not the verdict.** Pre-registering the blank-pair comparison turned an
open-ended sweep of 4,406 reports into a twenty-minute question with a written branch, and the branch it
fired was the one that forbids spending the card. That is the instrument paying for itself on first use.

**And the NARROW claim the audit left open is now measured too — on the cells it named.** `knee-07wb` /
`knee-pju4` survived `confident224` only as a claim about the three labels whose UNK share is extreme, so
the gate's blank set was checked per label rather than in aggregate:

| finding | blank pairs | the reader speaks on | its accuracy | majority class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Synovitis | 41 | 11 | 0.727 | 0.659 |
| Baker's | 29 | 7 | 0.857 | **0.966** |
| Fracture | 26 | 24 | 0.875 | 0.846 |

Baker's is a straight loss. The other two lead by +0.068 and +0.029 on ELEVEN and twenty-four asserted
cells — a single flipped cell moves Synovitis by 0.09, which is larger than the lead itself.

**The finding is about the RULER, not the reader.** The image-annotated set is 57 studies, so a per-label
blank-cell claim is being asked of denominators of 7 to 24. That cannot resolve anything at any reader
size, and no bigger model changes it. The narrow route therefore does not need a loadable 35B — it needs a
truth set with more annotated studies, which we do not have. Retire it as unmeasurable here rather than
leaving it open as if a stronger reader would settle it.

## 2026-08-30 — the roster was hand-written, and the project's second-best solo was unshippable (`knee-0dtv`)

`comp/members.roster` is the ONLY definition of what a package contains: a member absent from it cannot
be shipped no matter what any other file says. Nothing writes it. A run that finishes writes a
checkpoint, a holdout record and a ledger section — and then the roster is edited by hand, so every
member in it is there because somebody remembered.

`knee-0dtv` was filed on five seats: building a sixteen-seat entry found five of its sixteen best
members missing from the roster. The bead was three times too small. The new check
(`python -m kneemri.kaggle.roster_check`, the thirteenth) swept the whole processed root and read

```
123 scoreable of 200 checkpoints: 47 packaged, 0 declined, 76 undocumented
```

Seventy-six, not five. And the worst of them is not `labelwise_dense_s2026`. It is
**`stackfit_s2026`, 0.8631 solo** under LogitAverage on the 909-study fold-0 holdout — the
**second-best single checkpoint this project owns** (behind `calib_dense_hold_s2026` 0.8634, ahead of
`merged_span_cf` 0.8618), and it could not take a seat in any entry ever shipped. `raptor_distill_s2026`
0.8613 and `distill_pairs_s2026` 0.8594 were in the same state.

**THE RULE IS NOT A SCORE FLOOR, and checking that is what stopped this becoming a second bug.** The
first instinct was to package everything above some cut. Measured against the pool the roster ALREADY
packages, that would have declined this project's own instruments: the packaged set descends to
`focus_mcl_s2026` 0.5332, `mae_matched_s2026` 0.6735, `lora_r8_v3small_224_s2026` 0.8215,
`dinov3_base_lora_s2026` 0.8268, `crop80_tissue_s2026` 0.8345. Every one of those is a NAMED INSTRUMENT
— the only non-DINOv2 trunk, the only different physical crop, the MCL specialist, the medical
pretraining. So the cut is `MERIT = 0.8459`, the solo of `extended_ws_s2026`: the weakest member this
roster has ever added on merit rather than as an instrument. Above it, ship. Below it, decline IN WRITING,
and the way back on is to name the instrument the member would be — never to re-quote the number.

> **CORRECTION 2026-09-01 (`claims_check`, knee-kpq0).** This paragraph read `MERIT = 0.8460` and the
> roster line for the same member read 0.8462; disk reads **0.845878**. One digit, one consequence:
> `res392_lr8e-6_ws_s2026` scores 0.845878 as well — it TIES the member the cut is named after — and was
> written into `comp/members.declines` as "below the merit level". Nothing else moved: the next member
> under the cut is `wsfold0_e6` at 0.8457 and the next above is `intensity392_ws` at 0.84593, which was
> added, so the 30/46 split stands with that one line to re-price by `record_mix` rather than by a number.

**The split: 30 added, 46 declined.** Thirty undocumented members clear 0.8459 and joined the roster
(0.8631 down to 0.8459). Forty-six are declined in `comp/members.declines`, each with its reason:
thirty-four below merit, eleven smoke/probe runs that never became members, and `confident224_s2026` —
a REAL arm scored under an older label table, written down as such so it is not mistaken for a twelfth
smoke run and so `knee-8hau`'s rescore has somewhere to land. After: `123 scoreable, 77 packaged, 46
declined, 0 undocumented`, exit 0.

**Why the check is two-sided.** "Everything scoreable ships" would be the wrong rule — twelve of the
finds genuinely should not ship. What was missing is not a policy that everything ships; it is a PLACE
TO WRITE DOWN that something does not, so the set difference is taken by a machine instead of by memory.
And a bare name in the declines file is a finding too: it records that somebody once decided, not what
they decided, which is the same defect one file over.

**What this does NOT do.** It does not push the package. Thirty new roster lines mean a dataset push
before any of them can be mounted — a separate, deliberate step. `knee-0dtv` was about the definition,
and the definition is now enforced.

### The 30 newly-shippable members buy +0.0002, and the honest curve is flat from THREE seats

Same evening, immediately after the roster fix, because the fix is what made the question askable: the
honest greedy had never once been run over the whole pool. `record_mix --largest-pool --vote logit
--seats honest` over all 200 checkpoints on disk — 111 survive the split-and-label-table narrowing
(the eleven smoke runs plus `confident224_s2026` drop out as a group, named in the log) — reads

```
   1 members: held-out 0.8624   in-sample 0.8634   bias +0.0010
   3 members: held-out 0.8729   in-sample 0.8741   bias +0.0012
  12 members: held-out 0.8743   in-sample 0.8776   bias +0.0034
  20 members: held-out 0.8750   in-sample 0.8773   bias +0.0023
best honest count 28 at 0.8753, against the in-sample peak 0.8777 at 13
```

**Against the previous unrestricted `honest12` at 0.8751 that is +0.0002.** Thirty members that could
not take a seat in any entry ever shipped — `stackfit_s2026` 0.8631, the project's second-best solo,
among them — were added to the pool, and the honest curve did not move. The member-count axis is
saturated: the pool already spanned whatever these thirty span.

**Read the shape, not just the peak.** Three seats reach 0.8729. The next TWENTY-FIVE buy +0.0024 in
total, and every step of it is inside the bias term the same rows report. The in-sample peak sits at 13
and the honest peak at 28, which is the estimator wandering on a flat surface, not a real optimum at
either count. A "best count 28" that is +0.0010 over count 8 is a coordinate on a plateau.

**Two consequences, and they point opposite ways.**

For SCORE: this closes "add more members of the kind we already build" as a lever, on our own honest
ruler and at full pool size. It was already narrowed by the 23% quality pass-through; it is now closed
by saturation, which is a stronger statement — pass-through says gains arrive small, saturation says
there are no gains left to pass through. What stays open is a genuinely different DECODE or CORPUS
(`knee-nj4l`, `knee-ombx`), which is exactly what a saturated pool of one architecture predicts.

For EFFICIENCY: three seats deliver 99.7% of what twenty-eight deliver. That is the strongest support
the efficiency lane has, and it was bought for free by a run that was aimed at score.

**A caveat the number carries and the plateau does not remove.** This is offline on 909 fold-0 studies,
and it is a statement about SEATING, not about weighting: the greedy seats members it then averages
under one rule. A weighted fit over the same pool is a different question and this does not answer it.

### The weighting caveat, discharged the same hour: no rule beats the one already shipped

The saturation entry above closed on a caveat — "this is a statement about SEATING, not about weighting;
a weighted fit over the same pool is a different question and this does not answer it." `vote_ceiling`
answers it, over the roster the fix had just enlarged, and it costs nothing (holdout records are on disk;
no card, no slot, no inference). Weights fitted on one half of the studies, scored on the other, both
directions, flat scored on the identical halves so the paired inflation cancels:

```
reading 77 members over 909 studies
  RankAverage            honest 0.8710  vs flat +0.0000  (fit-on-self 0.8710, overfit gap +0.0000)
  QualityWeightedRank    honest 0.8710  vs flat -0.0000  (fit-on-self 0.8710, overfit gap +0.0000)
  LabelQualityRank       honest 0.8711  vs flat +0.0001  (fit-on-self 0.8715, overfit gap +0.0004)
  LogitAverage           honest 0.8720  vs flat +0.0010  (fit-on-self 0.8720, overfit gap +0.0000)
  MedianLogit            honest 0.8707  vs flat -0.0003  (fit-on-self 0.8707, overfit gap +0.0000)
BEST honest rule: LogitAverage at 0.8720 (+0.0010 vs flat)
```

**The best rule is the one already shipped**, and its margin over flat rank is +0.0010 — a tenth of the
noise bar. `QualityWeightedRank`, the rule whose own docstring asked for exactly this read, comes in at
−0.0000: after its weights are paid for it is indistinguishable from not weighting at all.
`LabelQualityRank` is the only rule that overfits measurably (+0.0004 fit-on-self over honest), and even
its overfit number does not reach flat plus the floor. So the vote axis is closed on the enlarged
roster the same way the count axis is: not "we picked well", but "there is nothing here to pick".

**One ordering fact worth keeping, because the two runs share a ruler.** All 77 packaged members flat
reads 0.8720. The honest greedy's chosen 28 read 0.8753. **Choosing beats including by +0.0033** — more
than any vote rule buys over any other. The lever on this pool was never the rule and is not the count;
it is which members, and even that lands on a plateau. Both axes now say the same thing from opposite
sides: this pool is one architecture, measured out.

**Provenance correction, written minutes later against `interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-29_the-vote-has-nothing-to-weight.md`.**
This is a REPLICATION at a larger pool, not a discovery. `knee-xsfc` ran the same instrument earlier the
same day over 42 members and reached the same conclusion: `LogitAverage` 0.8725 (+0.0014 vs flat),
`QualityWeightedRank` +0.0000, `LabelQualityRank` +0.0002 with a +0.0004 overfit gap. The enlarged
77-member roster moves every one of those slightly DOWN — `LogitAverage` +0.0014 → +0.0010,
`LabelQualityRank` +0.0002 → +0.0001 — so the thirty new members did not give the vote anything more to
weight either. What is new here is only the denominator and the direction of the drift; the finding is
`knee-xsfc`'s. The ordering fact (77 flat 0.8720 against the greedy's chosen 28 at 0.8753) IS new, because
it needed the full-pool greedy that did not exist until tonight.

### The named seat order says WHY the thirty bought nothing, and it seats the two worst members in the pool

The honest curve gives counts; `--seats greedy` over the same 111 gives the ORDER, which is what actually
explains the null:

```
greedy  1: 0.8634  +calib_dense_hold_s2026
greedy  2: 0.8709  +merged_span_cf
greedy  3: 0.8741  +labelwise_dense_s2026
greedy  4: 0.8748  +blendhold_s2026
greedy  5: 0.8756  +finding_calib_dense_s2026
greedy  6: 0.8762  +margin_seat_s2026
greedy  7: 0.8768  +warm_calib_dense_s2026
greedy  8: 0.8771  +merged_blend_cf
greedy  9: 0.8773  +calib_span_s2026
greedy 10: 0.8775  +mae_matched_s2026
greedy 11: 0.8776  +focus_mcl_s2026
greedy 12: 0.8776  +through_dense_s2026
greedy 13: 0.8777  +contrast_dense_s2026
greedy 14: 0.8777  +small_batch6_s2026
```

**`stackfit_s2026` is not in it.** The project's second-best solo at 0.8631 — the member whose
unshippability was tonight's headline defect — earns no seat in the first fourteen. That is not a
disappointment, it is the mechanism: the greedy already had `calib_dense_hold` at 0.8634, and `stackfit`
IS `calib_dense_hold` plus EMA, measured flat when it was run (`knee-orjq`, the FLAT branch fired). A
member that differs from the incumbent by a lever measured flat has nothing to add to it. The roster bug
cost us a checkpoint we could not ship; the seat ruler says it would not have been seated. Both are true
and neither excuses the other — the bug was real, and the thing it hid happened to be a twin.

**The two WORST members in the whole pool are seated tenth and eleventh.** `mae_matched_s2026` scores
0.6735 solo and `focus_mcl_s2026` scores 0.5332 — near chance on a twelve-label mean — and the greedy
takes them ahead of every remaining member scoring 0.85-plus. This is the strongest direct evidence the
project has that **quality is not the seat criterion at the margin**, and it independently vindicates the
merit-level EXEMPTION written into `comp/members.declines` hours earlier: the instruments packaged below
the 0.8459 cut are not sentiment, they are seats. A score floor on the roster would have deleted the
tenth and eleventh best seats in the pool.

**What it does NOT license.** Two seats out of eleven is not a rule, the run is in-sample (the honest
curve is the one that may be quoted), and the same seats are inside the plateau where +0.0024 buys
twenty-five members. It licenses keeping the exemption, not building for it.

### The efficiency row went 16 to 245 because we improved, and the gradient there is the steepest thing we can see

`efficiency_read --live`, 2026-08-29 22:56Z, free — no slot, no card:

```
Dimitar Terziev: accuracy rank 29 at 0.943, efficiency rank 245 at 0.941
  232 teams rank above us on efficiency while scoring BELOW us — runtime alone
  OUR efficiency row is STALE (2026-08-28 22:37 snapshot; we submitted after it)
18 teams within 0.002 of 0.941 hold efficiency ranks 4 to 2140 (median 1287) — that span is runtime
top 20 efficiency ranks score 0.923 to 0.952 (median 0.937)
```

Fifteen hours earlier the same tool read **rank 16 at 0.925**, and `knee-7lyz` concluded from the zero
teams then above us that "runtime has stopped being the binding constraint; SCORE AT THIS RUNTIME is."
That conclusion is now inverted by 232. Nothing about the board changed — **we did**: the entry holding
our efficiency row moved from `soloseat` (one member, 0.925) to a multi-decode entry at 0.941. We bought
0.016 of accuracy and paid **229 ranks** for it.

**The gradient is the steepest quantity either board exposes.** Eighteen teams sit within 0.002 of our
accuracy and spread across efficiency ranks 4 to 2140. At a fixed score, runtime alone moves 2136 ranks.
The entire main board spans 0.930–0.952 and buys 2600 ranks with score; this axis buys 2136 with runtime
at score held flat. Any lane that pays that steeply deserves pricing before another seat is bought on a
plateau that has been flat for twelve entries.

**And it cannot be priced yet, which is the actionable half.** The efficiency snapshot is dated
2026-08-28 22:37 and `trioseat_v1` — 0.938 on **three seats and ONE decode**, the entry built exactly for
this lane — scored on 2026-08-29, *after* it. So the row describing us is a board we have already moved
on from, and the one entry whose whole design targets this axis has never appeared on it. The next read
after the snapshot refreshes is worth more than any submission we could fire into the lane now, and it
costs nothing. Do not spend a slot here until it lands.

**Open mechanism, named so it is not assumed:** this read does not establish how our row got reassigned
from 0.925 to 0.941. 473 of 2160 settled teams carry an efficiency entry below their public best and
none carry a better one, so the slot is separately held by design — but by what selection is unknown,
and the rules file (`comp/COMPETITION_RULES.txt` 61-64) states only the three prizes.

### Kernel logs cannot price the efficiency lane: the public rerun scores THREE studies

The efficiency board's snapshot predates `trioseat_v1`, so the lane cannot be priced until it refreshes.
Kaggle's kernel log looked like a way around the wait — it is a JSON list of `{stream_name, time, data}`
with per-record elapsed seconds, so the last record's `time` is the run's wall clock, free for any
shipped entry:

```
soloseat     (1 member,  1 decode)  63.6 s   board 0.925
calibsix     (6 members, 3 decodes) 73.4 s   board 0.941   <- holds our efficiency row
trioseat     (3 members, 1 decode)  93.5 s   board 0.938   <- built AS the cheap entry
fourseat     (4 members, 1 decode)  98.4 s   board 0.937
raptorseat   (7 seats,   3 decodes) 96.5 s   board 0.943   <- champion
raptorweight (7 seats,   3 decodes) 89.0 s   scoring
```

**The lead is dead and one log line kills it.** Every kernel prints `studies 1-3`: the public rerun
scores THREE studies. The gaps put 20–35 s in imports, 15–35 s in weight loading, and 4–8 s in all
decode-and-forward work combined. The 63–98 s spread is startup jitter. Worse than uninformative, the
apparent ordering is BACKWARDS from the design — the "cheap" three-seat one-decode entry reads 20 s
slower than the six-member three-decode entry holding our efficiency row — which is exactly how a bad
instrument does damage rather than nothing.

**A second reading, nearly filed, caught by opening the source.** `calibsix` and `raptorseat` print
`projecting 0.0h of 7.7h` and `0.0h of 7.6h`, which read as projected full-test runtimes; from them I
had already derived a hidden test set of about 8300 studies. `kneemri/inference/budget.py:81` formats it
`projecting {projected}h of {seconds}h` where `seconds` is the **ceiling**. The projection is 0.0h.
There is no projected runtime in any log we hold, and there never was.

**What remains.** The private rerun over the full hidden test is where the efficiency metric's runtime is
measured and we cannot observe it. The efficiency board snapshot stays the only instrument, and waiting
for it to refresh past `trioseat_v1` stays the move — still free, still worth more than a slot.

**One real gap, filed rather than fixed.** `Budget.report()` returns nothing until `measured()`, which
needs `index + fraction > 0`. A single-decode entry running a single chunk prints no projection on the
only chunk line it has. The entries built for the efficiency track are one-decode by design, so they are
precisely the ones that can never self-report a projection — on a private run where nothing else can
either. Low priority (the guard's real job is stopping a 9 h overrun, and a one-group entry is least at
risk of that), but it is the wrong way round.

### `cnx_mid_rate` is not a result about learning rates — it ran one epoch and left a `.partial` — 2026-08-30

`ledger_check` reported one UNRECORDED run — `cnx_mid_rate_s2026` — appearing in neither this file nor
the interpretations, holding a single epoch's score
(**0.7177**, superseded; see the 2026-09-01 entry below, which is the one that ranks the arm).
That number should never be quoted as the arm's result, and this entry exists to say why rather than
to leave it unrecorded a second time.

**Its metrics file holds two lines: the recipe, and epoch 0.** The recipe asked for **12**. There is a
`.partial` on disk dated 2026-08-29 10:47 and **no `.pt`** — which is also why it is absent from the
112-member pool sweep, and why `convergence_check` returns `1 runs: 1 unscored` rather than a verdict.
The run was killed after its first epoch. 0.7177 is a fact about a killed process, exactly the class of
mistake that put three runs into this ledger as facts about architectures (`convergence_check` exists
for it).

**What it was going to test matters more than what it scored.** The recipe:

```
variant cnxbase   backbone_lr 1.2e-4   train_size 448   slices 20   batch 1   epochs 12   fold 0
```

That is **both** follow-ups the `cnx_dense` entry demanded and neither of which had been run: the 448 px
retry its own pre-registration named *before the trunk is judged*, and a backbone rate 3× the 4e-5
adapter rate that was chosen for a ViT. So the fair-budget ConvNeXt question has now been **attempted
and left incomplete**, not answered. `knee-y59c` / `knee-zfgn` stay open on the evidence they already
had.

**Why it probably died.** `batch 1` at 448 px over 20 slices is the slowest configuration this project
has ever queued; twelve epochs of it is a many-hour arm. Anything that re-opens this axis should price
the wall-clock first — the trunk question is worth answering, but not at a ratio nobody computed.

**Not re-armed here.** Every arrangement of the members we own is already priced behind the champion
(`interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-30_the-board-priced-an-offline-constant.md`), and a second weak-trunk
member does not pay the +0.0042 that a top-10 spot costs. This is bookkeeping, not a plan.

## `contrast_pool` — the batch-size explanation is refuted, and the representation lane closes on mechanism

**2026-08-30, one 12-epoch fit, 362 s an epoch, 72 min of card. No slot.**

`contrast_dense_s2026` read 0.8547 against `calib_dense_hold_s2026`'s 0.8634 — **−0.0087**, eleven of
twelve labels down. Its own header, written before the run, named the suspect: *"a batch of twelve sees a
7%-prevalence finding roughly once"*, so for most findings the positives a supervised-contrastive term
needs are absent, the anchor forms no term, and the label drops out of the loss. The reading the ledger
recorded was deliberately narrow — *"supervised contrastive AT BATCH 12 costs 0.009"* — and the named
precondition for reading it any wider was a remembered pool of past readouts.

`RememberedContrast` supplies exactly that (`knee-agrj`). At capacity 8 each anchor is contrasted against
96 keys instead of 12, so a 7% finding is expected in ~7 of them rather than in ~1.

| run | contrast | keys per anchor | best | epoch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `calib_dense_hold_s2026` | none | — | **0.8634** | 6 |
| `contrast_dense_s2026` | SupCon | 12 | 0.8547 | 5 |
| `contrast_pool_s2026` | SupCon + memory | 96 | **0.8515** | 5 |

**−0.0032 against its single-variable control, inside the 0.0062 paired floor. −0.0119 against the
no-contrast control, well outside it.** The two contrastive curves are near-superimposed: same peak
epoch, and tails of 0.8487 against 0.8483.

**The mechanism fired, and that is what makes this a refutation rather than a null.** Training loss runs
5.859 against the control's 3.605 at epoch 0 and stays ~2.2 higher throughout — which is what widening a
log-sum-exp denominator eightfold does, and is not something a stale binary or an unlanded flag can
produce. The flag pair is in the recorded recipe as well, but the loss is the evidence.

**Seat value 0.0000.** The honest greedy over the 77 roster-named members peaks at 0.8763 with twenty
seats; adding this member makes it 78 records and the curve is identical at every count, to four decimals.
That is the sharp contrast with `contrast_dense`, which lost 0.0087 solo and still seats fifth — a solo
loss does not decide a member, and here the seat ruler agrees with the solo one.

**So none of the three pre-registered readings is the right one.** The arm was written expecting flat
against the no-contrast control (supervision not binding), a gain over `contrast_dense` (batch-size
artefact confirmed), or a loss against it (harmful independent of batch size). What happened is the
fourth: **eight times the contrastive population changed nothing measurable.** The positives were
supplied, the loss moved where the mechanism says it must, and the holdout did not follow. The batch-size
explanation `contrast_dense` offered for its own −0.0087 is therefore refuted on measurement, and the
supervised-contrastive term closes at this operating point on **mechanism** — the stronger closure, and
the one the arm named as the outcome worth having.

**What it does NOT close.** This is one contrastive formulation (SupCon over the readout, temperature 0.1,
weight 1.0) at one operating point. A representation term that shapes a different space, or attaches at a
different stage, is untested and is not answered by this. What is answered is the specific suspect, which
is what the 72 minutes were bought for.

## `stack_increments` — the two banked increments do not compose, and the bank-them branch closes

**2026-08-30, one 12-epoch fit, 363 s an epoch, 73 min of card. No slot.**

`knee-24bx` re-opened four increments that had each been measured alone, filed as under-floor, and
discarded on an arithmetic error: `board_transfer` was quoted at a 23% pass-through when the module fits
**+0.98 [+0.94, +1.08] at or above 0.8670** — one-for-one. Under a one-for-one transfer an offline
+0.003 is +0.003 on the board, twice the board's own resolution, so a stack of increments summing past
the 0.0062 paired floor is worth building. The arm stacked the two whose mechanisms are prima facie
disjoint: the **label TABLE swap** (+0.0034, moves the target) and **architecture-distant distillation**
(+0.0035, adds an ordering term from a foreign teacher).

| run | increments | best | epoch |
|---|---|---|---|
| `calib_dense_hold_s2026` | none (control) | **0.8634** | 6 |
| additive prediction | table + distillation | *0.8703* | — |
| `stack_increments_s2026` | table + distillation | **0.8642** | 9 |

**+0.0008 against its control, against a predicted +0.0069.** The paired floor is 0.0062; this is an
eighth of it. The pre-registered NULL band was 0.8600–0.8668 and the run landed inside it, at 0.8642.

Epoch trace: 0.7525, 0.7883, 0.8346, 0.8347, 0.8519, 0.8565, 0.8596, 0.8609, 0.8625, **0.8642**. The peak
is the last recorded epoch of ten under a twelve-epoch budget, so `convergence_check` reads it as bound by
the budget rather than converged — but the gap to close is 0.0061 and the last three epochs moved 0.0033
in total, so a longer fit does not reach the prediction.

**What the NULL says, and it is the sharper of the two branches.** Additivity was declared an ASSUMPTION
in the bead, not a measurement, and the named risk was that the terms share mechanism — *"the increments
are one increment wearing two names"*. That is what the number says: one term's worth arrived, and not
even that cleanly. Both terms act on what the model is asked to ORDER — the label swap by changing the
target table, distillation by adding a teacher's ordering — so they compete for the same headroom rather
than stacking.

**It closes the bank-the-increments branch of `knee-m69u`.** The remaining two unstacked increments
(specialist per column +0.0043, supervision policy +0.0034) are not re-armed on this reading: their sum
with these two was the whole case, and the case required composition that has now been measured absent.
The six-arm roster retrain (~7 h of card) that ADDITIVE would have licensed is **not armed**.

**What it does NOT close.** The individual increments are unharmed — each still reproduces against its own
control, and each is still worth its own size on the board if it is the only thing changed. What is
refuted is that they SUM. It also leaves the non-DINOv2 trunk lane standing as the only remaining branch
of `knee-m69u`, which is where the card went next (`swin_supervised`).

## swin_supervised — the supervised trunk, and the reading it cannot support (2026-08-30)

`knee-ryzy` armed the first trunk on this registry pretrained WITH LABELS: `microsoft/swin-base-patch4-window12-384-in22k`,
21,841 human-assigned classes against nine self-supervised encoders. `swin_supervised_s2026` read **0.8331** at epoch 6, and
epochs 7-11 declined monotonically (0.8261, 0.8255, 0.8269, 0.8268, 0.8256), so it converged and overfit
rather than being truncated — `convergence_check` calls it STOPPED, not a floor.

**0.8331 lands in the pre-registered SEAT-ONLY band (0.8300-0.8559), at that band's floor.** Priced with
`seat_value --candidates swin_supervised_s2026.pt --against greedyseat_v1`: the roster of 7 scores 0.8763
and the roster plus Swin scores 0.8751, **-0.0012**, band [-0.0020, -0.0003]. The best possible swap is
-0.0013, so there is no seat to be had by displacement either. A negative costs roughly 3x on the board,
so ~-0.0040 there. **No seat, no slot**, exactly as the arm's own SEAT-ONLY branch required (+0.002 or
nothing).

**And it is the most decorrelated member the project has produced.** Its nearest-neighbour correlation to
any seated member is **0.8346**, mean 0.8132, against seated members' 0.8772-0.9225. That is the finding
in the row: maximal diversity could not pay for a 0.020 solo deficit. Diversity is a multiplier on a
competitive member, not a substitute for one — which is the same thing the routing and vote-rule nulls
said from the combiner side.

**The number is QUALIFIED, and by a defect in our own harness rather than by the trunk.** `EncoderSurgery.blocks()`
took the longest `ModuleList` in the tree as the encoder's blocks. Swin holds its 24 `SwinLayer` as
2/2/18/2 across four stages, so discovery found only stage 2's eighteen, `--unfreeze-last 6` opened
`layers.2.blocks.12-17`, and **`layers.3` — the final two blocks, 1024 wide, the top of the network — was
frozen for the whole run**. `cnx_own_recipe` (0.8186) and `cnx_dense` (0.7927) carry the same handicap,
27 of 36. Fixed in `knee-94ec` by grouping lists on their element type; every flat trunk returns the same
twelve objects it always did, so no other number in this ledger moves.

So the honest reading is **"this Swin run, at this recipe, with its top frozen, earns no seat"** — not
"supervised pretraining is dead". `swin_wholetop` (`knee-tsiz`) re-runs the byte-identical invocation on
the fixed discovery, and it is the arm that decides which of those two sentences is true.

## Seven "undertrained" runs were plateaus — the budget axis does not reopen (2026-08-30)

Card-free, no slot. `convergence_check` over the whole processed root read 135 runs and called **eleven**
UNDERTRAINED. Seven of those eleven had gained between 0.0004 and 0.0020 across their final three epochs:

| run | last four epochs | gain over three |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mixup_dense_s2026` | 0.8548 0.8541 0.8546 **0.8552** | +0.0004 |
| `mixup224_strong_s2026` | 0.8510 0.8514 0.8515 **0.8516** | +0.0006 |
| `cnx_dense_s2026` | 0.7921 0.7909 0.7927 **0.7927** | +0.0006 |
| `encoder_adapt_s2026` | 0.6887 0.6888 0.6902 **0.6902** | +0.0015 |
| `crop80_tissue_s2026`, `schedule_8_s2026` | — | +0.0020 each |

**The rule was an argmax over a flat tail.** `peak >= done - 1` asks where the maximum sits, and on a
plateau the maximum sits wherever the noise put it. Being bound by a budget is a SLOPE, not an argmax.

**And the false verdict pointed at the one fix already refuted.** UNDERTRAINED argues for a longer
schedule; the 24-epoch arm measured a longer schedule as actively harmful under `one_cycle` — an oversized
budget stretches the anneal and leaves the rate far from annealed where the model actually converges. So
seven plateaus were standing recommendations to re-run a closed axis.

`rising()` now requires the tail gain to clear **0.0062**, the paired holdout floor — the smallest
difference this 909-study holdout resolves, reused here with the same argument rather than a fresh constant.
The corpus reads **102 converged, 9 truncated, 3 stopped, 5 undertrained, 16 unscored**.

**The five that survive are the check on the fix**: `lora_r8_small_336` (+0.0784), `adapt_null` (+0.0789),
`mae_matched` (+0.0901), `encoder_adapt_lower` (+0.0073) and `wholestack_fold2` — and the first three ran
FOUR epochs, where a budget genuinely binds. The rule keeps exactly the runs whose budget was short.

**What this changes about numbers already quoted.** `cnx_dense`'s 0.7927 and `mixup_dense`'s 0.8552 are
their recipes' own numbers, not floors owed a longer run. `cnx_dense` remains handicapped for the separate
reason `knee-94ec` names (its top 9 blocks of 36 never trained), which a longer budget would not have fixed
either. Bead `knee-25wj`.

## vit_in21k truncated at epoch 5 of 12, on a trajectory instrument rather than on its score (2026-08-30)

`vit_in21k_s2026` (ViT-B/16 in21k, 336 px, `--unfreeze-last 6`, `--backbone-lr 4e-5`, 12 epochs
`one_cycle`, whole-stack, fold 0) was killed after epoch 4 with the card handed to `swin_wholetop`. Its
score is a **FLOOR of 0.7847**, not the trunk's number, and `convergence_check` will read it TRUNCATED.

| epoch | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| holdout mean AUC | 0.7239 | 0.7541 | 0.7751 | 0.7755 | 0.7847 |

**The kill was decided on a distribution, not on the stall at epoch 3.** Across the **99 runs in the
processed root with ten or more recorded epochs**, the gain from epoch 3 to the run's peak is median
**+0.0215**, p90 **+0.0383**, and **max +0.0529** (`encoder_adapt_gentle`). The arm's pre-registration
needed **0.8393** to earn a seat. From epoch 4 at 0.7847 that is **+0.0546** — larger than the biggest
epoch-3-to-peak gain this project has ever recorded, and the comparison is generous twice over because
that maximum is measured from an EARLIER epoch and belongs to a 24-epoch run.

The other anchor points the same way: `swin_supervised` sat at **0.8192 at epoch 3** and was still
DECLINED as too weak. `vit_in21k` was **0.044 below that** at the same epoch.

So the seven remaining epochs (2.3 h of card) could only decide COSTS (0.8000-0.8392) versus REFUTES
(<0.8000), and **both branches close the trunk for seating identically**. No action hung on the
difference, which is what makes the truncation a saving rather than a lost result.

**What this does NOT say.** It is not a verdict on ViT-in21k, and it is not a verdict on supervised
ImageNet pretraining. It is one recipe, one rate, fold 0, stopped early. Re-opening it means answering
the trajectory argument — an arm whose epoch-3 value sits in the band seat-worthy runs occupy (0.82-0.84)
— not re-quoting 0.7847. The plumbing suspects were cleared BEFORE the read and none of them fired:
`GridFit` passes `interpolate_pos_encoding` (the class exists for exactly this trunk), `normalization=HALF`
is declared, block discovery finds all twelve `ViTLayer`, and the recipe log confirms every flag landed.

**The queue surgery, because it is the part that can go silently wrong.** `run_train` emits `ARM DONE`
**on success only** (`lib.sh:616`), so a killed trainer writes `ARM FAILED` and the watcher gated on
`ARM DONE vit_in21k` would have waited forever with the card idle. The stalled watcher was killed and
replaced with `after.sh ... "pid:50388"` — the pid gate, on the trainer's WINDOWS pid so `_alive` resolves
it through `tasklist` rather than through a `kill -0` that fails open across bash sessions — **armed
before the kill**, so the queue was never unarmed. No marker was hand-written: a fake `ARM DONE` would
have entered the record as a completed run. Beads `knee-gnzx` (the epoch-3 gate), `knee-tsiz`.

## The non-DINO lane does not seat by distance, and the favourable test is the one that failed (2026-08-30)

Two of the project's non-DINO trunks score within 0.0006 of each other solo and were given opposite
verdicts: `vjepa_warm_s2026` (0.8337) sits on the roster, `swin_supervised_s2026` (0.8331) was declined.
The roster line for the first is an argument about distance — the most decorrelated member the project has
ever produced — so the pair is a clean test of whether that argument is worth a seat. Both were priced on
one ruler, card-free, against the same 7-member champion roster (`seat_value --against greedyseat_v1`):

```
roster of 7: 0.8763
  +vjepa_warm_s2026.pt:      0.8756  (-0.0007)  [-0.0016, +0.0002]   nearest 0.8119  mean 0.8012
  +swin_supervised_s2026.pt: 0.8751  (-0.0012)  [-0.0020, -0.0003]   nearest 0.8346  mean 0.8132
```

**`vjepa_warm` never seated on merit.** Priced against the champion roster it is negative, like the member
that was declined. Its band includes zero, so it is unreadable rather than convicted — but it is nowhere
near the +0.0015 under which this ruler has never been shown to pick up a board tick.

**And the more favourable test is the one that failed.** `vjepa_warm` is the more distant member by a wide
margin (nearest neighbour 0.8119 against 0.8346, mean 0.8012 against 0.8132) *and* scores higher solo, and
it still prices no better in any way that clears the floor. So "maximal diversity pays for a solo deficit"
has now been tested twice at the ~0.833 level, the second time under the conditions most favourable to it,
and failed both times. Distance is not the missing ingredient here: it is already spent, and it is not
enough.

The consequence is a bar, and it is higher than the arms in this family were written against.
`swin_toprate`'s SEAT branch (0.8393) was derived from its frozen-top control rather than from the roster,
and the measurement says the roster will not take a non-DINO member at 0.8393 either — closing from
-0.0007 to +0.0015 has to come from solo quality now that distance is maxed. The roster's merit level is
0.8459 and every seated member is above it, so ~0.846 is the real bar, against a family ceiling of 0.8331.

**No slope is fitted through these two points**, and the reading does not extrapolate: only the sign
transfers between roster pairs, and a third point has broken an ordering before. The claim is the sign,
twice, at maximum distance — nothing about the value.

What it does not say: the non-DINO lane is not dead. This is a fact about the LEVEL, not the architecture —
a non-DINO trunk reading 0.85+ solo has never been tried and is untouched by it. Nor does it unroster
`vjepa_warm`; an unreadable band is not a conviction, and that member's line is answered with a number.
See `knee-tild`, `knee-tsiz`.

### The non-DINO trio as a BLOCK buys nothing either, and the greedy never seats one (2026-08-30)

The seat measurement above priced each non-DINO member alone. The remaining version of the diversity
argument is that mutually distant members contribute as a GROUP where none of them earns a seat singly —
three trunks that disagree with the roster and with each other. `record_mix` answers it from the holdout
arrays already on disk, with no card and no inference pass:

```
A: roster alone            7 members: held-out 0.8766  in-sample 0.8763   <- peak
B: roster + 3 non-DINO     7 members: held-out 0.8766  in-sample 0.8763   <- same peak, same seats
                           8 members: held-out 0.8758  (-0.0008)
                           9 members: held-out 0.8748  (-0.0018)
                          10 members: held-out 0.8728  (-0.0038)
```

`vjepa_warm` 0.8337, `swin_supervised` 0.8331, `cnx_own_recipe` 0.8186 against a roster whose weakest
member is 0.8525. **The honest greedy does not seat any of them, and the peak is identical to four
decimals with and without them.** Forcing them in costs monotonically in the order they are forced.

So the block form of the argument fails the same way the single form did, and it fails without the
band-includes-zero ambiguity that made `vjepa_warm`'s -0.0007 unreadable: 8, 9 and 10 seats are all worse
than 7, in both directions of the honest split.

**Consequence for the slot.** There is no ensemble containing a non-DINO member that beats the roster, so
a submission built to satisfy the "use it on a submission" goal is measured to lose rather than merely
predicted to. The goal is reached by making a non-DINO member good enough to seat, which is
`swin_calib_dense` (`knee-csxq`), not by spending a slot on the members that exist.

**What it does not say**, and the limit is the same one the seat reading carries: this is a fact about
members at 0.819-0.834 against a roster starting at 0.8525, not about non-DINO architectures. It bounds
the LEVEL at which diversity stops paying. A non-DINO trunk at 0.85+ is untouched by it, and untried.

### The diversity search seats every non-DINO member first, and pays for each one (2026-08-30)

The earlier block reading — roster plus the three non-DINO trunks, honest greedy, no gain — left two
harness suspects standing, and both are now tested.

VOTE RULE, cleared. That reading did not name a vote rule while the board serves `LogitAverage`, and
this tool's own docs warn the seat curve moves with the rule. Re-run under `--vote logit` over the
roster plus `swin_supervised`, `vjepa_warm` and `cnx_own_recipe`: 80 of 95 records became members over
909 shared studies, and the honest peak is 19 seats / 0.8763 — the same count and the same number, to
four decimals, as the roster alone. None of the three is seated at any count from 1 to 24.

SEAT CRITERION, cleared, and this is the stronger reading. The honest search is quality-driven, so
"the greedy never took them" could always be answered with "the greedy was not looking for spread".
`--seats diverse` looks for exactly that: it takes the member least correlated with anything already
seated, and never opens the labels. It seats all three non-DINO trunks immediately —

  diverse 4: 0.8636  +lora_r8_v3small_224  (nearest 0.8083)
  diverse 5: 0.8642  +vjepa_warm           (nearest 0.8179)
  diverse 6: 0.8624  +cnx_own_recipe       (nearest 0.8200)
  diverse 7: 0.8622  +swin_supervised      (nearest 0.8425)

— because they ARE the most decorrelated members this project owns: nearest neighbours 0.818 to 0.843
against the rest of the pool's 0.91 to 0.94. The claim that these trunks buy disagreement is correct
and is confirmed here on the widest pool yet measured. What is refuted is that the disagreement pays.
The curve falls at each of the three, and the spread-built ensemble peaks 0.8725 at 50-52 seats against
the quality-built 0.8763 at 19 — diversity-first loses by 0.0038, six times the paired floor's sixth
and comparable to the floor itself.

READ THE DIVERSE NUMBERS AS ORDER, NOT AS SCORE. `diverse` chooses and scores on the same studies, so
its curve reports its own overfitting and only `honest` may be quoted. The seat ORDER is not a score,
and the non-seating is established independently on the honest curve above; the diverse curve is here
to show WHY, not to price anything.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT CLOSE. It does not say a non-DINO trunk cannot seat — it says these three
cannot, at the solo scores they have (0.8331, 0.8337, 0.8186) against a 0.8459 merit level, and that
no seat criterion available rescues them. The open question is unchanged and is what `swin_calib_dense`
(knee-csxq) asks: whether the lane's ceiling is the architecture or the recipe it was read on. Answer
that with a number, never by re-running a seat search over the same three members under a fourth rule.

### The non-DINO seat delta is UNRESOLVED, not negative — and that is what earns it a slot (2026-08-30)

A correction to the entry above, from running `board_transfer` rather than quoting a slope out of prose.

The compression SATURATES and the whole-record number does not describe us. Median +1.23 board points
per holdout point over all 392 orderable pairs; among entries at or above 0.8670 it is +0.98
[+0.94, +1.08] over 16 pairs, and at or above 0.8692 it is +0.80 [+0.70, +1.19]. The +1.55 and +1.82
figures that circulate are whole-record fits, and every entry this project would now ship sits in the
saturated part of the curve where the slope is ~1.0 or below.

THE READING THAT CORRECTS THE PREVIOUS ENTRY. That entry priced the non-DINO block at -0.0038 honest
and called the axis closed for shipping. The number is right and the conclusion did not follow: the
paired holdout floor is 0.0053, so -0.0038 is an UNRESOLVED pair on our own ruler, not a negative one.
`board_transfer` makes that distinction load-bearing rather than pedantic — it reports 9 inversions in
392 pairs, and ALL NINE are pairs the holdout left unresolved. Among the 252 pairs the holdout did
resolve at a gap of 0.0053 or more, the board has never once ordered the other way.

So the honest statement about a non-DINO entry is not that it is measured to lose. It is that our
offline ruler cannot settle it, and that the board is the only instrument that can — which is this
project's own standing test for what earns one of five daily slots, and the same argument
`recal_holdannot`'s TRANSFERS branch is pre-registered on.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT LICENSE. It does not re-open the three declined trunks as MEMBERS: their solo scores
(0.8331, 0.8337, 0.8186) are resolved against the 0.8459 merit level by a wide margin, and the diverse
search result above stands. It licenses ONE board reading of the composition axis, on a newly trained
trunk, to find out whether a maximally-decorrelated member transfers differently than the offline ruler
can see. One slot, one question, and the answer prices the whole axis either way.

### The fixed discovery made the Swin WORSE, and the seat went to the trunk that was already packaged (2026-08-30)

`swin_wholetop` finished 12 of 12 epochs, converged: 0.7444, 0.7816, 0.8109, 0.8164, 0.8168, 0.8189,
**0.8274 (peak, e6)**, 0.8228, 0.8223, 0.8197, 0.8186, 0.8180. `convergence_check` reads it CONVERGED, so
the number is the recipe's and not a killed process's.

It was the re-run of `swin_supervised` byte-identical on the fixed block discovery (knee-94ec), which
doubled trainable parameters to 37,869,696 and opened both 1024-wide stage-3 blocks. It came out **0.0057
below** the handicapped run it was built to correct, and the deficit was visible from e1: +0.0003, +0.0013,
-0.0001, -0.0028, -0.0041, and it never came back. This is the outcome `swin_wholetop.sh` pre-registered
under REFUTES: the frozen stage 3 was not a handicap on this trunk at this rate, it was the right amount of
trunk to move. The correction that follows is a RATE arm, and it is already queued as `swin_calib_dense`
(knee-csxq) at 4e-5 with `--calibrated-targets`.

THE MID-CURVE TIE-BREAK IS RETIRED AGAINST THE FINISHED CURVE. At e7 the deficit narrowed (-0.0033 against
e6's -0.0057) and I recorded that it broke the monotone-widening premise the knee-tsiz/knee-tild ruling had
rested on. The finished curve settles it: e8 -0.0108, e9 -0.0134, e10 -0.0145, e11 -0.0151 against
`swin_supervised`'s own epochs. e7 was scatter, and the ruling stands for the right reason rather than the
one first given.

WHAT IT COST THE ENTRY THAT WAS BUILT FOR IT. `kneemri-swinseat` was written, bootstrap-verified and
committed before this curve finished, seating `swin_wholetop_s2026` as a seventh member of the champion
six. `mount_check` REFUSED it — the member is not in the package — and rather than package a checkpoint
that had just failed its own bar, the kernel was retired and the entry rebuilt as `kneemri-vjepaseat`.

THE SEAT RULE WAS WRITTEN BEFORE THE NUMBER (knee-wqfz) and then overtaken by a better member. The rule
said: seat `swin_wholetop` if its finished peak reaches 0.8331, else seat `swin_supervised`. It reached
0.8274, so the Swin seat was `swin_supervised`'s. But `vjepa_warm_s2026` beats BOTH on every axis measured
on a shared ruler — 0.8337 solo against 0.8331 and 0.8274, nearest-neighbour agreement 0.8119 against
0.8346 — and unlike either Swin it is ALREADY on the roster, already in `dimiturnt/kneemri-members`, and
already mounted from `dimiturnt/vjepa2-hf`. So the entry costs no 7.5 GB re-upload and the slot is spent
hours earlier.

THE HONEST STATEMENT ABOUT THE GOAL. The goal was to train a non-DINO trunk and spend a submission on it.
The training half ran and did not produce a seatable member: `swin_wholetop` is 0.0186 under the 0.8459 seat bar
merit level and under its own control. Shipping it anyway would be spending the slot on the checkpoint's
provenance rather than on the axis. The axis is what the goal is for, so the slot goes to the strongest
non-DINO member the project owns, and the training half continues in `swin_calib_dense`.

WHAT NONE OF THIS LICENSES. It does not re-open the ConvNeXt pair (knee-uk4f): that re-open was always
priced off `swin_wholetop`'s delta, which is now negative at every epoch of a finished curve, so it is
priced worse than before rather than better. And it does not make distance a seat argument — knee-053z has
failed the distance-to-seat inference three times. Distance is why `vjepa_warm` and not another non-DINO
member; the reason the entry is worth a slot is that the champion is six `--fold -1` members and no offline
ruler can price it at all.

## 2026-08-30 — recal_holdannot LANDS: the reader's scale was a real defect, and fixing it is free (`knee-8wa0`)

`recal_holdannot` = `holdannot`'s recipe with the supervision table swapped for `report_labels_v3.csv`,
whose six reader levels are replaced by their measured positive rates on the 58 radiologist-read studies
(`kneemri.evaluation.level_calibration`, fitted under knee-7oep). Every other flag byte-identical. The map
is strictly increasing, so the TABLE's own per-label rank AUC does not move — only what the model is asked
to fit does.

Read on both rulers as knee-9198 requires, and on GOLD first as the arm pre-registered, because the proxy's
truth IS the report table and is therefore biased against label-side movement.

| ruler | control `holdannot` | `recal_holdannot` | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| **GOLD** (`supervision_gap`, 58 annotated studies) | 0.8932 | **0.9037** | **+0.0105** |
| **proxy** (`ruler_check` on `report_labels_v2`, 909 studies) | 0.8506 | 0.8515 | +0.0009 |
| proxy, confident-only ruler (71.0% of cells kept) | 0.8740 | 0.8754 | +0.0014 |

**This is the arm's own LANDS branch: gold up by more than the 0.0062 floor, proxy not down.** The reader
over-calls in the middle of its scale — the 0.68 level is 62% negative and was trained as 0.68 positive on
12% of cells — and re-pointing the gradient at the measured rate moves the model toward the image-read
process at no cost on the report-derived one. It is worth a slot on its own terms.

**READ THE PROXY NUMBERS FROM `ruler_check`, NOT FROM THE TRAINING LOG.** `recal_holdannot`'s own log ends
`best holdout mean AUC 0.8964`, which is +0.0477 over the control and is NOT a result: the arm passed
`--labels v3` with `--eval-labels` unset, so its holdout truth was binarised at 0.5 against the RE-MAPPED
values and the ruler moved with the arm. `run_comparison` refuses the pair outright — *"the two runs were
scored by different label tables over their 909 shared studies"* — which is the guard working. The matched
proxy above comes from re-scoring the run's stored holdout record against v2. Any future label-VALUE arm
must pin `--eval-labels report_labels_v2.csv`, the way `blendlabels` did; `holdannot.sh`'s clone did not,
and the 0.8964 sat in the log for an hour looking like the largest single-arm gain the project has ever
measured.

**HONEST SIZE.** n=58 on the gold ruler is a level, not a selector (knee-kddo): +0.0105 clears the 0.0062
floor but not by much, and the printed interval is on the reader-model GAP, not on the arm-control delta.
One arm, one recipe corner (224 px, whole-stack, 12 slices). What it establishes is a SIGN and a free
lunch, not a size. It is also an order of magnitude under the 1.5% bar on its own, exactly as the label
lane was priced on 2026-08-25 (`blendlabels`, +0.0034): the lane is LIVE and SMALL, and v3 is now the
better table to build the lane's members on rather than a path to 0.950 by itself.

**FOLLOW-UP, in cost order.** (1) v3 is free — make it the default supervision table for new label-side
arms. (2) A dense-corner replication (`band_dense_hold` has a matched control on both rulers and costs one
arm) would say whether +0.0105 is a property of the re-map or of the 224 corner. (3) Only then a roster
rebuild, which is many arms and should not be bought on a single n=58 read.

### `warm_calib_lowlr` — a 4x lower rate moved the warm start by less than the noise floor, so the ramp was NOT the cause — 2026-08-30

`warm_calib_lowlr_s2026` best holdout **0.8577** @ epoch 4 of 12 (`convergence_check`: not truncated —
it ran all twelve and declined through eight of them). Against its two references: the warm control
`warm_calib_dense_s2026` **0.8562** (+0.0015) and the cold parent `calib_dense_hold_s2026` **0.8634**
(−0.0057).

**The single flag is `--backbone-lr`, 4e-5 to 1e-5**, exactly as `warm_calib_dense`'s own verdict sent
it — same encoder file, same twelve epochs, same recipe. The flag landed: the log opens `encoder
initialised from calib_dense_hold.enc.pt, adapted on cache 0 (223 tensors, 0 left stock)`.

**The number lands in the arm's `0.8572–0.8643` band by five ten-thousandths, and the band's own reading
does not survive the trajectory.** That branch reads "THE RAMP WAS THE CAUSE, QUALITY IS STILL FLAT". But
the branch boundary was drawn at the warm control plus 0.0010, which is INSIDE the 0.0062 arm-vs-arm
floor — so the pre-registration wrote a band a noise-sized delta could enter. Quartering the backbone rate
moved the outcome by +0.0015. **A lever that is the cause does not survive a 4x reduction of itself
unchanged.** The honest reading is the opposite of the band's label: the ramp is not what costs the warm
start its 0.0057.

**What the epoch curve says instead.** 0.8540 · 0.8572 · 0.8546 · 0.8530 · **0.8577** · 0.8526 · 0.8536 ·
0.8506 · 0.8481 · 0.8486 · 0.8489 · 0.8491. Training loss falls monotonically 0.8206 → 0.4467 across the
same twelve epochs. **The model is at 0.8540 before it has trained at all, and every epoch after that
trades holdout for loss.** That is the same shape the 4e-5 arm drew. A warm encoder arrives already
holding what twelve cold epochs would have built — and fine-tuning on top of it, at either rate, only
fits the training set.

**So warm starting is a TIME mechanism with no quality term, and that is a usable result rather than a
null.** One epoch of a warm start ≈ twelve cold ones, to within 0.009 of the cold parent's converged
number; the eight-epoch saving `warm_calib_lowlr.sh:14` was written to buy is real. What it does not buy
is a better member, and no rate makes it one. Members stay cold-trained; the warm path is for arms whose
question is not the checkpoint's quality.

**Which cell of the grid this closes, and which it does not.** rank-0 × warm × {4e-5, 1e-5} is now
measured twice and flat both times. Branch **A** of `knee-wbwq`'s chain (schedule) is SPENT. Branch **B**
— the actual capacity arm, a LoRA parent warm-started WITH a fresh `--lora-rank`, where `fitted_encoder.py`
merges instead of falling through — is untouched by this and is the only live cell. `warm_calib_dense_short`
(**C**) was gated on A or B clearing; A did not clear, so it stays gated on B alone.

**Card note, so the epoch times read right.** Epoch 10 took 648s against the run's own ~365s median
because I ran `witness_check` on the same card mid-arm. That is the contention `card_check` exists to
prevent, and it is mine.

### `cnx_warm_anneal` — a second trunk, a second warm restart, and the same absence of a quality term — 2026-08-30

**`cnx_warm_anneal_s2026` peaks at 0.8142, epoch 2 of 6, against a parent peak of 0.8186.** The
pre-registration named four bands
before the run started; this lands in **CONVERGED (0.8126–0.8225)** — "the trunk was already at its
ceiling and the restart adds nothing". Not the DIRECTIONAL band, not the ramp band.

| epoch | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| holdout AUC | 0.8141 | 0.8136 | **0.8142** | 0.8105 | 0.8074 | 0.8068 |
| train loss | — | — | 0.4636 | 0.4393 | 0.4240 | 0.4172 |

**The shape is the finding, not the peak.** Loss falls monotonically from 0.4636 to 0.4172 while the
holdout AUC falls with it, every epoch after the second. The `one_cycle` anneal at epoch 5 — the part
of the schedule that is supposed to collect the gain — produced the run's *worst* number. This is not a
run that was cut off before it could pay; it is a run that paid nothing and then took some back.

**It reproduces `warm_calib_lowlr` on a different trunk.** That arm (dense, 12 epochs, 4× lower rate)
concluded warm starting is a TIME mechanism with no quality term. This is cnx, 6 epochs, the parent's
own rate, and it says the same thing from a different direction: the restart opened 0.0045 *below* the
parent it started from (0.8141 vs 0.8186) and never got back. Two trunks, two schedules, two rates, one
absence. The mechanism is not "the ramp walked it off" — a 4× rate cut did not rescue the first one, and
here the decline continues through the anneal, where a rate artefact would have reversed.

**What this does NOT rule out.** Warm starting still buys wall-clock: one warm epoch reached within
0.009 of the converged parent. That use is untouched. What is now measured twice is that it does not
buy QUALITY, so a warm restart may be used to reach a known number faster and never to exceed one.

**`trajectory_check` could not arbitrate it, and the arm ran to completion because of that.** The gate
refused: `only 1 run(s) match a 6-epoch budget past epoch 3, and 8 are needed before a spread may decide
anything`. The floor fix (knee-e8sm) made short budgets readable, not read — the 6-epoch corpus is one
run deep, and it is this one. Killing on judgment while the instrument refuses is the exact state that
check exists to remove, so the arm was left alone and read afterwards by `convergence_check`, which
found it clean: six epochs asked, six recorded, peak at e2. The number is a peak, not a floor.

## The best solo in the pool is worth +0.0002 as a seat, and it is not a twin (2026-08-31)

`stack_increments_s2026` scores **0.8642** on the fold-0 holdout — the highest solo number this project
owns — and had never been priced as a seat. `roster_check`'s 2026-08-29 sweep is what surfaced it: it
was packaged and scoreable and nobody had ever asked what it adds.

`seat_value --candidates stack_increments_s2026.pt --against greedyseat_v1`, card-free, on the 909-study
fold-0 holdout:

| reading | value |
|---|---|
| roster of 7 | 0.8763 |
| + `stack_increments_s2026` as an 8th seat | 0.8765 (**+0.0002**), band [-0.0002, +0.0007] |
| best swap it could make (for `calib_dense_hold_s2026`) | 0.8766 (**+0.0003**) |
| its nearest-neighbour agreement with the roster | 0.9062 (mean 0.8885) |

**The band includes zero and the best swap is a quarter of the +0.0015 this ruler needs to pick a board
tick.** Zero, on the strongest member available.

**And the twin explanation does not cover it, which is the part worth keeping.** The seated members'
own nearest-neighbour agreements span 0.8772 to 0.9225; this candidate's 0.9062 sits in the middle of
that range, so by the roster's own scale it is no closer to its neighbours than the members already
seated are to theirs. It is not being rejected as a duplicate. It is a genuinely differently-behaved
model of clearly the best solo quality, and the ensemble cannot use it.

That is the cleanest support yet for `knee-uco3`'s inert-seat reading, and it is the FIFTH: three board
operations on the seating (reweight, add, swap) each returned an unresolvable move, and now the best
offline candidate prices at zero offline too — so the board flats are not a board-noise story. The
constraint is the roster, not the ruler and not the member.

**What it does NOT say.** Nothing here prices a member built on a corpus or a decode path the roster
does not already hold — `stack_increments` is a table-plus-distillation member on the same corpus and
the same decode as its neighbours. The route statement's conjunction is untouched by this, and this is
evidence FOR it: quality alone, at the top of the pool, buys nothing.

## Every operation on the champion's seating is now measured, and all of them are flat (2026-08-31)

Five readings landed within a day, four offline and one on the board, and they close a question rather
than adding a point to it.

**The three offline zeros.** Each priced a different explanation of what an eighth seat could buy, all
against `greedyseat_v1` (roster of 7, 0.8763) on the fold-0 holdout and the `report_labels_v2` ruler.

| candidate | what it tested | seat value | band | best swap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `stack_increments_s2026` | the pool's BEST SOLO, ordinary diversity | +0.0002 | [-0.0002, +0.0007] | +0.0003 |
| `merged_labelwise_cf` | the MOST DECODE-DIVERSE candidate ever priced here (nearest 0.8873, mean 0.8583, against a seated spread of 0.8772-0.9225) | +0.0005 | [-0.0002, +0.0012] | +0.0005 |
| `merged_distill_cf` | BOTH quality levers in one member (the distill teacher and the merged corpus) | +0.0000 | [-0.0005, +0.0006] | +0.0001 |

None clears +0.0015, under which this ruler has never been shown to pick a board tick. Quality alone,
diversity alone, and the two together each return zero, from three different directions.

**The board reading that matters more.** `holdswap_v1` (ref 55900461) is `raptorweight_v1` with
`calib_dense_hold_ff` for `lr4e-5_ws_cf` — a same-count, blind-for-blind seat SWAP — and it scored
**0.944 against the control's 0.944**. Dead flat. Put beside `vjepaseat_v1` (0.943, an ADDED seat on the
architecture axis with the most distant member the project owns), `raptorseat_v1` (0.943),
`fleettwo_v1` (0.942) and `raptorweight_v1` (+0.001 for a reweight), every operation available on a fixed
pool — add, reweight, swap, on both the architecture and the corpus axes — now has a flat or negative
reading on the instrument that can actually see the champion.

**So the standing reframe was wrong, and it is worth saying which part.** The reframe was that the offline
zeros describe a blind RULER rather than a saturated pool: `seat_value` prices against `greedyseat_v1` at
0.936, while the shipped champion is 0.944 and five of its six members are `--fold -1` blind fits that
`RecordMix` excludes by construction, so the champion's lane is unmeasured offline. That much is still
true and still limits every offline number here. What it does NOT license is the inference drawn from it —
that a seating gain might be hiding in the champion's lane where the ruler cannot look. `holdswap_v1` looked
there directly, with the board, and found the same zero. The ruler's blindness is real; it was not
concealing anything.

**The consequence is a redirection, not a smaller bar.** knee-urvf already said the ensemble tracks
best-single + ~0.015 and that the bonus has not grown in fourteen days. With the arrangement now measured
as saturated from every side, MEMBER QUALITY IS THE ONLY FREE TERM, and card spent on rearranging seats is
card spent on a measured zero. knee-uco3 should be read as evidence for knee-urvf rather than as a separate
finding.

**What this does not close.** It says nothing about a member that is BOTH distant and at or above the
seated quality level — every distant member tested so far has been 0.017-0.020 short on solo score, which is
the size `vjepaseat_v1`'s row puts on the requirement. That is a member-quality problem, so it lands in the
same lane. It also says nothing about a genuinely different external corpus; the merged-corpus cell is now
three collisions deep (`merged_dense_cf` -0.0028, `merged_labelwise_cf` -0.0026, `merged_distill_cf`
-0.0005) and is one cell wide, which is why MRNet (knee-ombx) is still the corpus lever and another cross of
the two corpora already here is not.

**What was spent, and on what.** `swin_supervised_ff` was armed to put the project's most decorrelated
member into shippable blind form and was killed seven minutes in, once `vjepaseat_v1`'s row was read: it had
already run that experiment with a MORE distant member and returned flat. The card went to
`stack_increments_ff` (knee-8ft1) instead — the pool's best solo refit `--fold -1 --ema`, so that the one
lane still open can be shipped without paying the ~0.008 blind-vs-fold-0 penalty that has kept it out of the
champion. The single overnight slot went to `spanseat_v1`, priced at ~10% before it was fired and fired
anyway because the slot cannot be banked and nothing buildable in the window priced better.

## Feature distillation from the foreign trunk is FLAT, and that closes knee-8009 on both cells (2026-09-01)

`raptor_feat_pre` → `raptor_feat_fit`, swinbase, 336 px, 20 slices, 12 epochs one_cycle, ~930-1010 s an
epoch. Stage one shaped the trunk toward `raptor_features.npz` at `feature_weight` 20.0:
`raptor_feat_pre_s2026` recorded **0.8201**. Stage two fit the labels from that encoder with a cold head:
`raptor_feat_fit_s2026` peaked at epoch 6 with **0.8334**, then slid to 0.8211 by epoch 11 while the
loss fell — converged, not truncated.

Against the arm's own pre-registered control, `swin_supervised_s2026` at 0.8331 cold, that is **+0.0003**:
inside the FLAT branch (-0.0061 to +0.0014), a twentieth of the 0.0062 floor.

**The pre-registration named this outcome a result rather than a null, and it holds.** A REPRESENTATION
target ties the cold trunk where a LOGIT target lost 0.0077. So what the -0.0077 measured was the LEVEL
of the target, not distillation as a mechanism — a foreign teacher's features are neither harmful nor
worth 3.9 hours of card. knee-8009 closes on both of its cells: the trunk cause for distillation is
spent, and only the corpus cause (knee-ombx, MRNet) is still open.

**No seat reading exists for it.** `run_train` refused to price the seat against the champion —
`raptorweight_v1` seats five blind `--fold -1` members that carry no holdout record, so 1 of 6 seats is
scoreable and a marginal contribution needs at least 2. The member is 0.031 under the pool's best solo,
so a seat pass against `honest12` was not bought either.

**The teacher's in-sample exposure did not have to be discounted.** `foreign_overlap` reads raptor at
98.6% in-sample on this corpus, which is why a positive here would have been an upper bound. A flat
reading needs no such correction: the memorised teacher could not lift the student even with the
advantage.

### `cnx_mid_rate` re-ran and finished — the entry above quotes the ABORTED attempt — 2026-09-01

The entry above ("it ran one epoch and left a `.partial`") was true when written and is now stale. The
arm was re-run and completed: `cnx_mid_rate_s2026.metrics.jsonl` holds **12 of 12 epochs, best 0.7993 @
epoch 6**, last 0.7884, and `cnx_mid_rate_s2026.pt` exists. The first attempt survives beside it in a
`.metrics.1.jsonl` file — one epoch only, and its score is the one the older entry quotes.
That older score belongs to a killed process rather than to an architecture, which is exactly the
confusion `convergence_check` exists to prevent, and it is why the ledger now carries both entries
instead of an edit that would have hidden the first.

**Read 0.7993, never 0.7177.** The run peaked at epoch 6 of 12 and declined to 0.7884, so it is neither
TRUNCATED nor UNDERTRAINED; the budget was not the binding constraint and the score is a real ceiling
for this recipe, not a floor.

**It is still not a shippable member, and the reason is not convergence.** Priced against `honest12` by
`seat_value` on 2026-09-01 it is the most DECORRELATED candidate in the pool — rank 0.7598, JS 0.0304

(board ref 55895006). That is the exact `vjepaseat` failure mode: distant and weak buys nothing, and
`vjepaseat` measured -0.001 for it. The full argument is in `comp/members.declines`; re-open it by

finding — the most distant member we own is also among the weakest, which Kimi's Q-F research
