## RadImageNet DenseNet closes the convolutional trunk lane EMPTY, and the difficulty axis opens

`radnet_family` (12 epochs, RadImageNet DenseNet-121, otherwise `band_dense`'s recipe) peaked at
**0.6716** against its own pre-registered floor of 0.75. Epochs 7-11 read 0.6501 / 0.6642 / 0.6681 /
0.6667 / 0.6586 — a converged run, not a truncated one, and 0.19 below the non-DINOv2 seat bar of
0.8521. The pre-registered branch that fires is THE CELL IS EMPTY FOR A REASON: only capacity re-opens
it. This was the largest open lever on the trunk axis and the one arm this session's plan said could
plausibly deliver 1.5%. It did not, and the plan was wrong about where the 1.5% is.

What replaced it came out of three arms already on disk, read together for the first time:

| arm | difficulty signal | how it is spent | holdout |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `disagreed_full` | member disagreement | static tilt, alpha 1.0 from step one | 0.8471 |
| `disagreed_uniform` | — | matched control, alpha 0.0 | 0.8507 |
| `certainty_ramp` | label certainty | schedule, 6 of 12 epochs | **0.8584** |
| `band_dense` | — | ledger's uniform draw | 0.8578 |

The static tilt COSTS 0.0036 against its own control. The schedule PAYS 0.0077, above the 0.0062
holdout floor. The two differ in WHEN the intervention lands, not in whether difficulty is used — and
that is the same shape Zhou et al. (ISBI 2023) report on elbow-fracture radiographs, +0.0245 binary AUC
from an easy-to-hard curriculum. `certainty_ramp` is on the roster at 0.8584.

The 2x2 therefore has one empty cell, the schedule applied to the signal that lost, and it is the one
place the two neighbours point opposite ways. `disagreed_ramp` (knee-zer5) fills it: alpha 1.0 reached
over 6 of 12 epochs, both controls already on disk.

### The 2x2 closes: it is the SCHEDULE that pays, not the signal (2026-09-02)

`disagreed_ramp` filled the empty cell and read **0.8574** (converged, peak epoch 7 of 12,
`convergence_check`: 1 converged). The grid, all four cells now measured against the same control:

| | static, alpha 1.0 from step one | ramped over 6 of 12 epochs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **member disagreement** | `disagreed_full` 0.8471 (**-0.0036**) | `disagreed_ramp` 0.8574 (**+0.0067**) |
| **label certainty** | not run | `certainty_ramp` 0.8584 (**+0.0077**) |
| **neither** | `disagreed_uniform` 0.8507 — the control both deltas are taken against | |

The signal that LOST when applied flat is the same signal that PAYS when ramped, and it pays within
0.0010 of the other signal's ramp — which is noise on a 0.0062 holdout floor. So the two ramps are one
reading, not two: **the difficulty SIGNAL is nearly free to choose, and the SCHEDULE is the whole
effect.** Both ramps clear the floor; the static tilt is the only cell below it, and it is below on the
wrong side of zero.

That is a mechanism and not a knob: a static tilt reweights the loss before the model can tell a hard
study from a mislabelled one, so it spends capacity fitting the second; a ramp lets the easy mass set
the representation first and admits the hard mass once there is something for it to correct. It is the
shape Zhou et al. (ISBI 2023) report on elbow-fracture radiographs (+0.0245 from easy-to-hard), and it
now holds here across two unrelated difficulty definitions.

What it does NOT license: a seat. `disagreed_ramp` is rostered at 0.8574 — level with the pool's best
member (`band_dense` 0.8578) and second to `slot_dropout` (0.8592) — but the member axis is closed on
seven board flats, and one more dinov2-small member of ordinary quality is exactly what those seven
flats measured. The ramp's value is as a RECIPE the trunk-family arm inherits, not as a seventh seat.

## One label table is priced against its twin: `stack_increments_fx` against `stack_increments_base`

This heading read "the label lane is priced, and it does not pay" until 2026-09-04. One twin pair
prices ONE table; it never closed the lane. The lane closes by exhaustion over every table the
project can build, and that argument lives in
`interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-03_the-label-lane-closes-by-exhaustion.md` — read it there, not here.

| arm | labels | best holdout | delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stack_increments_base` | `report_labels_v2.csv` | **0.8635** (e9, e11) | control |
| `stack_increments_fx` | `blend_hybrid_fx.csv` | **0.8595** (e6) | **−0.0040** |

Byte-identical arms but for `--labels`, run on the same card in the same hours, both twelve epochs,
neither truncated — `base` peaks at e9 and holds 0.8635 through e11, `fx` peaks at e6 and declines
monotonically after (0.8559 / 0.8586 / 0.8588 / 0.8579 / 0.8582). So the number is a fact about the
label table, not about a killed process.

**−0.0040 lands in the band the pre-registration did not name.** It is past NULL (±0.0015) and short of
REGRESSION (below twin − 0.0062). It cannot be called a regression: 0.0040 is inside the 0.0062 holdout
floor. It is emphatically not CARRIES (needed 0.8697) or PARTIAL (needed 0.8650).

**In substance the NULL clause fires, and it prices more than one file.** `blend_hybrid_fx` beat the
plain report label on the only ruler whose truth is not report-derived — the 57 radiologist-annotated
studies, mean 0.9030 against 0.8955, Fracture 0.9346 against 0.8147 — on a correction that was
pre-registered before measurement, cleared two independent permutation nulls (p = 0.0022, p = 0.0010),
carried a bootstrap CI excluding zero, and showed a coherent acute-trauma placebo pattern. All of that
survived, and **none of it transferred to training.** The finding is therefore about the RULER, not
about the correction: a gain measured on 57 gold studies does not predict a gain under training, which
is what the arm was built to find out. That prices the entire label lane — including the blocked rubric
re-read and the negation pass — and it retires the lane rather than the one file.

**What it does not settle.** The gold ruler is 57 studies; the training holdout is 909. A correction
worth +0.0075 on the first is well inside the second's noise in both directions, so this arm bounds how
BIG a label effect can be, not whether one exists. The honest statement is that no label correction this
project can validate is worth more than the floor, so no further card time goes to the lane.

## crop160_span — the field widened, and the margin story splits (2026-09-02)

`crop160_span` ran 12/12 epochs and peaked **0.8564 at e8** against its control **band_span 0.8565**:
**-0.0001**, the arm's own NULL branch on the mean. bead knee-ii0q.

The arm was not written for the mean. It was written because `crop80_span` cropped IN, 130 mm -> 80 mm,
and lost most on the structures at the field's margins — MCL -0.0265, ACL -0.0263, against a mean of
-0.0099 — and the decode-geometry family was closed on reading that pair as ONE margin effect. Nothing
had ever been read going out. This is that read, at 420 px so mm/px is held (0.381 vs 0.387) and field
of view is not confounded with resolution.

**Going out, the pair splits.** Peak-epoch per-label against the same control:

| finding | crop160_span | band_span | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| MCL | 0.7955 | 0.7869 | **+0.0086** |
| ACL | 0.8730 | 0.8854 | **-0.0124** |
| Fracture | 0.8184 | 0.8146 | +0.0038 |
| Lateral Meniscus | 0.8399 | 0.8406 | -0.0007 |
| Medial Meniscus | 0.9031 | 0.9042 | -0.0011 |
| mean | 0.8564 | 0.8565 | -0.0001 |

One mechanism cannot lose both structures together when the field narrows and then move them in opposite
directions when it widens. So the margin explanation is wrong about at least one of MCL and ACL, and the
likeliest reading is that ACL's loss under crop80 was never about the margins at all — it is central in
the frame, and what it lost going in was the joint's FRACTION of the frame rather than tissue at the edge.
Going out, that fraction falls again (60% of series cannot fill a 160 mm frame and are padded), which
would cost ACL in both directions. That is a testable statement and nothing here tests it.

**What this does NOT do.** It does not re-open the decode-geometry family. Both per-label moves sit inside
per-label noise: the 0.0062 paired floor is computed on the MEAN over twelve findings, and a single label
carries fewer positives, so its half-width is WIDER, not narrower. Reading +0.0086 on one label as a
result would be exactly the denominator error CLAUDE.md names. The closure stands on the mean; what it
loses is its explanation.

Rostered as shippable (0.8564 clears the 0.8521 non-DINOv2 bar, and it is the pool's only member fitted
at a field wider than 130 mm), not as a seat claim.

## 2026-09-02 — slice coverage: two arms ran on 2026-08-31 and nobody read them

Kimi's Q-BO reply ranks **slice coverage** as the one lever from the published record that is both
clean-signalled and still unread here: frontier public notebooks decode 64 slices, our arms stop at
12-20 on VRAM, and Qiu et al. 2024 report +0.056 mean AUC from better ROI/slice geometry. The axis was
not unread. `stack224` and `cover_labelwise` both finished on 2026-08-31, wrote holdout records and
metrics, converged (`convergence_check` flags neither), and then entered no ledger section at all — so
the finding was paid for and thrown away, and a research answer was about to send the card after it a
second time.

| arm | what moves against `base224` | best AUC | Δ vs `base224` 0.8509 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base224` | the control: 12 slices, band 0.2-0.8, 224 px, `--variant base` | **0.8509** | — |
| `stack224` | **36 slices**, band opened to 0.05-0.95 | 0.8476 (e9 of 13) | **−0.0033** |
| `cover_labelwise` | 36 slices, band 0.05-0.95, labelwise slice pooling | 0.8495 (e9 of 14) | **−0.0014** |

**Tripling the slice count buys nothing.** Both deltas are negative and both sit inside the 0.0062 paired
holdout floor, so the honest reading is FLAT rather than harmful. Neither clears the 0.8521 non-DINOv2
seat bar; both clear the 0.8459 merit bar.

**What is NOT isolated here, and it matters.** `stack224` moves two flags at once by construction — 36
slices only reaches new tissue if the band opens with it, which its own header says — and
`cover_labelwise` moves a third (the pooling operator). So this closes the COVERAGE CONCEPT, not the
slice count alone. A run at 36 slices inside the 0.2-0.8 band is not on disk and would separate them;
given both readings land under the floor on the mean, that separation is not worth a card hour.

**The VRAM ceiling is real and is the reason the axis stops here.** Both arms peak at 21.86 GB against
the 12-slice recipes' 16.24 GB, on the reservation curve already recorded above: allocation is a
function of slice count and nothing else. 64 slices at 224 px does not fit, so matching the public
frontier's decode density would need the resolution to drop below 224, which `res392`/`base224` already
priced as flat in the other direction.

**Consequence for Q-BO.** Of Kimi's four ranked candidates, external labelled data already read flat on
our external-corpus seat axis, TTA/multi-view is spent through `SlotHead`'s six slots, and slice coverage
is this section. That leaves label/target engineering as the only one of the four with no arm against it
— and Kimi's own CheXpert scaling citation bounds it at a few AUC points for a large labeler gain, which
is under what the 0.008 board gap needs.

| Medial OA | 0.8968 | 0.8733 | labelwise_dense_s2026 | 333 |
| ACL | 0.8976 | 0.8779 | stackfit_s2026 | 248 |
| Medial Meniscus | 0.9135 | 0.8961 | small_batch6_s2026 | 482 |
| Baker's | 0.9279 | 0.9061 | merged_dense_cf | 217 |

### Per-label seat choice is DIRECTIONAL, and the oracle is two-thirds selection bias

Mean of per-label BESTS is 0.8767 against the best single member's 0.8642 — an apparent +0.0125 from
letting each label pick its own seat. That is an ORACLE: twelve choices over 102 members, all scored on
the same 909 studies. The honest control, 20 random splits of the holdout, selecting per label on half A
and scoring on half B, against the single member with the best MEAN on A scored on B:

```
gain over best-single-member: mean +0.0046  sd 0.0033  min -0.0014  max +0.0134
splits positive: 19/20
```

**+0.0046, positive in 19 of 20 splits, against a 0.0062 noise floor.** The SIGN survives out of sample;
the SIZE does not clear the bar. Directional by this project's own rule — keep it if it is ever free,
never plan around it. Two-thirds of the oracle was selection bias, which is the number to remember the
next time a per-label table looks like a lever.

### Why per-label surgery cannot close the gap, in one line of arithmetic

The score is the mean of twelve. A label is worth **1/12 = 0.083** of any move made to it. Dragging MCL
from its 0.7897 median to 0.85 — a huge per-label move, bigger than anything this repo has ever done to a
single label — is worth **+0.005** on the board. Closing the 0.008 gap this way needs **+0.096 summed
across the twelve columns**. Per-label reading says WHICH mechanism is missing; it is not itself the
mechanism.

### And the specialist route was already refuted, at maximum tilt

`--focus-label MCL` puts the WHOLE encoder behind one finding, which is the strongest tilt the mechanism
allows. `focus_mcl_s2026` regressed **its own target label by -0.0576 paired**. The arm's own
pre-registration is what makes that readable: if maximum tilt does not recover the gap, no partial
reweighting will. It stays ambiguous between "jointness is free" and "one finding starves an encoder" —
but either way the reweighting family is not worth an arm at 1/12 leverage.

**What this points at instead.** The two weak labels fail for DIFFERENT reasons and only one of them is a
modelling problem. Fracture has **68 positives in 909** — the rarest label by a factor of two, so its
column is largely a sample-size floor and the holdout cannot even resolve a change to it. MCL is
anatomically a CORONAL structure, and the decode is sagittal-dominant; but coronal slots are already in
the six (`COR_FLUID_FS` 93%, `COR_T1` 60%), so the plane is present and the tilt failed. That leaves
input GEOMETRY - a localized crop, where a coronal structure occupies a usefully larger fraction of the
frame - rather than loss weighting, which is the same place Kimi's top-1%-vs-median table points (Q-BP,
two-stage localize-then-classify, 9 of 9 - though confounded, see Q-BQ: all nine shipped spatial
supervision).

## `mrnet_warm_s2026` — killed at epoch 9, and the killer is probably my own test run

The owner's question, asked directly: can a finding be learned from the FOREIGN corpora alone and then
read on ours? `mrnet_warm` is the warm-start half of it — MRNet weights as `--init`, then our canonical
recipe at 224 px, against the `base224` control at **0.8509**.

It never answered. `convergence_check` reads it **TRUNCATED**: best epoch 6, a 10-epoch run, 12 asked.
The trajectory was 0.7666 / 0.7985 / — / 0.8319 / 0.8387 / 0.8478 / **0.8485** / 0.8443 / 0.8455 /
0.8441, at 221 s an epoch. Under `one_cycle` the anneal never ran, so 0.8485 is a **FLOOR**, 0.0024
under the control and inside the 0.0062 holdout noise floor — which is to say the arm was still open
when it died, not losing.

**No checkpoint exists.** The process vanished before writing one, so this produced no member, and
nothing here can be rostered or declined on merit.

Two things it DID establish. The warm start demonstrably fired: epoch 0 read 0.7666 where `base224`
reads 0.8509, which is the signature of foreign weights being loaded rather than a flag that did
nothing. And the recipe runs — 221 s an epoch, 15.57 GB reserved, nine clean epochs.

**WHY IT DIED, and this is the expensive part.** `logs/mrnet_warm.log` ends on a clean epoch line: no
traceback, no OOM, no `ARM DONE`. Two `git push` runs at 23:22Z and 23:27Z each ran the pre-push pytest
(2213 tests, 73 s), and the arm's last metrics write is 23:25Z, between them. Arms run in `.venv-arm`
exactly so that a `uv sync` cannot rewrite the interpreter underneath them, and the standing note
covers `uv sync` — it does NOT cover a plain pytest run, which is what happened here. The mechanism is
NOT established and must not be written down as if it were; `ortho_fresh_lowlr`'s "exit 127" is the
other candidate instance, and it was read as a method failure at the time. Filed P1. Until it is
proven either way, no pre-push pytest runs while an arm holds the card.

Re-run queued behind `ortho_pool_read` on `pid:66204`, because a 44-minute arm that answers a question
the owner asked is the right thing to put in a card gap.

## `ortho_pool_read` — killed at 75% of epoch 0. The arm was mispriced by 9x, and the probe is untested.

The arm's own cost line said **~950 s an epoch, ~3.2 h total**, derived by scaling the 224 px ortho arms'
432 s by the 2.25x pixel ratio. Measured: it reached **step 217 of 291 in 113 minutes** with the card at
100% and `card_check` reporting a single process, so no contention. That is **~151 minutes for epoch 0**
and a **~30 hour** twelve-epoch arm. Killed at 01:23Z on 2026-09-03 under the rule written into the wake
before the number was read (kill above ~2500 s an epoch).

**The pixel ratio was the wrong multiplier.** These flags are not the 224 px arms scaled up: this recipe
reserves **67549 MiB** on a 32607 MiB card, so it runs on `recompute_activations`, which buys the memory
by recomputing the forward pass in the backward. The 224 px ortho arms did not need it. So the step cost
carries a gradient-checkpointing factor that the 2.25x estimate never contained, on top of the pixels.
Anything that flips `recompute_activations` on relative to its anchor must be priced by a throughput
smoke, not by scaling the anchor's epoch time.

**What this does NOT say.** Nothing about the probe. `feature_probe` reads `ortholarge` +0.0203 above
`v3large` at focal-max and +0.0202 at mean_max on the same 909 studies, and that pair is still the only
controlled in-domain-SSL-continuation measurement this project owns. No epoch row was ever written, so
there is no score, no checkpoint, and no entry for the pre-registered branches. The arm is unrun, not
refuted — `knee-6hfi` stays open.

**What the re-arm has to do differently.** Get the epoch cost from a measurement before spending the
card: `arm_check --only <arm> --smoke <throwaway dir> --smoke-studies 60` gives a per-step rate at the
real flags in under a minute. Then buy the cost down on an axis that is not the trunk — fewer slices, or
a shallower `unfreeze_last` — accepting that each such change moves a second variable away from the
`depth_regions_narrow_s2026` = 0.8554 control and has to be declared when the result is read.

### Correction, same hour: the cause is VRAM SPILL, not gradient checkpointing.

The section above blamed `recompute_activations` for the 9.3x. Wrong — that flag is on in the control
too. The controls, read off their own metrics rows:

    depth_regions_narrow_s2026   variant SMALL   336 px  12 sl  regions 4  recompute True   250 s/epoch
    lr4e-5_ws_s2026              variant SMALL   336 px  12 sl  regions -  recompute True   235 s/epoch
    ortho_lpft_s2026             variant ORTHOLARGE  224 px  12 sl  recompute True          432 s/epoch

So the arm's own estimate was sound arithmetic: this trunk at 224 px costs 432 s, and 336 px is 2.25x
the pixels, giving ~970 s. What it missed is that 970 s only holds if the run FITS. The gate line said
the recipe reserves **67549 MiB on a 32607 MiB card**. It did not OOM — on Windows WDDM the allocator
spills to host memory and keeps going, which presents as 100% GPU utilisation at 31735 MiB and about a
tenth of the throughput. A memory fault that reads as a compute cost.

Note also that the control is a **small** trunk. The arm's docstring called itself the control "with
`--variant ortholarge` and nothing else moved", which is true of the RECIPE and false of the COST: it
is a small-to-large swap, and the pixel ratio was only ever the multiplier between this trunk at 224 px
and itself at 336 px.

**The fix is the batch, and it moves no variable.** `--batch 4 --accumulate 3` holds the effective
batch at 12 and cuts the reservation to roughly a third, so the pre-registration against
`depth_regions_narrow_s2026` = 0.8554 stands unchanged. Re-queued behind `mrnet_warm_s2026` with
`after.sh --smoke`, so the smoke measures the real per-step rate on the card before forty minutes go
into it. If the smoke still reads a spilled rate, the next cut is slices, and THAT one is a second
variable and has to be declared.

## `mrnet_warm_s2026` — 0.8487, converged, and the same trajectory twice

The first run of this recipe died at epoch 9 with best 0.8485 and no checkpoint, and the ledger recorded
it as a FLOOR because `convergence_check` reads a truncated `one_cycle` run that way. The re-run
finished all twelve epochs and reproduced it epoch for epoch:

    epoch      6        7        8        9       10       11
    re-run   0.8487   0.8457   0.8464   0.8455   0.8452   0.8446
    killed   0.8485   0.8443   0.8455   0.8441     —        —

So **0.8485 was never a floor** — it was the peak, and the anneal that the truncation argument said we
had not seen turns out to lose 0.004 rather than gain. `convergence_check` does not flag the re-run.
The reading that matters is not the score but the SHAPE: two independent runs of one recipe landing
within 0.0014 of each other at every shared epoch says the peak belongs to the recipe, not to a seed.
This is a replicate rather than a banned seed sweep, because the first run died rather than finished.

**Where it sits.** +0.0028 over the 0.8459 merit bar, which is inside the 0.0062 holdout floor and is
therefore directional; **-0.0034 under the 0.8521 non-DINOv2 seat bar**. On merit alone it would be a
decline. It is rostered anyway, and on one argument only: it is the project's **first external-corpus
member**, a trunk warm-started from MRNet knee MRI, and every other seat in the pool is DINOv2. The
warm start demonstrably fired — epoch 0 opens at 0.759 against `base224`'s 0.8509, which is what a
foreign trunk being dragged onto this corpus looks like.

**That argument is a hypothesis and is not yet tested.** A distinct trunk is a reason to EXPECT
decorrelation, never a measurement of it, and `knee-nj4l` says the champion's monoculture is the
mechanical cause of the plateau — which is exactly the claim this member could confirm or refute.
Filed: `vote_ceiling` over the champion's members plus this one, and the pairwise prediction
correlation against the DINOv2 seats. If it does not decorrelate, the roster line becomes a decline.

## `recal_dense_s2026` — REPLICATES, four days after it ran, on a reading nobody took

The arm finished on 2026-08-30 and its ledger row carried one number: proxy 0.8610 against
`band_dense_hold`'s 0.8573. Its header pre-registers on the GOLD delta and says so in the first line,
*"PRE-REGISTERED, on GOLD first, because the proxy's truth IS the report table and is biased against
label-side movement."* That gold reading was never taken. Taken now, on CPU, off the cached
`--hold-annotations` predictions, no card and no slot:

| | gold-58 | proxy-909 |
|---|---|---|
| `band_dense_hold_s2026` (control) | 0.8956 | 0.8573 |
| `recal_dense_s2026` (arm) | **0.9128** | 0.8610 |
| delta | **+0.0172** | +0.0037 |

**REPLICATES**, verbatim from the header: *"gold above `band_dense_hold`'s by the floor or more, proxy
not down by the floor. The re-map is a property of the TABLE and not of a corner. Price a roster rebuild
on v3 and spend a slot."*

So `report_labels_v3.csv` — the reader's six confidence levels replaced by their measured positive rates
— is gold-positive at **two different corners**: +0.0105 at 224 px / 12 slices (`knee-8wa0`) and +0.0172
here at 336 px / 20 slices, and **free on the proxy both times** (+0.0009 and +0.0037, both inside the
floor). Two corners, same sign, and the proxy is blind to both.

**What replicates is the SIGN, not the size.** n=58 on the gold side, a level and not a selector
(`knee-kddo`); the 58 are 1.47x finding-enriched; and 0.0062 is a REPORT-ruler floor — no gold-ruler
floor has been measured, so "2.8x the floor" is an argument and not a matched multi-seed number. Nothing
here licenses quoting +0.017 as a board delta.

**Why it sat unread, and why that is the finding.** The proxy ruler IS the report table. An arm that
improves the LABEL SIDE moves the thing it is being scored against, so the proxy charges it for the
correction — which is exactly what `2026-09-03_the-report-ruler-over-calls.md` measured from the other
direction. Every arm on the label axis is therefore read on the wrong ruler by default, and this project
has run at least four of them. `knee-v78o1` holds the scope: 24 arms carry `hold_annotations=True`, 8
had a gold reading, 16 did not. This is the first of the sixteen to be collected and it selected a
branch. The rest are computing.

**Second reading from the same run, free.** Against the radiologist, `recal_dense` beats its own training
labels by **-0.0470, CI [-0.0717, -0.0218]**, 11 of 12 findings positive, MCL the lone inversion
(-0.0692). That is the same shape the eight-member pool showed at +0.0516, on a member that is not in
that pool — an independent instance of the reader being the weaker half.

### Amendment to the `recal_dense_s2026` entry above — the gold ruler's own floor, measured after the fact

The entry above compares a GOLD delta of +0.0172 against 0.0062 and calls it "2.8x the floor". **0.0062 is
the REPORT ruler's floor, measured on 909 studies, and applying it to a delta measured on 58 is a category
error** — a tolerance borrowed from a different instrument. The entry flagged that no gold floor had been
measured and then quoted the number anyway. Measured now, with `annotated_readings --against`, which
resamples the 58 studies and reports the paired interval directly:

    against calib_dense_hold_s2026 (gold 0.9117)
      stackfit_s2026            +0.0101  [-0.0044, +0.0252]   spans zero
      labelwise_dense_s2026     +0.0054  [-0.0113, +0.0222]   spans zero
      recal_dense_s2026         +0.0011  [-0.0121, +0.0122]   spans zero
      stack_increments_s2026    +0.0005  [-0.0115, +0.0142]   spans zero

    against band_dense_hold_s2026 (gold 0.8956) — recal_dense's OWN pre-registered control
      recal_dense_s2026         +0.0172  [+0.0004, +0.0343]   clears

**The gold-58 paired half-width is roughly ±0.015**, about 2.4x what the 909-study report holdout gives.

**What survives.** `recal_dense`'s REPLICATES selection stands — read against the control its header
actually names, the interval excludes zero. But it excludes zero by **+0.0004**, so the branch is selected
and the SIZE is not a number to plan on. "v3 replicates off the 224 corner" is the claim; "+0.0172" is not.

**What does not survive, and it was mine.** `stackfit_s2026` reading +0.0101 on gold while flat on the
proxy was written up two wakes ago as a member the proxy undervalues. It is not: the interval spans zero,
its proxy FLAT branch stands unchallenged, and the same goes for `labelwise_dense_s2026` at +0.0054. Both
are withdrawn as pairwise claims.

**The general consequence, and it bounds this whole sweep.** At ±0.015 the gold set cannot separate two
members closer than that, which is most of the member field — and no n we can reach fixes it, since
halving the interval needs about 232 annotated studies against the 58 that exist. `knee-kddo` already said
these 58 are a LEVEL and not a selector; this puts a number on it. The gold ruler resolves level-scale
effects — the pool beating the report table by +0.0516, CI [+0.0296, +0.0729], is 3.4x this half-width and
never depended on member-vs-member resolution — and it resolves nothing member-scale. So the sixteen
missing readings of `knee-v78o1` can confirm or deny LARGE effects and cannot re-rank the roster. That is
still worth having: two of the first seven changed what an arm's branch says. It is not a new selector.

## ortho_pool_read attempt 1 — VOID, and the exit code lied about why

Ran 2026-09-03 02:15Z, died 03:58Z at epoch 6 of 12. Six epochs landed: 0.7537, 0.7885, 0.8078, 0.8282,
0.8331, 0.8408, at ~928 s each and a flat 12.84 GB reserved throughout.

**Do not read 0.8408 against this arm's pre-registered bands.** It is a truncated `one_cycle` score, so it
is a FLOOR and not a score, and the truncation was operator plumbing rather than anything about the trunk.
The arm has been relaunched byte-identically at 04:13Z; its recipe line was re-verified as
`"variant": "ortholarge"` with `"image_size": "336"`, which is the disbelief test its own header demands.

**The cause, and the three readings it took to get there.** The marker said `trainer exit 127`. That code
is what the environment note at the top of `lib.sh` teaches as the signature of a gate rewriting the venv,
so it was first diagnosed as a gates kill. It was then diagnosed as a WDDM host spill, on the arm
docstring's `reserves 67549 MiB on a 32607 MiB card`. Both are wrong. The real line sat 295 lines up the
same log:

```
RuntimeError: CUDA driver error: out of memory
```

and the 67549 figure belongs to the FIRST attempt at `--batch 12`; the configuration that died prints
`gate: this recipe reserves 25737 MiB`, which fits. A driver-level OOM at a flat 12.84 GB on a 32 GB card
is host-side or context-level, not an allocator OOM, and it coincides to the minute with the heaviest
member of a co-running CPU batch starting (`swin_calib_dense_s2026`, 03:58:33). That remains a hypothesis:
free host RAM at the moment of death was never sampled and now cannot be. `knee-4j0lz` carries it, with
the instruction to sample it on the next deliberate co-run rather than reason further from one log.

**Two changes came out of it, and the second is worth more than the arm.**

`lib.sh`'s failure marker now quotes the cause — the last exception line, or the last non-marker line when
there is no exception. The information was always in the log; nothing carried it to the one line an
operator reads, which is why a wrong diagnosis was cheap to make twice in twenty minutes.

That immediately re-opened `ortho_fresh_lowlr`, which had been carried as a possible method failure. Its
log is 55 lines with **no epoch line at all**, ending `waiting for VRAM: 30.3 GB free, this run wants
31.9 — 1530 s of 1800`. It asked for more VRAM than the card has, waited out the full timeout and gave up
having trained nothing. It is evidence about nothing, its pre-registration stands untouched, and its fix
is the one just validated here — hold the effective batch with `--batch 4 --accumulate 3`. `knee-9ac93`.

**And a trap found while confirming it.** Relaunching an arm TRUNCATES the failed run's log: `tee` is
called without `-a`. The evidence for attempt 1 above survives only because it was read before the
relaunch. Read a dead arm's log BEFORE re-arming it.

## The CNN trunk's rate was already measured, four times, and the ladder that would have re-measured it is retired

2026-09-03. Four `cnxbase` runs sit in the models root, all at 336 px, 20 slices, `--variant cnxbase`,
differing in the trunk rate and little else:

| `--backbone-lr` | run | mean AUC | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4e-5 | `cnx_dense_s2026` | **0.7927** | the ViT adapter rate, 12 epochs |
| 1e-4 | `cnx_warm_anneal_s2026` | 0.8105 | peak at epoch 3 of 6, then declining |
| 4e-4 | `cnx_own_recipe_s2026` | **0.8186** | 12 epochs — the fair-budget number |
| 1.2e-3 | `cnx_top_rate_s2026` | 0.7762 | TRUNCATED at epoch 3, still rising — a floor, not a peak |

Moving the trunk rate an order of magnitude is worth **+0.0259**, four times the 0.0062 report-holdout
noise floor and past the 1.5% bar. `cnx_dense`'s 0.7927 is a fact about a ViT adapter rate applied to a
convolutional trunk, not about the trunk — which is what its own 2026-08-24 retitle predicted, in a run
that already existed when the prediction was written.

**`cnx_rate_ladder.sh` is deleted.** It was written this morning to spend ~1.5 h of card on 1.2e-4 and
4e-4, both inside the range above, at three epochs against these twelve. Sixty lines of header argued the
case and cited this ledger twice. It was queued and only failed to run because of an unrelated cache miss.
That is the sprawl tax with a number on it: the scarcest resource, against an answer on disk under four
names nobody had joined. `knee-n18qi`.

**What is still open is unchanged in shape.** 0.8186 is 0.027 below the 0.8459 seat bar, so the trunk does
not enter on quality and never claimed to — the argument was always distance (`cnx_dense` reads
nearest-neighbour 0.7941 against a seated roster flooring at 0.8724, 0.078 further out than any seated
member's nearest neighbour). Whether a member 0.027 short but genuinely off-family earns a seat is an
ENSEMBLE question, it costs no card, and `cnx_own_recipe_s2026`'s holdout vectors are already written.

**The refusal that looked like a contradiction is not one, and the reading matters for what these four
numbers mean.** All four ran at 336 px on `cnxbase`, and on 2026-09-03 `encoder.py:343` refused exactly
that: `cnxbase is patch 32, which cannot tile a 336 px read — use 320 or 352`. The check is CORRECT and
postdates the runs. `cnxbase` is stride 32 over four halving stages, so 336/32 = 10.5 and the grid comes
out truncated — the four runs above read a 10x10 grid, which is a 320 px read wearing a 336 px flag, with
the outer 16 px silently dropped. That does not invalidate them: they are all truncated identically, so
the rate comparison between them is clean, and 0.8186 is a real number for this trunk at an effective 320
px. It does mean a future `cnxbase` arm at the legal 352 is NOT the same read as these, and its delta
against 0.8186 carries a resolution change as well as whatever else it moves.

**And the ensemble question it left open is now answered, off the card, in the negative.** The standing
argument for a convolutional seat was never quality — it was distance: `cnx_dense` reads nearest-neighbour
0.7941 against a seated roster whose own spread floors at 0.8724. `member_curve` over the five best s2026
seats (`stack_increments` 0.8642, `stackfit` 0.8631, `labelwise_dense` 0.8613, `band_span` 0.8565,
`depth_regions_narrow` 0.8554) plus `cnx_own_recipe_s2026` reads **best-5 0.8724 without it and best-6
0.8698 with it forced in**, and it enters no best subset at any size from 2 to 5. The −0.0026 is inside the
0.0062 report floor, so the claim is not that it hurts but that there is **no evidence of the lift the
distance predicted** — the one measurement that could have made a 0.027-short trunk shippable. It stays
declined, and the decline names the re-open: `knee-uk4f` says all four of these runs trained with stage 3
frozen (ConvNeXtV2-base is 3/3/27/3, so `--unfreeze-last 6` opened blocks 21-26 of stage TWO and left the
1024-wide top cold), so the family is re-opened by thawing the top and re-running, never by re-quoting the
distance. The four-row rate table above is unaffected: every run in it is handicapped identically, so the
comparison between them is clean and 0.8186 is this trunk's number at a frozen top.

### `rampsix` ran on 2026-09-02, left no ledger row, and pre-registered two readings it cannot produce — 2026-09-03

The arm is on disk and finished two of five members before dying on the third. Nothing was written here,
so for a day the repo's state was: two checkpoints nobody could account for, and an OPEN P1 bead
(`knee-fxgm`) describing work that had already half-happened.

| member | finished | holdout | note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `final_ws_ramp` | 2026-09-02 20:18, 12 epochs | **none** | `auc: nan` on every row |
| `through_dense_ramp` | 2026-09-02 22:03, 12 epochs | **none** | `auc: nan` on every row |
| `grade_ladder_ramp` | died 23:47, no `.pt` | — | `.metrics.jsonl` holds one `recipe` row and nothing else |

**THE RECIPE FIRED — that is checked, not assumed.** The resumed member's recorded recipe carries
`sample_spread=train_spread_honest12.npz`, `sample_alpha=1.0`, `sample_ramp=6`. The ramp is on. (Note
`certainty_ramp=0` in the same record: this arm ramps through the `sample_*` flags, and the
similarly-named key is a different mechanism.)

**WHY BOTH PRE-REGISTERED READINGS ARE UNREADABLE, WHICH IS THE ENTRY.** The arm sets
`FIT="--fold -1 --ema"`. A dark member holds nothing out, so:

- *Reading 1*, the kill-gate — "the first two members must each clear +0.002 solo over their calibsix
  originals or the remaining three are not run" — has no holdout to be read on. It is not unrun; it is
  **unreadable by construction**, and the arm ran past it because there was nothing to stop at.
- *Reading 2*, the offline ensemble over the champion's six, is null the same way `corpusdose_v1` and
  `corpusfull_v1` are null in `comp/board.jsonl`: the pool contains dark members, so every holdout study
  is in-sample for part of it.

The arm's header states "A board slot is NOT pre-committed here; the offline ensemble read is the gate."
That sentence names as the gate the one number the arm's own `FIT` line makes impossible. Filed P0, and
it is a live instance of `knee-v78o1` (an arm's second pre-registered reading can silently never be
taken).

**WHAT IS NOT DAMAGED BY THIS.** The *dose* was measured elsewhere, on readable members with a matched
control: `certainty_ramp` 0.8584 and `disagreed_ramp` 0.8574 against `disagreed_uniform` 0.8507, both
ramped over 6 of 12 epochs, both clear of the 0.0062 floor; the same signals applied flat cost -0.0036.
So the question `rampsix` asks is not "does the ramp work" — that is answered — but "does a uniform lift
pass through to the ensemble", and `calibsix` is the precedent: +0.0038 pooled solo went to +0.0056 and
+0.0084 ensembled, a pass-through **above one**, because every member moves together and the ambiguity
term is preserved rather than spent.

**THE GENERAL RULE THIS BUYS, WHICH IS BIGGER THAN THIS ARM.** Five of the champion's six seats are dark.
Therefore *no member-side change to the champion is offline-measurable at all* — not this one, not the
next one. An arm that refits dark members must pre-register a **board** reading or declare itself
unmeasurable BEFORE it spends the card, because the alternative is what happened here: 4.2 h of card for
a number that never existed. Q-CN was sent to the researcher asking whether any estimator prices a dark
pool without a slot.

The resumed run continues at member three. Its value is the ensemble question and the board is its only
ruler.

## `ortho_stack` read 0.8417 and the lane it was built to decide is STILL OPEN — 2026-09-04

Thirteen rows against a 12-epoch recipe, peak **e6 0.8417**, last e11 0.8371. Converged, not truncated —
the anneal ran and the arm declined after its peak, which is a fit, not a killed process.

| arm | trunk | recipe | holdout |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `band_dense` | **`dinov2-small`, 22M ViT-S/14** (read from its checkpoint config, not its header) | default batch, rank term ON, no pair memory | **0.8578** |
| `ortho_dense` | ortholarge | 224 px / 12 slices | 0.8452 |
| `ortho_stack` | ortholarge | whole stack, batch 1 / accumulate 12 / pair-memory 66 | **0.8417** |
| `v3large_stack` | v3large (incumbent) | identical to the row above | **0.8277** |

**THIS NUMBER DOES NOT CLOSE THE IN-DOMAIN TRUNK LANE, and reading it as if it did is the exact failure
the arm header pre-registered against.** `band_dense` ran at batch 12 with the ranking term ON; this arm
runs at batch 1 with a 66-step pair memory standing in for the pair mass that batch size used to supply.
So `ortho_stack` − `band_dense` = −0.0161 moves TWO variables — the trunk and how the objective gets its
pairs — and the trunk is the only one the lane is about. `v3large_stack` is the matched control: the same
recipe on the incumbent trunk, running now. Until it lands, the only honest statement is the one against
`ortho_dense`: **−0.0035 at the same trunk**, inside the 0.0062 floor, so moving from a 224 px / 12-slice
read to the whole stack bought the ortho trunk nothing.

**WHAT THE PAIR WILL AND WILL NOT SAY.** If `v3large_stack` lands near `band_dense`, then the pair-memory
substitution is sound and the −0.016 is the trunk: the in-domain trunk lane closes, and `ortho_dense`'s
written decline (−0.0050 at the seat, trunk size and continuation corpus moving together) stands with a
second, geometry-independent point behind it. If `v3large_stack` lands near 0.842 as well, the deficit is
the RECIPE, both ortho rows were measured under a handicap, and the lane is still undecided — the worst
outcome available, and the one this pair exists to make visible rather than to hide.

**THE CONTROL LANDED AT 0.8277, AND IT IS THE TOP BRANCH: `ortho_stack` − `v3large_stack` = +0.0140,
above the 0.0062 floor. The knee continuation carries to the operating point we actually ship.** That
contrast is matched by construction — the two checkpoints' configs differ in `variant` and in nothing
else — and it is the only statement here that does not depend on the paragraph above.

**BUT `band_dense` IS NOT THE TRUNK EITHER ARM'S HEADER SAYS IT IS, so the hedge above was posed against
a control that never existed.** `ortho_stack.sh` names it "identical flags with the incumbent trunk" and
the table's first row called it v3large. Read from the checkpoint rather than the prose,
`band_dense_s2026` carries `variant=small` and `pair_memory=0`: the arm passes no `--variant`,
`options.py:186` defaults it to `SMALL`, and `backbone.py:103` maps that to `facebook/dinov2-small` — a
**22M ViT-S/14, from DINOv2**. So `ortho_stack` − `band_dense` = −0.0161 moves the TRUNK SIZE, the trunk
FAMILY and the pair mechanism at once, and `v3large_stack` − `band_dense` = −0.0301 does the same.
Neither prices the recipe, and the "worst outcome available" the paragraph above described cannot be read
off these rows at all. `v3large_stack.sh:5` had the direction right and the size wrong (it says an 86M
ViT-B); `ortho_stack.sh` had it backwards outright. Both headers and the table are corrected, filed P1 as
knee-4joaj.

**The number that survives all of this is the one nobody was looking at: a 22M DINOv2-small at 336 px /
20 slices reads 0.8578, above every 303M ViT-L row the project owns at that geometry.** Under the
pair-memory recipe the ViT-L loses to a trunk a fourteenth its size. That is either a real statement
about capacity at this data scale or the entire measured cost of the batch-1 substitution, and the two
are not currently separable — which is exactly what `band_pairmem` is queued to fix.

| operating point | ortho | v3large | continuation delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 224 px / 12 slices | `ortho_dense` 0.8452 | `v3large_dense` 0.8258 | **+0.0194** |
| whole stack / 20 slices | `ortho_stack` 0.8417 | `v3large_stack` 0.8277 | **+0.0140** |

**That is the delta-of-deltas Q-CW asked for: −0.0054 as the token budget goes 2352 → 8820.** It is a
third of the floor, so the honest reading is that the continuation gain is FLAT in resolution over this
range, not that it shrinks. Reading (a) — the gain is resolution-bound and the fine-tune recovers it from
data — is refuted at the point we ship. **The in-domain trunk lane is OPEN**, and `ortho_dense`'s written
decline now has an argument standing against it rather than beside it: that decline priced the trunk at
the SEAT (−0.0050) under a recipe we now know handicaps every trunk in it by 0.03.

**WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY.** It does not say ortholarge belongs on the roster. Both ViT-L rows sit well
under the small-trunk `band_dense` = 0.8578 on the fitted ruler, and the project has NO measurement of a
ViT-L at 336 px / 20 slices without the pair-memory substitution — `ortho_stack.sh:38` prices that
configuration at 106144 MiB against a 32 GB card, so the un-handicapped ViT-L row is not merely unrun, it
is unrunnable at this geometry. Every ViT-L number the project owns at the shipped operating point carries
the batch-1 handicap, and its size is unmeasured. That is the gap the family's headers have been reading
past, and it is why the four-row table above supports exactly one comparison.

Priced against the 1.5% bar: the continuation is worth +0.0140-0.0194 solo wherever it has been measured
MATCHED, which does not clear it alone, and no ortho row has yet beaten a small-trunk member that costs a
fraction of the serve. So this lane earns card time behind `radnet_pinned`, not ahead of it. The cheap
instrument that would price the handicap is `band_dense`'s own flag set at `--batch 1 --accumulate 12
--pair-memory 66` on the SMALL trunk — same trunk, same geometry, one variable, and it fits — after which
every ViT-L row above becomes readable rather than suggestive.

**NEITHER ORTHO ROW WAS IN THIS LEDGER BEFORE TODAY.** `ortho_dense`'s reasoning lived in
`comp/members.declines` and its number in `interpretations/`, so a grep of this file for the trunk that has
absorbed the last week of card time returned nothing at all. `ledger_check` did not catch it because the
number IS recorded — elsewhere. A decline is an argument and belongs where declines live; the measurement
belongs here.

## Three runs the ledger never held: the feature-distillation pair and `clip224_tight` — 2026-09-04

`ledger_check` named them; the roster and the declines file already priced them; this file said nothing.
Recording the measurement here, since a decline is an argument and belongs in `comp/members.declines`,
but the number belongs in the ledger.

| run | what it is | holdout | disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `small_feat_pre_s2026` | stage one — a small trunk fitted to the teacher's FEATURES, head only carries the run | 0.7939 | not a member; declined in writing |
| `small_feat_fit_s2026` | stage two — that trunk fine-tuned on the labels | **0.8571** | on the roster |
| `clip224_tight_s2026` | CLIP trunk, tight 224 px crop | 0.8488 | on the roster |

**`small_feat_fit` at 0.8571 is 0.0007 under `band_dense` (0.8578) — the same number, on a SMALL trunk.**
Both were selected on the same 909-study holdout, so the 0.0007 is not a ranking; what it says is that
feature distillation from the strong trunk gives back essentially all of the strong trunk's solo score at
a fraction of the serve cost. Stage one alone reads 0.7939, so the labels do the last 0.063 — the pretrain
is a starting point, not the member.

**WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY.** It is not evidence that distillation adds an ensemble seat. A student fitted
to a teacher's features is, by construction, the LEAST diverse thing that could be added next to that
teacher — the seat has to be measured, not inferred from the solo. That measurement has not been run and
is not queued: the open lever is the trunk lane (`ortho_stack` / `v3large_stack`), and a distilled student
priced against its own teacher is a cheaper-serving question, not a score question. Recorded so the number
stops being invisible, not because it opens anything.

## A frozen trunk can now be priced as a SEAT with no card time — and three of them buy nothing — 2026-09-04

`feature_probe --emit-holdout` claimed in its own help to write a file "seatable beside members" and did
not: three arrays where a member's record carries five, and the binarised label column where a member
carries `Targets.scores`. Both defects only ever surfaced four frames deep inside `seat_value`, the first
as `KeyError: epoch` and the second as a ruler refusal. The second is the one worth remembering: the
graded reader level (0.08 / 0.28 / 0.68 / 0.82 / 0.94) is not the whole difference — `Targets.load` then
overwrites the 58 image-annotated studies with a hard 0/1, which is 13 of the 909 holdout studies and 156
cells. A rounding check would have called those two arrays the same table.

With that fixed, a ridge on cached features is priceable against the champion twelve in seconds:

| probe (fold-0 holdout, own ridge penalty) | solo mean | seat into honest12 | best swap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ortholarge@mean` (dinov3-vitl16, knee-continued) | 0.8170 | +0.0014 [+0.0007, +0.0021] | +0.0019 |
| `v3large@mean` (dinov3-vitl16) | 0.7968 | +0.0008 [+0.0000, +0.0015] | +0.0014 |
| `orthodiff@mean` (diffusion U-Net, 256-d GAP) | 0.7435 | +0.0001 [-0.0007, +0.0010] | +0.0012 |

None clears the +0.0040 under which this ruler has never picked a board tick, so none of the three earns
a fitted arm on its frozen reading alone. OrthoDiffusion is the clearest decline: it is genuinely DISTINCT
(js 0.0418 against the roster's own 0.0150) and still adds nothing, which is the case the diversity
argument keeps predicting should work and which keeps not working — distinctness without accuracy is not

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY. A probe is not a fitted member: `radnet121` probes 0.8197 and the same trunk
FITTED reads 0.6716, so the mapping is not even monotone in general and no probe number licenses a seat.
The narrow claim these three support is the reverse one — a trunk whose FROZEN representation cannot
reach the readable floor has not been shown to be worth a card, and that is now a minutes-long question
instead of a forty-minute one. The one ordering they do reproduce is the continuation term: ortholarge
over v3large, +0.0006 of seat value, the same sign as the +0.0194 the fitted pair reads and the +0.0203
the frozen probe read at each trunk's own penalty. n=2 orderings is an anecdote, not an oracle; it becomes
one if a third trunk with both readings agrees.

## The DATA axis closes before it costs a card week — in-domain knee-MRI pretraining is published as a wash — 2026-09-04

With the patch axis closed on premise, the member axis closed on seven board flats, the convolutional
trunk lane closed on its own gate and the label axis priced at ~zero by Q-EH, the only untouched axis
left was DATA. We hold download credentials for fastMRI knee and SKM-TEA and have never used either.
Every rule here says data outsizes knobs, so this looked like the schedule for the next several days.

**It is not, and the reason is a published table rather than an arm.** Q-EJ found Zhang et al. (MedIA
2024), which is almost exactly the experiment: pretrain on ~10,000 fastMRI knee exams, evaluate
downstream on Stanford knee MRI / MRNet for abnormality, ACL and meniscus. Mean AUC against a labelled
budget:

| pretrain | 80 subj | 200 | 400 | 800 |
|----------|---------|-----|-----|-----|
| none | 0.433 | 0.429 | 0.474 | 0.562 |
| ImageNet | 0.682 | 0.737 | 0.799 | **0.824** |
| best in-domain (anatomy-aware MTL) | **0.755** | **0.783** | **0.801** | 0.819 |

The in-domain gain over ImageNet is +0.073, +0.046, +0.002, **−0.005**. It is enormous against scratch
(+0.257) and gone by 800 labelled subjects. **Scratch is not our baseline.** Our labelled corpus is
~4,400 studies — more than five times the point where the advantage has already crossed zero, against a
pretraining pool (~10,000 exams) larger than the ~1,500 volumes our fastMRI credentials cover. The
survey position agrees (VanBerlo et al. 2024): in-domain SSL gains are "most prominent when unlabelled
examples greatly outnumber labelled examples," and ours would not outnumber them at all.

**The objective is not a rescue.** The only in-domain variant that beat ImageNet at any budget is an
anatomy-aware multi-task pretext (relative slice orientation and location). Generic SSL on the same data
scores far worse on the same downstream task: MAE 0.624, BYOL 0.753, SimCLR 0.800. So the arm that is
cheap to build — MAE or SimMIM on reconstructed fastMRI slices — is the one the table says loses to the
initialisation we already use. The arm that won is a hand-built anatomical pretext, which is a
multi-week build for a gain the same table shows expiring below our labelled scale.

**The sequence mismatch subtracts again.** Zhang et al. deliberately matched sagittal T2W fat-suppressed
on both ends. fastMRI knee is mostly PD/T2; PRISM (2025) exists because multi-sequence heterogeneity
breaks naive pretraining, and it needed 336k volumes to handle it. Any RSNA protocol spread makes the
effective in-domain corpus smaller than the raw volume count, never larger.

**What this costs and what it buys.** The arm would have been the single largest card commitment the
project has made — a pretraining run plus a full roster retrain, multiple days — priced against a
mechanism whose own published curve predicts zero at our labelled scale. It was retired for the price of
one letter. This is the second axis in one day closed on PREMISE rather than on a number (the first was
patch size, Q-EI), and both were closed before the card was spent rather than after.

**What it does NOT say.** It is not evidence that our corpus is at the labelled-data ceiling — Zhang's
curve is about where in-domain pretraining stops beating ImageNet, not about where supervised accuracy
saturates. It is also not a verdict on external data as LABELLED augmentation, which is a different
mechanism and untested here.

**Where this leaves the schedule.** Every axis that could be opened by starting an arm is now closed, so
the honest move is the one Q-EJ named independently: stop opening arms and price the pool. There are 103
packaged members and 186 scoreable checkpoints, and the seat curves this project has shipped against were
all built on roughly 22 same-split members. A whole-pool seat sweep costs no card and no slot.

## The pool priced card-free: the offline ruler cannot see our top band at all — 2026-09-04

Q-EK asked how a full-fit member's seat is priced and the answer is that it is not. Kimi found no paper
measuring whether the CV-sibling ordering survives a full-data refit, no published curve for the refit
gain against fold fraction, and no cheap unbiased scheme — influence functions price training samples not
members, bagged surrogates measure diversity not seat value, nested CV costs a full retrain. **Champion
seats are priced by convention, not by measurement.**

**But the same answer kills the explanation I was about to reach for.** In k-fold the refit sees
`k/(k-1)` times the data; under an `N^{-β}` error scaling that is worth a low single-digit thousandth at
our corpus size. So the +0.007 between `honest12` (0.937, twelve scoreable members) and
`raptorweight_v1` (0.944, six) is **not the refit**. It is seating, diversity, or the seventh seat — the
champion carries a foreign `raptor_v4_swa` rank-voted at 1/3 that `champion.json` deliberately keeps out
of `members`, and `honest12` is ours-only.

**And `entry_offline` states the structural fact plainly: every board entry at 0.936 and above is
IN-SAMPLE.** The offline ruler tops out below our own top band. That is the real reason the member axis
reads closed — not that seating stopped mattering, but that above 0.936 nothing we ship can be measured
before it is shipped. Every closure was measured where the ruler still works.

**The board agrees, from the other side.** Nine entries now sit at 0.943-0.944 across six, seven and
eight seats: `raptorweight`, `holdswap`, `spanseat`, `stackseat`, `halfcham`, `lensseat`, `monotone`,
`raptorseat`, `vjepaseat`. Each is the champion serving with one thing changed — a weight, one seat, the
vote, the lens, the calibration. **Every single-seat change lands on the same number.** That is not a
saturation argument built from one curve; it is nine board reads of the same plateau, and it says a seat
swap cannot deliver the +0.009 to the leader.

**What the sweep found.** `seat_value --against honest12` over the packaged pool classifies each
candidate TWIN / SCALED / NOISY / DISTINCT, and only DISTINCT is a seat. Roughly half the pool reads
DISTINCT, which is more real diversity than the ~22 same-split members every shipped seat curve was built
on. The sweep is card-free and takes seconds a batch; it timed out only because a 120-candidate mix is
built in one piece, so it is run in batches of ten.

**One anomaly, and it was mine — CORRECTED the same hour it was written.** The paragraph here first
said `focus_mcl_s2026` reads rank **0.0445** against a roster boundary of 0.8956, that far below chance
is what an inverted prediction array looks like, and that a shippable roster member might be inverted. It
is not. `seat_value` prints `focus_mcl_s2026.pt: nearest 0.0445  mean 0.0319  solo 0.5332` — `nearest`
and `mean` are rank DISTANCES, small meaning most distinct, and the member's solo AUC is printed on the
same line. Recomputed independently off the holdout array: per-label AUC 0.671 / 0.735 / 0.674 / 0.355 /
0.674 / 0.424 / 0.400 / 0.313 / 0.434 / 0.626 / 0.642 / 0.450, mean **0.5332**, matching the roster line
exactly. Its seat value against `honest12` is **−0.0002 [−0.0011, +0.0008]**, a straddle of zero.

**The reading defect is the finding.** One `seat_value` report uses the word `rank` for a SCORE in its
member-axes block and for a DISTANCE in its candidates block, and the batched sweep interleaves the two.
That is what turned a printed 0.5332 into a P1 about an inverted member (knee-hmxko, closed; the naming
is knee-hmxko's follow-on). It is the same class as the denominator errors this project keeps paying
for: the number was right, on the same line, under a word that means two things. What IS true about the
member is smaller and was never the claim — its checkpoint is from epoch 2 and five of twelve labels sit
below 0.5, so it is a coin-flip member seated for distance.

**What this does NOT say.** It is not a measurement of any champion seat — that is exactly what Q-EK
established cannot be done cheaply. It prices candidates against the best entry the ruler can still see,
and the ordering is what transfers, never the value.

## The learned combiner closes on measurement, not on argument — a level-2 fit LOSES to the flat vote — 2026-09-04

After seat count, seating, weighting, re-lensing and calibration each closed, one combiner question was
still genuinely untried: every entry this project has shipped reduces the pool with a fixed rule whose
only freedom is one scalar per member, shared across all twelve findings. `votefit` fitted that vector
and `stackseat` swapped a member; neither is a level-2 model. `kneemri.evaluation.stack_combiner` fits a
ridge per FINDING over the members' ranks, and optionally lets a finding read what the members said about
the other eleven — a thing no vote can express at all, since a vote sees one column at a time.

Priced on `honest12`'s twelve scoreable members over the 909 holdout studies. Contiguous blocks, each
scored by a fit that never saw it; the ridge penalty picked on a split of the KEPT rows only; the flat
vote scored on the same rows.

**THE FIRST READING WAS MY BUG AND IS CORRECTED BELOW (2026-09-04).** It is left visible because the
wrong numbers had already been written up here as a mechanism, and the mechanism was the part that was
wrong. First reading: own-finding 5 blocks 0.8571 (−0.0179), own-finding 10 blocks 0.8640 (−0.0110),
crossed 5 blocks 0.8674 (−0.0076). The write-up read those as fit variance and concluded "at this pool
size the variance a fitted weight adds costs more than the structure it buys." That conclusion did not
survive the fix.

A textbook ridge shrinks the weight vector toward the ORIGIN. The module's own docstring claimed the
large-penalty end of the grid was the flat vote, and it is not: scaling a weight vector down does not
turn it into the all-equal vector, and an AUC reads only the ordering, so the largest penalty produced a
rescaled version of whatever direction least squares left rather than the control. **The grid did not
contain its own baseline**, so the combiner could lose to the thing it was being compared against by an
arbitrary amount, and every number above is a statement about that defect. The fix is one term:
penalise `w − prior` with `prior` set to the vote's own weights (`1/m` on the target finding's member
columns, zero elsewhere), so the largest penalty reproduces the flat vote exactly.

| combiner | mean AUC | vs flat vote |
|---|---|---|
| flat vote (`RankAverage`) | **0.8750** | — |
| ridge, own finding, 3 blocks | 0.8734 | −0.0016 |
| ridge, own finding, 5 blocks | 0.8745 | −0.0005 |
| ridge, own finding, 10 blocks | **0.8763** | **+0.0013** |
| ridge, own finding, 20 blocks | 0.8758 | +0.0008 |
| ridge, own finding, 30 blocks | 0.8758 | +0.0008 |
| ridge, every finding (cross), 5 blocks | 0.8669 | −0.0081 |
| ridge, every finding (cross), 10 blocks | 0.8697 | −0.0053 |

**The harness is validated by its own baseline.** The flat vote reads 0.8750 here against the 0.8751
`comp/board.jsonl` recorded for `honest12` — so the two sides are being scored under the rule the ledger's
numbers were taken under, and the comparison is not mislabelled.

**The block trend is monotone, which is what says the remaining movement is fit variance and not noise.**
−0.0016 → −0.0005 → +0.0013 → +0.0008 → +0.0008 as the fit's training rows go 606 → 727 → 818 → 863 → 879.
It rises with rows and then plateaus at about +0.001. The block count was NOT chosen after the fact: the
plateau is the reading, and +0.0013 at ten blocks is one point on it rather than a result.

**So the axis is closed, but not for the reason first written here.** A learned per-finding combiner is a
TIE with the flat vote, not a loss — about +0.001 at the asymptote, against a 0.0062 report floor and a
0.0015 board resolution. There is roughly one thousandth of learnable structure in how twelve members
should be weighted per finding, and no slot may be spent on it. Crossing findings still loses (−0.0053 at
ten blocks), which is the honest version of the earlier claim: reading the other eleven findings costs
144 features of variance and buys back less.

**It was pre-registered as a null and it is one.** Kimi's Q-EL answer arrived the same hour: Müller et al.
2022 found simple mean / soft majority vote EQUAL OR BETTER than SVM and logistic-regression stacking
across medical-image ensembles, and the only case where an input-conditioned combiner clearly won was
Hussain et al.'s per-body-part model, where the base models had genuine regional specialization. A panel
of similar DINOv2/DINOv3 recipes has none. The recommended bar in that same letter was "if it does not
beat mean by >0.001, no combiner is worth a card." It sits ON that bar and never above it.

**What this closes and what it does NOT.** The COMBINER axis is closed at a TIE: nothing that reduces our
existing pool differently is worth a card or a slot. It does not say the ensemble is at its ceiling — Q-EL also
answered the size question, and +0.016 over best single is NORMAL for medical imaging with strong singles
(MURA: +0.01–0.02; Shen et al. mammography: +0.03; a public three-family blend on THIS competition:
~+0.001). Our mix is not under-combining. The remaining distance lives in the MEMBERS, which is where the
next arm goes.

**The one heterogeneity finding worth carrying forward.** The pool is near-homogeneous — DINOv2/DINOv3
recipes plus one foreign CoAtNet seat that is in-sample and therefore unscoreable. Kimi's transfer of the
public frontier: "if you add heterogeneity, add exactly one non-DINO member; anything more is seating
theatre." A conv member trained on OUR corpus would be the first non-DINO seat this project can actually
PRICE, which is a different object from the foreign one the champion already carries.

**The non-DINO seat, priced and refused (2026-09-05).** The paragraph above named the arm this project
had never run: a conv member trained on OUR corpus, the first non-DINO seat that could actually be
PRICED rather than assumed. `coatnet_hybrid_s2026` is it — CoAtNet-2, twelve epochs, whole-stack, our
objective. It read **0.8259** solo against a 0.8460 pre-registration, and more decisively it seats at
**-0.0006** against honest12 with band [-0.0012, -0.0000]; its best available seat, replacing
`mae_matched_s2026`, is also negative. A candidate whose best case is negative has no seat to find.

Kimi's transferred rule — "add exactly one non-DINO member; anything more is seating theatre" — is
therefore refused on the one instance this project could measure. Not refuted in general: one
architecture at one size is one point. But the specific hope that heterogeneity per se buys a seat is
now a measurement rather than a plan, and the seat-value band is tight enough that a bigger version of
the same idea is not licensed by it.

The informative part is the per-column shape. coatnet_hybrid's three weakest columns are MCL 0.715,
Fracture 0.743 and Lateral OA 0.782 — the pool's own weak three, in the pool's own order. A trunk that
genuinely saw different structure should have failed somewhere ELSE. It failed in exactly the same
places, which says the weakness is in the SUPERVISION or the DATA and not in the trunk family. That is
the same conclusion `colmcl` reached from the board side, arrived at from the architecture side, and it
is why the next slots go to locating the board's headroom rather than to another trunk.

Control `band_dense_s2026` 0.8578 (peak e8). Twelve epochs run, peak e6 **0.8462**, plateau e7-e11
(0.8424 / 0.8448 / 0.8427 / 0.8415 / 0.8415) — `convergence_check` silent, so this is a converged
number and not a killed process. **Delta -0.0116**, which lands under 0.8516: the arm's OWN lowest
pre-registered branch, "IT COSTS AGAIN".

Eleven of twelve columns fall and one rises:

| column | control | errors_rank | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| ACL | 0.8740 | 0.8842 | +0.0102 |
| MCL | 0.7931 | 0.7616 | **-0.0314** |
| Lateral Meniscus | 0.8464 | 0.8177 | -0.0287 |
| PF OA | 0.8583 | 0.8386 | -0.0197 |
| Fracture | 0.8088 | 0.7911 | -0.0177 |
| Medial Meniscus | 0.9047 | 0.8906 | -0.0141 |
| Medial OA | 0.8797 | 0.8701 | -0.0097 |
| Lateral OA | 0.8156 | 0.8060 | -0.0096 |
| Synovitis | 0.8764 | 0.8672 | -0.0092 |
| Contusion | 0.8705 | 0.8670 | -0.0036 |
| Effusion | 0.8595 | 0.8560 | -0.0035 |
| Baker's | 0.9065 | 0.9045 | -0.0020 |

THE MECHANISM IS IN THE ORDERING, not the mean. MCL is the largest loss, and MCL is the column the
overcall detector fires on hardest — `report_labels_v2` is the worst of the four reader tables on the
58-study panel, and the audit counts 108 false positives against 32 misses. So the cells the detector
calls wrong are the cells that carry MCL's supervision, and dropping them drops the column. This is a
broad effect rather than one column's artifact: the loss is monotone across the table with a single
exception, which is what a supervision cut looks like and not what noise looks like.

That is `errors_dense`'s reading confirmed a second time from the opposite direction. Per its own
pre-registration the axis now lives or dies on `errors_relabel` (knee-f8hv5) — RELABEL rather than
PRUNE, on the card since 02:05Z, ETA ~04:00Z.

Per Q-RULER4 and Q-RULER6 (Kimi, 2026-09-05) this delta has NO offline protection against board
reversal: control and arm differ in SUPERVISION, which is exactly the case where the shared-label-noise
assumption behind a paired comparison fails, and the model-free discordant-pair bound over the 58-study
panel is vacuous (smallest 0.31 against deltas of ~0.01). The sign is trusted here because it is large
and monotone, not because the panel protects it.

### `errors_relabel` — relabelling is FLAT, and the flat prices the whole lane against the detector's recall — 2026-09-05

Arm `experiments/arms/errors_relabel.sh`, bead knee-f8hv5, reading `logs/errors_relabel_ledger.log`.

**0.8522 @ e6 against `band_dense` 0.8578 — MEAN −0.0056.** The arm's own pre-registered FLAT band was
`0.8578 > s >= 0.8516`, so it lands inside it by 0.0006, at the bottom edge. Twelve of twelve epochs ran,
peak at e6 with e11 at 0.8482, so `convergence_check` reports it neither truncated nor undertrained and
the number is quotable. Per-label the whole table is inside its own error bar: half-widths up to ±0.0310
against a spread of −0.0250 (PF OA) to +0.0093 (ACL).

**The plumbing landed and was verified before the score was read.** The recipe line carries
`unread_targets = relabel_rank1932_a06.csv`, `labels` stays `report_labels_v2.csv` — which is correct,
the correction is supplied through `--unread-targets` and not by swapping the table — and the corrected
table holds exactly 1,932 rows as the header demanded. So this is a fact about relabelling, not about a
flag that never fired.

**What the treatment actually changed, with its denominators.** 1,932 corrected cells of 52,872 read
cells is **3.65% of the corpus**. On the gold panel the detector's precision at the matched budget is
0.720, so of those 1,932 about **1,391 were genuine errors corrected and about 541 were correct cells
corrupted** — a net of about **+850 cells made right, 1.6% of the corpus**. (That precision is measured
at gold budget 25 over 684 scoreable cells and EXTRAPOLATED to the 1,932-cell corpus cut; it is not
measured there, and the corpus cut is the gold budget scaled by the same 1.294% gold-to-corpus ratio
that makes 1,932 × 0.01294 = 25 exactly.)

**Why that is a null and not a refutation of relabelling.** The gold panel carries 140 disagreements over
684 scoreable cells — a **20.5% cell error rate**. If that rate holds corpus-wide the corpus contains
about **10,840 wrong cells**, and this arm fixed about 850 of them: **7.8% of the defect**. A treatment
reaching under a tenth of the corpus's label noise producing a delta inside the noise floor is exactly
what the model predicts, not evidence against the mechanism. The binding constraint is the detector's
**recall of 0.129**, not the corrector: at separation AUC 0.7628 the ranking cannot be extended to a
larger budget without precision falling through the break-even `p = 0.5` that `B(2p−1)` requires.

**So the LABEL AXIS closes at THIS DETECTOR, in all three treatments and both directions.** Prune at full
budget costs −0.0158 (`errors_dense`); prune by ranking costs, and costs most where the detector fires
most (`errors_rank`); relabel at the net-benefit-optimal budget is flat (here). The budget knob is priced
out by arithmetic — 1× is the peak of `B(2p−1)` and 1× is what ran — and the asymmetric-cost knob `k` is
unmeasurable, assumed in every published family and measured in none (Q-K, Kimi 2026-09-05). There is no
remaining knob on confident learning worth a card.

**What reopens it is a detector, and only a detector.** The requirement is now numeric rather than
directional: to touch a materially larger share of 10,840 wrong cells at precision above 0.5, a
replacement needs separation AUC materially above **0.7628** on all disagreements and, more sharply,
above **0.6903** on the misses, where ours is close to blind (precision under 0.11 at every budget) and
where a report-mined table should be worst by construction. That is the ceiling the detector-ceiling bead
argues, and it is why the next build on this axis is a SimiFeat-style kNN detector over the cached 336 px
features rather than another arm.

Same Q-RULER4/Q-RULER6 caveat as `errors_rank`: control and arm differ in SUPERVISION, so the paired
holdout comparison has no offline protection against board reversal. Here it matters less — a flat has
nothing to reverse.

### neighbour_errors — the SimiFeat replacement is BUILT and MEASURED, and it does not reopen the lane — 2026-09-05

No card, no slot. `python -m kneemri.evaluation.neighbour_errors --against-confident`, full output in
`logs/neighbour_errors_combined.log`. A similarity-weighted 10-neighbour vote over six frozen 336 px trunks
(ortholarge, v3large, large, small, radnet121, vjepa2l), read on the SAME gate, the SAME 58-study census and
the SAME budgets confident learning is read at, so the three rankings below are directly comparable.

| ranking | all disagreements (n=140) | confident false positives (n=108) | misses (n=32) | precision @budget 25 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| confident learning (the floor) | 0.7628 | 0.7580 | 0.6903 | 0.720 |
| neighbour vote | 0.6830 | 0.7714 | 0.3588 | 0.200 |
| rank-average of the two | 0.7511 | 0.8020 | 0.5161 | 0.480 |

THE COMBINATION IS THE BEST FALSE-POSITIVE RANKING THIS PROJECT HAS, BY 0.0440, AND IT STILL DOES NOT PAY.
False positives are 77% of the census and the defect a relabel actually corrects, so 0.8020 against 0.7580
is a real gain on the stratum that matters. The reopen condition was not an AUC on that stratum, though — it
was the NET BENEFIT, and net benefit is `B(2p - 1)` in the precision at the budget, not in the area under the
whole curve. Confident learning reaches precision 0.720 at budget 25; the rank-average reaches 0.480 and the
vote alone 0.200. Both are BELOW the 0.5 break-even at every budget read, so the peak does not move to a
larger budget — it moves off the table. A ranking can be better over its whole length and worse where it is
spent, and this is that case.

WHY THE VOTE LOSES OVERALL, AND IT IS THE PREDICTED REASON. The multi-label compromise stated in the module
docstring is that a study carries ONE embedding and twelve labels, so the twelve findings share one
neighbourhood. The vote's own majority mask flags 11,824 cells — 22.363% of read, against cleanlab's 6.523%
— which is what a globally atypical study looks like when it is flagged on several findings at once. That is
a property of the design, measured, not of the corpus.

THE MISSES ARE THE OTHER HALF AND THE VOTE READS THEM BELOW CHANCE (0.3588). A miss is a finding the reader's
table calls absent that the radiologist called present; a neighbour vote asks whether the label agrees with
its neighbours, and a false NEGATIVE agrees with the many negatives around it by construction. This is not a
tuning failure and no k fixes it — the detector is structurally blind to the direction, which is why the
rank-average drags cleanlab's 0.6903 down to 0.5161 on that stratum instead of lifting it.

THE LABEL AXIS STAYS CLOSED, NOW AT TWO DETECTORS RATHER THAN ONE. What was a single method's recall limit is
now a measured statement about the family: training-free neighbour voting over frozen embeddings — AQuA's
best-performing family — is worse than confident learning here at the operating point that pays. Reopening
still needs precision above 0.5 at a budget large enough to reach a material share of the corpus's wrong
cells, and neither detector nor their average is within reach of it. Do NOT spend a card arm on a relabel
built from this ranking: `errors_relabel` was flat on a ranking with precision 0.720 at its budget, and this
one is worse there.

## `ortho_slow_trunk` reads 0.8265 — and it peaked on its LAST epoch, which is the finding — 2026-09-05

The arm asked one thing: is the ortho trunk's shortfall a RATE problem. It ran the full twelve epochs
(`convergence_check`: `1 runs: 1 converged`) and reads **0.8265**, best epoch **11 of 12** — the last one.

Against the pre-registered branches (`>= 0.8554` recovers the probe's lead, `>= 0.8526` recovers most,
`>= 0.8402` closes the ortho trunk, `< 0.8402` is a null on the rate hypothesis only) this lands in the
bottom cell at **0.8265**, 0.0137 below the closing branch. So by its own registration the ORTHO TRUNK
DOES NOT CLOSE here; what is null is the rate hypothesis, and only that.

**But the branch table cannot be read straight, because the curve never turned over.** The epoch series
is monotone to the end — 0.7390, 0.7746, 0.7892, 0.8034, 0.8088, 0.8159, 0.8195, 0.8226, 0.8258, 0.8249,
0.8265 (e10), 0.8265 (e11) — and the peak IS the last recorded epoch. That is the UNDERTRAINED shape:
the budget bound the run, not the recipe. A lower rate needs more steps to reach the same place by
construction, so a twelve-epoch budget inherited from a 4e-5 recipe is the harness suspect the branch
table did not name, and it is a faulty-TRAINING reading, not a fact about the trunk. The honest statement
is: **at twelve epochs the slow rate does not catch up.** Whether it catches up at twenty is unmeasured,
and is NOT queued — `trajectory_check`'s corpus puts the median epoch-3-to-peak gain at +0.0210 and the
p90 at +0.0380 over n=96, and this arm is 0.0289 short of `ortho_dense`-class numbers with its own curve
already flattening (+0.0007 over the last three epochs). Eight more epochs at 924 s is 2.1 h of card for
a gain the curve's own slope prices near zero.

The ortho trunk stays open as a QUESTION and closed as a QUEUE ITEM: nothing about it is worth card
while the position axis (`band_surgical`) and the initialisation axis (`band_lpft`) are unmeasured on a
trunk that already reads 0.8578.

**STALE AS OF 2026-09-05 14:11Z — both of those are now measured, and neither left a queue item.**
