### `band_lpft` — LP-FT's ID gain is a convergence-speed effect, and a long fine-tune erases it — 2026-09-05

Arm `experiments/arms/band_lpft.sh`, bead knee-6hfi, reading `logs/band_lpft_ledger.log`.

**0.8513 @ e6 against `band_dense` 0.8578 — MEAN −0.0065.** The arm pre-registered four bands; this
lands 0.0003 below the FLAT floor of `0.8640 > s >= 0.8516`, i.e. in the fourth band, *worse than the
control by more than the 0.0062 holdout floor* — by 1.05× of it. Twelve of twelve epochs ran and
`convergence_check` lists the run in neither the truncated nor the undertrained set, so the number is
quotable and is not a fact about a killed process.

**The warm start landed, which is what the fourth band told us to check first.** That band reads
"SUSPECT THE WARM START BEFORE THE MECHANISM", and the suspicion is retired rather than assumed: the
recipe line carries `init = band_lpft_head.pt`, `init_scope = all`, against a control whose config
predates the flag entirely. Stage 1 froze the trunk, so the trunk weights the stage-2 run loads are the
same pretrained weights the control starts from and the only difference between the two runs is a head
that has already seen the data. The arm's one variable moved, and it moved alone.

**The mechanism fires, and it is spent by epoch 2.** Epoch-matched against the control, the head warm
start is worth **+0.0233 at e0** — a real effect, in the direction Kumar et al. predict, and the largest
single-epoch gap the pair ever shows. Curve: 0.7662 / 0.7813 / 0.8180 / 0.8246 / 0.8407 / 0.8417 /
**0.8513** / 0.8431 / 0.8481 / 0.8474 / 0.8464 / 0.8458. The control plateaus 0.855–0.858 from e5; from
e2 onward `band_lpft` tracks it from *below* and never crosses back. So the published +1% ID is not
refuted so much as *relocated*: on this trunk at this budget it is a head start that twelve epochs of
fine-tuning fully repay, and the only regime where it could show up as a score is one too short to
converge — which is not the regime any member here ships in.

**Per label the loss is not diffuse.** Four deltas clear their own paired 95% interval and all four are
negative — MCL −0.0387\*, PF OA −0.0203\*, Medial Meniscus −0.0154\*, Medial OA −0.0149\* — against
zero marked positives (largest unmarked gain ACL +0.0166, half-widths to ±0.0364). By structure scale,
focal −0.0106 against regional −0.0006: the cost concentrates on exactly the findings whose ranking
depends on fine within-slice contrast, which is what a head fitted on frozen features and then chased
by a trunk should cost.

**What this closes and what it does not.** LP-FT **closes as a recipe change** for DINOv2 whole-stack
at 12 epochs: it costs a floor-width, it costs it on the model-bottlenecked labels, and there is no
schedule cell left where the head start survives to the peak. It does **not** close Kumar's actual
headline, which is OOD (+10% OOD, ID only +1%) — a flat-to-negative ID reading is *consistent* with
that paper rather than contrary to it. But our only OOD ruler is the Kaggle board at one slot a read,
the member axis is closed on seven board flats, and a member 0.0065 behind the incumbent is not a seat
that a slot can be spent to price. So the OOD half stays **unmeasured and unqueued** — an open question
with no affordable instrument, not a branch anyone should re-derive from the ID number.

## The public top of this leaderboard is running mechanisms we have already priced — 2026-09-05

Board read 21:07Z (rank line refreshed against the 2026-09-07T00:10Z read): **rank 45 of 3239 at 0.944; leader 0.954; gap 0.010.** Our slope is
+0.00037/day against the frontier's +0.00024/day, so the gap closes in 62 days. Grinding does not get
there and only a step change does, which makes "what is the top doing" a measurement worth taking
before another arm is queued. It costs no slot: `kaggle kernels list --competition ... --sort-by
scoreDescending` and a `kernels pull` are free.

**The highest-scoring public kernel is 0.937** (`renta0426/rsna-knee-0-937-weak-label-dinov2-meniscus-resid`,
37 votes, pulled to the data root — a foreign kernel is third-party code and is not vendored here). Its
own front page names the whole signal path: DINOv2 + DINOv3 over six protocol-aware slots, RadImageNet
for medical-domain error diversity, and a Raptor CoAtNet 2.5D leg, **blended by TARGET in rank space**
with the meniscus and fracture weights carried over from its scored parent. Underneath it is a
`SlotHead` over `cls_mean`-pooled ViT features with window pooling — structurally what we run.

**Every named mechanism in it is already priced here, and the headline one is closed.** Target-wise
fusion is a per-finding learned combiner, which `stack_combiner` measured on `honest12`'s twelve members
over the 909 holdout studies: ridge per finding **+0.0013** at its best block count, cross-finding
**−0.0053 to −0.0081**, against a flat vote that reproduces the ledger's own 0.8751. The Raptor
checkpoint is already mounted by our entries. RadImageNet-for-diversity is the convolutional trunk lane,
closed on its own gate.

**So the public frontier is 0.007 BELOW us and is not carrying an axis we have not read.** That is a
real negative: the 0.010 to the leader is in something not public, and it is not recoverable by reading
public kernels harder. The remaining lever is a better MEMBER, not a better combiner — every combiner
question this project has asked (seat count, seating, weighting, re-lensing, calibration, level-2 fit)
is now closed by measurement.

**What this does NOT say.** It is not a claim about the leader, who has published nothing; it is a claim
about what is publicly visible. And it does not re-open the public-notebook floor as a target — that
floor was already left.

### Resolution 336 to 392 does NOT lift the meniscus columns — card-free, 2026-09-05

`supervision_gap` puts Lateral Meniscus at **−0.1925**, the largest model-bound gap this project has
measured: our report label predicts the radiologist at 0.8422 while a published member fitted on those
labels reaches 0.6497. The signal is in the supervision and the model does not pull it out of the pixels.
The obvious mechanism is SIZE — a meniscal tear is a millimetre-scale signal at the horns, and 336 px
over a 130 mm field is about 0.39 mm a pixel. So: does more resolution recover it?

The pair already exists on disk and costs nothing to read. `res392_ws_s2026` against `lr4e-5_ws_s2026`,
one variable (392 px against 336 px), same whole-stack recipe, same 4e-5 backbone rate, both scored on
the same 909 studies by `column_headroom`:

| column | 336 px | 392 px | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ACL | 0.8706 | 0.8815 | **+0.0109** |
| Fracture | 0.8066 | 0.8170 | **+0.0104** |
| Contusion | 0.8685 | 0.8777 | +0.0092 |
| Baker's | 0.9076 | 0.9120 | +0.0044 |
| Effusion | 0.8542 | 0.8563 | +0.0021 |
| PF OA | 0.8392 | 0.8397 | +0.0005 |
| **Lateral Meniscus** | 0.8460 | 0.8459 | **−0.0001** |
| **Medial Meniscus** | 0.8983 | 0.8963 | **−0.0020** |
| Medial OA | 0.8763 | 0.8705 | −0.0058 |
| MCL | 0.7908 | 0.7821 | −0.0087 |
| Synovitis | 0.8546 | 0.8446 | −0.0100 |
| Lateral OA | 0.8178 | 0.8044 | −0.0134 |
| **mean** | **0.8525** | **0.8523** | **−0.0002** |

**The two meniscus columns are the two flattest columns in the table.** Lateral Meniscus moves by one
ten-thousandth and Medial Meniscus moves backwards. Whatever the model is missing about the meniscus, a
17% linear resolution increase does not supply it — so the size hypothesis is refuted at this step size,
and a 448 px or 420 px arm aimed at meniscus has no reading behind it. That is a card hour not spent.

**What it does NOT say.** It does not close resolution as an axis: 336→392 is a small step, and a
mechanism that needs 2x might still exist. It does not price the columns that DID move — ACL +0.0109 and
Fracture +0.0104 up against Lateral OA −0.0134 and Synovitis −0.0100 down is a rotation of about the size
this project keeps seeing when the mean does not move, and single-seed per-column deltas at n=909 with
68 to 558 positives are not results. The one thing the table settles is the column it was built to ask
about, and it settles it negative.

Beads: knee-zsyp4. Reading: `interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-05_the-offline-column-map-ranks-our-labels-not-our-model.md`.

**The mechanism is the dilution argument this ledger already made** (line 5095: max pooling "divides its
evidence by the slice count. Adding slices makes the dilution WORSE"). A lateral meniscal tear is focal —
it is carried by two or three slices of a stack — so under a max over 36 slices the chance that a
non-carrying slice wins the argmax rises with the count. The findings that move UP under 36 slices are
the diffuse ones (Contusion +0.0205, Medial OA, Lateral OA, MCL), which is the same argument with the
sign flipped: a finding spread across the stack gains from seeing more of it.

**The pooling operator is the lever, and it is measured here at fixed slice count.** `stack224` and
`cover_labelwise` differ in ONE flag — max versus labelwise slice pooling, both at 36 slices in the same
0.05-0.95 band — and Lateral Meniscus reads **+0.0113** on that swap alone, MCL +0.0259, PF OA −0.0110.
That is the cleanest per-column pooling read on disk, and it says the operator redistributes across
columns rather than lifting the mean (+0.0019).

**What this does NOT say.** These are single-seed per-column deltas at 68 to 558 positives, so no single
row is a result; Lateral Meniscus at −0.0432 clears the floor by 7x and Fracture at −0.0255 by 4x, and
the rest do not. `stack224` also moves the band open with the slice count, so the 12-vs-36 comparison is
the coverage CONCEPT and not the slice count alone — but the pooling comparison at fixed 36 is clean.

**What it changes.** The naive "more image for meniscus" story is now refuted twice, card-free and in
opposite directions: 336->392 px moved both meniscus columns by ~0 (section above), and 12->36 slices
moved Lateral Meniscus DOWN by 0.0432. Any arm aimed at the largest model-bound column should move the
POOLING, not the coverage, and should expect to trade MCL and Contusion for it. That is also the answer
to Q-MENISCUS-2, taken from our own disk rather than the literature.

### Slice pooling and slice count INTERACT: max wins short stacks and loses long ones — card-free, 2026-09-05

The section above read one max-versus-labelwise pair at 36 slices and called the operator a per-column
redistribution. **That was one pair, and the tree holds two more.** `base224` / `labelwise224` /
`attend224` are the same three operators at 12 slices and 224 px, and `band_dense` / `labelwise_dense` /
`attend_dense` are the same three at 20 slices and 336 px — each triple one flag apart. Reading the
column that motivated the question:

**Lateral Meniscus, three operators, three slice counts**

| slices | max | labelwise | attend |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 12 (224 px, band 0.2-0.8) | **0.8460** | 0.8342 (−0.0118) | 0.8280 (−0.0180) |
| 20 (336 px, band 0.1-0.9) | 0.8464 | **0.8566 (+0.0102)** | 0.8551 (+0.0087) |
| 36 (224 px, band 0.05-0.95) | 0.8028 | **0.8141 (+0.0113)** | not on disk |

**The sign flips with the slice count, and it flips for both learned operators independently.** At 12
slices max is the best of the three by 0.0118 and 0.0180; at 20 and 36 it is the worst by 0.0102, 0.0087
and 0.0113. Five of the six deltas clear the 0.0062 paired floor and all six agree in direction within
their count.

**This is the dilution argument with its sign made explicit.** A max over a short stack is close to
optimal for a focal finding — few slices, so few chances for a non-carrying slice to win the argmax — and
it degrades as the count rises, which is exactly where a learned aggregator earns its parameters. The
mechanism predicted the 36-slice loss; it also predicts that the loss is recoverable by the operator, and
it is, by about a quarter of it.

**The means, for scale.** 12 slices: 0.8509 max, 0.8517 labelwise, 0.8503 attend. 20 slices: 0.8578 max,
**0.8613 labelwise**, 0.8569 attend. 36 slices: 0.8476 max, 0.8495 labelwise. So the operator moves the
mean by at most +0.0035 anywhere, inside the floor — the earlier "redistribution, not improvement"
reading survives on the MEAN and is wrong as a statement about the column, which is what it was written
to be about. `labelwise_dense` at 0.8613 is already the project's third-best solo and already rostered.

**Where it does NOT generalise, checked rather than assumed.** The interaction is clean on Lateral
Meniscus and does not repeat on the other columns that ought to be focal. Fracture reads 0.8184 /
0.8124 / 0.8194 at 12, 0.8088 / 0.8124 / 0.8173 at 20, 0.7929 / 0.7911 at 36 — no consistent sign. MCL
reads 0.7803 / 0.7997 / 0.8059, then 0.7931 / 0.7800 / 0.7899, then 0.7859 / 0.8118 — the sign inverts
between the two recipes. So this is a statement about ONE column, and "focal findings prefer learned
pooling" is a mechanism that fits it, not a result that has been shown for focal findings as a class.
With 68 positives Fracture cannot settle its own row either way.

**What it changes.** Three things were true of the meniscus lane this morning and all three are now
measured: resolution 336->392 moves it by zero, slice count 12->36 moves it DOWN 0.0432, and the pooling
operator moves it UP 0.0102 to 0.0113 but only once the stack is long. The best Lateral Meniscus reading
the project owns is `labelwise_dense` at 0.8566, and it is on the roster. The arm the interaction points
at is labelwise pooling at a HIGHER count inside the tight 0.1-0.9 band — 36 slices at 336 px is on the
reservation curve at roughly 12.3 GB with `--recompute-activations`, so it fits — but the honest
prediction is that its MEAN stays flat and only the one column moves, which is a per-column instrument
and not a >=0.010 lever. It is not queued ahead of the depth arm for that reason.

### The input-geometry family re-audited against a NEW hypothesis, and it holds — card-free, 2026-09-05

`knee-m69u` asks for a new axis, and today's reading of `knee-urvf` puts the whole target at +0.010 of
holdout on ONE member. That combination is what makes a re-audit worth writing down even when it finds
nothing: the hypothesis was specific, it was not the one these arms were built against, and it still
lost. The claim was that our pipeline treats every knee as though its geometry were identical — uniform
slices through a fixed band, no anatomical normalisation of the slice axis — and that this is the one
input assumption no arm has ever varied.

**It is varied, on four legs, and three of them were already answered before today.**

* **Multi-plane input is not missing.** `train_series.csv` carries 24371 series over 4407 studies, 3 to
  14 each with a median of 5, tagged by plane and by the two acquisition axes. `slots.py` routes them
  into six slots chosen so each of the twelve findings has a sequence that shows it well, a missing slot
  becomes zeros plus a mask, and `--whole-stack` members run all of it.
* **In-plane registration is measured and unlicensed.** `alignment_damage` on 909 holdout studies:
  focal-minus-regional differential **+0.0103, 95% [-0.0305, +0.0421]**, against a pre-registered sizing
  argument that needed about 0.051 to clear the bar. The interval spans zero, and both raw gaps came out
  negative, which retires the alignment proxy as a study-quality signal at the same time.
* **Through-plane slab normalisation is a NON-PROBLEM, and this is the part that was worth checking.**
  The band is FRACTIONAL — 0.1-0.9 of each study's own stack — so it already adapts to slab extent per
  study, and there is no scatter for a registration step to remove. The axis also carries three trained
  points: 0.20-0.80 = 0.8525, **0.10-0.90 = 0.8565**, 0.00-1.00 = 0.8427. An interior optimum, so the
  band is a filter and the outer slices actively cost. That result lives in the docstring of
  `core/data/corpus/band_coverage.py` and, until this row, was referenced nowhere in this ledger.

**What survives, stated narrowly so it is not re-audited a fourth time.** Every leg above concerns the
slice BUDGET or the WINDOW. None concerns WHICH slices are taken inside a fixed budget, and none
concerns a localiser pointing the classifier at a structure. Those two are open, and both sit upstream
of the aggregation stage this ledger already calls saturated from three directions (more slices -0.0001,
more slots +0.0002, every combining rule within 0.0019). The localiser leg carries a measured headwind
before it starts: `crop80_span` cost 0.0099 against the 130 mm crop with MCL -0.0265 and ACL -0.0263
leading the loss, so cropping in gave back what widening out had paid for. Sent to Kimi as Q-SINGLE-A
and Q-SINGLE-B; the withdrawn legs went with their reasons so no search is spent on them.

**No lane is currently priced at or above 0.010, which is what `knee-m69u` asked to have said out loud.**
The card ran `mricore_corpus` and then the compensated depth arm, whose ABOVE branch would have licensed
re-running the whole foreign-trunk family with layer decay, on the grounds that every trunk negative was
measured through a recipe that never let the trunk move. That branch did not fire; see the depth-axis
entry at the end of this file for what it read instead.

**Why this note exists at all.** The docstring of `band_coverage.py` records the cost of the opposite
habit: left in the present tense after its own question was settled, it invited a 2026-08-25 audit that
set out to build a cache for an operating point the pool had already adopted. A closed axis that does
not say so is a standing invitation to redo the work, and today it nearly bought a second one.

### mricore_corpus reads 0.8390 and the in-domain MRI trunk closes as a QUEUE ITEM — 2026-09-05

**The number, with its shape.** 0.8390, best epoch **11 of 12 — the last one**, monotone from e0 0.7338
through e11 0.8390 with the training loss falling 1.2315 to 0.7099 and never flattening. That is the
UNDERTRAINED shape, not a converged one: the budget bound it, so 0.8390 is what twelve epochs bought and
not what the trunk is worth. Recipe stamped in the launch log: 336 px, 20 slices, band 0.1-0.9, batch 2
accumulate 3, backbone_lr 4e-5, unfreeze_last 6, layer_decay 1.0, one_cycle, whole_stack, attend slot
pooling, max slice pooling. 636 s an epoch, 7.66 GB reserved.

**Against the four branches pre-registered in `logs/mricore_corpus_ledger.log`.** Seat bar 0.8521 —
missed by 0.0131. Natural-image control 0.8455 — missed by 0.0065. RadImageNet control 0.8214 — cleared
by 0.0176. That is the third branch: **the in-domain MRI trunk does not earn a seat and does not pay
against the natural-image recipe, so the lane closes on the gate.**

**What it does NOT establish, and this is the load-bearing part.** The branch was drawn before the shape
was known, and an arm that peaks on its final epoch has not been shown a ceiling. `ortho_slow_trunk` read
0.8265 with the identical pathology — best epoch 11 of 12, monotone, convergence_check clean — and this
ledger recorded then that the ortho trunk "stays open as a QUESTION and closed as a QUEUE ITEM". The same
verdict applies here for the same reason, and it now has two points rather than one.

**The pattern across the whole foreign-trunk family, which is new.** Four trunks have been run under this
recipe: `radiodino_corpus` 0.8214, `coatnet_hybrid` 0.8259, `ortho_slow_trunk` 0.8265, `mricore_corpus`
0.8390. Every one of them inherits `unfreeze_last 6`, `unfreeze_offset 0`, `layer_decay 1.0` — six blocks
at a flat rate — and the two whose epoch curves were examined both peaked on their last epoch. The
natural-image control at 0.8455 does NOT share that shape. So the family may be measuring our schedule
rather than their pretraining, which is precisely the suspicion `band_deep_matched` was built to settle
and which took the card at 14:52Z. If that arm clears 0.8640, every row in this paragraph is a reading of
a recipe that never let the trunk move, and the family is owed a re-run rather than a closure.

**Priced honestly for the pool.** 0.8390 is 0.0252 below the best solo the project owns and well outside
the 0.0062 paired floor, so it is not a member and not a seat candidate on quality. Whether it is a
DIVERSITY seat is a separate question this row does not answer: it is the only MRI-pretrained trunk in a
pool that is otherwise a DINOv2-small monoculture, and the champion's own principles record twice that a
member losing its matched control can still win a seat on error structure. That is a seat_value reading,
not a solo one, and it costs no card.

### The contiguity axis closes by arithmetic, and the docstring that opened it was wrong — card-free, 2026-09-05

`adjacent224` was refuted in August (0.8462 against `native224` 0.8502, -0.0040, converged) and the axis
was closed on it. Its close note named the one condition that would re-open it, before the result was
known: adjacency "does not rule out adjacency at a DENSER stack where span is not the thing being spent.
If `merged_dense_cf` (20 slices, 0.1-0.9) pays, adjacency is worth one re-test there and only there."
That condition looked MET — the operating point moved to 20 slices over 0.10-0.90, `band_dense` reads
0.8578 as the best single member the project owns, and `merged_blend_cf` sits in the champion. An arm was
written against it, a 55.6 GB cache was started, and both were thrown away twenty minutes later without
touching the card, because the premise underneath the re-open condition does not hold.

WHAT THE PREMISE WAS. `Spacing`'s own docstring asserted that "under `SPREAD` no two of the sampled
slices are ever adjacent in the volume, AT ANY WIDTH". Every argument on this axis rested on that
sentence, `knee-e6sj` included: if spread never samples two consecutive slices, then the model can never
see the 3D continuity a meniscal tear is defined by, on any band, and contiguity is an untested lever.

IT IS FALSE, AND FALSE EXACTLY WHERE WE OPERATE. It holds only when the slice budget sits far below the
in-band count. Series depth, measured over a 12-study sample (68 series): min 16, p25 26, median 32,
p75 38, max 160. `band_indices` puts `int(0.1*(depth-1))` to `int(0.9*(depth-1))` in the band, so a
median study offers 25 in-band indices — and we ask for 20 of them. Consecutive pairs out of a possible
19, spread against adjacent:

| series depth | in band | spread adj-pairs | adjacent adj-pairs | spread span | adjacent span |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 (min)     | 13 | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 |
| 26 (p25)     | 21 | 18 | 19 | 20 | 19 |
| 32 (median)  | 25 | 14 | 19 | 24 | 19 |
| 38 (p75)     | 31 |  8 | 19 | 30 | 19 |

At the minimum depth the two rules return the IDENTICAL index set. At p25 spread already delivers 95% of
the available contiguity, at the median 74%. Meanwhile `ADJACENT` pays the full span cost at every depth
— 24 indices of span down to 19 at the median, 30 down to 19 at p75 — which is the same
span-for-contiguity trade the August arm was read as losing (Regional -0.0073 against focal -0.0018,
broad rather than confined).

WHY THAT CLOSES THE AXIS RATHER THAN MOVING IT. The contrast between the two rules is large only on DEEP
series, and deep series are precisely where adjacency discards the most span: at depth 160 spread covers
128 indices and adjacent covers 19. So the two things the re-open condition needed — a big contrast and a
cheap span — are anti-correlated by construction. A denser stack is not where adjacency gets a fair test;
it is where `SPREAD` CONVERGES TO `ADJACENT`. There is no operating point reachable from here that
satisfies both, so the axis does not close on a second measurement, it closes on arithmetic, and
`knee-e6sj`'s re-open condition is retired rather than merely unmet.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY. It does not say the rival's +0.018 was wrong. They ran 9 slices across 24, a
budget well under the in-band count, which is the regime where the old docstring sentence IS true and
where spread and adjacent really are different samplers. Their operating point has the property ours
lacks. It also does not touch slice COUNT or band WIDTH, both of which are measured elsewhere and both
of which stand.

THE COST OF THE WRONG SENTENCE, written down because it is the transferable part. One false clause in a
strategy docstring generated a P1 bead, survived its own arm's refutation intact, and was about to buy a
second arm plus a 55.6 GB decode at the exact operating point where it is least true. Nothing in the
gates could catch it: it is prose, it is self-consistent, and the code beneath it is correct. What caught
it was refusing to write the arm's mechanism paragraph from the docstring and instead computing the two
index sets — six lines, no card. The docstring now carries the table instead of the claim.

### The depth axis closes on its OWN re-run, with the rate confound removed — 2026-09-05

Arm `experiments/arms/band_deep_matched.sh`, bead knee-zt3l6, reading `logs/band_deep_matched_ledger.log`.
`--unfreeze-last 12 --layer-decay 0.7 --backbone-lr 9.8e-5 --batch 2 --accumulate 6`, twelve epochs,
~580 s an epoch. Control `band_dense` 0.8578.

**0.8487 at e11**, against the arm's own four pre-registered branches: ABOVE 0.8640 licenses the trunk
family, 0.8516-0.8640 decay-neutral, **0.8421-0.8516 closes the depth axis**, below 0.8421 suspect the
harness. It landed in the third band, -0.0091 against the control, outside the 0.0062 paired floor.

**WHY THIS IS THE READING AND THE AUGUST ONE WAS NOT.** `band_dense_llrd` ran the same ladder at
`--backbone-lr 4e-5` and read 0.8483 — three ten-thousandths from this arm — and the ledger REFUSED its
BELOW branch, correctly. `StudyModel.parameter_groups` anchors the ladder at the TOP opened block, so
opening twelve blocks does not merely add six whisper blocks beneath the control's six: it also re-grades
the control's own six down to a geometric mean of `0.7^2.5` = 0.41 of the rate they shipped at. That arm
moved two things and its training loss said so, flooring ~0.13 high and still descending at e10. This arm
absorbs the ladder's geometric mean into the anchor (`4e-5 / 0.7^2.5` = 9.8e-5), so blocks 6-11 run at a
geometric mean of 4.0e-5 — the control's flat rate — while blocks 0-5 run from 1.15e-5 down to 1.9e-6.

So the confound is removed and the answer does not move: 0.8483 confounded, 0.8487 matched. Opening the
encoder's bottom half costs ~0.009 at this operating point, and it costs it for the reason the ladder was
supposed to rule out rather than for the rate. The depth axis is CLOSED on a matched arm.

**CONVERGENCE, stated because the score is only readable with it.** Twelve of twelve epochs ran, and the
peak IS the last epoch (e10 0.8485, e11 0.8487), so `convergence_check` classes it UNDERTRAINED rather
than TRUNCATED — the budget bound it. The final increment is +0.0002, a thirtieth of the floor, so the
undertraining is nominal and the score is not a floor in any useful sense. A longer budget could not
plausibly recover 0.009.

**WHAT IT DOES NOT CLOSE.** This is one encoder (DINOv2-small) at one corner (336 px, 20 slices,
0.1-0.9). It says nothing about depth on a trunk whose pretraining is not natural-image, and the
`ABOVE 0.8640` branch that would have licensed re-running the foreign-trunk family did not fire — so that
family stays closed on its own ~25 arms, not on this one.

## Diversity without a solo bar buys nothing — three distinct families priced to zero in one day — 2026-09-05

knee-cj40f licensed exactly one card-free measurement against the CNN axis: how decorrelated
`radnet_pinned` actually is from the ViT incumbents, on the argument that a branch which is weak but
genuinely different can still earn a seat. It is now measured, and so are the two other non-incumbent
families the project trained this week. All three read the same thing.

| candidate | solo | nearest rank | JS nearest | seat vs honest12 | best available seat |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `radnet_pinned_s2026` (RadImageNet DenseNet, BN pinned) | 0.7505 | **0.6415** | 0.0261 | −0.0009 [−0.0017, −0.0001] | −0.0001 |
| `coatnet_hybrid_s2026` (CoAtNet-2 conv/attention hybrid) | 0.8259 | 0.8223 | 0.0253 | −0.0006 [−0.0012, −0.0000] | −0.0005 |
| `mricore_corpus_s2026` (radiodinob16 trunk) | 0.8390 | 0.8607 | 0.0164 | −0.0007 [−0.0012, −0.0002] | −0.0006 |

The roster of twelve has a rank boundary of 0.8956 and a JS boundary of 0.0150. `radnet_pinned` is the
most decorrelated member this project has ever produced — 0.6415 is a quarter of the way to chance,
against a pool whose own members sit at 0.87-0.90 — and its best available seat is **−0.0001**. Not
positive-but-small. Zero, from the most different thing we own.

**The pattern is a SOLO BAR, not a diversity deficit.** The three candidates span 0.09 of solo AUC and
0.22 of rank divergence, and their seat values are indistinguishable from each other and from zero. What
they share is that every one of them sits 0.02 to 0.11 below the pool's best solo of 0.8578. This
reproduces on our own corpus what NVIDIA's IJCAI-ECAI 2022 result stated and what `radnet_pinned`'s own
pre-registration gated on: a branch more than about five points off the incumbents measures as diverse
and still ensembles worse. We now have it at three points on our own data rather than one citation.

**What this closes.** The CNN axis stays closed, and it is now closed by MEASUREMENT rather than by the
price of the arm — which is what knee-cj40f asked for and the only thing that could have re-opened it.
It also retires the standing hope that architecture diversity is the missing 0.009 to the leader: the
diversity is available, it has been bought three separate ways, and it is worth zero at this solo gap.

**What it does NOT say.** It is not evidence that a DISTINCT member cannot pay. It is evidence that one
below the bar cannot. The re-open condition is unchanged and now has a number attached: a non-incumbent
family that lands within about 0.01 of 0.8578. None of the three came within 0.02, and `coatnet_hybrid`
converged (12/12 epochs, peak not at the end) so its 0.8259 is not a budget artefact.

**Cost: zero card, zero slots.** Three `seat_value` runs of about ten seconds each, against three
checkpoints that already existed.

## The gold-58 supervision ladder is a leak, not a result — and the ruler gap survives it — 2026-09-05

Nine `--hold-annotations` checkpoints scored on the 58 radiologist-annotated studies, paired against
`band_dense_hold_s2026` with resampled 95% intervals. Seven of eight read positive, three cleared their
own interval, at 0.014-0.022 — magnitudes that would clear the 1.5% bar on a ruler none of them trained
on. I wrote that up as a five-knob confirmation of the ruler-bias account. It is not one. Zero of the
eight rows are clean.

| arm | delta vs control | what carries gold information into it |
|---|---|---|
| `labelwise_dense_s2026` | +0.0215 clears | `--calibrated-targets` |
| `base_clean_s2026` | +0.0195 clears | `--calibrated-targets` |
| `recal_dense_s2026` | +0.0172 clears | trains on `$RECAL` |
| `calib_dense_hold_s2026` | +0.0161 inside | `--calibrated-targets` |
| `contrast_dense_s2026` | +0.0155 inside | `--calibrated-targets` |
| `finding_calib_dense_s2026` | +0.0142 inside | `--calibrated-targets` |
| `contrast_pool_s2026` | +0.0136 inside | `--calibrated-targets` |
| `margin_calib_s2026` | -0.0067 inside | `--calibrated-targets` |
| `band_dense_hold_s2026` | control 0.8956 | nothing — plain `--labels`, no calibration |

**Two separate paths, one origin.** `Supervision.MEASURED_AGREEMENT` was fitted on these same 696 cells,
which `annotated_readings --help` already says out loud; that covers the seven `--calibrated-targets`
arms. `recal_dense` was the one I identified as the clean exception because it carries no such flag — and
it is contaminated by the other path. `kneemri/evaluation/level_calibration.py:156` fits the level map
**on the annotated rows** and then applies it to the whole table, the gold studies included, by design:
"a study's report reading is recalibrated whether or not a radiologist also read its images, because the
recalibration is a statement about the reader." A true statement about what recalibration IS, and it
means the gold readings are inside every row of `$RECAL`.

So the ladder measures this: **eight arms whose supervision constants were fitted from the 58 gold
studies beat, on those same 58 studies, one control that never saw them.** The rank ordering of the
deltas is not informative either — it orders the arms by how much gold-derived signal their supervision
carries. `--hold-annotations` does not undo it. That flag drops the annotated CELLS from the loss; it
cannot drop constants fitted from them and then baked into every study's label.

**The refusal is too narrow, and it says so in the wrong words.** `annotated_readings.withheld` checks
one thing, `options["hold_annotations"] == True`, and on the strength of it the tool prints *"9 member(s),
none of them trained on these cells"*. Literally true and materially false: none read those cells, all
eight were TAUGHT from constants fitted on them. A reader who trusts that line — I did — reads a leak as
a clean measurement. Filed as knee-6r2wq (P1): the refusal has to cover fitted-constant provenance,
`--calibrated-targets` and a `$RECAL`-family label table alike, and the census line must not claim
independence it did not check.

**What survives, and it is the thing that mattered.** The control's own two-ruler gap is untouched by
all of this, because `band_dense_hold` is the one checkpoint with no gold-derived supervision anywhere in
it: **0.8956 on the 58 annotated studies against ~0.857 on the report holdout, same weights, +0.039
apart** — six times the 0.0062 noise floor. That is a fact about two rulers, not about a treatment, so
nothing in the leak touches it. Our report labels over-call (108 false positives against 32 misses over
the 58), and the holdout that ordered every seat decision in this project carries that same over-calling.

**And it is why `relabel_hold` is now the whole test rather than the last rung of a ladder.** Its
treatment is `--unread-targets` from a confident-learning detector fitted on the REPORT labels; the
radiologist readings never enter it, by either path. It is the only supervision arm this project owns
whose gold-58 reading will mean what it appears to mean. The four pre-registered branches in its header
stand unchanged — and it now has no ladder standing behind it to soften a null.

## 224 px costs 0.0049 of solo AUC and buys 3.2x the throughput — 2026-09-05

`band224` is `band_dense`'s recipe at 224 px instead of 336, and it was armed to price the RECIPE rather
than to find a seat. It converged 12 of 12 epochs, peak at e9.

| | 336 px (`band_dense`) | 224 px (`band224`) |
|---|---|---|
| solo holdout AUC | 0.8578 | **0.8529** |
| seconds per epoch, this card | 450 | **142** |
| twelve-epoch arm | ~90 min | **~28 min** |

**−0.0049 of AUC for 3.2x the throughput,** both measured on this card on the same day rather than
inferred from pixel counts. The AUC cost is under the 0.0062 holdout noise floor, so as a MEMBER the two
recipes are not separable — which is also why `band224` is declined as a seat (−0.0002 against honest12,
nearest-neighbour rank 0.9097 against a 0.8956 boundary: a near-twin, not a diversity buy).

**What it changes is the price of every question, not the answer to any of them.** The open lane is
supervision — the confident-learning selector, its budget, prune against relabel — and until today each
point on it cost ninety minutes of card, which is why the axis has exactly one refuted point on it
(`errors_dense`) and one running (`relabel_hold`). At 28 minutes a point, a dose curve is three arms in
an hour and a half instead of four and a half hours. That is the difference between pricing the axis and
sampling it.

**The constraint on spending it.** A 224 arm has to be read against a 224 control, and the control has to
be a `--hold-annotations` fit or the gold ruler will refuse it. `base224_s2026` exists and is not held, so
it cannot serve. The first 224 label-axis arm therefore owes a `band224_hold` control alongside it — 28
minutes, and then every subsequent point on the curve is a single 28-minute arm against it.

Not being spent tonight: `relabel_hold` and `rank966_hold` are both matched to `band_dense_hold` at 336
and must stay there. This buys the arms AFTER them.

## The label-correction lever was founded on the wrong table, and closes at 0.1% — 2026-09-06

`train.csv` is not a label table for these studies. It carries a value for **58 of our 4407**: 52188 of
its 52884 target cells are nan, and every one of the twelve targets is nan on 4349 rows. What our members
are scored against is the reader's `labels/report_labels_v2.csv` — 4406 studies, zero nan cells, the soft
0.08/0.28/0.68/0.82/0.94 convention every holdout record on disk already carries.

Two numbers were produced against the wrong file, and both moved when it was corrected.

| reading | on `train.csv` | on `report_labels_v2.csv` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| foreign family, fold-matched over the corpus | 0.8211 (4407) | **0.8929** (4406) |
| `label_contradiction`, fold-0 holdout, five members | 6.2% of cells (675/10908) | **0.1%** (13/10908) |

The control holds: the same family on the 909 still reads **0.8812**, unchanged, because that path takes
its truth from a holdout npz and never touched the csv. That is what makes this a table defect rather
than a serving one.

**The corpus census, three independent ways, on the correct table:**

| instruments | candidate cells | denominator |
| --- | --- | --- |
| their corpus OOF + our four OOF folds + one fold-0 member | 66 (0.1%) | 52872 cells, 4406 studies |
| our four OOF folds alone (`oof_fold1..4_s2026`) | 51 (0.1%) | 41964 cells, 3497 studies |
| five fold-0 members, the original census re-run | 13 (0.1%) | 10908 cells, 909 studies |

`oof_folds.sh` pre-registered "far BELOW the fold-0 census ⇒ the label route closes here for the second
time". It lands at 0.1% on every denominator, against a ~2% threshold pre-registered as the level worth
acting on. **The route is closed, and the 6.2% that opened it was an artefact of reading truth out of a
98.7%-nan file.** The 336/12 full-strength OOF re-derivation that was contingent on this is cancelled
(~4.7 h of card), as is the correction arm.

One caveat kept in writing: their family alone contradicts the reader **nowhere** (0 cells), and its
predictions are flatter than ours (1st/99th percentile 0.060/0.895 against our 0.018/0.966). A
conjunction census is not a fair instrument for a compressed calibration, so their 0 is not evidence
about labels. Our own four-fold reading, whose spread matches the original census's members, is the one
that carries the closure.

**What this leaves standing, and it is the better half:** `foreign_oof_corpus.holdout.npz` is now an
honest out-of-sample opinion on all 4406 studies from a family that reads **0.8929** fold-matched — above
our best solo (`stackfit_s2026`, 0.8631) and above their own 909 reading. As a label corrector it says
nothing. As a distillation teacher it is the strongest per-study signal this project has.

## Distillation from a foreign teacher DESTROYS distance instead of importing it — 2026-09-06

`foreign_distill_s2026` finished twelve epochs (peak e9, `convergence_check` clean) and answers the
question `foreign_distill.sh` pre-registered, on the column that question needed.

| member | teacher | solo | seat on greedyseat base of 7 (Rank) | nearest, rank | js divergence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `band_dense` | none | 0.8578 | seated | 0.8959 | **0.0273** |
| `distill_pairs` | ours (fold-0 twins) | 0.8594 | — | 0.9079 | 0.0249 |
| `foreign_distill` | **theirs** (5 DINOv3 folds, 0.8929 fold-matched) | 0.8595 | **−0.0004 at 1x → −0.0027 at 4x** | 0.9003 | **0.0190** |

Roster boundary: rank 0.8936, js 0.0147. All three students land SCALED, none DISTINCT.

**The seat is negative at every weight on both rulers** — Rank −0.0004 / −0.0012 / −0.0020 / −0.0027 at
1-4x on a 0.8763 base; Logit −0.0001 → −0.0018 on a 0.8768 base — and the distance column says why. The
foreign teacher did not move the student away from our pool, it moved it **toward** it: js divergence
0.0273 → **0.0190**, a 30% collapse against the no-teacher control, with rank agreement rising 0.8959 →
0.9003. Our own teacher does the same thing slightly less hard. **A student trained toward an ordering
ends up agreeing with the pool that already holds most of that ordering, because the label term holds 0.7
of its loss and the labels are what our pool is already fitted to.** What survives the transfer is the
corpus's ordering, which we own; what does not survive is the family-specific structure, which is the
entire reason the seat is worth anything.

**The number this sits beside is the whole finding.** Same family, same released weights, same
predictions:

| use of `teacher_foreign_corpus.npz` | delta |
|---|---|
| SEATED directly (their weights mounted) | **+0.0178** at 6x on the served base of 8, **+0.0218** on the greedyseat base of 7 |
| ABSORBED into a student | **−0.0004** at 1x, worse at every larger weight |

Distillation is lossy in exactly the dimension seating is not. Together with `foreign_recipe_v3small`
(their recipe transcribed and retrained here: 0.8087 against their weights' 0.8812), this closes both
cheap routes to a foreign family. **A foreign family is worth having as MOUNTED WEIGHTS or not at all** —
neither its recipe nor its ordering carries the thing that makes it distant. The one case where
distillation would still be the only route is a licence that forbids shipping the weights.

**What is NOT closed, and is on the card next.** The third use of the same teacher file: `foreign_dissent`
(knee-1vdcz) re-weights the pair mass toward the pairs THEIR ordering gets wrong, rather than reproducing
it. `dissent_seat` ran that flag at the same strength on OUR teacher and read 0.8509 with no seat — but
that arm was killed at epoch 8 of 12 (a floor, not a landing) and its teacher was our own pool, whose
complement to itself is noise. The pre-registered column is js divergence against `band_dense`'s 0.0273:
dissent must move it UP where distillation moved it DOWN, or every non-seating use of a foreign teacher
is closed.

## The UNK cell is a constant, so a prior cannot fix it and a mask is the only treatment — 2026-09-06

Census of `blend_hybrid_fx_v4b.csv`, denominator **4407 studies per column**, all twelve printed
(`__verdict == UNK`):

| finding | UNK | frac | mean value on UNK | mean value on stated | conf on UNK | sd(value \| UNK) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ACL | 355 | 0.081 | 0.2644 | 0.2682 | 0.0500 | 0.011 |
| MCL | 430 | 0.098 | 0.2613 | 0.1905 | 0.0500 | 0.029 |
| Medial Meniscus | 250 | 0.057 | 0.2661 | 0.4847 | 0.0500 | 0.020 |
| Lateral Meniscus | 442 | 0.100 | 0.2635 | 0.2519 | 0.0500 | 0.023 |
| Medial OA | 1125 | 0.255 | 0.2598 | 0.4530 | 0.0500 | 0.074 |
| Lateral OA | 1457 | 0.331 | 0.2718 | 0.3500 | 0.0500 | 0.091 |
| PF OA | 815 | 0.185 | 0.2720 | 0.5142 | 0.0500 | 0.064 |
| Effusion | 942 | 0.214 | 0.2654 | 0.5424 | 0.0500 | 0.008 |
| **Synovitis** | **3713** | **0.843** | 0.2685 | 0.7211 | 0.0500 | 0.050 |
| Baker's | 2024 | 0.459 | 0.2625 | 0.4268 | 0.0500 | 0.018 |
| Contusion | 916 | 0.208 | 0.2464 | 0.3068 | 0.0500 | 0.055 |
| Fracture | 2486 | 0.564 | 0.2865 | 0.2210 | 0.0500 | 0.054 |

Confidence on an UNK cell is **0.0500 exactly, on every cell of every column**, and the value is a
sentinel near 0.26 taking between 6 and 158 distinct values across thousands of rows. The UNK cell is a
constant with jitter. Stated cells, by contrast, run 0.19 to 0.72 in mean and carry conf 0.87-0.93.

**The consequence for the three candidate treatments.** The board scores AUC, a *ranking* metric. A
constant target on a subset produces gradient that pulls those studies' logits toward one value: it
teaches no ordering and actively **compresses** the ordering on the rows it covers. For synovitis that
is 84.3% of the corpus compressed at weight 1.

- **PRIOR (set the UNK target from the gold positive rate among UNK cells)** replaces 0.265 with another
  constant. It moves where the compression sits, not whether there is one. Its only real effect is on
  calibration, which the vote does not read. **AUC-neutral by construction** — this is the argument that
  retires it, not a measurement.
- **MASK** removes a gradient measured to carry zero information, and lets the image decide — the reading
  this ledger already owns twice (effusion and contusion both beat their own labels).
- **WEIGHT** at mattiaangeli's `W = 0.25 + 0.75*conf` gives an UNK cell **0.2875**, i.e. 29%, not zero.
  It is a genuine third option, not a soft mask.

**A porting trap, recorded because it inverts the treatment.** stevenleehans' `2|p − 0.5|` masks silence
*only because their sentinel is exactly 0.5*. Ours is 0.265. Ported literally, an UNK cell gets weight
`2 × |0.265 − 0.5| = 0.47` — our silence comes out at nearly half weight — while a *stated* cell near 0.5
(a "maybe" the reader committed to) is weighted toward zero. The formula does the opposite of what it
does in their kernel. **Mask on the `__verdict` column**, the field that states silence, never on a value
that silence has to be re-inferred from.

Cost of masking, stated: the synovitis head trains on **694 studies** instead of 4407 (fracture 1921,
Baker's 2383). Taken anyway, because the head sits on a trunk trained by eleven other columns at full
data, so what shrinks is the head's fit and not the representation.

Card: zero. Two cpu reads of one csv.

## The window sampler was never missing — it is `trainer.py:532`, and whole-stack is its LIMIT — 2026-09-07

Written after an order to "port his window sampler into our loader" turned out to be an order to build a
thing that has been running since before this project had a board row. Card-free, one morning of reading.

**The claim under audit.** dread's training script draws k=12 windows per step over a 64-slice stack and
averages k_eval=24 at inference, and his kernel comment (`knee-mri-twelve-findings-from-a-single-model.py:315-317`)
attributes the collateral ligaments and the lateral meniscus to the peripheral slices that a narrow span
throws away. Read as a mechanism, that is: *sample windows across epochs so depth costs no per-step VRAM,
then average windows at serve.*

**We already do both, and the second one is measured.**

- `kneemri/training/trainer.py:523-532` — `plan()` returns `[(batch, int(generator.integers(0, corpus.slices - self.window + 1))) for batch in batches]`. A random window start per BATCH, redrawn every epoch, over a cache deeper than the window. `core/data/corpus/prefetch.py:47-48` reads it as `corpus.window(batch, start=start, width=self.width)`; `study_cache.py:72-84` serves `width` slices of every slot from `start`, with `slices` documented as "how many slices per slot the cache holds, which bounds the windows a member can read". The cache is a stack and the window slides inside it — it is not a fixed pick.
- The serve side takes the CENTRE window only (`trainer.py:681`, `middle = (corpus.slices - self.window) // 2`). The k_eval analogue exists separately as **overlap TTA**, and this file already prices it: windowed members gain +0.0152 / +0.0141 / +0.0146, whole-stack members gain **~0**, under the heading "Whole-stack and overlap TTA are the same mechanism". Averaging overlapping windows in PREDICTION space is how a model that cannot afford the whole stack approximates seeing it; reading the whole stack in FEATURE space measured better.

**So his sampler is the budgeted version of what our members do at full budget.** His 64 slices at 480 px
do not fit a step; our 20 at 336 do, and `--whole-stack` reads them all. The degenerate case is worth
naming: on a 12-slice cache with a 12-slice window, `integers(0, 1)` is always 0, so members fitted on the
12sl caches carry the sampler and never sample. Members fitted on the 20sl caches have been running his
mechanism the whole time.

**WHAT IS ACTUALLY UNTESTED, and it is a VRAM question rather than an anatomy one:** does window sampling
beat a whole-stack read once the stack is DEEPER than whole-stack can hold? At 1.335 GB/slice, whole-stack
dies past about 20 slices at 336 px, and sampling is what buys depth beyond that. That cell is blocked on
disk, not on card (see below).

## The published raptor corpus is 0.15-0.85, read off its own pixels — 2026-09-07

The corpus dread published records no geometry, so it was recovered by matching its slices to the maxspan
build: 50 studies, each 44-slot plane downsampled 4x and normalised-cross-correlated against all 64 maxspan
slots of the same study. Mean best-match NCC 0.950, 41.9 of 44 slots valid per study, 99.6% of adjacent
matched positions monotone within a run. Slot layout confirmed independently of the NCC by per-slot
occupancy over all 3200 studies (the missing-plane runs break at the same fractions in both corpora: Sag0
at 0.97, Cor0 at 0.74). Crop confirmed by tissue bounding box on matched pairs, ratio median 1.000, IQR
[1.000, 1.000] over 2096 pairs.

| | published 44 | maxspan 64 |
|---|---|---|
| slots | Sag1 12 / Sag0 10 / Cor1 8 / Cor0 6 / Ax 8 | Sag1 18 / Sag0 14 / Cor1 12 / Cor0 8 / Ax 12 |
| span | **[0.15, 0.85]** | [0.02, 0.98] |
| crop | 140.0 mm | 140.0 mm |

**THREE CONSEQUENCES.** (1) Cell C moves TWO variables against A', not three — slot count and span; the
crop is constant. (2) His kernel's serve span `[0.06, 0.94]` is NEITHER corpus: a first slot at 0.06 never
lands inside any run's interquartile range on the published one. His released weights were fitted at
0.15-0.85 and are served at 0.06-0.94, so the geometry mismatch is his. (3) Our own span ladder now gives C
a DIRECTION rather than a neutral band: 0.20-0.80 = 0.8525, 0.10-0.90 = 0.8565, 0.00-1.00 = 0.8427, an
interior optimum. A' at 0.15-0.85 sits beside our second-best point; C at 0.02-0.98 sits essentially at the
point that lost 0.0138. If span behaves on his stack as on ours, **C reads below A'**. The one thing that
could overturn that is the sampler above — depth accruing across epochs instead of thinning a fixed budget
— which our fixed-slice-count ladder cannot see. That makes C the cell separating "wider span is bad" from
"wider span is bad only when you pay for it in density".

## The next geometry cell is blocked by DISK, not by card — 2026-09-07 (knee-8d6m1)

`df /d` reads 3.7 T used, **39 G free**. The cache directory alone is 656 GB, and dread's two corpora added
~54 GB today. A 336 px cache at 40-64 slices is 120-191 GB; at 224 px, 64 slices is 85 GB. Neither fits. So
the deeper-than-whole-stack cell cannot be built until an array dies.

**The array census (researcher, D16, 11:20Z).** Every cache array was resolved to the members fitted on it
by rebuilding the cache key from `study_cache.py:220` + the three suffix rules and reading each member's
recipe from the first line of its `.metrics.jsonl` (234 members) or its `.pt` payload (41). Population = 314
names with a holdout record or a roster line; 275 resolve, 39 claim no array (no `.pt` on disk).

- **True orphans — nothing with a holdout record or a roster line resolves to them — total 33 GiB**:
  `224px_12sl_merged` 17.3, seven small foreign arrays 14.1, five `_first60` smoke caches 2.1. That is the
  whole answer to "what does nothing need", and it is *less* than the 39 GB already free.
- **Declined-only arrays, 102.6 GiB**: `336px_16sl` 44.5, `336px_12sl_tissue` 33.4,
  `224px_20sl_0.1-0.9band` 24.7 — every member on them is in `comp/members.declines` with a written reason.
- **One-roster-member arrays, ~295 GiB**: the two 64.9 GiB merged 20sl arrays, `336px_20sl` 55.6,
  `420px_12sl_160mm` 52.1, `merged3` 48.4, `224px_12sl_tissue` 14.8.

**An array is needed for exactly three things** — a NEW arm on that recipe, a re-serve/TTA reading of the
member on our stack, and an `init=` warm-start that re-reads the same corpus. Nothing else: nine roster
members are shippable today with their array already deleted (`res392_ws_s2026` and `intensity392_ws_s2026`
among them, the roster's own line-1 solo at 0.8523), because the `.pt` payload carries `holdout` and
`targets` itself. **Deleting a one-member array costs the OPTION of re-reading that member, not the
member.**

**And every array is a VIEW, so deletion is reversible.** The merged arrays are provably base + rijeka rows
(5143 = 4407 + 736 for all three; `merged3` 6393 = 5143 + 1250 mrnet), built by `build_merged.py:74` /
`merged_cache.py:94-95` by memmap copy — so 217 GiB of merged arrays rebuild from a base array plus a 1.5
GiB foreign one, which is exactly why the seven "orphan" small foreign arrays are the LAST thing to delete
rather than the first. The rest come from raw DICOM, and all four raw trees are present
(`rsna_knee_abnormality/train_series` 4411 entries, `mrnet`, `kneemri_rijeka`, `fastmri`). `decode_bench`
measures processes(4) at 0.12 s/study at 12 slices over 4407 studies = 9 min, scaling with planes, so a 20sl
rebuild is ~15 min and the worst array is well under an hour. `atime` cannot rank the arrays — every file
reads the same timestamp, so access-time updates are off on this volume, and the member mapping above is
the only honest test. No process of ours holds any of them open: A', cell C and effv2l all read dread's
corpora under `D:/kaggle/input/`, not a processed cache.

second-largest.

So the pre-registered signature did not land, and the honest reading is that one of these is true and 58
rows cannot separate them: either the UNK cells that matter are not where the corpus UNK RATE says they
are — Synovitis sits at 0.75 on both members, i.e. the column is hard for the IMAGE, so freeing its
labels cannot buy what the pixels do not carry — or the gain is a calibration effect on the two
highest-prevalence columns and Fracture is noise. Nothing here licenses an arm; it licenses the ruler
question, which is where it has gone.

Denominator stated: every gold number above is 58 studies with the `n+` positives shown, not the corpus.
A twelve-column table on 58 rows shows large per-column moves by construction and no per-column interval
was computed, so no single column above is a finding on its own.

## 2026-09-07 — D35: the seat axis is closed by a FIT, not by a tally

201 honest fold-0 members, 896 gold-removed studies, L75mid, proxy = five parents rank-mean @2/3 +
`raptor_v4_swa` @1/3 = 0.9237 (five parents alone 0.8993; parents' mean solo 0.8865). Three seat shapes per
member, all paired against the proxy: (b) sixth ours-member at 1/6 x 2/3 = 0.111 · (c) REPLACES raptor at
1/3, read against −0.0244 · (d) 1/7 beside raptor inside the foreign block.

Two-variable fit, 151 members with lift > −0.03, ALL families:
  (b) = −0.0009 + **0.076**·lift + 0.0139·(1−corr)   R² 0.87
  (c) = −0.0290 + **0.313**·lift + 0.0557·(1−corr)   R² 0.98
Within `small` alone the coefficients are the same (0.084/0.0194; 0.313/0.0554). So the FAMILY does not change
the slope — the seat WEIGHT does (~0.7-0.9 per unit weight), and family enters only through corr. D34's 0.25
was a paired child-replaces-parent read at weight 0.133 on three members: the high end of that frame's
scatter, not a different mechanism.

**What the bar costs, and why this is mechanism-closed rather than tally-closed.** (b) ≥ +0.005 needs solo
**0.934** at corr 0.83, or 0.947 at corr 0.90. An honest 1/3 seat merely BEATING the in-sample raptor needs
solo 0.949. The best honest solo on disk is 0.8972 and the best (b) over all 201 members is **+0.0014**
(`labelwise_dense_s2026`). No single seat at weight ≤ 1/3 can pay +0.005 from any family at any solo that
exists. The seven board flats were not seven unlucky draws; they are the fit. Denominator: 151 members, 896
studies, one frame.

Cross-family premium at equal solo is real and small: A''s four coatnet2-his cells read (b) +0.0002..+0.0003
and honest-1/3 +0.0025..+0.0028 against 20 same-family `small` members at the same solo reading (b) −0.0009..
+0.0002 (median −0.0004). So ≈ **+0.0007 at weight 0.111, ≈ +0.005 at weight 1/3**, bought with corr 0.82-0.83
against 0.88-0.94. Diversity pays at the WEIGHT the foreign block already has, and almost nothing at a sixth
ours-seat's weight.

**The in-sample raptor is inflated ~9x, and the board agrees with the honest number 1:1.** `raptor_v4_swa` at
1/3 reads +0.0244 on the 896 — it trained on them. Its honest stand-in, his own recipe with fold 0 held out
(`repl2x2_a_swa`, solo 0.8787), is worth **+0.0027** at the same 1/3 (0.8993 → 0.9020), and the BOARD's
0 → 1/3 step read **+0.003**. Every offline reading that wanted raptor's share raised toward 0.9 was the
inflation talking.

Consequence for the entry staged today: `kneemri-cleancalib` seats `final_ws_df` as a SEVENTH ours-member,

### D43 — the block pays for CORR, not for solo: the six-twin retrain is cancelled — 2026-09-07

**The measurement** (researcher, `d42_block.py` / `d42_block.out` / `d42_control.out`). Take the champion
proxy — five fold-0 parents rank-mean at w = 2/3 plus `raptor_v4_swa` at 1/3, 0.9237; the five alone 0.8993,
their mean pairwise corr 0.871 — and swap each parent for a DISTILLED CHILD of its own family, across all
2^5 - 1 = 31 subsets. The children carry **+0.0052 of solo** between them. On the block they read
**-0.0014**. The control — five UNDISTILLED siblings at **+0.0036 solo** — reads **-0.0002**. Composition is
additive to 1e-4 at every k, so this is not a saturation artefact of one subset. Block internal corr climbs
0.871 -> 0.931 (distilled) or 0.904 (control): the (1 - corr) term eats the solo term, five times out of five.

**So the null belongs to the FAMILY, not to distillation.** A treatment that lifts a member's solo while
leaving it inside its own family's error pattern reaches the block at roughly 0.08 of its solo, not at the
w = 2/3 a seat-count argument would give it.

**What it cancels.** The six-twin `retrain_six_distill` block — 5.7 h of card — was licensed by a solo gate
(`clean_calib` >= +0.004, then the twins). Under this measurement that gate is the wrong instrument: it
prices exactly the quantity the block does not credit. Cancelled in `after_clean_calib_chain.sh` (commit
f776bc3e); the card went to `foreign_labels_dense` (75 min, the label axis) and `hisrecipe_distill` (2.4 h,
a foreign recipe, corr 0.750-0.833) instead — both of them attempts to move CORR rather than solo.

**The gate every seat treatment is judged by from here.** Not `delta >= 0.004` on a solo but

    swap_gain = proxy(child in place of parent) - proxy(parents)      GO iff swap_gain >= +0.0010
    corr guard: corr(child, block-minus-parent) <= corr(parent, block-minus-parent) + 0.01

`clean_calib`'s own pre-registration under it is +0.000..+0.0005, **NO-GO** — and its reading is still taken
and still printed, because a pre-registered number stays readable after it stops being deciding.

### D48 — gold-58 is the only ruler that shows the board's sign for his family, and it moves OUR members by +0.041 — 2026-09-07

Zero card. Researcher job 9 (`d48_job9.py`, `d48_gold.py`, scratchpad). Two questions were asked; the second
answer is the one that matters to us.

**Asked: does a member trained on his labels inherit his family's board deficit? No, not through the labels.**
His soft table and our v2 levels are nearly the same object on the 896: label corr 0.73-0.89 per column, his
label predicts our ruler at 0.947 macro and ours predicts his at 0.942, and his own OOF reads 0.8984 on OUR
ruler against 0.8922 on HIS. A model fitted to his labels is not better read by his labels, so eleven of twelve
columns are the same ruler twice and there is nothing there to import.

**The exception is Synovitis, and it is where every his-family gain this project has measured lives.** He calls
232 of 896 positive where we call 69 (label corr 0.29, cell disagreement 21%). It is the one column where his
OOF beats `raptor_v4_swa` on OUR ruler (+0.070), and it carried +0.0124 of D47's +0.0063 seat gain. Rank corr
across columns between "his OOF beats raptor" and "label disagreement" is +0.66. **Consequence, now the standing
gate:** a corr-to-block drop concentrated in Synovitis / MedMen / Bakers is a LABELS artefact and does not fire
the D45 decorrelation gate; only a drop spread across the ligament/OA columns does. Read per column, never on
the macro.

**Asked as a caveat, answered as the finding: the 13 fold-0 gold rows.** The 58 all-twelve-annotated studies are
the only ruler on disk that is not derived from report text, and 13 of them sit in fold 0 where our members are
honest. On those same rows, changing nothing but the truth table:

| | report ruler (v2 L75mid) | gold ruler (radiologist) | move |
|---|---|---|---|
| ours5 (honest) | 0.866 | **0.907** | **+0.041** |
| his DINOv3 OOF | 0.848 | 0.843 | -0.005 |
| `raptor_v4_swa` (in-sample) | 0.867 | 0.890 | +0.023 |
| gap ours5 - his | -0.018 | **-0.064** | boot95 [-0.127, -0.016] |

Report-vs-gold cell disagreement on those rows: 22% (35 of 156). On all 58 gold rows his OOF reads 0.845, BELOW
our v2 report LABEL's own 0.870 — his model tracks the reports less well than the reports track the radiologists.
The -0.064 is the board's size and the board's sign; the report ruler on the identical rows shows -0.018. So the
family's deficit is a RULER effect, not a labels effect and not a split-leak effect (an in-sample model reads

Correction carried from D47: the split transcription is `kneemri/evaluation/foreign_split.py` (md5 of the report

## D50/D52 — the board's ruler is a REBUILT COMMON FRAME, not the ledger's `offline` column, and not gold

Read 2026-09-07, researcher, CPU, read-only. Frame: 896 gold-removed fold-0 studies, L75mid, every member
rebuilt on the SAME frame rather than quoted from its own record. 36 board rows that are honest (the entry's
members did not train on the studies it is scored against) and rebuildable.

| predictor of the board score | R² | slope | resid SD |
|---|---|---|---|
| **rebuilt common-frame L75mid** | **0.962** | **+1.14** | **0.0016** |
| the ledger's own `offline` field | 0.802 | — | 0.0036 |
| gold-13 (the radiologist rows) | 0.475 | — | 0.0059 |

**The ledger's `offline` column is twice as noisy as a rebuild, and gold is not the board's ruler at all.**
The `offline` field is a MIXED frame — each member's number was taken on whatever holdout its own arm wrote,
under whatever variant of the macro was current — and re-scoring all 36 on one frame halves the residual. That
is the single largest improvement to the offline→board transfer this project has made, and it is free: no card,
no slot, no new member. **P1: `board_check` and the ledger should carry the rebuilt common-frame number as the
`offline` column, and the mixed-frame one should be retired.** Until they do, every transfer constant quoted
from this file is fitted on the 0.0036 ruler.

**The band is 0.904-0.937 and the champion is 0.944, which is OUTSIDE it.** Every prediction made for an entry
at the top of the board is an extrapolation by up to 0.007 above the fit's highest row, and it must be said out
loud wherever the slope is used. `kneemri-stack`'s pre-registration says it in its own docstring.

**D48's "+0.041 on ours5" is the POOL-WIDE offset, not a member effect.** Measured across the pool it reads
+0.030 ± 0.030 (n=256), so ours5's +0.041 is one draw from it. Spearman(gold-13, report-13) = **+0.63** against
a disjoint-13 null of +0.43 [0.18, 0.63] — the reordering IS the thirteen rows, and the thread D48 opened
(that L75mid ranks our members partly on report-derivable structure) does not survive its own falsification
test. What remains true and unexplained is the seven board flats; this is no longer a candidate explanation.

**The champion's five parents are mid-pool on the gold-vs-report axis** (+0.018…+0.057, percentiles 0.37-0.78),
so selecting members on the report ruler did NOT buy a report bias. That was the mechanism worth fearing and it
is measured absent.

**v3 ≡ v2 on every AUC ruler BY CONSTRUCTION.** The v3 recalibration is a per-column MONOTONE remap, and every
AUC-family metric is invariant to one. So pre-registration (2) of the recal family is undefined — not refuted,
undefined — and the family does not re-open on an AUC number. It could only ever move a threshold metric.

### The swap gate is now a module, and its guard had never been computed

`kneemri/evaluation/seat_swap.py` (245ed896) ports D43's gate: `swap_gain = proxy(child in place of parent) −
proxy(parents)`, GO iff `swap_gain ≥ +0.0010` AND the corr guard holds. The guard as D43 WROTE it — child
against the rank-mean of the FOUR REMAINING parents, versus the parent against those same four, `GUARD_SLACK =
0.01` — had never been coded, and computing it changes the published verdicts:

| swap | gain | child-vs-rest | parent-vs-rest | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `labelwise_dense` | +0.0013 | 0.909 | 0.911 | **GO** (the only one) |
| `clean_calib` | −0.0008 | 0.953 | 0.905 | NO-GO, and the guard refuses it independently |
| `recal_dense` | +0.0005 | 0.929 | 0.911 | NO-GO |
| `base_clean` | −0.0005 | — | — | NO-GO |

Acceptance, pre-registered with the researcher and reproduced exactly after the port: frame 896, champion proxy
0.9237, five alone 0.8993, parents mean pairwise corr 0.871, 1 of 4 pass. Two facts the port produced that the
prose gate could not: **`recal_holdannot`'s truth table differs from the frame's on 100% of cells**, so its
published +0.0008 is a RULER move and not a seat move and it must be struck from the five published readings;
and the rank-transform asymmetry that was suspected of carrying the readings is worth **0.0000**.

**A four-swap table read as a one-swap one.** The module's `--pair` flag first shipped as `nargs="+"` without an
accumulating action, so four `--pair` flags silently priced only the LAST one. Fixed with `action="extend"` and
recorded here rather than in the diff, because a gate whose whole purpose is to refuse three of four swaps had a
failure mode that reported one of them.

## The width axis saturates at nine seats, and diversity without lift is worth +0.0004 (D53 / D56 / D58, 2026-09-07)

Three researcher jobs land on one number from two directions. Kernel space throughout, frame 896
gold-removed fold-0, L75mid, `LogitAverage` block with `RaptorSeat` at 1/3.

**D53 — the seat curve is flat past nine.** Nine seats read **0.9260**, five read 0.9234. Over **189**
candidate tenth seats the best is `ramp_dense_gate` at **+0.0004 [-0.0000, +0.0009]**; 0.11 of the 189
are positive at all and **none** clears +0.0010. Greedy all the way to fifteen seats buys **+0.0014
cumulative** — on D50's slope that is +0.0016 board, which is exactly the transfer ruler's own residual
SD, and no individual step lands outside its own interval. Two independently constructed nines (the
shipped one at 0.9260, a greedy-from-five one at 0.9264) sit inside noise of each other, so **the ceiling
at nine is a property of the POOL, not of which nine**. Spearman(delta at 5, delta at 9) = **0.943** with
top-10 overlap 8/10: seat value is a MEMBER property, but the BLOCK sets the exchange rate — delta9 is
about **one third** of delta5 (delta5 range [-0.0018, +0.0011] vs delta9 [-0.0013, +0.0004]). D53 §4 adds
that no candidate moves MCL / LatOA / Fracture by >= +0.005 beside the nine (best: MCL
`merged_labelwise_cf` +0.0026, LatOA `finding_calib_dense_s2026` +0.0011, Fracture `margin_seat_s2026`
+0.0026) — the weak columns are weak in EVERY member, so a seat cannot buy them. §5: raptor's own fold-0
checkpoints as an extra ours-member are +0.0000 (`repl2x2_a_swa`) and -0.0000 (`effv2l_f0_swa`), and
splitting raptor's 1/3 into 1/6+1/6 costs **-0.0093 / -0.0104**.

**D56 — the best-case diversity member confirms it from the member side.** `foreign_labels_dense_s2026`
(his 12-finding labels, our dense recipe) is the ONLY member in the pool on the D45 decorrelation gate:
corr-to-nine **0.881** at solo **0.8862**. Shape verdict SPREAD — 0.39 of the 0.533 total corr drop sits
in Synovitis + MedMen + Baker's, under the 0.5 share that would call it an artefact, so the
decorrelation is real. It still prices at **+0.0004 [-0.0001, +0.0008]** beside the nine and +0.0005 as a
`calib_span` swap beside the five; both pre-registered GO rulers wanted +0.0010, so `warm_hislabels` was
never armed. Beside the FIVE the same member clears easily (+0.0012 swapping `lr4e-5_ws`, +0.0011 as a
sixth) — the 1/3 exchange rate again, not a contradiction. **Decorrelation without solo lift buys
+0.0004 at nine seats.** Any future arm whose pitch is "a more diverse member" is priced at ~0 before it
runs; the pitch has to be solo LIFT or a different axis.

**D58 — and the arrival table was read against the wrong control.** The +0.030 MedOA / +0.026 PFOA /
+0.019 Baker's column gains were measured against `through_dense`; the member's byte-identical twin is
`labelwise_dense_s2026` (arm header :21-23). Against the RIGHT twin the member is **-0.0105 macro**,
Synovitis **-0.074**, and only Baker's clears (+0.0081 [+0.0003, +0.0192]). A `mixed_labels_dense` arm
and a six-twin block retrain on column-mixed labels were ordered at 18:40Z on the wrong table and
**withdrawn at 18:50Z** before either was built — best case after the correction was +0.0005…+0.0009
board for 7.5 h of card. His labels retire as a TRAINING axis on our recipe; what remains of his lead is
his RECIPE, which is what `hisrecipe_distill` tests.

**Two harness facts from the same job, both verified in `core/data/labels/targets.py`** (the letter said
`kneemri/data/`; the module lives under `core/`):

1. `:439-443` — a labels table with **no `__conf` column** trains every cell at weight **1.0** (`raw =
   derived[confidence] … if confidence in derived.columns else ones`). His table has none, so the
   his-labels arm moved VALUES and WEIGHTS in one step and never isolated the labels it was testing.
2. `:332-343` — `Supervision.applied` remaps any cell `np.isclose` to one of our five levels
   (`applied[np.isclose(value, level)] = rate`). His LatOA has **1176 cells at exactly 0.08**, which the
   map rewrites to **0.041** — BELOW his own 0.05 negatives. That is an order inversion inside the one
   column the arm existed to move. The docstring's promise ("values the reader never emits pass through
   untouched") holds only while the foreign scale misses our levels; a collision is silent.

Any future foreign-label arm nudges colliding values off the levels and states what it did with `__conf`.
Guard bead filed (P2): `targets.py` should refuse or warn when a non-v2 table collides with a level.

**What this closes.** Width (a tenth seat), diversity-without-lift (a decorrelated member), and foreign
labels as a training target — three of the four open member axes, all on measurement rather than on
argument. What remains, ranked by weight x lift: block lift via better targets, an honest 1/3-class
object (`hisrecipe_distill`), column lift on MCL / LatOA (`lean_weak_columns`, running), and a ruler for
the two blind columns (`resnet50d_short`).

## D63-D68 — the per-column member weights, and where they stop

**The rule.** One `(members x findings)` mixture, each column its own convex combination of the seats,
served as `ColumnWeightedLogit` instead of `LogitAverage`. `kneemri/evaluation/column_weights.py` holds
the table, its shrinkage, its column-flattening and the frame every seat reading is taken over; the fit
itself was done outside the repo by the researcher.

**The port reproduces the fit.** `comp/colweights_v2_fit.csv` is `d63_W8.csv` converted to the repo's
name-keyed format, columns renormalised after rounding (they arrived at 0.9999-1.0002). Read through the
repo path against the eight members' own holdouts:

| shrink | uniform | weighted | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.00 | 0.9260 | 0.9316 | **+0.0055** |
| 0.75 | 0.9260 | 0.9305 | +0.0044 |

**+0.0055 at lambda=1 is D68's in-sample number to the digit**, which is what the equality check was for:
a port that landed a different number would not be a smaller effect, it would be a different computation.
`comp/colweights_v2.csv` is the shipped table at lambda=0.75 with ACL left FITTED — the r=0.30 that
motivated flattening ACL was the TEN-member fit; the eight-member fold-r is 0.75.

**The honest number is the OOF one: +0.0027 [+0.0012, +0.0040]**, 5 study-folds seed 0, 300 paired draws,
against nine-uniform 0.9260. In-sample +0.0055 is what it was shrunk from (2.0x). 84 fitted numbers
(12 columns x 7 free weights). Nested inner-CV chose 0.75 in 4 of 5 folds. Per-column OOF at lambda=1:
Effusion +0.0021, ACL -0.0017, MCL +0.0068, LatOA +0.0102, Fracture +0.0083.

**Denominator note.** An in-repo +0.0031 and the researcher's +0.0035 are the same reading against
different baselines — ten-uniform 0.9265 versus nine-uniform 0.9260. Every number above is quoted
against 0.9260.

### D68b — the rule cannot reach the champion, and the blocker is DARKNESS

The table's eight rows are `calib_span_s2026`, `grade_ladder_s2026`, `merged_blend_cf`,
`lr4e-5_ws_s2026`, `through_dense_s2026`, `labelwise_dense_s2026`, `warm_calib_dense_s2026`,
`warm_calib_lowlr_s2026` — all fold-0 members with real holdouts, which is what made a per-column fit
possible at all.

`comp/kernels/kneemri-stack/kneemri-stack.py:174-188` serves a different set: `final_ws_cf`,
`calib_span_ff`, `grade_ladder_cf`, `merged_blend_cf`, `lr4e-5_ws_cf`, `through_dense_cf`,
`labelwise_dense_ff`, `warm_calib_dense_s2026`, `warm_calib_lowlr_s2026`. `comp/members.roster` says the
`_ff`/`_cf` suffixes are **not a naming convention** — `calib_span_ff` is "calib_span_s2026's flags plus
`--fold -1 --ema`", `grade_ladder_cf` is "grade_ladder_ff's flags plus `--calibrated-targets`", and so on.
They are different trainings.

**Three of nine overlap.** `ColumnWeights.vote` joins by NAME and refuses the mismatch, which is correct:
renaming the rows to make it pass is exactly the positional-join failure the class exists to prevent.

To weight the CHAMPION you must refit on the champion's seats, and **six of its nine are `--fold -1`**:
they hold nothing out, so no per-column holdout matrix exists for them and none can be produced without
first training fold-0 twins of six dark members. The rule is not blocked by lambda, by ACL, or by the 84
fitted numbers. It is blocked because the thing it would weight cannot be measured.

**What shipping it anyway would cost.** The eight fold-0 members are a NEW package, not a champion
variant, and its uniform baseline exists offline (0.9260) but **nowhere on the board** — all 116 rows of
`comp/board.jsonl` were checked and hold no eight-member fold-0 uniform entry. So the pre-registration
"X+0.0031" has no X, and reading it honestly costs TWO slots (uniform, then weighted) to price ~+0.004
board on a stack that starts below the champion's 0.944. That is 40% of a day's slots spent on a package
we would not ship.

**Held, not killed.** `comp/colweights_v2.csv` and the passing equality check stay on the shelf. The
asset that would unlock them is fold-0 twins of the six dark seats (~6 x 1.4 h of card), which would also
give the champion's own seating its first honest offline number — it has never had one. That competes
directly with the six labels-v3 twins queued behind `recal_calib`, and the choice is the coordinator's.
