Synovitis +0.0118 (120 pos), Baker's -0.0126, ACL -0.0228 (249 pos). Nine of twelve shifts sit inside the
frame's own half-width, i.e. they are claims the frame never actually made.

**And the per-column PROFILE is not an asset** (researcher D84c, same day): the restricted-seat curve is
monotone in k on both frames and maximal at all twelve (896 +0.0055, 4406 +0.0151) — no subset beats the
plain seat — and the ranking of which columns pay has Spearman **0.056** between the two frames. The 896
says Fracture/MedMen/Synovitis, the 4406 says MCL/PFOA/Baker's. D16's column-restricted decline
(README:8862-8868) now stands on measurement rather than on a flat reading.

**What the surface cannot do:** only a model with five-fold out-of-fold predictions has an honest row here,
which is ours and his and nothing else. A one-fold member costs a five-fold run to put on it. The two
surfaces are out-of-fold under DIFFERENT splits, so a delta is a fair model-vs-model comparison per row and
not a matched-fold one. `column_headroom.py` stays REFUTED (knee-zsyp4) and is not the thing to extend.

### D85 addendum — what a change of frame alone does to a column ORDERING (the null ceiling)

`ColumnSurface.agreement` re-reads ONE surface twice — the full 4407 rows and the 909 subset the frame
holds — with the model, the truth table and the base all held fixed, so the only moving part is n. The
column ordering agrees at **rho +0.713** on `teacher_clean_full` and **rho +0.839** on
`teacher_foreign_corpus`.

That is the CEILING for any per-column ranking claim in this project: shrinking a frame from 4407 rows to
909 costs 0.16-0.29 of column order all by itself, with nothing else changed. It bears directly on
researcher's D84c cross-frame profile rho of **0.056** — mastermind flagged that as confounded (the two
frames also had different bases).

**RETRACTED the same day, by researcher's D85 split-half: the sentence this addendum originally closed on
— "n alone leaves 0.71-0.84, so n alone cannot explain a 0.056" — does not follow, and n explains most of
that 0.056.** Two reasons, both mine:

1. **Different object.** +0.713/+0.839 ranks twelve column AREAS, separated by tenths. D84c's 0.056 ranks
   twelve per-column seat DELTAS, separated by thousandths (+0.0006 … +0.0018). The limit paragraph below
   said the first is an upper bound on the second — and an upper bound of 0.71 licenses no statement at all
   about whether a 0.056 is explicable, which is exactly what the retracted sentence claimed.
2. **Nested, not disjoint.** The 909 rows are a SUBSET of the 4407, so the two readings share every row of
   the smaller one. Researcher's null splits the corpus into disjoint halves, which is the matched
   construction; a nested subset is optimistic by construction.

The number that governs is theirs: a per-column DELTA ranking split-half against itself reads **0.588** at
n=4406 and **0.237** at n=896 (interval touching zero). So the ceiling on any cross-frame agreement is
0.588, not 1.0, and D84c's 0.056 un-confounded rises to **0.189** — about a third of the achievable
agreement. `ColumnSurface.agreement` stays: it is the right null for an AREA ordering, which is what it
documents. It was quoted for a delta ordering, which is a denominator error of the usual shape.

Honest limit (kept, and it is what should have been read the first time): an ORDERING OF AREAS is more
stable than an ordering of small per-column DELTAS, because the areas are separated by tenths and the
deltas by thousandths. So +0.713/+0.839 is an upper bound on what a delta-profile could hope for, not a
matched control for one.

## D86 — the board's own blur, measured on tied pairs instead of fitted as a residual: **0.0020** — 2026-09-08

Zero card. `python -m kneemri.evaluation.board_transfer`, new `tied()` / `blur()`.

The question is what board delta our record can certify at all, and it arrived as a regression residual:
researcher's least-squares fit of board on offline over 41 `ensemble` rows read **sd 0.0076**, falling to
**0.0039** when one 2026-08-12 one-member row (`solo_v1`) was dropped and **0.0021** on the modern >=4-member
subset. One row carrying half a constant is the shape this project has been burned by three times, and
`board_transfer`'s own docstring already declines a line through these points: the pairs are unmatched, so
least squares reports its extremes.

The instrument answers it without a line and without deleting a row. `tied()` is the complement of
`pairs()` — every pair whose offline gap is under `DELTA_FLOOR`, i.e. the pairs the ruler called EQUAL. On
those, the offline axis is held still by construction, so the remaining board gap is the board:

| population | tied pairs | median abs board gap |
|---|---|---|
| all `ensemble` entries | 147 | **0.0020** |
| entries with >= 4 members | 132 | **0.0020** |

**0.0020, and the member floor does not move it.** That independently confirms researcher's 0.0021 by a
different estimator, and it dissolves the question mastermind asked next: whether `solo_v1` should be
`scope: excluded`. It should NOT, and it stays. Its distance from a fitted line is a property of the LINE —
the estimator this record supports is a median over pairs, which one row cannot drag, and which reads the
same number with the solos in as with them out. A row is excluded for being DISHONEST (`raptor_solo`'s
98.6% in-sample offline), never for being far from a fit.

**Consequence, and it is the operative one:** a board delta under **0.0020** is a move this record cannot
certify. Mastermind's withdrawn "ignore anything under 0.008" would have re-opened axes closed on real
0.006-0.008 falls; the cut is 0.002, and the 0.002-0.004 band is a direction. The champion's 0.944 -> the
owner's 0.955 is +0.011 board, roughly +0.008 offline kernel at the pairwise compression this file's own
`--near` cell prints — five times the blur, which is why the target is a MEMBER question and not a seating
one.

## D89 — the contamination question was answered twice before it was asked, and its consequence is DIRECTIONAL: the corrupted axis is weight-on-the-foreign-seat, and it is biased against removing it — 2026-09-08

Zero card, zero new compute. This is a ledger read, which is what it should have been the first time.

**The P0 as posed — "run `foreign_overlap` on `raptor_v4_swa` against our 909" — needs no run.** The record
already holds the answer in two places, one specific and one general:

- `README:6629`: *"`foreign_overlap` reads raptor at 98.6% in-sample on this corpus."* 896 of our 909
  holdout studies sit in their published label table; the 13 absent are exactly the gold studies falling in
  fold 0.
- `README:8822`, stated as a rule after the `repl2x2_c` band was withdrawn: *"any reading of a released
  foreign checkpoint on our 909/896 is **in-sample by construction**, and no `foreign_overlap` call is
  needed to establish it"* — his training script defaults to `--folds 0` with the fold hook firing only
  above zero, and the block his released arms were trained by passes no `--folds` at all.

So **`raptor_v4_swa`'s 0.9432 solo is in-sample**, and so is the 0.9260 nine-seat kernel that carries it at
1/3. `foreign_overlap`'s own docstring closes it: on the two rulers where both models are honest — the gold
58 and the board — the families **tie**.

**What this does to D87.** My midpoint reading ran on all 4407 corpus rows, of which 4349 are in their
table: **98.7%**. So **+0.0507 is an upper bound on the foreign family's real lead over our teacher, not an
estimate of it** — the same defect that voided `raptor_solo`'s 0.8938, arriving one ruler later.

**What it does NOT do to the two-column exception, and this is the point.** Contamination biases the
foreign predictor **upward**. An inequality that survives a bias pointing the wrong way is stronger than
one measured clean, not weaker. Our teacher beats it on Effusion (+0.0141 [+0.0059, +0.0225]) and Synovitis
(+0.0227 [+0.0105, +0.0358]) **while it is memorising the rows**. And the record already carries an
independent replication of exactly that pair: `README:8825-8835`, A′ minus `raptor_coat384`, a **different
checkpoint** on a **different ruler**, twelve columns of which only three are positive — **Effusion
+0.0079, Synovitis +0.0096**, Baker's +0.0030. Two readings, two members of the family, two rulers, the same
two columns. That is a property of the family, not a draw from noise.

**The operative consequence — the corruption has a direction, and it is not uniform.**

- Comparisons that **hold the foreign seat fixed** carry the inflation as a roughly constant offset. They
  stay ordinally usable, and that is most of the record, including D88's frontier table.
- Comparisons that **change the foreign seat's weight** are measured on a corrupted axis, and the sign is
  knowable in advance: **down-weighting or removing a member that memorised the holdout looks worse offline
  than it is.** Researcher's own d34_seat readings are all of this shape — replacing it costs −0.0227,
  halving the foreign block costs −0.0100 — and every one of those penalties is an over-estimate.
- Therefore **Job 35 is biased against its own hypothesis before it runs.** A negative from it is
  uninformative; a positive would be strong. Pre-registered here rather than after the number lands.

**And the honest comparator for the family already has a name in this file:** cell C (`README:8823`) — same
fold file, same epoch budget, same ruler, both out of sample. `hisrecipe_distill` is that shape: his trunk
and his labels with **fold 0 held out by us**, so its OOF-896 solo is honest by construction. Its teacher is
`teacher_clean_full.npz` (`arms/hisrecipe_distill.sh:63`) — **ours, 0.8777, not raptor** — so it inherits
none of this on its own offline number.

### `weakdraw.sh` — KILLED, and not for being wrong about Fracture — 2026-09-08

Held for a gate, then killed for two independent reasons, neither of which is its hypothesis.

1. **Its gate is not constructible.** It was held pending a re-derivation of per-column decorrelation and
   headroom for candidate seats on the 4,406 surface. Researcher measured all 307 `*.holdout.npz` under
   `$MODELS`: **275 are 909 rows (fold 0)**, four are 896, the rest are stubs or partials, and **exactly one
   member file covers the corpus** (`foreign_oof_corpus.holdout.npz`). Candidate-seat per-column statistics
   cannot be computed on that surface at all. Holding an arm for a gate nobody can satisfy holds it forever.
2. **Its axis has no plausible size.** D88: across 30 classifiable steps the offline frontier has never moved
   by +0.004 on any ensembling axis, seating reads −0.0029, and the frontier has been flat for eleven days.
   The arm needed 2.7 h of card for an operation whose best-ever realized instance is smaller than the
   board's own 0.0020 blur.

**What is NOT concluded:** nothing about whether Fracture is under-weighted. That question is untouched; it
was never measured, and this arm's death is about a missing ruler and a missing size, not about its subject.
If a corpus-wide candidate-seat surface ever exists, the question is re-opened by rebuilding the gate, not by
re-quoting this decline.

#### AMENDMENT, same day, 01:30Z — the kill stands as a QUEUEING decision and the running arm was NOT stopped

The entry above was written while `weakdraw_frx_s2026` was **live on the card**, and mastermind's D139 §1
read that correctly as a defect and defaulted to killing the process. The default is overturned here on one
line of evidence, and the evidence is the marginal price rather than a preference:

- `weakdraw_flat_s2026` had **already completed all twelve epochs** (holdout + checkpoint on disk, 00:36Z).
  It is the α=0.0 control; `frx` is the α=1.0 arm. The reading is the PAIR, so killing `frx` does not
  recover `flat`'s hour — it spends it.
- `frx` stood at **epoch 7 of 12, 50 min elapsed, ~24 min remaining** (366 s/epoch, `started` 1788827841).
  The decline priced this arm at **2.7 h of card not yet spent**. That price was real when it was written
  and is not the price of the decision in front of anyone now: the choice is 24 minutes against destroying
  a completed pair.
- Under `one_cycle` the last epochs ARE the anneal, so a kill at e7 does not yield a cheap negative — it
  yields a **FLOOR**, which `convergence_check` will then refuse to let anyone quote. Paying 50 minutes to
  buy an unquotable number is the one outcome worse than either state.

So: the arm ran to completion, its holdout is a real record, and **the decline stands for what it was about
— `weakdraw.sh` does not get queued again** on the two reasons above. Nothing here re-opens the Fracture
question or the axis.

**The check this cost, filed as knee-jc5z3:** *an arm's script must not be recorded as KILLED or declined
while that arm is live.* `arm_check` can read this file's heading for the script it is about to arm, and
`queue_check` can read it for the scripts already running. Both directions are the same defect: the ledger
and the process table disagreeing with nobody noticing.

## Card gate for an arm — the two rows, and they are priced differently — 2026-09-08

Mastermind D137 §1(d), **amended by D139 §2 and re-derived by D140 §3**. An arm is one of two shapes and the
bar is not the same one. Getting the shape wrong is not conservative: applied literally to a FLEET-WIDE arm,
the seat row would have refused `deep32_batch6` (a `band_dense`-family member lands near 0.864 solo), which
would have been a serious error.

**SEAT arm** — the product is one more candidate member.

- Bar: expected solo **≥ ~0.89** on the 896 / `L75mid` frame. 110 of 182 members are below it.
- Derivation, and quote THIS one: the seat-value-vs-solo slope is **not linear across the pool**. D140 §1
  refits it on nested bands and the CIs are disjoint — honest12 full-range [+0.0044,+0.0165] against
  `>= 0.860` [+0.0419,+0.0559], and the slope rises monotonically with the band floor in all three rosters.
  On the `>= 0.88` band (n=73–77, tight CI) the +0.0015 seat bar lands at a SOLO score of **0.889 against
  the honest12 roster / offline solo 0.892 against twin5 / offline solo 0.894 against twin6**, and the
  board-blur bar at 0.897 /
  0.894 / 0.898. Those six are candidate SOLO bars on the 896 / `L75mid` frame — they are not board
  numbers and none of them is a score of the honest12 entry, which scored 0.937.
- **Do NOT re-derive it from D133 §2.** That fit ran across solo 0.4597–0.8959, where 70 of 182 candidates
  below 0.87 flatten it, and it produces **0.9662** — a threshold outside the measured range, in the same
  letter that measured 18 of 182 candidates clearing +0.0015 with max solo 0.8959. D133 §2 is WITHDRAWN.
- 0.885 (D137's figure) is below all six local bars. It is defensible and is not being moved; it is written
  here as **~0.89 from the `>= 0.88` band fit** so the next re-derivation does not land on 0.9662 and
  conclude the gate is far too soft.

**SEAT arm, CORRECTED — the gate is D35, two variables, and the ~0.89 line above is D35 with the
correlation term deleted — 2026-09-08 (C149 §3, on D146 §3).**

```
honest seat = -0.0046 + 0.313*(solo - 0.8865) + 0.0557*(1 - corr)
```

- Origin `experiments/repl2x2_c.prereg.md:38-41`, pre-registered in D36 **before the members it is now
  validated on existed**. Out-of-sample validation: D146 §3 applies it unchanged to all nine Commission C
  survivors, across the trunk gap, **max error +0.0004**.
- `corr` is nearest-neighbour correlation to the pool. Every unit of `1 - corr` is worth **0.0557** — the
  term the solo bar drops, and the reason no solo-monotone threshold can represent the pool: `repl2x2_a`
  has the **lowest** solo of the nine and pays the **most**.
- **The ~0.89 solo bar is a band-local special case, valid only near nn-corr ~0.92** — our own trunk family
  and nothing else. Do not extrapolate it below corr 0.81 or above solo 0.90; nine points. D140 was never a
  bar missing a domain clause; it was this model with a term deleted, and the deletion is why the best
  candidate in the set was refused.

**Provenance — four terms, and the FIRST is decisive on its own (D148 §3, correcting C146 §2).**

1. **Did a LOCAL ARM TRAIN THE WEIGHTS.** `repl2x2` has `after_cellc.sh` plus a `[cv] fold 0/1` log line;
   the void members have a decode arm that states it serves someone else's released program unchanged.
2. mtime — the void stops cleanly at 2026-08-28.
3. row count **896, not 909**.
4. a committed prereg.

`epoch=-1` and `source=foreign` are **NOT** discriminators: `raptor_ft_repl2x2_a.holdout.npz` carries both
and is ours. Both are writer tags. Row-set identity cannot separate either, since honest `calib_span_s2026`
carries the identical 909 study set.

**FLEET-WIDE arm** — the product is a mechanism every seat carries.

- Bar: **`d` ≥ +0.008 per member**, `d` measured **solo-versus-its-own-control**, ONE arm.
- **Exempt from the ~0.89 line entirely.** The member the arm produces is an instrument for `d`, not a seat.
- The `×0.65` fleet damper is applied **afterwards, to the pool move**, and never to `d` (D93). A fleet-wide
  mechanism therefore costs **1.4 h to price, not 11** — eight retrains buy the gain, never the measurement.
- Untouched by D140: `d` never passes through a seat slope.

## D93 — `d` is a PRE-POOL number, so the fleet-wide candidate list was already measured, and priced against the +0.011 bar it has exactly one live row — 2026-09-08

Job 37, asked by mastermind after D91/D92 established that a single-member change enters the kernel at
`1/(k+1)` (0.13 at k=8, measured on 248 real members) while a fleet-wide change enters at ~0.65 of `d`,
making the fleet multiplier **≈5×, not 9×**, and converting the +0.007 pool bar into a **per-member
`d` ≈ +0.008 to +0.011**.

### The methodological point, which is the actual finding

**`d` is measured solo-versus-its-own-control. It is fixed before any pool exists. The `1/k` damper acts on
the POOL MOVE and never on `d`.**

Two consequences, and the second reverses a plan:

1. A fleet-wide mechanism costs **1.4 h to price, not 11** — one arm, read as `d`, multiplied by 0.65 only
   afterwards. Eight retrains buy the *gain*, never the *measurement*.
2. This project has been doing exactly that all along. `extended_slots`, `resolution`, `intensity_augment`
   and the `rate_*` family are each a fleet-shaped mechanism run once for its `d`. **Their `d` column was
   never divided by anything.** What was divided by `1/k` was their SEAT VALUE — a different column — and
   the two were being read as one number.

So D91's *"we simply stopped paying the entry fee"* and D92's *"every idea was tested as a single member and
silently divided by nine"* are half wrong, and it is the load-bearing half. The cheap fleet-wide probes were
run, at the correct price, and they came back **+0.0002, +0.0002, −0.0064**. The eleven flat days are not
only a denominator artefact.

### Row 8 — the epoch axis, closed tonight at zero card

`python -m kneemri.experiments.convergence_check`: **254 runs — 195 converged, 14 truncated, 3 stopped, 14

`slots.py:79-95` documents `EXTENDED_SLOTS` — the canonical six plus `COR_FLUID_NOFS`, `AX_T1`,

slot, 2,335 of them in those three, 83,297 slices the model never sees.** That is a genuine and well-argued
fleet-wide input change, and the arm was written: `experiments/arms/extended_slots.sh`. It scored **0.8459,

Recorded because the mechanism is sound and will be proposed again: **what is refuted is this execution at
`d` = +0.0002, not the physics of showing the model more coronal series.** What it does refute is spending
11 h to apply that execution eight times. The re-opening move is a different execution, never a re-quote of
the slice count.

Left open, and worth settling: `slots.py:87` says **9.9%** of series unrouted; `oof_oracle.py:176`,
`README:1054` and `interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-11_what-actually-moved-the-number.md:920` all say
**17.4%**. Two numbers for one quantity, 1.8× apart, in four places.

### What this predicts about tonight's number

Row 9 changes trunk **and** resolution at once, and row 5 prices the resolution half at +0.0002 fleet-wide,
measured twice. So if `hisrecipe_distill`'s OOF-896 lands materially above our band, **the credit belongs to
the architecture and not to 384 px**, and the fleet retrain is his trunk at OUR resolution — cheaper than
1.7 h/seat, not dearer. If it lands inside our band, row 9 closes and the fleet-wide list is empty. That is
a reportable state of the world, not a gap to fill with the next idea.

- Rows 4–8's `d` are each ONE arm against ONE control. A mechanism can be mis-executed once.

```
corr coefficient   bounded above by ~ +0.006, consistent with ZERO   (D35: +0.0557.  D157 refit: -0.0030)
solo coefficient ~ +0.0385                                           (D35: +0.313)
```

**Corrected 2026-09-08 (M167 / C169 / D158).** This block first read `corr ~ +0.0055`, `solo ~ +0.025`,

MIDPOINT = 0.5`, while every regression here is `ledger75` — so the solo was withdrawn in favour of 0.8173.

different quantities and may not be substituted. The lever arm shrank from 0.253 to 0.175 and the residual
it was derived from vanished, which is why the corr term now reads as consistent with zero rather than

Consequences, unchanged in direction: **decorrelation alone cannot buy the gap at any reachable (1 − corr)**;
and a member at solo 0.920 with ordinary correlation prices at **+0.0028 offline ≈ +0.0032 board** at the

**What is NOT closed by this.** Every one of those instruments prices the MARGINAL operation — add or swap
ONE member into a fixed pool. **Nothing in this repo prices making all twelve better**, which is a
pool-wide shift with no term in any model held here. The pool being saturated as an averaging device is
consistent with everything: it is why the ensemble reaches 0.944 from a best solo of 0.8964, and why the
thirteenth member buys nothing. Saturation is not failure — it means the averaging lever has been fully
collected, and the next number to measure is the exchange rate `d(ensemble)/d(mean solo)` at fixed k.

Two rules this row now carries, both earned by getting them wrong first: **a seat value states ADD or SWAP

Mechanism, and it is why "decorrelated" is the wrong word for this member: swapping the trunk to OURS left

much weaker, so the 2×2's corpus-versus-trunk decomposition is still not separated — cell D moved trunk and

pull it INTO the pool (0.87–0.92) is refuted on the pool's own ruler.
Supporting that: neither SWA nor the epoch-ensemble pays anything, which is what a flat noisy basin looks
like. **Distance bought by weakness is not distance that pays.**

## The SEE axis, opened 2026-09-08 (D181-D184, zero card, zero slot)

D180 closed the marginal-member lane on the (solo, nnCorr) surface: 242 priced members, 0 clearing
+0.0015, every recipe knob inside its own permutation null, geometry worth 0.008 of the 0.09 needed. The
question that survived it was whether any lever changes what the trunk SEES rather than what it does with
what it sees. This section is the inventory of that axis and the one arm it produced.

### The inventory (D181)

`CacheFlags.add_to` is called by the trainer (`kneemri/training/flag_vocabulary.py:104`), so every cache
flag is settable on `train` today. Over 290 committed arm scripts with comment lines stripped:

```
  flag                settable  default   distinct non-default values used
  --slices               yes    12        4   (20 x171, 36 x3, 32 x1, 16 x1)
  --image-size           yes    336       3   (224 x57, 448 x2, 420 x1)
  --crop-mm              yes    130.0     3   (80 x3, 160 x1, 140 x1)
  --centre               yes    image     1   (tissue x7)
  --band-low/--band-high yes    0.20/0.80 3   (0.1/0.9 x180, 0.05/0.95 x3, 0.0/1.0 x1)
  --spacing              yes    spread    1   (adjacent x1)
  --scheme               yes    canonical 5   (merged x10, merged3 x3, multiscale x1, mrnet x1, extended x1)
  --tie                  yes    first     0   <- the only settable-and-never-set flag
```

**`--tie` is the only literally-never-set flag, and it is not the lever.** `TIES = ("first","last")`
(`slots.py:107`); it decides which acquisition fills a slot when several tie for maximal slice density.
Three facts, the third decisive: a smoke index `index_336px_12sl_last_first60.json` exists from 2026-08-18
and was abandoned; the rule has a measured correlate (`slots.py:362-364`, residual against the published
members correlates **+0.664** with contested-slot count, +0.496 controlling for series count); and its own
docstring, `slots.py:100-106` verbatim, says *"For TESTING against the published members' recorded
predictions, not for switching on."* It changes the input only for studies with a contested slot, and that
fraction is not on disk in any artefact. A change of DEGREE over an unmeasured denominator — refused as an
arm, recorded here so nobody surfaces it as new.

**A single-plane member is NOT buildable today, and the blocker is the name space, not the machinery.**
`RIJEKA_SLOTS = (SLOTS[0],)` (sagittal-only, `slots.py:166`) and `FASTMRI_SLOTS = (SLOTS[1],
COR_FLUID_NOFS)` (coronal-only, `:214`) both exist and `SCHEMES` (`:289`) is an open registry — but every
corpus decodes into the same directory, and those two names mean FOREIGN corpora. Measured:
`index_336px_20sl_0.1-0.9band_rijeka.json` 736 studies, overlap with our 4,407 index **0**;
`index_336px_12sl_mrnet.json` 1,250, overlap **0**. `train --scheme rijeka` on our corpus reads
identifiers FROM THE CACHE (`train.py:52`, into `Targets.pair` at `:66`), so it would train on 736 Rijeka
studies or die in the label join; with the cache absent it would BUILD, writing our corpus over theirs.
The fix is ~3 lines (a new scheme name plus a `SCHEMES` entry), not an arm.

**Twelve cache keys have mask+index and no images** — completed builds whose pixels were reclaimed
(`study_cache.py:383` unlinks progress once the mask is written), so `StudyCache.decoded()` refuses them
and each needs a full re-decode: `224px_12sl_adjacent`, `224px_36sl_0.05-0.95band`, `336px_12sl_0-1band`,
`336px_12sl_80mm_tissue`, `336px_12sl_80mm_tissue_0.1-0.9band`, `336px_12sl_extended`,
`336px_12sl_merged3`, `336px_16sl_0.1-0.9band`, `336px_20sl_0.1-0.9band_merged`,
`336px_20sl_140mm_0.1-0.9band`, `336px_20sl_merged`, `448px_12sl`. **"The flag was set once" and "the
cache is loadable" are different questions and the arm scripts answer only the first.** And one build is
stopped in flight: `progress_336px_20sl_0.1-0.9band_adjacent.npz`, mtime 2026-09-05 18:26, done **2,200 of
4,407**, with no images file — so `_resumed`'s precondition (`study_cache.py:404`) fails and it restarts
from zero. The adjacent axis was already being built at the working geometry three days ago.

### `--scheme extended` is strictly additive, and it gains a slot on 34.2% of studies (D182)

Read off `mask_336px_12sl_extended.npy` (4407x9) against `mask_336px_12sl.npy` (4407x6), both on disk, no
decode:

```
  canonical six, extended mask vs canonical mask     IDENTICAL, 0 cells differ
  extra slots filled  COR_FLUID_NOFS / AX_T1 / AX_FLUID_NOFS   841 / 564 / 566  of 4,407
  studies gaining >= 1 extra slot                    1,508 = 34.2%
    gaining exactly 1 / 2 / 3                        1,052 / 449 / 7
  mean filled slots per study                        4.568 -> 5.015  (+0.447, +9.8%)
  studies with zero canonical slots that gain one    0
```

**Denominator: the whole 4,407-study corpus, not a fold and not a holdout.** `slots.py:79-93`'s own 9.9%
is a rate over SERIES (2,421 of 24,371) and is the wrong denominator for sizing an arm; the per-study rate
is three and a half times larger. Behind it: **83,297 slices of imaging no member has ever seen**, none of
them localisers — coronal PD without fat suppression is a standard meniscus sequence and axial T1 reads
patellar cartilage.

**The identity matters more than the 34%.** `EXTENDED_SLOTS` appends and never inserts, and the mask
confirms the routing agrees cell for cell, so an extended member is not a re-decode under different rules
— it is **every current member's input plus three channels**. Nothing is taken away, so a flat read cannot
be blamed on having disturbed the six.

**The head takes nine slots.** `n_slot` is a constructor argument threaded `model.py:182/204/226/239` ->
`slot_head.py:54` and `:62` (`slot_emb = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(n_slot, hidden) * 0.02)`), sourced from
the cache. Two hardcoded-six sites remain: `ortho_diffusion.py:163` iterates `SLOTS` directly, so the
ortho family cannot be fed by this cache; and `SlotAffinity.requested` (`anatomy.py:230-248`) **raises**
when the head's slot count is not six, so **`--anatomical-prior` cannot be passed to an extended arm**.
That one closes rather than blocks: `aprior_dense` is `band_dense` plus that flag and reads **0.8557,
−0.0021**.

### The shipped CSV is NOT the routing (D183) — and D181's computability claim is withdrawn

The `Fluid_Sensitive` / `Fat_Suppression` columns cannot reproduce the slot assignment. The CSV says
`SAG_FLUID_NOFS` is fillable on **0** studies where the decoded mask has it filled on **2,760**; `SAG_T1`
4,266 vs 1,871, a factor of 2.3. `StudyCache.planes_of` (`study_cache.py:490`) reads exactly one column,
`Anatomical_Plane`, and `Slot.accepts` compares `Acquisition` properties recovered from a DICOM header
probe (`acquisition.py:277-279`, `:287`). **The 40.1%-contested figure derived from the CSV is void.**

Per-slot occupancy over 4,407, which is the fact that survives:

```
  SAG_FLUID_FS 4,119 (93.5%)   COR_FLUID_FS 4,210 (95.5%)   AX_FLUID_FS 4,343 (98.5%)
  SAG_FLUID_NOFS 2,760 (62.6%) COR_T1 2,827 (64.1%)         SAG_T1 1,871 (42.5%)
  COR_FLUID_NOFS 841 (19.1%)   AX_T1 564 (12.8%)            AX_FLUID_NOFS 566 (12.8%)
```

**The canonical six are already 24% empty on average.** The extended scheme is not adding a fourth plane
to a full table; it is filling a table that was never full.

### What the three extras carry, who gains them, and the confound (D184)

**The 12x9 affinity table**, computed by calling `FindingAnatomy.affinity` for every `ANATOMY` row against
every `EXTENDED_SLOTS` slot. The extras score **1.00 (primary plane, matched sequence) on seven cells
across seven findings**: MCL and both menisci via `COR_FLUID_NOFS`, PF OA via `AX_T1`, Effusion /
Synovitis / Baker's via `AX_FLUID_NOFS`. **PF OA has NO 1.00 cell among the canonical six** — its primary
plane is axial with `needs_fluid` false, and the only canonical axial slot (`AX_FLUID_FS`) mismatches on
sequence at 0.50. `AX_T1` is the single slot in the nine that reads patellofemoral OA properly. The extras
LOSE for ACL, both OA columns, Contusion and Fracture — all three extras are non-fat-suppressed and marrow
oedema is invisible without fat suppression.

**The gainers are the corpus's SICKER third.** Population 4,406 with a `report_labels_v2.csv` row, cut
midpoint, Fisher exact two-sided, gainers vs non-gainers: **Lateral OA 1.90x**, ACL 1.53x, MCL 1.44x,
Medial OA 1.44x, PF OA 1.32x (all p<1e-4), Contusion 1.22x, Lateral Meniscus 1.19x, Medial Meniscus 1.09x,
Effusion 1.06x; flat: Synovitis 1.01 (p .888), Baker's 0.92 (.144), Fracture 0.85 (.174). Ordering and
signs survive on the 909-study holdout frame (319 gainers / 590 non). **They are not the rare-positive
third**: Fracture has ~20 positives on the 909 gainer frame, below `column_surface.py:8`'s ±0.067
half-width, so no per-column Fracture or Synovitis claim off an extended arm is readable.

**THE CONFOUND, stated before any delta exists.** Protocol extension is indication-driven. `AX_T1` arrives
where PF OA is **LESS** common (0.399 vs 0.460, p 0.008) — opposite in sign to the affinity mechanism —
and `AX_T1` studies carry 1.54x the Synovitis rate and 0.42x the Baker's rate. Under the canonical scheme
a study with `AX_T1` is indistinguishable from one without; under extended, **the presence bit itself is an
input**. So a positive delta is attributable to three channels of PIXELS *or* to three bits of PROTOCOL
METADATA correlating with pathology. Separator, no training: re-score with the three extra channels zeroed
and the mask left intact. Upper bound requested card-free in M189: fit the three presence bits alone
against the twelve columns on the 909 frame and read the macro.

### The arm, and why its control is the one it is

`experiments/arms/extended_band.sh` = `band_dense`'s invocation verbatim plus `--scheme extended`. **Of the
79 members at 336/20/0.1-0.9band on the default trunk, `band_dense` is the ONLY one whose `run_train` line
is recipe + geometry + `--labels` and nothing else** — no distillation, calibrated targets, EMA, held
annotations, encoder weights, slot dropout or batch override. Its ledger row is **0.8578** at the midpoint
on the 909 frame, recomputed off `band_dense_s2026.holdout.npz` and matching this file's earlier row.
Nearest alternatives rejected: `band_dense_long` 0.8587 (24 epochs, and `aug_long` reads peak-to-finish
−0.0182 at that budget) and `attend_dense` 0.8569 (its gate sat outside every optimiser group and ran as a
fixed mean). The arm is built on this rather than on `labelwise_dense` (0.8959 @ledger75, the pool's best
solo) because that member differs from the control by three flags; the labelwise extension is the
follow-up that produces a shippable member, and only if the axis reads.

Cache: `images_336px_20sl_0.1-0.9band_extended.npy`, (4407, 9, 20, 336, 336) uint8 = **89.6 GB**, built
2026-09-08 06:39Z. Pre-registered: **>= +0.0015 add into honest12 @ledger75 -> the SEE axis is live** (the
plane scheme and mm-FOV multiscale follow); **+0.0000 to +0.0015 -> real input, inert evidence, stop paying
decode-scale costs**; **negative -> nine slots dilute slot attention faster than three channels inform it,
which is a fact about the HEAD and makes `--slot-pooling attend` the follow-up.**

### The confound is real, redundant, and therefore not a threat to the arm (D185)

Statistic / population / cut, once: per-column ROC-AUC and its unweighted 12-column macro, population
**holdout909** (the `studies` array of `band_dense_s2026.holdout.npz` — the frame the arm is read on), cut
**midpoint**. Bits read off `mask_336px_12sl_extended.npy` columns 6:8.

**The three presence bits fitted ALONE against the twelve columns are above chance**: cross-fit macro
**0.5431**, in-sample ceiling 0.5895 (three binary features admit 8 patterns, so the ceiling is what a
learner with the labels in hand gets and nothing generalises there — quote 0.5431). `COR_FLUID_NOFS`
carries almost all of it (ACL 0.593, Lateral OA 0.576, PF OA 0.568). `AX_T1` alone is at or **below** chance
nearly everywhere and its two most negative columns are **Baker's 0.446 and PF OA 0.472** — the indication
effect pointing opposite to the affinity table, on the arm's own frame, on the one slot the affinity table
called PF OA's only proper read. Bit prevalence on the 909: 170 / 112 / 124.

**On top of the member the same bits are worth −0.0021.** Per-column logistic on `[logit(band_dense
prediction), bit0, bit1, bit2]`, 5-fold cross-fit, same rows, same cut: macro **0.8578 -> 0.8557**. The
member column reproduces the ledger's `band_dense` figure to four decimals on a path that never read the
ledger, which is the harness check that validates D184 §4's control under two independent computations.
Per-column deltas run −0.0181 (Fracture, 68 positives, noise) to +0.0065 (Baker's); dropping Fracture the
other eleven still average about −0.0006.

**So the metadata channel is non-empty and ALREADY SPENT** — the pathology those bits mark is pathology the
canonical six already show. A positive extended delta cannot be charged to three bits of protocol. The
zeroed re-score is therefore NOT mandatory; it stays a follow-up conditional on a positive read, because
−0.0021 bounds the POST-HOC channel only and a trunk trained on those channels can exploit bit-by-image
interactions a four-parameter logistic cannot represent.

**And slot routing is independent of slice depth — measured, not argued** (read off the live decode's
`progress_336px_20sl_0.1-0.9band_extended.npz`, which carries a `(4407, 9)` mask and a `(4407,)` done, at
3,600 of 4,407): canonical six 20sl-extended vs 20sl-canonical **0 cells differ**; extras 20sl vs 12sl **0
studies disagree**; per-extra filled 699 / 467 / 443 identical; gainers 34.3% against 12sl's 34.3% on the
same rows; index order identical to both the canonical 20sl and the 12sl index. D182 called this an
argument; on 3,600 studies it is a measurement.

## 2026-09-08 — the dense corner is an OFFSET, not an interaction: a flat knob does not get a re-run (D190)

**A knob that reads flat at the default geometry does not get a dense-corner re-run.** Measured over the
eleven knob axes that have a member at BOTH geometries, the dense corner is a **+0.0031 median offset**
with ordering preserved (**Spearman 0.64, Pearson 0.73**), the largest swing any axis has ever shown
between the corners is **0.0063**, and **no axis has ever crossed from a real negative to a real
positive**. Controls read fresh at each corner: `base224_s2026` 0.8509, `base_dense_s2026` 0.8512.

Five of the eleven flip SIGN, which is not a reversal: every flipping axis has a default-side delta of
|d| ≤ 0.0028, against a 0.005 noise floor, and the largest a flip ever reaches at the dense corner is
+0.0057. A sign flip on a number that has no sign is a coin landing the other way. The axes that are
CLEARLY negative at default stay negative and mostly get worse — label errors −0.0046 → −0.0092, ortho
−0.0091 → −0.0060. The dense corner is not a different regime in which different things work; it is the
same regime with a small constant added.

**SCOPE LIMIT, AND IT IS REAL: this covers KNOBS, not trunk swaps.** The two encoder axes with a member
at both corners move four to six times anything a knob shows, in both directions — convnext
(`cnx_own_recipe_s2026` / `cnx_dense_s2026`) **−0.0262**, dinov3-base (`dinov3_base_lora_s2026` /
`v3base_dense_s2026`) **+0.0184**. Neither crosses zero, so the rule's answer is unchanged, but a trunk
that gains +0.0184 from the corner is not described by "a +0.0031 offset". **A KNOB that read flat at
default geometry does not need a dense-corner re-run. An ENCODER might.**

**WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY.** n=11, single seed throughout, twins hand-paired by name. The claim is a
NEGATIVE one ("no reversal observed"), which is the kind a small n can carry; it would not support a
positive claim about the offset's size, and +0.0031 should not be quoted as a quantity.
`labelwise_dense_s2026` has no default twin on disk and is absent from the table.

**CONSEQUENCE:** it frees no slot, but it closes a class of proposal that had been generating them —
every dense-corner re-run of a flat knob was buying a ±0.006 look at a 0.015 question.

## 2026-09-08 — `--corpus-oversample` was unrunnable, and the merged3 cache is a 90-second CONCATENATION

`merged3_oversample` is the first arm in 292 to set `--corpus-oversample` (D189 §6, word-boundary
census). It took three launches to get onto the card, and each failure was a different thing that had
never been exercised because no arm had ever asked. All three are now fixed; the arm is training.

**1. The cache had been reclaimed, and rebuilding it is cheap.** `images_336px_12sl_merged3.npy`
(51.97 GB) was absent — the control `merged3_corpus` ran on it 2026-09-01 and it was deleted since.
`arm_check` said `UNCACHED 336px_12sl_merged3` and I dismissed the warning in the prior window on the
control's `"recompute_activations": "True"`, which is a memory-for-compute trade INSIDE the backward
pass and says nothing about the image array. The arm died in 19 s and the card sat idle 08:21–08:36Z.
**Read `arm_check`'s UNCACHED line as blocking; it has no false-positive mode.** The rebuild is
`build_merged --scheme merged --extra-scheme mrnet --merged-scheme merged3 --slices 12 --image-size 336`
and it is a CONCATENATION of two caches already on disk (merged 5143 studies + mrnet 1250 = 6393), not a
decode: **90 seconds**, disk-bound. A merged3-geometry cache is therefore never a reason to defer an arm.

**2. THE TRAP IN THAT COMMAND, which cost a label table.** `--extra-labels` defaults to `rijeka_acl.csv`
and is NOT slaved to `--extra-scheme`. With `--extra-scheme mrnet` the array is merged correctly and the
LABEL table is not: it wrote `merged3_labels.csv` at **5142 rows against the correct 6390**, silently,
over the control's own training table. Nothing downstream could have noticed — every value in it still
looks like a label. Restored exactly, because `merged3_labels_tagged_raw.csv` IS that table plus the
`corpus` column: dropping the column reproduces it at (6390, 37). **Pass `--extra-labels` explicitly, or
pass `--labels-only` never — the array and the table are written by one command and only one of them
carries the scheme.**

**3. THE PLUMBING DEFECT: a run refused for landing exactly what it asked for** (bead filed P1).
`landed.py:360` computed the expected `sampling_tilt` as `sample_alpha if sample_spread is not None else
0.0` — modelling the disagreement-spread draw policy and not the corpus one. `MixedCorpus.tilt()`
reports its FACTOR on that same key, deliberately (`sampling.py:268`: "how many times heavier a
non-target position is than a target one"), so the arm died in its first second on
`sampling_tilt: asked 0.0, the model shows 2.22`. The switch-coverage partition is TOTAL over
`TrainingOptions` FIELDS and `corpus_oversample` IS compared on its own key, so the gate was green while
a SECOND key also carried the flag — **the coverage forcing-move is over fields, and this hole is over
KEYS.** Fixed by mirroring `run_setup.drawing`'s own precedence (MixedCorpus first; the two flags are
refused together at `run_setup.py:208`), with the null case (`--sample-alpha` and no spread file) kept.

The general lesson, and it is the one CLAUDE.md already states from the other side: **a flag no arm has
ever set has an untested path from the CLI to the card, and the three things that break are the cache,
the companion flag nobody slaved, and the assertion that was written when only one producer existed.**
Budget a first-of-its-kind flag at three launches, not one.

## 2026-09-08 — `reading_check` had been dead for a day, and behind it `lean_weak_columns` was REFUTED

**The check could not refuse.** `python -m kneemri.experiments.reading_check` exited 1 with
`NotImplementedError: Non-relative patterns are unsupported` on every invocation from 2026-09-07
`84660bf5` — a traceback, no report. `pathlib.Path.glob` rejects an absolute pattern, and five arms
declare one (`base_lr2e5`, `deep32_batch6`, `resnet50d_lr`, `resnet50d_short`, `vjepa_cold`), four of
them landed the same day. `found()` now resolves an absolute declaration directly and only a relative
one falls through to the three roots: the absolute spelling is the MORE honest one, because it names
the artefact without depending on which root the checker happens to try. A `test_found_absolute`
mirror test holds it. Found by the researcher (D193 §1) reading the module rather than its exit code —
`| tail` had been reporting tail's status over the traceback.

**The one finding it was holding.** `lean_weak_columns` ran Sep 7 22:40, wrote checkpoint, holdout
record and metrics, declared `# reading: logs/lean_weak_columns_ledger.log`, and never wrote it. The
`recal_dense` shape exactly: every other gate green, the deciding number never taken. Taken now with
`run_comparison --control margin_seat_s2026 --arms lean_weak_columns_s2026`, which is the arm's own
named control (same fold, same recipe, differing only in `focus_label None -> MCL+Lateral OA`):

    lean_weak_columns_s2026  e11  mean 0.8501    control margin_seat_s2026  e10  0.8525    MEAN -0.0024

      Lateral Meniscus +0.0210*   PF OA -0.0122*   Contusion -0.0088   Baker's -0.0087
      Fracture -0.0082   MCL -0.0081   Synovitis +0.0060   Medial Meniscus -0.0055
      Lateral OA -0.0046   ACL +0.0022   Effusion -0.0013   Medial OA -0.0005

**REFUTED on its own pre-registered terms.** The arm named MCL and Lateral OA and predicted +0.02 to
+0.05 on them if label balance were the binding constraint. MCL fell 0.0081, Lateral OA fell 0.0046,
and no column rose by the predicted amount. The header said to disregard the mean, so the flat mean
carries nothing either way — the refutation is the two named columns failing to rise, which is the
claim a single fold can support.

**And the paired floor says nothing else in that table is readable.** `run_comparison` prints this
pair's own half-widths at **up to +/-0.0203**, so both target deltas are deep inside noise: read them
as *did not rise*, never as *got worse*. The only column past 0.02 is Lateral Meniscus, which the arm
did not name and did not upweight — on the standing rule (an unnamed column that moves is a candidate,
not a result) it is not offered as a consolation. It licenses one cheap question if the axis is ever
revisited: `--focus-label` moved a column it was not pointed at by more than the two it was, which is
either seed scatter or evidence the mechanism re-allocates capacity rather than fixing balance.

**One correction to the arm's header.** It calls its control *"`margin_seat` itself at 0.8578-class"*.
Measured, `margin_seat_s2026` is **0.8525** @midpoint/n909/e10; **0.8578** is `band_dense_s2026`. The
header attached the wrong member's number to the right control — the `nn_corr@pool251` shape, a scalar
quoted without its subject. It does not change the verdict.

**The generalised lesson.** A check with no test that it RUNS is a check that can die silently: nothing
in nox invokes `reading_check`, so a crash in one method was invisible to every gate for a day. The
assertion worth having on a check of this kind is *"exits 0 or 1, never raises"* against the live arm
tree.

## 2026-09-08 — `train --help` has never printed, and 87 flags were invisible behind the crash

`python -m kneemri.training.train --help` exited 1 with `TypeError: %o format: an integer is required,
not dict` from `argparse._expand_help`. argparse interpolates every help string against `%(default)s`
params, so ONE unescaped `%` anywhere in the vocabulary takes down the whole help — not that flag's
line, the entire listing. The offender was `--unread-targets`, whose text quotes *"the 27.3% of pairs
carrying the constant 0.28"*; `flag_vocabulary.py:400` now escapes it `27.3%%`, which is how the three
other percentages in that file were already written. `--help` now prints **87 flags**.

This is the shape that hides for a long time: nothing in nox or CI asks a CLI to print its own help,
and an agent that wants to know what flags exist greps the arm tree instead — which is exactly how the
`--variant` axis came to have 24 registered values and no census. Found while looking for the trunk
flag, not by any gate.

## 2026-09-08 — `mricore_rate` REFUTES, decided by a CEILING at e4 and truncated 8 epochs early

`mricore` at `--backbone-lr 4e-4` against its control `mricore_corpus_s2026 = 0.8390 @midpoint/n909/e11`,
one variable, every other flag byte-identical. Pre-registered branches in `experiments/arms/mricore_rate.sh`:
LANDS >= 0.8590, PARTIAL +0.0060..+0.0200, FLAT +/-0.0060, REFUTES <= 0.8330. Reading at
`logs/mricore_rate_ledger.log`, bead `knee-m69u`.

    e4 0.7751   needs +0.0579 for the 0.8330 REFUTES ceiling
    gain e4 -> peak over 191 corpus runs: median +0.0108, p90 +0.0240, max +0.0562
    generous ceiling 0.8313  ->  CANNOT REACH, at either boundary

**REFUTES, and the branch was decided by an upper bound rather than by a final score.** This is the one
shape in which a truncated run is fully readable: truncation leaves a FLOOR on the score, and REFUTES needs
a CEILING. Even the single largest e4->peak gain in the whole 191-run corpus lands at 0.8313, under the
0.8330 boundary — so the remaining 8 epochs could not move the branch, and were not spent. `trajectory_check`
exited non-zero at both boundaries; the arm was truncated 10:08Z and the watcher handed the card to
`extended_band` inside a minute. **~90 minutes of card recovered.** `convergence_check` will read this run
TRUNCATED and its score as a floor, which is correct and does not weaken the verdict.

**The margin is thin and is stated rather than smoothed: 0.8313 against 0.8330 is 0.0017.** The criterion met
is the tool's own — arm plus the LARGEST historical gain still misses — not a comfortable one. A trajectory
better than any of the 191 would have flipped this to the low edge of FLAT, never to PARTIAL or LANDS.

**What it costs the rate axis, per the arm's own pre-registration.** 4e-4 is past this trunk's optimum, so
the convnext curve's shape (peak 4e-4, collapse by 1.2e-3) is NARROWER than the argument assumed, and the
probe for the remaining four one-LR families (`vjepa2`, `medsam`, `radiodino`, `raddino`) is **1.2e-4, not
4e-4**. The transfer from the two convolutional sweeps was flagged in the arm as an ANALOGY and it did not
hold off the convolutional families. What is NOT refuted is that a borrowed `4e-5` default is unpriced on
five families — that hole is still open, and it is now a smaller-step question.

## 2026-09-08 — blindness above 0.870 is REFUTED; the band-to-band slope spread is an artefact, not saturation

`python -m kneemri.evaluation.transfer_strata`, run 09:12Z, output at `logs/transfer_strata.log`. 37
rebuildable ensemble entries, 5 difficulty bands of ~182 studies cut on member disagreement across a fixed
41-member reference pool, 12 of 12 findings scoreable in every band. **Correlation and spread columns added
09:35Z; the slope-only version of this row, published 09:20Z, carried a mechanism that is now retracted.**

    band  studies  disagreement   ratio*  sd(offline)  sd(board)   OLS r  OLS slope
    Q1        182        0.0764   +0.42        0.0145     0.0080   0.822     +0.455
    Q2        182        0.1014   +0.58        0.0100     0.0080   0.870     +0.697
    Q3        182        0.1147   +0.74        0.0084     0.0080   0.871     +0.836
    Q4        182        0.1237   +0.74        0.0079     0.0080   0.748     +0.757
    Q5        181        0.1382   +0.66        0.0094     0.0080   0.906     +0.772

`*` is the tool's own column and is NOT an OLS slope: `transfer_strata.py:233 compression()` returns the
**median board-per-holdout ratio over the entry PAIRS the band resolves**. The last three columns are an
OLS fit computed separately over the same 37 entries. Two different estimators; they agree on the ordering
and on Q1 being the lowest, which is what makes the artefact below common to both.

**The blindness branch is REFUTED, and it is the whole of the result.** `transfer_strata.py:19` named the
live possibility that the holdout is blind above 0.870, in which case every plan ending in "improve the
offline number" is unfunded. Every stratum reads a positive ratio AND an OLS correlation of 0.75 or better.
Offline movement is funded, at about 0.7 of face value, uniformly.

**RETRACTED: that the compression is SATURATION, and the rule that a gain be re-priced by WHERE it landed.**
Both estimators divide by a per-band offline spread, and that spread is what actually varies. Board score is
a per-entry constant, so `sd(board)` is identical in every band and the OLS slope is
`r · sd(board)/sd(offline)` — the ordering is the offline-SPREAD ordering unless r moves, and r does not
move with difficulty (0.748 at Q4, in the MIDDLE, is the lowest). The published "1.8x compression in the
easy band" is the 1.84x spread ratio 0.0145/0.0079. The median-pair-ratio column inherits the same defect
by a shorter route: a band whose per-pair `delta offline` is noisier has a noisier DENOMINATOR, which drags
the median ratio down without anything about transfer changing.

Saturation additionally predicts its own signature — entries BUNCHED near a ceiling — and Q1 is the
opposite on both counts: the widest entry spread of the five, and per D195 §3 the lowest mean member macro
(0.7773, sd 0.0213). Regression dilution (a noisier per-entry offline estimate in Q1) fits both columns but
is not established either: disattenuating Q1 fully would push r above 1, so part of that spread is real.
The band-dependence is UNEXPLAINED and must not be planned against.

**Method rule this buys.** A ratio or slope fitted inside a subset divides by that subset's own spread and
is not comparable across subsets. **Report the correlation and the spreads alongside every stratified
slope.** The tool prints neither; that is why the artefact reached a published file, fifteen minutes ahead
of the check that killed it. The pair split (hard +0.71 vs easy +0.62) is the same comparison at a smaller
effect size with no interval — directional at best, and not independent support for the retracted rule.

**What it still cannot say.** ~180 studies a band, so per-label AUCs inside one are wide. The 37 entries span
days and a kit that changed underneath them, exactly as `board_transfer` states; stratifying asks the
confounded question where the hypotheses differ, it does not repair the confound. Full write-up:
`interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-08_transfer-is-saturation-not-blindness.md` (filename retained for the
inbound links; its title now states the amended reading).

## 2026-09-08 — `--corpus-oversample 2.22` does not lift the mean, and the floor is why that is all it says

`merged3_oversample_s2026` vs control `merged3_corpus_s2026` (0.8521 @e7), the only difference being
`corpus_oversample 1.0 -> 2.22`. `convergence_check`: UNDERTRAINED, best e11 of 12 asked — not truncated,
so the number is quotable. Reading at `logs/merged3_oversample_ledger.log`.

    MEAN -0.0105     Fracture -0.0516*  MCL -0.0441*  Synovitis -0.0128  Baker's -0.0123
    Medial Meniscus -0.0095  Lateral OA +0.0071  Medial OA +0.0060  ACL -0.0023  Effusion -0.0023
    Lateral Meniscus -0.0020  Contusion -0.0015  PF OA -0.0006
    paired floor, this pair's own: half-widths up to +/-0.0299
    by structure scale: focal -0.0065  regional -0.0161

**VERDICT: DID NOT RISE.** The pre-registration named +/-0.006 as reading B and the expected outcome. The
point estimate is -0.0105, past that band's low edge and well INSIDE this pair's own paired floor of
+/-0.0299 — so the honest statement is that oversampling the merged corpus does not lift the mean, NOT that
it harms it. The two starred columns are Fracture and MCL, the pool's two most label-bottlenecked findings
(Fracture has ~68 positives on this frame, below `column_surface.py:8`'s own half-width), and
`run_comparison` flags the pair as a READER change. A -0.05 on Fracture is what that column does.

**Consequence: per-corpus head conditioning is not scoped as a build.** That was the decision this arm was
run to make (`after_ourtrunk44.sh` header), and it is made. The flag stays available and documented; nothing
follows it.

**Note the floor.** +/-0.0299 is the widest paired floor this ledger has recorded, five times the
significance bar. An arm read against this control cannot resolve anything smaller than a very large effect,
which is a fact about the CONTROL's frame and should be checked before another arm is queued against it.

## The transfer constant is CONDITIONAL: ~1.0 mid-ladder, ~0.5-0.7 at the champion — and the band cut is retired — 2026-09-08

D197, researcher, 10:24Z, answering M198. Card-free and slot-free; an independent 37-entry rebuildable
population and three estimators that do not share `board_transfer`'s machinery.

**There is no single constant.** The slope of board on offline is ~1.0 across the whole ladder and
~0.5-0.7 inside the top ten to fifteen entries, and the difference is real.

| quantity | value | population | cut |
|---|---|---|---|
| reliability of `offline@holdout909/midpoint` | 0.9763 (sd 0.0133, 200 stratified split-halves, Spearman-Brown) | 37 rebuildable ensemble entries | midpoint 0.5 |
| observed OLS slope, board on offline | +1.0169 (r 0.8854, sd(off) 0.0070) | same 37 | same |
| disattenuated slope | +1.0416 | same 37 | same |
| slope in the top 10, selection-free and dilution-corrected | +0.487 (sd 0.216) | top 10 of the 37 | same |

**THE PRACTICAL OUTPUT, and it is the number to write into every plan: to move the board +0.010 from
where the champion sits, an arm must deliver +0.017 OFFLINE.** Not +0.010, not +0.014. The 0.7 this
project multiplies by is `compression_above`, a TOP-REGIME CONDITIONAL — `board_transfer.py:370-374`
already says `compression` answers the whole-record question while pricing an arm uses
`compression_above`, and `:458-459` prints the whole-record figure with "the wrong number to price an arm
with" attached. Since essentially every arm we run is aimed at the champion, 0.7 is the right constant
for our plans and at the very top it is if anything generous (0.5-0.6 there).

**The fall survived four attempts to explain it away.** (a) Noisy-denominator bias in the pair ratio:
median ratio by delta quartile is flat, 0.9031 / 1.0466 / 0.9339 / 0.9274, and a separation-floor sweep
climbs only 0.9399 → 0.9616 while n falls 380 → 40. (b) Entry-level selection-on-noise: selecting on
half A and measuring on the independent half B puts the honest estimate at or BELOW its matched control
at every k — selection bias predicts the opposite. (c) Pair-level selection: a selection-free OLS with
the regressor measured on an independent half falls just as steeply, 0.9956 → 0.4826, and reads 0.9956
at k=37 against the +1.0169 computed a different way. (d) Within-slice regression dilution, the
strongest candidate: in-slice reliability barely moves (0.949 → 0.914) while sd(offline) more than
halves, so the correction is worth +0.047 at k=37 and +0.001 at k=10. **The fall is a property of the
board, not of the ruler.**

**The band cut is RETIRED as a planning axis.** Every corrected band slope sits BELOW the whole-frame
+1.0169: Q1 0.614, Q2 0.788, Q3 0.957, Q4 0.863, Q5 0.866. Cutting the frame into difficulty bands and
regressing inside one loses board-relevant information whichever band is chosen — **score on the whole
909**. The Q3-Q1 gap survives the dilution correction (+0.343) but does not clear its interval
(95% [-0.015, +0.589], 0.972 of bootstrap draws above zero), and 0.972 is exactly the value that gets
written down as a finding and then fails to replicate. This closes from the entry side the axis D195
closed from the member side, by a different statistic.

**A docstring defect to fix.** `board_transfer.py:23-24` records +1.55 / +0.99; the live run says
+1.05 / +0.72. The module warns in its own header that this constant has been misquoted from prose three
times, and the drift is now present in the module itself.

**Direction-only caveat.** At k <= 10 the spread over splits is 0.16-0.22 on 6-12 pairs.
`board_transfer.py:153` already stamps that regime `DIRECTION ONLY, too few pairs to price an arm with`.
Read 0.5 as "clearly below 1.0", never as a third decimal.

## The consensus frame is BLIND to the labeler axis by construction — the constraint is treatment DENSITY, not ruler width — 2026-09-08

D198, researcher, 10:40Z, answering M199. Card-free, slot-free. **NO**, and not for the reasons M199
pre-registered — the frame fails both bars (`acc@gold58/consensus` 0.8740 < 0.95; 1,890 studies with
>= 8 of 12 findings < 2,000) but those were the wrong reasons to reject it.

**THE STRUCTURAL REASON. A consensus frame keeps 4.1% of the treatment's own cells.** A cell enters the
frame only where the two readers AGREE; a better label table earns its keep exactly where it DISAGREES
with v2. The two sets are near-disjoint by construction, so the frame deletes the axis's footprint and
then reports the axis flat. `blend_hybrid_fx_v4b` binarises differently from v2 on 1,254 cells and 51
survive, against a 0.579 baseline keep rate — **Effusion, the column the arm was built to fix, keeps 8 of
520**. Where the v2-truthed 909 frame MIS-SCORES the disputed cells, the consensus frame REMOVES them.

**And the deeper finding, which is the one to carry: the gold 58 holds 19 treated cells of 684 (2.8%).**
The ruler is not too narrow — the TREATMENT is too small a fraction of any random frame, and no increase
in width fixes that. On those 19 cells v4b is **0.632 correct against v2's 0.368**; pooled over all 684
it is 0.803 vs 0.795, because 665 of 684 cells are byte-identical between the tables. That is why
`+0.0131 [-0.0045, +0.0332]` (README:8591) crosses zero, and it was never a width problem.

**A GENERAL RULE, and it is the second one today: dropping noisy cells UN-ATTENUATES every delta, so no
number measured on a cell-filtered frame is comparable to a v2-frame number.** Four control pairs that
differ on architecture, geometry, density and recalibration — never on the label table — inflate by a
median ~2x when moved onto the masked frame, and the treated pair's 3.81x sits inside that control range:

    pair                                   v2 delta          consensus delta    ratio
    TREATED   v4hybrid / holdannot     +0.0027 +/-0.0062     +0.0104 +/-0.0078    3.81
    control   base224 / adjacent224    +0.0046 +/-0.0062     +0.0092 +/-0.0120    1.98
    control   band224 / band_dense     -0.0044 +/-0.0054     -0.0087 +/-0.0074    1.98
    control   holdannot / recal        -0.0013 +/-0.0054     -0.0083 +/-0.0064    6.18
    control   band_dense / band_deep   +0.0125 +/-0.0061     +0.0142 +/-0.0126    1.14

This is D197 §1's disattenuation arithmetic applied to LABEL noise instead of entry noise, and it stands
beside this morning's stratified-slope rule: a subset ruler is not the same ruler.

**The per-column read came back inverted from the arm's own pre-registration** (`labels_v4hybrid.sh:30-49`)
— CAN MOVE 3 cols mean **-0.0018**, flat 4 cols +0.0046, CANNOT REACH 4 cols **+0.0173**, the only column
clearing zero being Lateral Meniscus +0.0301 [+0.0100, +0.0509] on the CANNOT-REACH list. **This is NOT
read as a refutation of the labeler axis**, because the keep-rate table says the instrument could not
have seen a success. It refutes the FRAME.

**What the axis actually needs: adjudicate the DISPUTED cells, do not annotate more studies.** 1,254
treated cells over 1,076 studies (696 on the CAN MOVE columns), 4,917 reader-disputed cells. Annotating
~150 treated cells is worth ~35x annotating 150 more studies (2.8% vs 100% treated-cell density), and at
the +0.26 per-cell effect ~100 adjudicated cells separate the tables decisively (paired binomial
half-width ~+/-0.10 at n=100, ~+/-0.07 at n=200) — a direct reading of the LABELER with no training run
in it. Requested as a blinded pack in M200: the researcher builds it and holds the key, main answers it
from report text alone, the researcher scores both tables against those verdicts, with untreated control
rows mixed in to bound the adjudicator's own noise.

**The limit to keep attached to that reading:** adjudicating against REPORT TEXT measures PARSER
FIDELITY, which is Wollek's axis, not label correctness against the images. The gold-58 nineteen remain
the underpowered but image-anchored check that the two readings agree in sign.

**Two facts that change what is buildable.** Qwen3.8 has ALREADY swept the whole corpus —
`.agent-runtime/scratch/report_labels_v3.csv`, (4407, 37), finished 2026-09-06 14:53 — so M199's
UNBUILDABLE branch and its ~1.8 h estimate are dead. The local learned reader exists on **58 studies
only**, which is what made the three-way frame unbuildable as specified; a third reader is not wanted
anyway, since a stricter frame deletes MORE of the treatment.

**Circularity checked and clean** (the equation is CORRECTED below, 2026-09-08 — `blend_hybrid` +
`fracture_contusion` is `blend_hybrid_fx`, and v4b is that plus a third, then-unwritten step; the
circularity verdict survives it, since `report_labels_v4` predates the Qwen sweep by three days):
`blend_hybrid_fx_v4b` = `blend_hybrid` + `fracture_contusion`, and
`table_blend`'s inputs are our v2 plus the foreign public tables — Qwen is not an ingredient. The frame
is blind, not rigged.

**Population warning.** D198's gold-58 row is a 13-study intersection (+/-0.0791), a different population
from the 57-study reading behind the +/-0.015 half-width at README:7063. The two must not be compared.

## `blend_hybrid_fx_v4b` is `blend_hybrid_fx` plus ONE grafted column, and that column is the regression

2026-09-08, main, card-free and slot-free, off tables on disk plus D200's blinded adjudication.

The ledger recorded v4b as `blend_hybrid` + `fracture_contusion`. That composition is `blend_hybrid_fx`,
which is a DIFFERENT FILE that also exists, and the step between them went unwritten for five days. It is
now named, implemented and proved by an oracle: `--rule effusion_reread` over `blend_hybrid_fx.csv`
reproduces `blend_hybrid_fx_v4b.csv` (`core/data/labels/table_correction.py`, `ColumnGraft`).

**What the graft is.** `report_labels_v4` is v2 with the missing study and ONE column re-read — Effusion,
positive rate 0.605 → 0.490 (researcher's label-source audit, 2026-09-07). v4b takes that column whole:
verdict and `__conf` from the donor on every row, and the VALUE re-levelled wherever the re-read landed on
a different level than v2 did. Measured over the 4,406 shared studies:

| column | v4b vs `blend_hybrid_fx` | v4b verdict vs `report_labels_v4` |
|---|---|---|
| Effusion | 559 values, 520 verdicts | 1.0000 |
| the other eleven | 0 | — |

So **every difference between v4b and `blend_hybrid_fx` is the Effusion column**, and the eight columns
D200 scored v4b as WINNING are `blend_hybrid_fx`'s wins, not v4b's. The graft's own footprint splits
508 cells `YES` → `UNK` (value onto the UNK sentinel 0.265) and 51 cells lowered 0.88ish → 0.795.

**And D200 prices exactly that footprint at 58/59 against it.** A blinded reader scored those cells `YES`
from the report text at **0.983**. It is not a cut artefact: every one of the 520 flips separates by more
than 0.20, median |v4b − v2| = 0.4150.

**The conclusion follows without a card.** v4b differs from its own base in one column, that column is a
confirmed recall regression, therefore **`blend_hybrid_fx` dominates `blend_hybrid_fx_v4b` and no further
arm should take `--labels blend_hybrid_fx_v4b.csv`.** This is not selection-on-the-measurement: the column
is identifiable as the only one whose UNK rate moves (0.099 → 0.214, every other column identical to three
decimals) with no adjudication at all, and the adjudication only supplied the SIGN.

**What it costs backwards.** `labels_v4hybrid_s2026` (README:8590) and the board's `kneemri-v4solo`
(0.922) were trained on the grafted table; both are now readings of `blend_hybrid_fx` plus a bad Effusion
column, and neither is void — but the +0.0131 twelve-mean on the gold 58 was earned DESPITE the graft, not
by it. The oracle's residual is 5 Effusion values of 4,406 (0.9989), all at `(origin 0.68, donor 0.68)` —
a level the re-read did not change and the hand-built table moved anyway, so the residual is in the shipped
table, not in the rule.

### D201: the champion never carried the column, and the board had already run the A/B

Two questions were open after the graft was identified: does anything SHIPPED carry it, and is the
−0.0054 ledger delta the column or the ruler? Both are now answered off disk, no card and no slot.

**Carriers census (researcher, 2026-09-08).** 0 of the 6 `raptorweight_v1` seats carry the grafted table —
every seat traces to `experiments/arms/calibsix.sh:115-133,141` and `final_fit_six.sh:48`, all passing
`--labels "$LABELS"` = `experiments/lib.sh:72` = `report_labels_v2.csv`. Of 287 label-naming arms, **3**
name v4b and only ONE ran (`labels_v4hybrid_s2026`, on `comp/members2.roster:30`, absent from
`comp/champion.json`'s `chosen`); `compose_v4b_clean` and `compose_v4b_oof` have zero files on disk. Every
teacher is v2-derived (`teacher_clean.sh:49`, `oof_fold0.sh:54`), so no distilled member inherits it
second-hand. **The champion is clean; the axis closes with no re-fit and no slot.**

**Per-column decomposition** (matched, same 909 studies, byte-identical truth, arm vs control):

| column | delta | share of macro |
|---|---|---|
| Effusion | −0.0252 [−0.0407, −0.0105] | 39% |
| Medial OA | −0.0148 [−0.0248, −0.0053] | 23% |
| the other ten | each straddles 0 | — |

macro arm 0.8524 vs control 0.8578, **delta −0.0054** — reproduces the ledger row exactly.

**This is NOT a decomposition of the graft, and I mis-read it as one for an hour.** The arm trains on
`blend_hybrid_fx_v4b.csv`; the control `band_dense_hold` trains on `$LABELS` = `report_labels_v2.csv`
(`experiments/arms/band_dense_hold.sh:39`, `lib.sh:72`). Those two tables differ on EVERY column —
measured over the 4,406 shared studies, Medial OA differs in 4,404 cells (mean |d| 0.0481), Effusion in
4,406 (0.1016), ACL in 4,404, Lateral OA in 4,397. So the pair prices *blend + fracture lift + graft*
against v2, not the graft. Against the graft's own base the same diff reads **0 Medial OA cells and 559
Effusion cells** (`fx` vs `v4b`), which is the ColumnGraft footprint and nothing else. Medial OA therefore
needs no second mechanism: it is the BLEND, and the bead opened for it closes on that arithmetic.
The Effusion −0.0252 is likewise blend-plus-graft, so it may not be quoted as the graft's price.
**Nor may the board A/B**: `v4solo_v1` trained on `blend_hybrid_fx_v4b` and `holdsolo_v1` on
`report_labels_v2` (`comp/SUBMISSIONS.md:3629-3638` says so in as many words), which is the same
whole-table comparison. The ONLY reading that prices the graft's own cells is D200's blinded
adjudication, because it scores the 520 moved cells directly from the report text and never touches a
label table at all.

**The confound this table CANNOT remove, stated before the reading is used.** Truth here IS the v2 table,
so an Effusion-local loss is predicted by both hypotheses (a worse column, and a correct column measured
against a v2 ruler). What separates them is ONE non-v2 reading, not two: D200's blinded report-text
adjudication, 58/59 against the graft over the 520 cells the graft itself moves. The board A/B
(`v4solo_v1` **0.922** vs `holdsolo_v1` **0.928**, `comp/SUBMISSIONS.md:3629-3638`) agrees on the sign
and is worth having, but it compares `blend_hybrid_fx_v4b` against `report_labels_v2` — a whole-table
difference, every column moved — so it prices the TABLE and cannot be cited against the column. What
retires the ruler-artefact defence in `kneemri-v4solo.py:9-10` is the blinded adjudication alone.

**Medial OA is unexplained and stays open.** Its interval excludes zero, it is 23% of the delta, the graft
touches no such column, and it contradicts D200's 5/5 in v4b's favour on that column. Filed rather than
explained — a column that moves with no mechanism is either a second difference nobody has found or a
correlated ruler effect, and neither is licensed to be assumed.

### D202b — the learned combiner, re-read after its own bug was fixed

`stack_combiner`'s docstring records a first honest reading of **-0.0179 own-finding / -0.0076 crossed**
taken while the ridge shrank toward the ORIGIN, so the grid could not recover the flat vote as its limit
and a negative delta meant nothing. The penalty is now centred on `prior`. Re-run over the same twelve
seats, 909 studies, 5 contiguous blocks:

| features | flat vote (RankAverage) | learned stack | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| own finding | 0.8750 | 0.8745 | **-0.0005** |
| every finding (`--cross`) | 0.8750 | 0.8669 | **-0.0081** |

The fix worked — own-finding went -0.0179 → -0.0005, i.e. the combiner now recovers its control and finds
nothing above it. A per-member-per-finding weight buys **0.0000 within resolution**, and letting a finding
read the other eleven columns LOSES 0.0081, which is over the floor and is a real cost. `knee-orjq` asked
whether directional gains ADD under a learned combiner; on the scoreable pool the answer is no, and the
0.950 plan may not assume it. Caveat stated in the tool's own output and repeated here: this is a
statement about the SCOREABLE pool, and five of the champion's six seats are `--fold -1` and invisible to it.

**Cost of D202 + D202b: zero card-hours, zero slots.** Both were answerable off the 323 holdout records
already on disk, and both had been standing as open axes in prose for days.

**THE RULER HAS FAILED UPWARD ON BOTH THINGS THAT EVER MOVED THE BOARD.** `base_dense` priced -0.0066
against its matched control and ticked the board. And by the researcher's D203 §6 the foreign
`raptor_v4_swa` member reads about **-0.079** against our own members on our ruler, and that seat moved
0.941 -> 0.943. Sixteen offline rejections stand unshipped; the two accepted seats were both offline
negatives.

**THAT IS NOT AN ANTI-CORRELATION AND MUST NOT BE WRITTEN AS ONE.** A ruler that is reliably wrong is a
ruler you invert and win with; nobody wins that way, so the sign is not the finding. The finding is that
the offline ADD and the board measure **different distributions**. Our holdout is 909 studies drawn from
OUR corpus, decoded by OUR pixel path, supervised by OUR label table — the same three things every
candidate was fitted under. So an ADD asks only *"do you add on studies you were built to fit?"*, which
is an **in-distribution redundancy** measure, and sixteen negatives is exactly what a saturated
in-distribution pool looks like. Both seats that moved the board were **out-of-distribution** members —
`base_dense` a different architecture, `raptor_v4_swa` a different pixel path — and they paid where this
ruler is blind, not against it.

**The consequence: this project has never measured generalisation, and that is the lever.** The open
question is not the ruler's sign but whether an out-of-distribution readout exists, and one does at zero
training cost: the researcher's D203 §1 establishes his `all_vols.npy` covers all 4,407 of our studies
at (44, 336, 336) — **a different pixel path over the same studies and the same labels**. Scoring the
members we already own on HIS decode is a distribution-shift readout with the corpus and the supervision
held fixed, and it needs a loader adapter and no card. That, not the sixteen ADDs, is what decides which
arm to build next — and it re-opens `intensity_aug` (off in 286/288 runs), which lost on the
in-distribution ruler and was never asked the question it exists to answer.

**`extended_band_s2026` was killed at epoch 3** on this reading (0.8278, needing +0.0300 against a
median cohort gain of +0.0202, pre-registered P = 0.18) — it is a slice/band knob whose ADD would land
where the other sixteen did. Cost of D203: **zero card-hours, zero slots**, and 3.5 h of card returned.
