```
same members, same aggregation      solotop_v1/topviews_v1   0.925, 0.925          spread 0.0000
                                    sixfresh_v1/sixfresh_v2  0.931, 0.931          spread 0.0000
same members, aggregation varied    5 groups, 3-7 seats      median 0.0010   max   0.0030
```

`sixfresh_v2`'s own prose is *"identical code and members to sixfresh_v1 on the REFRESHED kit (cf6a99f,
was e3c884e) — the kit is the only variable"*, so **the KIT confound is measured at 0.0000**. Hold every
future board delta against **0.000 same-aggregation / 0.001-0.003 aggregation-varied**. This constant is
written here because `board_transfer`'s slope has now been quoted wrong from prose twice.

**2. The saturation statement, reached from the board side.** Over every nested one-seat pair the project
has ever submitted, **the largest offline ADD any single seat has ever made is 0.0013, median 0.0002.**
Under a *perfect* slope of 1 the record's biggest step predicts a board move of 0.0013 — **1.3
quantisation steps** of a board quoted to 0.001, and below the 0.0030 the board moves when only the
combiner changes. So the ruler is not failing to transfer: **the pool has stopped producing steps big
enough for the board to resolve.** That is D203's conclusion arriving from the opposite direction, and it
sharpens it — the pool looks saturated because every seat now added is *in-distribution* with the ones
already seated.

**3. Why the slope itself is not usable, stated so nobody refits it.** A naive OLS reads **+1.832, se
0.663, 95% CI [+0.533, +3.132], r +0.777, permutation p 0.030** — and must not be used. n is **7**
distinct set-to-set comparisons over 9 board rows, so the rows are dependent (`basedense_v1` is an
endpoint of three) and the se is understated, not conservative. Jackknife: dropping the single leftmost
point (`longseat_v1 -> crossenc_v1`, x -0.0013 y -0.0040) takes the slope **+1.83 -> +0.83** and r
**0.78 -> 0.56**; that point's y is itself larger than the 0.0030 six identical members produce. And the
decisive fact is not n: **all seven pairs are dated 2026-08-20 to 2026-08-22**, board span 0.925-0.932,
against a plateau of 0.937-0.944. Fifteen fit-eligible rows postdate 08-22 and **not one of them nests by
exactly one seat** — after 08-22 the record changes seating, fold discipline and combiner together. The
fit is entirely twelve board points below the regime the question was about. Neither M208 §3 branch is
licensed.

What WOULD answer it: two submissions, an entry and that entry plus one seat, everything else held
including combiner and kit, **the seat chosen so its offline ADD is at least 0.004** (3x the
identical-member spread). No seat that has ever existed adds that much, so it is a two-slot experiment on
a member that does not exist yet.

**4. Denominator correction — D206 §9 must not be quoted.** D206 said `members_named` is on 89 of 123
rows and *"all 89 also carry `board` AND `offline`"*. The second half is wrong (that census tested key
PRESENCE; 47 carry `offline: null` explicitly):

```
rows in comp/board.jsonl                             123
  carrying members_named                              89
  board not None                                      88
  board AND offline not None                          41   <- the real pool
  after dropping scope=excluded                       38   <- the denominator
  minus in-sample / no-record / LEAKED offline_scope  37   <- fit-eligible
```

**The denominator for anything joining offline to board is 38, not 89.**

**5. THE SEAT / DISTANCE QUEUE IS CLOSED FOR CAUSE.** Prediction-space member distance — rank
correlation, JS divergence, Mahalanobis, `NEAREST`, `MEAN` over predictions
(`kneemri/evaluation/member_distance.py`) — is **done, priced and finished**, and this line records the
kill so it is not re-opened in a new coordinate system:

- The ruler was validated at **+0.7086** and then produced **sixteen offline rejections** while the two
  seats that moved the board were both offline negatives (D203).
- Raw, all four statistics correlate **negatively** with gain (-0.5313), because distance is confounded
  with quality. That negative sign is the anti-correlation reading, and it is **rejected on principle**:
  a reliably wrong ruler is one you invert and win with, and nobody wins that way.
- The board has answered the seating axis **seven times flat**, and §2 above says why it must: no seat
  the pool can produce moves the board by more than one quantisation step.

So: **no card and no slot to a seating, selection, weighting, distance or re-lensing operation.** The
axis is not "unpromising", it is *measured out* — the ceiling on the whole family is 0.0013 offline,
against a board that cannot see 0.0030.

What is NOT killed, and is the successor: **the same question asked in a space the pool is not saturated
in.** D203/D206 put an out-of-distribution readout within reach at zero training cost (his decode over
our studies and our labels), and `kneemri/embeddings/` already builds and caches trunk features that
**nothing has ever run an analysis over** — no Mahalanobis, no PCA, no kNN, no OOD score in feature
space. Feature-space distance is worth building **only** as the representational half of that
generalisation readout, never as a seat selector; the selector is what lost sixteen times.

## D208/D209 — the sagittal slice axis is ALREADY canonical, the pool cannot see slice order anyway, and the medial/lateral question relocates to the coronal mirror

Two letters, one axis, and a retraction the researcher wrote against their own finding. Recorded here
because the first version of it would have queued a training arm and the second version closes the family.

### 1. What was measured, and the denominators

`frac_reversed@sag_series = 0.0000` over **9864 of 9864** sagittal series in `corpus4407` — zero
unreadable orientation tags, zero ambiguous planes, so there is no parsed-subset denominator underneath.
Every sagittal acquisition in the archive is stored with the through-plane normal `r_x x r_y` pointing to
the patient's right. The headers carry NO per-study variation.

`frac_reversed@sag_series_cached = 0.4752` over **9651 of 9864** (side resolved on 97.8%). The bimodality
D208 measured is manufactured by us, on purpose, by `Laterality.normalise`
(`core/data/corpus/laterality.py:51-63`), which for a right knee flips the sagittal stack along
`dims=[0]` — the SLICE axis. `side` is per STUDY, which is why all three sagittal slots flip together and
why a one-bit-per-study shape was the right thing to look for.

Agreement of the cached sign with the per-study Spearman direction: **401 of 401**, all three sagittal
slots, zero exceptions. The header sign sits at the coin value (0.4920 / 0.5120 / 0.4831) because it is
constant while the correlation is not.

**These two numbers describe the same corpus and a reader handed either one alone draws the opposite
conclusion.** They are the denominator rule earning its keep.

### 2. The attribution problem, and why the first reading did not survive it

D208 section 2 read the bimodality as a defect in our pipeline and concluded that every member with a
sagittal slot had trained on a slice axis whose direction was random across studies. That reading is
**RETRACTED** by its own author (D209), on the argument M212 raised: the statistic correlates OUR order
against HIS index, so the sign of the correlation is the XOR of two orderings and cannot name a side. The
1.000 within-plane agreement does not attribute it either, because our three sagittal slots map to only
TWO of his blocks (slot 0 from 0-11; slots 3 and 5 from 12-21), so one per-study bit on HIS side hitting
both his sagittal blocks predicts the same table. Crossing pairs at 0.476-0.568 rule out a whole-volume
flip on his side and nothing narrower.

The header read settles it from our side alone, with no his-data: the archive is constant, so the bit is
ours, and it is deliberate. **Our sagittal order is the anatomically canonical one** (medial to lateral
the same way for both knees); his is raw header order, which is constant in patient coordinates and
therefore INCONSISTENT in anatomy across knees. No canonicalisation arm. Nothing to canonicalise.

Recorded as a retraction and not a correction, because a reader who meets only the first version queues
the arm.

### 3. The independent reason the arm was void: the pool is order-blind by construction

Measured on our side while the attribution was in flight. `kneemri/models/slice_pooling.py` defines six
poolings; usage across every arm in the tree:

```
max 311 - labelwise 28 - attend 18 - depth 4 - channels 4 - moments 1
```

`MAXIMUM` is a bare per-dimension `amax`. `attend` and `labelwise` score each slice FROM THAT SLICE ALONE,
so scoring is permutation-equivariant and the pooled output is permutation-INVARIANT. `moments` is
mean+spread. Only `depth` (DepthAttention — mixes each slice with its through-plane neighbours) and
`channels` (three consecutive slices as encoder channels) can observe order at all. The file states this
itself at `slice_pooling.py:28-32` — DEPTH is *"the one slice pooling that can see ORDER... Named beside
the two order-blind ones because that is the comparison it exists to make"* — and `depth_attention.py:36`
adds *"ABSOLUTE DEPTH IS DELIBERATELY NOT SUPPLIED."*

**8 of 366 arms can observe a sagittal reversal.** So even had the bit been his, the arm was void: 97.8%
of the pool is invariant to the thing it would have fixed. Two independent closures of the same arm, from
opposite ends, and neither cost card time.

Splice consequence: the per-study sign in `kneemri/evaluation/foreign_readout.py` stays and is exactly
`side == "R"` (free, from `Study.side`, no correlation and no his-data needed); the static
`reversed_=True` constant in `BLOCKS` goes. A constant was never the right shape for a per-study bit and
is now provably the wrong one. On the 213-of-9864 side-unresolved series the empirical sign remains the
only source.

### 4. The inversion hypothesis this raised, and why it is DEAD — recorded so it is not re-raised

The hypothesis was worth stating and is worth killing in writing: sagittal depth IS the medial-lateral
axis, Medial Meniscus and Lateral Meniscus are separate findings in our twelve, so order-blind pooling
might be destroying the exact axis two labels are defined on — which would make `depth` pooling's measured
null a FAULTY-DATA verdict (an order-aware operator tested on randomly-ordered stacks) rather than a
refutation.

**Section 1 removes the faulty-data clause.** The cached sagittal order is anatomy-canonical by
construction, so `depth_true` was measured on correctly-ordered data. It read **0.8461, -0.0015 against
`attend_true`, second-worst of four operators** spanning 0.0019 (max 0.8457, order-aware 0.8461, mean
0.8473, permutation-blind gate 0.8476). The existing ledger row already concluded *"SLICE ORDER IS NOT A
LEVER EITHER"*; what D209 adds is that the row was ENTITLED to conclude it. The family is correctly closed
and this is the second time in two weeks a closed family was nearly re-opened on a mechanism that had
already been controlled for.

### 5. Where the question DOES survive — the coronal/axial mirror, and the open number

`Laterality.normalise` does two different things with opposite visibility:

```python
if plane in (Plane.CORONAL, Plane.AXIAL):
    return torch.flip(images, dims=[-1])   # WIDTH — a within-slice MIRROR
return torch.flip(images, dims=[0])        # SLICE ORDER — sagittal
```

Sagittal `dims=[0]` is a slice reorder — invisible to 97.8% of the pool per section 3, so a
wrongly-resolved side costs almost nothing there. Coronal/axial `dims=[-1]` is a left-right mirror INSIDE
every slice, visible to every pooling, every trunk, every member without exception: `amax` over a mirrored
image is a mirrored feature. And a left-right mirror on a coronal slice IS a medial-lateral swap, against
the same two labels, on the plane that carries them.

So the canonicalisation is only as good as the side resolution behind it, and the exposure is
plane-asymmetric in a way nothing has measured. `side` is unresolved on **213 of 9864 sagittal series
(2.2%)**; where resolved it comes from a Type 2C `Laterality` tag on **4636 of 9864 series (47.0%,** split
2296 L / 2340 R, so not a biased corner **)** and a `centre_x` geometry fallback on the rest.
`core/data/corpus/diagnose_laterality.py` exists to measure the tag-vs-geometry-vs-used disagreement in
seconds of header reads, and its own docstring says it was written for the medial/lateral target
asymmetry.

**OPEN, unpriced, assigned to the researcher in M213 and deliberately not turned into an arm:**
`side_disagreement@corpus4407`, the both-present-subset rate with its denominator stated, which source
wins in `Laterality.of_study`, and the count of disagreeing studies that have a coronal or axial slot
populated. A fraction of a percent makes this a footnote. A few percent on the plane every member can see
makes it the first data defect this project has found that is both universally visible and cheap to
correct — and only then is an arm priced. No number, no arm.

### 6. Unrelated, delivered alongside: the permutation refits to nothing on the 909

D206's slot permutation, refitted on `holdout909` (909 of 909 in our 336px cache index AND served by one
of his two shards, so this is the holdout itself, not a shard intersection), holds with a smallest argmax
margin of **0.599**. Slots 3 and 5 both take his block 12-21 on their own votes (0.863 / 0.976) — his
layout, not a tie. Nothing in the splice needs refitting.

### 7. D210 CLOSES it — the number came back a footnote, so there is no arm

Section 5 said "No number, no arm". The number is in, header reads only, no card and no slot:

```
side_disagreement@corpus4407      three-way tag / tag-stripped-geometry / used, 4407 studies, 24371 series
  tag present, study level         2203 of  4407   0.4999
  tag present, series level       12000 of 24371   0.4924
  used side resolved               4335 of  4407   0.9837
  geometry resolvable              4267 of  4407   0.9682

frac_side_wrong@tag_and_geometry     30 of 2135    0.0141   (in-subset; the subset is 2135/4407 = 0.4845)
                                     30 of 4407    0.0068   (the corpus rate, and it is a FLOOR)
  direction   tag L / geometry R  18      tag R / geometry L  12
```

Converted to the thing a member actually eats — mirrored coronal/axial slot-instances — it is **80 of
11380, 0.0070**. Every study in the corpus populates at least one coronal or axial slot (4407 of 4407),
so exposure is TOTAL and the study rate converts to an input rate with no attenuation at all. That is
the one structural fact worth keeping: there is no corner of the corpus a side error cannot reach. The
rate is still 0.70%, which is below every bar this project uses, so it is a footnote and it is written
as one.

Three things recorded beside it, none of them priced, all of them the same ledger line:

- **The tag wins outright, and arbitrarily.** `Laterality.of_study` (`core/data/corpus/laterality.py:39-49`)
  takes `tagged[0]` — the first tagged series in `sorted(iterdir())` order. Not a vote, never cross-checked
  against geometry, which is reached only when NO series in the study carries a tag. **25 of 2203 tagged
  studies (0.0113) carry both an L and an R tag across their own series**, and `tagged[0]` resolves those
  by directory sort order; ten of them are in the disagreeing 30 and the other fifteen agree with geometry
  by coin flip, not by resolution.
- **0.0068 is a lower bound, not an estimate.** Neither source is ground truth, so the 2105 agreeing pairs
  could still be wrong together. It is a rate of OBSERVABLE disagreement over the 48.45% of the corpus
  where both sources exist at all. Against the dead-zone reading: `median |centre_x|` on the disagreeing 30
  is 95.1 mm against 81.0 mm on the agreeing 2105, so these are not marginal geometry calls.
- **The larger neighbour: 72 studies (0.0163) resolve NO side.** `normalise` returns `images` unchanged
  when `side != "R"`, so a right knee among those is simply never mirrored — 152 mirrored slot-instances
  of 11380 (0.0134), roughly half of them wrong, arriving by a different mechanism and twice the count of
  the disagreement set. Still a footnote.

**And a denominator correction to section 5 above**, which is the same error the `@`-scoping rule exists
to catch: the 47.0% tag rate quoted there is `4636 / 9864` — `tag_rate@sag_series`, the sagittal cut,
because that section's whole population was sagittal. Over all three planes it is `12000 / 24371 = 0.4924`
series-level and `0.4999` study-level, and `Study.side` consumes the STUDY-level rate because one tagged
series anywhere in a study is enough. Same archive, different denominator. The number in section 5 is
right; its label was not.

**Verdict: the coronal/axial mirror axis is CLOSED at 0.70% of mirrored inputs.** It is the correct place
for the medial/lateral question to have relocated to, it was cheap to ask, and the answer is no. A fix
would be free of card time — `Laterality.of_study` could prefer a unanimous geometry over a contradicted
tag — but a change that can reach 0.70% of inputs cannot produce a measurable score move, so it stays
unbuilt rather than unlogged. Re-open by answering the number, not by re-raising the mechanism.

## Every masked adaptation this project ran switched attention OFF, and the gate that catches it is a RATIO — 2026-09-08

**The finding, from researcher D251/D252 (n=240 raw softmax rows, five checkpoints).** Four of four
adapted encoders are degenerate in per-block attention entropy; `adapt_null` (`--lr 0`) reproduces stock
to three decimals, which is the control that makes the other four readable. Two opposite shapes, both
fatal: `adapt_small_e8_unitfix` blocks 8-11 at 5.372 / 5.507 / 5.532 / 5.512 against `ln(257) = 5.549`
(driven to UNIFORM), and `adapt_small_e6`, `adapt_small_e6_lr1e5`, `pretrain_small_matched_e8` block 11 at
0.000 / 0.035 / 0.023 nats (collapsed onto one key). A one-sided margin-to-`ln(N)` test reads the last
three as HEALTHIER than stock and passes the worst checkpoint most comfortably.

**What this retires.** `pretrain_unitfix` drove its loss 0.9122 -> 0.5570 over eight epochs and was read
for a fortnight as an objective fitting. It was an encoder switching attention off: a texture average
needs no routing, and the loss falls while the trunk stops being a trunk. Every flat adaptation score in
this ledger that ran through a masked pretrain is a fact about that, not about the adaptation axis.

**The rate is already excluded as the lever.** `adapt_small_e6` collapsed at 1e-4 and `adapt_small_e6_lr1e5`
at 1e-5; a tenfold cut bought nothing.

**The gate, and the ruler defect it cost to find.** `kneemri.training.attention_health` measures stock at
epoch zero on held slices and refuses any epoch where a block loses too much. Its FIRST version was an
absolute 0.8-nat deviation, sized off D252 where stock spanned 1.7 nats. It refused a healthy encoder three
optimiser steps into a 5e-5 smoke on a trunk spanning 2.48 — and researcher D256 derived the same defect
from the opposite end, measuring stock v3large's top block at 4.657 against `ln(201) = 5.303`, so a block
driven ALL the way to uniform moves 0.646 and PASSES a 0.8 gate. Nats do not survive a change of
configuration. The replacement is `RETENTION_FLOOR = 0.25`: each block must keep at least a quarter of
stock's OWN distance to whichever end it is closer to losing — headroom `ln(keys) - H` over stock's headroom
toward uniform, `H` over stock's `H` away from it. Two-sided, because three of four failed the far way; a
ratio to the same-trunk epoch-zero baseline, so nothing is re-derived per trunk. On D252's own table the
degenerate population keeps <= 11.4% and stock keeps 100%, and that arithmetic is asserted in
`tests/unit/kneemri/training/attention_health.py::test_floor_separates_the_d252_populations`.

**Three harness defects found on the way, all real, none of them the cause.** (1) transformers 5.15.0
defaults to `sdpa`, whose fused kernel never materialises the attention matrix, so `output_attentions=True`
returns a tuple of `None` silently and the check reads as a clean pass — fixed with
`set_attn_implementation('eager')` for the read. (2) A model in `train()` draws stochastic depth and dropout
fresh per forward, so two readings of ONE encoder differ by their draws — the read is forced to `eval()`.
(3) The probe batch is frozen. What settles that all three are now sound is the **`--lr 0` control**: with
the weights pinned, every block of both epochs reads `+0.00` against the reference. The reading is
deterministic to two decimals, so any deviation the gate reports IS the weights.

**The target is not what drives the early transient.** Matched smoke, three steps at 5e-5, identical
masking / seed / slices, only the objective moving: pixel+spectral min retention **0.63**, latent **0.65**.
LIMIT: D252's collapse arrived at epoch 6-8, so this settles the transient and not the endpoint.

**And a published latent-target continuation of this exact trunk is CLEAN** (D256, n=240, raw 201-key rows).
OrthoFoundation — `dinov3-vitl16` continued with DINO-style self-distillation on 1.25M knee images — reads
max |delta| 0.423 nats against stock, no block near either end, prefix mass unmoved (0.123 vs 0.128 at
block 23). So on-domain adaptation of this architecture does NOT have to destroy routing, and the suspect
list narrows from the objective family to OUR recipe: mask ratio 0.6, our rate, our target. That is the
question `latent_adapt` (knee-lm37v) is on the card to answer, and it is why the next arm if it refuses is
the mask ratio and not the objective.

### The latent target dies exactly as the pixel one did, and the mask ratio only bites at 0.15 — 2026-09-08

`latent_adapt` (v3small trunk, `--objective latent --epochs 8 --slices-per-step 96 --lr 1e-4`, mask
ratio 0.6, the `SpectralMaskConfig` default) was **REFUSED by the attention gate at the end of epoch 0**,
790 s in at 306 slices/s — not at epoch 6-8, where every earlier collapse in this family was found:

```
keep 0.90 0.80 0.86 0.98 0.99 0.94 0.98 0.94 0.98 0.79 0.23 0.87   (floor 0.25)
vs stock +0.26 +0.65 +0.41 +0.08 -0.05 -0.25 -0.07 -0.28 -0.11 +0.34 +1.55 +0.12
```

Block 10 drifts **+1.55 nats toward uniform** and keeps 0.23 of stock's own headroom. The arm
pre-registered this as outcome 1 and it is what arrived.

**What it settles.** The TARGET is not the cause. The teacher never degenerated — spread held flat at
0.3836-0.3881 while the latent loss fell 0.387 → 0.0611, so the objective was learning and the routing
collapsed anyway. Pixel+spectral and latent, two unrelated target families, die the same way under the
same masking. Rate was already excluded (1e-4 and 1e-5 both collapsed on this trunk). What the two runs
still share is the **masking**: 60% of patches hidden, on 224px slices of a modality whose informative
structure is sparse and thin.

**And a published counterexample says the objective family is fine.** D256 profiled OrthoFoundation —
this exact `dinov3-vitl16` architecture continued with DINO-style self-distillation on 1.25M knee images
— at n=240 on raw 201-key softmax rows: max |Δ| 0.423 nats (block 10), top-block Δ 0.241, block 23 at
4.416 against stock's 4.657 and 0.887 below uniform, prefix mass 0.123 vs 0.128. A latent-target
on-domain continuation of this trunk keeps its routing. Ours does not. Neither the target nor the corpus
separates them; heavy masking is the largest remaining difference.

**What it costs to ask.** The gate now returns a verdict in ONE epoch, so a refusal costs 13 minutes
rather than the 5.3 h a full 8-epoch pretrain costs. That is what turns the mask ratio from an expensive
commit into an affordable ladder: `latent_mask_ladder.sh` runs 0.30, then 0.15 if 0.30 refuses, stops at
the first rung that survives epoch 0, and spends the remaining seven epochs plus the 12-epoch fine-tune
on that one — against the same `band_dense = 0.8578` control, byte-identical fine-tune stage.

**What it does NOT settle.** It does not price our learning rate against OrthoFoundation's, which is not
published in the abstract and has been asked for (M250 §4, arXiv:2601.18250). And a rung that survives
epoch 0 is not a rung that survives epoch 8 — the gate runs every epoch, and the earlier collapses in
this family all arrived late.

**The ladder answered within the hour, and the ratio is a real but sharply NON-LINEAR dial.** Three rungs,
one epoch each, everything else byte-identical:

```
mask 0.6   b10 +1.55   keep 0.23   REFUSED   790 s @ 306 sl/s
mask 0.30  b10 +1.53   keep 0.24   REFUSED   431 s @ 560 sl/s
mask 0.15  b10 +1.35   keep 0.33   SURVIVED  387 s @ 624 sl/s
```

The first halving moved the failing block by **0.02 nats** — nothing. The second moved it by **0.18**, nine
times as much, and carried `keep` from 0.24 across the 0.25 floor to 0.33. So the ratio is not a dial you
can turn a little: over 0.6 → 0.30 the collapse does not care at all, and only at 0.15 does the trunk begin
to keep its routing. My own pre-registration called rung 0.15 a refusal at b10 ≈ +1.5 / keep ≈ 0.24 and it
came back at +1.35 / 0.33 — the prediction was wrong in the direction that matters, and the ladder is the
reason we know rather than guess.

**What this does and does not license.** `keep 0.33` clears a floor of 0.25 with very little room, on the
epoch where every earlier collapse in this family was still healthy — the gate runs every epoch and the
D252 collapses all arrived at epoch 6-8, so surviving epoch 0 is not surviving the run. The rung is
continuing to eight epochs and then into the 12-epoch fine-tune against the same `band_dense = 0.8578`
control, and the honest reading of the ratio waits for whichever of the two ends it.

**Epoch 1 answered part of that already, and it is the sharper finding: the collapse MIGRATED rather than
stopped.**

```
epoch 0  vs stock … +0.33 +1.35 -0.07 | keep … 0.80 0.33 0.99    block 10 fails, TOWARD uniform
epoch 1  vs stock … +0.03 +0.31 -2.53 | keep … 0.98 0.85 0.53    block 10 heals, block 11 fails, INTO a sink
```

Block 10's uniform drift healed from +1.35 to +0.31 on a single epoch, and block 11 fell the other way:
entropy 2.88 against a stock ~5.4, prefix mass 0.16 → 0.64, two thirds of the attention on the prefix. The
gate still passes on `keep 0.53`, so the arm continues, but "mask 0.15 keeps the routing" is not what the
trunk did. It moved the damage one block up and reversed its sign.

That costs the rate ladder its main argument. The case for walking the rate was that spectral@1e-5 collapsed
into a sink while everything at 1e-4 collapsed toward uniform, so two modes at two rates meant the dial had
never been walked — recorded two paragraphs below, and now half wrong. One run at ONE rate produced both
shapes in adjacent blocks one epoch apart. The shapes are not a rate signature; they are two faces of the same
destruction, the last blocks losing their learned routing with the direction of the fall unowned by any knob
this family has. The ladder still runs (14 minutes for two rungs) but only as a test of whether MAGNITUDE
modulates a destruction whose shape is now rate-independent, which is a much smaller question than the one it
was written for.

**What every collapsing run still shares:** `lr 1e-4` one-cycle, all blocks trainable, our normalisation,
bf16 autocast. And the collapse SHAPES separate by RATE rather than by target or mask — spectral@1e-5
collapsed *away* from uniform (an attention sink: 0.000 / 0.035 / 0.023 nats), while everything at 1e-4
collapses *toward* uniform at the top blocks. Two failure modes at two rates is what `latent_rate_ladder.sh`
is for, and it is armed behind this one: 3e-5 then 1e-5 at mask 0.30, everything else fixed. Drift at block
10 that scales with the rate means gradient magnitude and the fix is rate plus a longer schedule; drift flat
across a 10x rate change means rate is out and the suspect is the trunk/objective interaction itself.

### `latent_register_dense` reads 0.8385 against nothing — the v3small zero point does not exist — 2026-09-09

`latent_register_dense_s2026` (v3small trunk continued with latent-MIM at mask 0.30, then the 12-epoch
dense supervised recipe: `--slice-pooling max --whole-stack --backbone-lr 4e-5 --slices 20 --band-low 0.1
--band-high 0.9`) finished at **0.8385** — epoch 10 of 12, n=909, midpoint cut. `convergence_check` names
it neither TRUNCATED nor STOPPED: the AUC trace runs 0.7221 / 0.7775 / 0.7981 / 0.8097 / 0.8206 / 0.8278 /
0.8344 / 0.8352 / 0.8376 / 0.8380 / **0.8385** / 0.8384, a clean plateau over the last three epochs. The
number is a real converged reading. What it is a reading OF is the problem.

**Its own arm header pre-registered the hole and the hole is real.** `band_dense`'s 0.8578 is a dinov2-small
number and cannot price a v3small encoder. Sweeping every arm carrying `--variant v3small` returns exactly
four scripts, and only one of them is at this supervised recipe: `errors_v3small_s2026`, **0.8280** — which
differs from `latent_register_dense` in TWO ways at once, since it carries `--label-errors` and no
adaptation. So the comparison the arm owed does not exist on disk.

**The transfer that would close the gap is not admissible as a control.** On dinov2 the same flag reads
`errors_dense` 0.8420 against `band_dense` 0.8578, i.e. `--label-errors` costs **−0.0158** there. Carry
that across trunks and a plain v3small lands near 0.844, which puts 0.8385 **inside [0.828, 0.844]**: the
latent adaptation at mask 0.30 is neither shown to help nor shown to hurt. That estimate is a knob-sized
delta measured on one trunk and substituted into a claim about another — the exact move this repo has
already priced wrong twice on the pool-label axis. It brackets; it does not price.

**Two arms have now been spent on an axis whose zero point was never measured, and a third is on the card.**
`latent_register_deep` (mask 0.60) started at 00:16Z. `v3small_control` (knee-j2ovn) is armed behind it —
the same 12-epoch dense recipe, v3small, no `--encoder-weights` and no `--label-errors`, ~2.0 h, no
pretrain stage. It is an INSTRUMENT and its own score is not the deliverable: it makes three holdout
numbers readable at once, one of them still being written. Its branches are in its header — ~0.844 closes
the mask axis on a measured zero, ~0.828 makes the adaptation +0.010 directional and the ladder live, and
anything outside [0.820, 0.850] impeaches every v3small number in this file that was read against a dinov2
control.

**The stock v3small attention line now carries the corrected axis**, printed by `latent_register_deep`'s
own gate at launch (commit `2d440c19`): `Hpatch 0.00 3.34 4.10 1.71 2.97 3.83 4.16 4.37 4.69 4.86 4.97
5.24`, against raw `H 0.00 3.28 3.74 1.73 2.88 3.76 4.03 4.01 4.45 4.45 4.26 5.21` and span 5.21 nats.
Stock registers already hold 0.31 of block 10's mass with cls at 0.01 — the register sink is the trunk's
own resting state, not something adaptation introduced.

### Mask 0.60 survives the corrected ruler through epoch 2 — the refusal that closed this family was the register sink — 2026-09-09

`latent_adapt` was **REFUSED at the end of epoch 0** at mask ratio 0.6 (2026-09-08, above), and that
refusal is what capped the whole masked-adaptation family at 0.30. `latent_register_deep` is the same
ratio on the same v3small trunk, one commit later (`2d440c19`, `AttentionHealth.axis`), and it is three
epochs in and still running. Block 11, the block that carries the disagreement:

| block 11 | stock | e0 | e1 | e2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| raw `H` | 5.21 | 5.41 | **3.25** | **2.49** |
| `Hpatch` | 5.24 | 5.50 | **5.55** | **5.53** |
| prefix mass | 0.06 | 0.08 | 0.68 | **0.82** |
| cls mass | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | **0.00** |

Raw entropy at the top block falls by 2.72 nats — a textbook collapse on the old axis. The patch
distribution behind it **rises** 0.29 nats above stock and holds there. The 0.82 that left the patches is
register mass and the class token, which is the only prefix key a downstream head reads, is at 0.00 on
every epoch. The old gate was measuring how much mass had left the patches and calling that a loss of
discrimination; on a four-register trunk those are unrelated quantities, and this run is the separation
made visible on the ratio where it mattered most.

**What this does NOT yet say.** It is three epochs of eight and `keep` at block 11 is 0.69 / 0.64 / 0.67
against a 0.25 floor — drifting, not settled, and a later refusal is still available. It is an attention
reading, not a score: nothing here says the adaptation makes a better member, and the fine-tune it feeds
still has no control until `v3small_control` (knee-j2ovn) lands behind it. What it does settle is that
the CAP was a measurement artefact. The mask ladder on register trunks was never tested; it was refused
by a ruler that could not see the axis it was refusing on.

**Stock is already sinking into its registers before anything is adapted** — block 10 at 0.31 register
mass, 0.01 cls. So the sink is this trunk's resting behaviour and the adaptation deepens it rather than
introducing it, which is the second reason a gate calibrated on dinov2 (1 prefix key, cls == prefix) could
not be carried across to it unexamined.

### RETRACTION: `latent_adapt` is a dinov2-small run, so it never capped anything on v3small — 2026-09-09

The section immediately above ("Mask 0.60 survives the corrected ruler through epoch 2") is wrong in its
central claim and this is the correction, written thirty minutes later off the same log.

**`latent_adapt` did not run on v3small.** `experiments/arms/latent_adapt.sh` carries no `--variant`, and
`pretrain.py:262` reads `--variant`, `default=SMALL`, where `SMALL` is `facebook/dinov2-small`
(`backbone.py:167`). Its own stock line proves it — `H 3.81 3.18 ...` with no `cls`/`registers` columns,
against v3small's `H 0.00 3.28 ...`. Different family, different block-0 behaviour, and **no registers at
all**, so its refusal at mask 0.6 was taken on the axis that was correct for it. The 2026-09-08 entry
above it calls it "v3small trunk"; that is the same error one day earlier, and it is what I read.

**So the ruler change did not enable this run, and I checked rather than assumed.** Recomputing epoch 7's
retention on the RAW axis by hand — `uniform = ln(446) = 6.100`, `_share` and the two-sided `min` exactly
as `AttentionHealth.retention` spells them — gives `1.00 0.95 0.90 0.94 0.95 0.93 0.96 0.98 0.98 0.99
0.71 0.45`. The minimum is **0.447 against a 0.25 floor: the old ruler passes this run too.** All eight
pretrain epochs completed either way.

**What is actually true, and it is still a finding.** The 0.30 cap on v3small was never measured on
v3small. It was inherited from a dinov2-small refusal and carried across a family boundary — the same
cross-trunk-control defect that leaves `latent_register_dense`'s 0.8385 pricing nothing (knee-j2ovn), in
the same axis, found the same night. v3small at mask 0.60 does not collapse on either ruler. The mask
ladder was closed by a number about a different architecture.

**And the log line that produced the misreading is a real defect, now fixed.** `AttentionHealth.report`
subtracted raw `entropy` for its `vs stock` column while `keep` already read the patch axis, so epoch 7
printed `vs stock -2.88` beside `keep 0.74` for block 11 with nothing saying they were two different
rulers. Both columns now come off `axis` (`test_report`). The `-2.88` was real and so was the `0.74`;
what did not exist was the collapse I read from putting them side by side.

**What survives from the retracted section:** the block-11 masses (prefix 0.85, registers 0.85, cls
**0.00** at epoch 7), the patch distribution holding at 5.46 against stock's 5.24, and stock v3small
already resting at 0.31 register mass on block 10. The mechanism reading stands. The claim that the
corrected ruler is what let the run proceed does not.

## The optimiser-path family already ran, and all three axes close — 2026-09-09

`knee-s9cr` is a P0 that prices six 224 px arms at ~19 min each and asks for the card. All six are on
disk, converged, and scored. The bead has been planning card time for work that was already spent, and
nothing in this file said the family had a reading. Taking it, at zero card cost:

| run | the one flag | holdout | vs control |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `native224_s2026` | control | **0.8502** | — |
| `warm224_long_s2026` | `--warmup 0.25` | 0.8512 | +0.0010 |
| `warm224_brief_s2026` | `--warmup 0.05` | 0.8498 | −0.0004 |
| `clip224_tight_s2026` | `--grad-clip 0.5` | 0.8488 | −0.0014 |
| `decay224_high_s2026` | `--weight-decay 0.1` | 0.8487 | −0.0015 |
| `decay224_low_s2026` | `--weight-decay 0.005` | 0.8454 | −0.0048 |
| `clip224_s2026` | `--grad-clip 1.0` | 0.8439 | −0.0063 |

`convergence_check` flags none of the seven as TRUNCATED, so every row is the recipe's number and not a
floor. n=909, midpoint cut.

**All three axes close, and they close the strong way — by BRACKETING.** Each is a pair straddling the
inherited constant: warmup 0.05 / 0.25 around 0.15, decay 0.005 / 0.1 around 0.02, clip 0.5 / 1.0 against
no ceiling at all. A single arm on one side of a constant cannot close anything, because a null there is
also what a wrongly-signed step looks like. A pair that is flat on BOTH sides says the constant sits on a
plateau. Every one of the six lands inside [−0.0063, +0.0010] against a 0.0062 floor, and the widest
excursion is NEGATIVE. There is no unnamed optimiser tweak here.

**What that does to `knee-s9cr`'s thesis.** The bead's argument was that a forum poster went 0.934 → 0.942
on unnamed "tweaks" at 224 px, and that the way to find an unnamed tweak is to try many cheaply. The
throughput half of that argument stands and is measured — 94 s/epoch against 290, for −0.0023. The search
half has now been run on the three most obvious candidates and returned three plateaus. Whatever carried
that poster's +0.008, it is not the optimiser path.

### Correction: `clip224_tight` is gradient clipping, not a CLIP trunk

The 2026-09-04 section above records it as "CLIP trunk, tight 224 px crop". Both halves are wrong.
`experiments/arms/clip224_tight.sh` is `native224`'s recipe with `--grad-clip 0.5` and nothing else moved,
on the same trunk and the same 224 px cache; its own header says so. The row was written from the arm's
NAME, and `clip` was read as the contrastive-language-image model rather than as the ceiling on a
gradient norm.

The number in that row, 0.8488, is right. Its description is not, and it mattered: read as a CLIP trunk
the row is evidence about architectural diversity in the pool, and read correctly it is one point on the
clipping dose curve above. This is the second name-read-instead-of-flag defect found today; the first is
`latent_adapt`'s absent `--variant` (retraction above, knee-q8ah2). Both were found by opening the arm
file rather than by reasoning about the ledger entry.

## The mask ratio is not an axis on the register trunk — `latent_register_deep` 0.8378 — 2026-09-09

The rung the 0.30 cap was blocking, run now that the cap is known to have been inherited from a
dinov2-small refusal (retraction above, knee-q8ah2). Pre-registered branch **2**.

| run | mask | holdout | vs dense |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `latent_register_dense_s2026` | 0.30 | **0.8385** (e10 of 12) | — |
| `latent_register_deep_s2026` | 0.60 | 0.8378 (e9 of 12) | −0.0007 |

Identical trunk, recipe, backbone rate, seed, slices and band — one flag apart. `convergence_check`
flags neither. n=909, midpoint cut.

**Both halves of the pre-registration were wrong about where the interest was, and that is the finding.**
Branch 3 said 0.60 might refuse and that the refusal would be the first real reading of the trunk's
limit. It did not refuse — all 8 pretrain epochs completed, and block 11 settles at prefix 0.85 with
**cls 0.00**, so the sink is entirely register mass and the one prefix key a downstream head reads never
moves. Branch 1 said a win would make the ratio a ladder. It is not a win.

**The epoch-by-epoch track is what closes this, not the final number.** Against dense: e2 .7994/.7981,
e4 .8219/.8206, e6 .8332/.8344, e8 .8373/.8376, e9 .8378/.8380, e11 .8376/.8384. Nine consecutive epochs
inside ±0.002. Doubling the mask ratio does not move the fine-tune at any point on the curve, so this is
not a converged-to-the-same-place result that a longer budget might separate — the two runs are the same
run.

**So adaptation STRENGTH is not what bounds this member, and that closure is now clean.** It could not be
stated before today, because the gate was refusing the rungs that would have tested it and the gate was
reading the wrong axis on a register trunk. With the ruler corrected and the cap shown to be a
cross-family inheritance, a flat 0.30→0.60 is a fact about the objective rather than about the
instrument. The masked-adaptation family does not have room in the mask ratio.

**Not rostered.** 0.8378 solo, below the 0.8459 merit level this pool has ever added at, and
Pearson 0.9427 against `latent_register_dense` on all 10908 holdout cells — the same predictions from a
near-identical run. `latent_register_dense` is on the roster for diversity (the only v3small trunk
carrying an on-domain latent-MIM adaptation); a second copy of it adds nothing that argument does not
already have. Declined in writing.

**What is still open on this member, and it is the reason `v3small_control` is on the card.** Neither
0.8385 nor 0.8378 prices the adaptation at all, because no run exists with this trunk and this recipe and
NO `--encoder-weights` (knee-j2ovn). `v3small_control` is that run and started 01:39:55Z. At epoch 1 it
reads 0.7833 against dense's 0.7775 and deep's 0.7762 — ahead of both, on one epoch, which is worth
nothing yet and is written down so it cannot be discovered later as a surprise.

## The latent-MIM adaptation is worth +0.0014 over no adaptation at all — `v3small_control` 0.8371 — 2026-09-09

The zero point this family never had. `latent_register_dense` (0.8385) and `latent_register_deep`
(0.8378) had only ever been priced against EACH OTHER, which measures the mask ratio and nothing else.
`v3small_control` is the same trunk, the same fine-tune recipe, the same seed, slices and band, with the
`--encoder-weights` line removed — the published v3small, unadapted.

| member                        | adaptation            | solo   | vs control |
|-------------------------------|-----------------------|--------|------------|
| `latent_register_dense_s2026` | latent MIM, mask 0.30 | 0.8385 | **+0.0014** |
| `latent_register_deep_s2026`  | latent MIM, mask 0.60 | 0.8378 | **+0.0007** |
| `v3small_control_s2026`       | none                  | 0.8371 | —          |

All three converged — `convergence_check` reports none of them TRUNCATED, STOPPED or UNDERTRAINED, so
these are the recipes' own numbers and not facts about a killed process. The whole family spans 0.0014,
against the 0.0062 noise floor measured this morning on the seven-arm 224 px optimiser bracket. **On
solo score, the on-domain latent adaptation buys nothing.** That closes the axis: not the mask ratio
(closed separately today at nine epoch-matched points inside ±0.002), but the adaptation itself.

### What this does NOT close, and the number that says so

The seat argument for `latent_register_dense` was never its solo score — it is rostered as the only
v3small trunk carrying an on-domain adaptation, which is a DIVERSITY claim. That claim survives, and the
correlations are the reason to keep it rather than a hope:

    Pearson dense vs control  0.9098   over 10908 holdout cells, max|diff| 0.6577
    Pearson deep  vs control  0.9131   over 10908 holdout cells, max|diff| 0.6034
    Pearson deep  vs dense    0.9427   over 10908 holdout cells, max|diff| 0.5814

The adapted members sit FURTHER from the unadapted control (0.910, 0.913) than they do from each other
(0.943). So the adaptation does move the model — it just moves it sideways rather than up. A member that
scores the same and predicts differently is exactly what an ensemble seat is for, and it is exactly what
a solo ruler cannot see. Read the other way round, this is the third measurement this week where the
in-distribution solo number and the redundancy number disagree about the same checkpoint.

What is closed is spending more CARD on this family: a third mask ratio, a longer adaptation, or another
objective on this trunk all have to beat a ceiling that has now been measured at +0.0014 over doing
nothing. The re-opening condition is an ENSEMBLE reading, not a solo one — if a seat study ever shows
`dense` adding where `control` does not, that is the adaptation paying in the only currency it has.

## The generalisation gap is a FLAT TOLL, not a re-ranking — eleven members, decode −0.0336 ± 0.0038 — 2026-09-09

The first measurement this project has ever made of what a member loses under a real distribution shift.
`foreign_readout` scores every member three ways on the SAME 909-study holdout under the SAME labels:
`native` as the ledger has it, `kept` on our own pixels routed through the shifted code path, and
`foreign` on his independent decode of the same studies. `kept − native` is a plumbing self-check that
must read ~0; `foreign − kept` is the only pixel number.

**Read the void notice first.** An earlier run of this same tool reported these members dropping about
−0.08, and that number is WRONG and must not be quoted. `foreign_readout` sized its read window against
`slab.corpus.slices` — his raw 44 — while `MappedSlab` SERVES the member's own slice count. Six 20-slice
members were scored on `view[:, :, 12:32]` of a 20-deep stack: **eight slices of twenty, silently**, with
a plausible number logged. Five 12-slice members took the same defect's loud face, an empty view that
raised inside dinov2 as a reshape of zero elements. Fixed under knee-kcvma by declaring `HoldoutSlab.depth`
as the SERVED depth, overriding it in `MappedSlab`, and adding `HoldoutPredictions.fits`, which now refuses
a window the served stack cannot carry rather than scoring whatever it overlaps. The table below is the
re-run, eleven of eleven, and its `slot_cost` column is what licenses reading it at all.

| member                          | native | kept   | foreign | slots   | **decode** |
|---------------------------------|--------|--------|---------|---------|------------|
| `stackfit_s2026`                | 0.8631 | 0.8631 | 0.8326  | −0.0000 | **−0.0305** |
| `band_dense_hold_s2026`         | 0.8573 | 0.8573 | 0.8213  | +0.0000 | −0.0360 |
| `small_feat_fit_s2026`          | 0.8571 | 0.8571 | 0.8217  | −0.0001 | −0.0354 |
| `crop160_span_s2026`            | 0.8564 | 0.8565 | 0.8300  | +0.0001 | **−0.0265** |
| `mixup_dense_s2026`             | 0.8552 | 0.8552 | 0.8254  | +0.0000 | −0.0298 |
| `mixup224_strong_s2026`         | 0.8516 | 0.8515 | 0.8174  | −0.0001 | −0.0341 |
| `warm224_long_s2026`            | 0.8512 | 0.8512 | 0.8173  | +0.0001 | −0.0339 |
| `aug_long_s2026`                | 0.8511 | 0.8511 | 0.8115  | −0.0000 | **−0.0396** |
| `native224_s2026`               | 0.8502 | 0.8502 | 0.8119  | −0.0000 | −0.0383 |
| `tissue224_s2026`               | 0.8491 | 0.8491 | 0.8165  | −0.0000 | −0.0326 |
| `latent_register_dense_s2026`   | 0.8385 | 0.8386 | 0.8061  | +0.0001 | −0.0325 |

Every `slot_cost` lands inside ±0.0001, so the shifted path serves our own pixels back at our own score
and the third column is about HIS PIXELS and nothing else. Denominator: 11 of 11 members in the pool,
all scored, none dropped.

### 1. The toll is flat — nobody is robust and nobody is fragile

`decode_cost` is **−0.0336 mean, sd 0.0038, spanning 0.0131 end to end.** The spread of the drop is
half the spread of the native scores it is drawn from (sd 0.0063), and the foreign column's spread
(0.0080) is barely wider than the native one. Eleven members across mixup, span cropping, tissue
normalisation, band selection, latent-MIM adaptation, two image sizes and two slice counts all pay
within a third of a point of each other. **There is no robust member in this pool.** Whatever this shift
costs, it is charged to the architecture family, not to the recipe — which is precisely why no amount of
reseating inside this pool has ever moved the board.

### 2. The offline ruler DOES transfer — Spearman ρ = 0.8818, p = 0.0003

Native rank against foreign rank over the eleven: **ρ 0.8818 (p 0.0003)**. The best native member is the
best foreign member; the worst is the worst. Four members move at all and none moves more than three
places. This settles a question that has been open in prose for a week: *the offline number is not lying
about which member is better under a shifted decode.* It ranks them the same.

### 3. A better member does NOT pay more for it — ρ(native, decode) = 0.1727, p = 0.61

The standing worry was that our small offline gains are bought with fragility — that a member half a
point better on our decode has overfitted our decode and will give it back. **Measured, it is not
happening.** The correlation between a member's native score and what it loses is 0.1727 with p = 0.61,
which over eleven points is nothing at all. And the two members that drop LEAST (`crop160_span` −0.0265,
`stackfit` −0.0305) are the 4th and 1st best natively. Fragility is not the price of the offline gain.

Also refuted, on the same numbers: the claim that **augmentation** members drop most. They occupy both
ends — `aug_long` is the worst in the pool at −0.0396 and `mixup_dense` is third-best at −0.0298.
Augmentation as a CLASS predicts nothing here.

### What it does point at, and it is the lever

The one member that separates from the pack is `crop160_span` at **−0.0265, a third less than the pool
mean and 0.0131 better than the worst.** That is mechanism-consistent rather than a coincidence of
ranking: D206 §5 measured his span running **20–50% wider than ours at the median**, three to four times
wider on the coronal-side blocks for a tenth of studies, and D205's control put resampling at ~0 of the
difference — so SPAN is most of what this instrument prices, and the
member trained at the WIDEST FIELD is the member that pays least for it. `crop160_span` is a fixed
160 mm crop at 420 px, not a jittered one — it is the only member in the pool whose field of view was
moved out toward his, and it is the one that pays least. Read together with §1, the pool has no
robustness axis *because every other member was fitted at one fixed 130 mm field*.

Note what that costs and does not cost: `crop160_span` reads 0.8564 against its own control
`band_span` 0.8565 — **NULL on our decode, best in the pool on his.** A member that is free
in-distribution and 0.0071 cheaper out of it is exactly the shape an offline solo ruler cannot see, and
it is the third measurement this week where the solo number and the out-of-sample number disagree about
one checkpoint.

That is a member-shaped lever, not a seating one. The arm it argues for is field-of-view JITTER — a
randomised crop extent rather than a second fixed one — because §1 says the pool's problem is that no
member ever saw the extent VARY, and a single wider fixed field trades one blind spot for another. The re-opening condition for the rest of this family is
the same as it has always been — an ensemble reading, not another solo one.

### `fovjitter160` reads NULL — jitter buys nothing the wide field had not already bought (2026-09-09)

The deciding reading is in, taken by `experiments/arms/fovjitter160_read.sh` on the card, with both
anchors reproducing to the fourth decimal — which is what licenses reading the third row at all:

| member                  | native | kept   | foreign | slots   | **decode** | vs 2026-09-09 pool |
| `crop160_span_s2026`    | 0.8564 | 0.8565 | 0.8300  | +0.0001 | **−0.0265** | reproduced exactly |
| `band_dense_hold_s2026` | 0.8573 | 0.8573 | 0.8213  | +0.0000 | **−0.0360** | reproduced exactly |
| `fovjitter160_s2026`    | 0.8544 | 0.8545 | 0.8248  | +0.0001 | **−0.0297** | new |

Against the arm's own pre-registered branches (`fovjitter160.sh:47-57`), −0.0297 lands in **NULL**
(−0.0265 to −0.0300): indistinguishable from the fixed wide field, +1.0 sd off the pool mean where the
fixed field is +1.87 sd. So **jittering the extent is not the mechanism.** Whatever `crop160_span` has,
randomising the width does not add to it, and per D269 (b) this was — as far as that search reaches —
the first direct test of fixed-wide against jittered extent on a transfer endpoint. It answers.

What it does NOT settle is whether the WIDTH is the mechanism. Both wide members sit above the pool and
the only 130 mm member in this reading sits at the pool mean, but that ordering is n=1 per cell and each
cell is a whole training run, so it stays directional and does not clear the bar on its own. The live
discriminator is D269 (c) — the padding composition — and it needs no new training: `crop_coverage`
records that only ~40% of series can fill a 160 mm field, so 60% of both wide members' studies are
pad-filled. If their lower toll is concentrated in the studies that FILL the field, the extent reading
survives; if it is flat across the two subsets, the extent story is wrong whatever the pooled number
says. That split is a subset AUC over per-study probabilities, which `foreign_readout --per-study` now
writes (commit `1e9f02ad`), so it costs one ~5 min readout and then nothing ever again.

### The CARVE budget sweep: adapting the norm affines per study CANNOT buy decode, at any budget — 2026-09-09

`carve_budget_sweep` ran three of its four pre-registered points against member `fovjitter160_s2026`
(native 0.8544) and the fourth was refused before it started. Ordered by how far the adapted parameters
actually travel — Adam displaces a parameter by roughly the learning rate per step whatever the gradient
is, so `lr x steps` IS the displacement, against LayerNorm affines of order 1.0:

| point    | lr    | steps | \|dθ\| | kept   | foreign | slots   | **decode** | total   |
|----------|-------|-------|--------|--------|---------|---------|------------|---------|
| control  | —     | 0     | 0      | 0.8544 | —       | —       | **-0.0297**| —       |
| `lr3s2`  | 1e-3  | 2     | ~2e-3  | 0.8504 | 0.8196  | -0.0040 | **-0.0309**| -0.0348 |
| `lr3s10` | 1e-3  | 10    | ~1e-2  | 0.8091 | 0.7736  | -0.0453 | **-0.0355**| -0.0808 |
| `lr2s2`  | 1e-2  | 2     | ~2e-2  | 0.7570 | 0.7210  | -0.0974 | **-0.0360**| -0.1334 |
| `lr2s10` | 1e-2  | 10    | ~1e-1  | REFUSED — see below                              |

**THE READING IS NOT "MONOTONE DAMAGE", IT IS SHARPER THAN THAT, AND THE TWO COLUMNS SAY DIFFERENT
THINGS.** Both are monotone in |dθ|, but by wildly different amounts. Across a **ten-thousand-fold**
range of displacement the decode cost moves **0.0063** — from -0.0297 to -0.0360, and it moves in the
WRONG direction the whole way. Over the same range `kept` falls **0.0974**, from 0.8504 to 0.7570. So
per-study adaptation of the norm affines does not trade member quality for decode: it spends the member
and buys nothing. There is no budget at which the decode cost turns, and the first point — a 0.002%
perturbation, small enough that a null there could have been dismissed as no-op — already carries the
sign that every larger one confirms.

That kills the ONE reading that would have licensed more card on this axis. BUDGET DAMAGES was the
branch that says "the felt sizes are destructive, try smaller"; the flat decode column says smaller does
not help either, because the decode cost is not budget-limited at all. It is REPRESENTATION-BOUND with
the model-side lever removed rather than untested: the affines are not where the missing information is.

**THE FOURTH POINT WAS REFUSED BY DECISION, and this row is not a measurement.** |dθ| ~ 1e-1 is past the
line the arm's own header drew — "the trunk is being broken, not adapted" — a catastrophe guaranteed
before it ran, changing no branch after it, for ~50 minutes of a card that had `ortho_lora` waiting.
`after_ortholora.sh` killed the reader at the gate; the sweep's own `SWEEP SWEEP DONE` marker in
`logs/after_budget.log` (`=== BUDGET SWEEP DONE ===`) is therefore the marker of a truncated sweep, not a complete one. Anyone
re-reading that log gets the same three points and this note.

**0.8349 at e10, against control `ortho_dense` 0.8452. Delta −0.0103, outside the 0.0062 paired floor,
