### D272 prices the warm-start collapse, and the repeat-geometry policy FLIPS — card-free, 2026-09-09

M273 asked one number: does a warm start collapse the diversity D267 measured in the 41-run cluster
(within-cluster r 0.8234@cluster75_pairs, median 0.883, seed floor 0.9746)? D272 answered on the same
statistic, population and cut.

| pair                                            | r      | pct of 2775 | short of seed floor |
|-------------------------------------------------|--------|-------------|---------------------|
| `warm_calib_dense` -> parent `calib_dense_hold`   | 0.9398 | 96.6        | 0.0348              |
| `warm_calib_lowlr` -> same parent                 | 0.9421 | 97.4        | 0.0325              |
| the two warm SIBLINGS against each other          | 0.9382 | 96.0        | 0.0364              |
| `cnx_warm_anneal` -> `cnx_own_recipe`             | 0.9091 | 75.5        | 0.0655              |
| `swin_distill_fit` -> `swin_distill_pre`          | 0.8801 | 47.5        | 0.0945              |
| `raptor_feat_fit` -> `raptor_feat_pre`            | 0.8556 | 33.6        | 0.1190              |
| `small_feat_fit` -> `small_feat_pre`              | 0.7916 | 22.2        | 0.1830              |

**The middle branch, which is the one that was not pre-decided.** A warm child sits at the 97th
percentile toward its parent — far closer than recipe variation, whose median is 0.883 — and stops 0.033
short of a seed twin. The SIBLING row is the sharper one: two children of one parent differing only in
rate correlate 0.9382 with each other, inside the same-recipe same-seed rerun bracket (0.958 mean, q5
0.917). That is the all-warm cluster in miniature and it reads PARTIAL COLLAPSE — warm siblings
correlate like re-runs, not like recipe variation. The four pre->fit rows span 0.79-0.91 with one BELOW
the cold median, so the factor is not a property of the operation; it tracks how much optimisation the
child still does. n is 2 children and 1 parent on the headline and D272 states it: directional, not a
constant.

**THE POLICY FLIPS ANYWAY, and the reason is not the correlation — it is what the diversity is worth.**
`geometry_check` measured 161.1 h, 52% of every card-hour this project has spent, refitting a geometry
already fitted, roughly 100 h of it recoverable by warm starting. The objection was that those refits
bought diversity. They did, and D272 says a warm start would erode part of it. But it is diversity **on
the axis the board has answered seven times flat**: sixteen offline seat ADDs negative, the seating
family's entire ceiling 0.0013 offline against a board that cannot resolve 0.0030, and both seats that
ever moved the board out-of-distribution members rather than in-cluster variants. Trading a decoration
on a measured-out axis for card-hours is the right side of that trade with the gap at 0.010 and the
deadline on 2026-10-22. **A repeat fingerprint is warm-started from now on unless the arm's question is
about the trunk's own initialisation.**

**`geometry_check` still does not BLOCK.** The erosion is partial rather than nil, and D272's fit-pairs
include a warm child FARTHER from its parent than two cold runs are from each other, so a hard gate
would spend a real asset to save a judgement. Its closing line changed from "a repeat is a WARM-START
CANDIDATE, not a verdict" to the recommendation plus the price. If the call is challenged, the arm that
settles it is the one D272 named and nobody has run: two children of `calib_dense_hold` under the two
most DIFFERENT objectives in the cluster, correlated — which prices the collision instead of inferring
it from rate-siblings.

### PADDING BITES is refuted three of three; EXTENT is withdrawn for want of a matched control — card-free, 2026-09-09

`fov_perstudy_read` wrote the per-study probabilities once, and `padding_split` cut them on whether a
study fills the 160 mm field. **430 fill, 479 are padded up to it** — close to `crop_coverage`'s 40/60.

| member                  | crop / px / slices | subset          | kept   | foreign | toll        |
|-------------------------|--------------------|-----------------|--------|---------|-------------|
| `fovjitter160_s2026`    | 160 / 420 / 12     | pooled n=909    | 0.8545 | 0.8248  | **-0.0297** |
|                         |                    | fills  n=430    | 0.8640 | 0.8320  | **-0.0320** |
|                         |                    | padded n=479    | 0.8469 | 0.8192  | **-0.0277** |
| `crop160_span_s2026`    | 160 / 420 / 12     | pooled n=909    | 0.8565 | 0.8300  | **-0.0265** |
|                         |                    | fills  n=430    | 0.8666 | 0.8402  | **-0.0264** |
|                         |                    | padded n=479    | 0.8484 | 0.8211  | **-0.0272** |
| `band_dense_hold_s2026` | 130 / 336 / 20     | pooled n=909    | 0.8573 | 0.8213  | **-0.0360** |
|                         |                    | fills  n=430    | 0.8690 | 0.8282  | **-0.0408** |
|                         |                    | padded n=479    | 0.8477 | 0.8162  | **-0.0315** |

**PADDING BITES is REFUTED, and it is the one branch this file settles.** It predicted that padded
studies carry a WORSE transfer toll — the composed failure mode, pad learned as a site cue. They carry a
BETTER one, or the same, in every member: -0.0277 against -0.0320, -0.0272 against -0.0264, -0.0315
against -0.0408. Three of three, and the two that separate do so in the direction opposite to the
prediction. Each individual gap is inside the bootstrap intervals, so the SIZE is not a reading; the
uniform SIGN across three members with different crops, resolutions and slice counts is, and it points
away from the mechanism rather than at it.

**A floor effect is the reason to believe it rather than a confound against it.** Padded studies are
simply harder — kept AUC is lower on them for all three members, the 130 mm one INCLUDED, which is a
member that pads nothing at 160 mm. So "fills" is a difficulty label as much as a geometry label, and a
harder subset has less headroom to lose in transfer. That biases toward finding a smaller toll on padded
studies, which is what we found — so the refutation is if anything under-stated, not manufactured.

**EXTENT SURVIVES and EXTENT FAILS are WITHDRAWN, not answered.** Both are statements about the wide
members' ADVANTAGE by subset, so both need a narrow control that differs in crop ALONE.
`band_dense_hold` is not one: it moves crop 160->130, resolution 420->336 and slice count 12->20 in the
same step. Reading a wide-minus-narrow difference off this table would charge to extent whatever those
other two flags did, and the differences in question (-0.0024 on fills, +0.0007 on padded) are an order
inside the intervals anyway. This is the SECOND half of this arm withdrawn for a missing control — the
by-rule half went with `fovjitter160_reflect`'s killed checkpoint. The arm bought one clean refutation
and two withdrawals, and the refutation is the composed failure mode D269 (c) was actually built for.

**Cost: zero card.** The per-study file was already on disk; every cut above is arithmetic on it. That is
the whole case for `--per-study` and it paid on its first use.

### `carve_adapt_read` reads a null on a 2e-5 perturbation — NOT a null on CARVE (2026-09-09)

The arm ran at 12:38Z against a control taken in the same hour on the same card, differing in the single
flag `--adapt`. The control reproduced the recorded table to the fourth decimal, which is what licenses
reading the adapt column at all:

| member                  | control decode | adapt decode | delta   |
| `fovjitter160_s2026`    | −0.0297        | −0.0298      | −0.0001 |
| `crop160_span_s2026`    | −0.0265        | −0.0266      | −0.0001 |
| `band_dense_hold_s2026` | −0.0360        | −0.0359      | +0.0001 |

Mean control **−0.030733**, mean adapt **−0.030767**, delta **−0.000033**.

**This may not be cited as a NULL on CARVE, and the arm's pre-registered NULL branch does not fire.**
The branch says the toll is representation-bound and the model-side lever closes. That conclusion needs
a mechanism that FIRED, and the arithmetic says this one could not have mattered whether it fired or not.

The mechanism did run — `test_on_moves_the_affines_while_it_is_open` asserts the affines move inside the
context manager, and the path is plumbed (`foreign_readout.py:256` → `holdout_predictions.py:123` →
`CardinalityAwareLN.on`). The defect is the SIZE of the step. Adam displaces a parameter by approximately
the learning rate per step regardless of the gradient, so `steps = 2` at `lr = 1e-5` moves LayerNorm
affines of order 1.0 by about **2e-5** — a perturbation of 0.002%. A reading cannot move by 0.036 under
that, and ours moved by 0.00003, which is the size the arithmetic predicts. A delta three orders inside
the NULL band, landing on the control to the fourth decimal on all three members, is the signature of a
budget that cannot act, not of a mechanism that acted and failed.

So the two numbers `2` and `1e-5` are now the suspects. They arrived here from prose. M274 asks the
researcher for CARVE's optimiser, learning rate and step count as the paper states them, what parameters
it actually adapts, and — the cheapest way the published number and this null are both true — whether the
optimiser is SGD rather than Adam, since under SGD the step is lr × gradient and 1e-5 means something
entirely different.

Meanwhile the budget stopped being a constant: `foreign_readout` now takes `--adapt-lr` and
`--adapt-steps`, and logs `|dtheta| ~ steps × lr` on every adapted run so a future reading states its own
perturbation size in its own log. The sweep is minutes of card per point. If a larger budget moves the
decode cost, the mechanism is live and the only open question is which setting is CARVE's. If NO budget
moves it, THAT is the representation-bound finding — and it will be a much stronger one than this,
because it will have been measured over a range where the perturbation was large enough to be felt.

### `fovjitter160_reflect` was KILLED at epoch 6/12 — the padding rule is UNANSWERED (2026-09-09)

The arm asked one thing: does a REFLECTED margin beat the border-replicate one when the jitter window
runs off the acquired field. Control was `fovjitter160_s2026` — same cache, same recipe, same seed, same
0.20 jitter, one flag moved — so it cost no extra card. It was killed at epoch 6 of 12, holdout 0.8422 at
epoch 5.

**Nothing from those six epochs is a fact about padding.** The recipe is `one_cycle`, so a run truncated
mid-schedule never runs its anneal; `convergence_check` reads such a score as a FLOOR, and no comparable
`decode_cost` exists because the checkpoint the reading needs was never written. Both pre-registered
branches — PADDING CARRIES (≥0.0038 better, the pool's own sd) and NULL (within ±0.0038) — remain open.
It may be re-run; it may not be cited.

Why it was killed, stated so the decision is auditable rather than a gap in the log: the arm produces no
shippable member and neither of its branches is an improvement — it is an INSTRUMENT, and the only thing
it licenses is a widened-jitter arm whose mechanism the D270 survey undercut the same morning (no paper
prices a classifier toll against reflection or crop-inside, and the FOV axis itself already read NULL one
section above). Against that it was holding the card in front of `carve_adapt_read`, which is minutes of
card for a published +0.035 against a 0.010 board gap. Zeros padding was never tried and stays rejected
on mechanism: 60% of series are already pad-filled at 160 mm (`crop_coverage`: image@160 over 733 of 1822
series), so a zeros margin would be indistinguishable from padding the pipeline already produces.

### D270 — what the literature says can shrink a toll like ours, and the two numbers withdrawn (2026-09-09)

The −0.0336 foreign-decode toll is flat across eleven members (sd 0.0038, ρ(native, decode_cost) 0.1727,
p 0.61). D270 is the researcher's ranked survey of every published method that shrinks a CLASSIFIER toll
in that cell, with its denominator attached, and it contains two retractions of their own earlier D266.

**CARVE (arXiv:2607.15556) is the only published result in our exact cell** — model fixed, multi-label,
normalisation already paid. Its equations, which arrived while `carve_adapt_read.sh` was still queued and
so corrected the objective before it read anything (`kneemri/inference/norm_adaptation.py`, commit
`36a3e2d2`):

- Eq. 8 — `k̂ = clip(round(Σⱼ p̄ⱼ), k_min, k_max)`, p̄ the entropy-retained-view average, k_min 1, k_max 8.
  Estimated label-free from the Bernoulli probabilities, which is what makes it usable here at all.
- Eq. 9 — with 𝒫 = TopK_k̂(p) and 𝒩 its complement,
  `L = −(1/|𝒫|) Σ_𝒫 log p − λ_neg (1/|𝒩|) Σ_𝒩 log(1−p)`, λ_neg 0.8. **Each term is meaned over its OWN
  set.** The draft written from prose divided both by the label count; at our median k̂ of 3 of 12 that is
  a quarter-weight sharpening term against 10/12 suppression.
- Recipe constants: V=8 weak views, retain the lowest-entropy 25%, Adam 1e-5, 2 steps, norm-affine only,
  episodic reset per scan. The dispersion gate τ=0.091 is for ABSTENTION only — the paper's own Fig. 6
  shows it is near-random as a viability detector, so it must not be used as one.

**THE HONEST COMPARATOR IS +0.036, NOT +0.034.** Internal CT-RATE 0.713→0.749 = +0.036; external
RAD-ChestCT 0.499→0.533 = +0.034 **from a near-chance base**, which is an operating-point repair rather
than a toll recovery; fVLM external 0.612→0.642 = +0.030. Our ρ=0.8818 ruler transfer is the paper's
INTERNAL regime, so +0.036 is the number `carve_adapt_read`'s branches are set against. Both cohorts were
HU-clipped and mm-resampled, so the toll CARVE shrinks is post-physical-normalisation — the same cell as
ours. The paper also warns the base-model gap (+0.11 between backbones) exceeds any adapter gain.

**The ranking below CARVE, and why every larger number is not larger.** CoWA (arXiv:2607.03715) is the one
unpriced neighbour — co-occurrence-weighted entropy on BN affines, six cross-institution CXR shifts; its
norm ablation is verifiable (AUROC 74.7±8.0 for ℓ_F vs 71.1/69.8/70.6) but **its Table 1 absolutes are
image-locked in both HTML and PDF**, so pull them from github.com/woojin716/CoWA before quoting a
CoWA-vs-TENT delta. DISARM++ +0.32 AUC (n=41, logistic regression on PCA'd features) and Saponaro +0.09
(ABIDE, ComBat on FreeSurfer morphometry with a Random Forest) are both measured against RAW baselines or
a feature endpoint: their delta buys back normalisation this repo already pays. LUMINA's deltas are
figure-only. Kim 2026 TB-SFDA is +0.011 AUROC and says itself that AUROC is harder to move than F1.

**Albert 2023 is independent literature-side support for our flat −0.0336.** Rectal MRI, 201 patients, six
centres, all arms N4-corrected: z-score is significantly worse than percentile+HM (which matches our
Lu-2024 null), normaliser choice buys ~0.01–0.03 AUC, and **no normaliser repairs the cross-centre
classifier toll** — Dworak collapses to ~0.52–0.58 AUC regardless. The most honest controlled comparison
found, and it says from the literature's side what our eleven members say from ours.

**A standing warning against the obvious next move.** "I Can't Believe TTA Is Not Better"
(arXiv:2604.09697) measures standard augmentation-averaging TTA on twelve medical combos: it DEGRADES
accuracy in 11 of 12, up to −31.6 points, mechanism BN-statistic mismatch. Our backbones are ViT/LN so the
named mechanism may not transfer, but shift-axis TTA is a hypothesis here, not a free lunch — gate it
per-member against a single-pass control.

**Two numbers withdrawn, both the researcher's own.** D266's "Caldera/DISARM++ 0.857→0.899" **does not
appear in the paper** — the verifiable DISARM++ classifier number is 0.6284→0.9459 (n=41, feature-LR, raw
baseline). And D266's mechanism claim for Saponaro was wrong: it is ComBat on FreeSurfer morphometric
FEATURES, not histogram matching and not pixels.

**Silent cells — nothing published, so no slot may be spent expecting a comparator.** BN/LN statistic
re-estimation on an MRI acquisition-shift classifier; test-time-only histogram matching; re-sampling TTA
over the decode axis; physics-parameter randomisation on a classifier; N4 on a classifier endpoint. And
the train-time side is thinner still: the medical shift-robustness literature is overwhelmingly
segmentation (BigAug, LDDG, RAS4DG, Karani, SITTA, InTEnt, DG-TTA), VORTEX's endpoint is reconstruction
with zero classifier numbers, and **no paper prices a classifier toll against consistency-across-decodes
or shift-invariance losses.** LDDG reports BigAug FAILED to generalise for skin-lesion classification,
which is consistent with our own n=11 flatness under mixup/crop/size variation.

### The field of view, per study, for all 4407 — 46% fill 160 mm and 97% fill 130 mm (2026-09-09)

The ~40% figure the paragraph above leans on came from `crop_coverage`, which measures RETAINED TISSUE
and so answers a related but different question. The physical width itself had never been read: the
`field_of_view_mm` axis was DECLARED on `StudyMetadata` and filled by nothing, and no
`canonical_metadata.csv` existed on disk. Three edits (`3fd73ee1`) and one `build_cache --metadata-only`
pass — **3.5 min of CPU, no card** — now answer it for every study, with no study unanswered.

The statistic is `min(rows × spacing[0], columns × spacing[1])`, the NARROWEST side, because a square mm
crop is bounded by whichever side runs out first; a 320×160 px frame at 0.5 mm is pad on two sides of a
130 mm crop however wide the other axis reads. `pixel_spacing` alone reports the ROW pitch and cannot
answer this. Per study it is the minimum over the series that answered, which is the one axis in
`Study.metadata()` deliberately NOT unanimity-gated: the study is fed to a member through several series
and the binding constraint on padding is the narrowest of them, so disagreement is not an absence of an
answer, it is the answer being the minimum — and gating it would blank exactly the multi-plane studies
the padding split needs.

| statistic | mm | | extent | studies that fill it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| mean | 154.39 | | 120 mm | 97.8% |
| sd | 16.67 | | 130 mm | 97.2% |
| min | 70.33 | | 140 mm | 83.3% |
| median | 159.36 | | 150 mm | 66.6% |
| 75th pct | 160.00 | | **160 mm** | **46.0% (2027/4407)** |
| max | 220.01 | | 180 mm | 8.5% |

Two consequences, both for the padding split and neither obtainable from `crop_coverage`. **46.0%** fill
160 mm — an independent corroboration of the ~40%, from a different quantity, which is what makes the
D269 (c) split worth taking at all. And **97.2%** fill 130 mm, so the default-extent members are padding
essentially nothing: `band_dense_hold` is a near-perfect CONTROL for a 160 mm padding question, exactly
as `fov_perstudy_read.sh` pre-registered before this was measured.

The arithmetic that turns the readout into the verdict is committed and tested ahead of the card
(`kneemri/evaluation/padding_split.py`, 7 tests). It prints the pooled toll FIRST — a run whose pooled
number does not reproduce may not be split at all — and it carries TWO masks rather than one, because
`nan >= 160` is False and a single-mask spelling files every unmeasured study under PADDED. That is this
project's denominator error in the shape a boolean makes easiest to make; here it is pinned by a test.

### D269 (c): the pad does NOT bite, and the extent advantage sits where the extent is real — 2026-09-09

The split ran, and it ran on a file the ledger above says does not exist. `fov_perstudy_read.sh` was
recorded as having died on the withdrawn fourth member before reading a single study; it did not —
`fov_perstudy.npz` is on disk and holds all three surviving members. So the deciding reading for the
padding composition cost **no card and no slot**, taken while `ortho_lora` held the GPU.

Every pooled toll reproduces its recorded value to the fourth decimal (−0.0297 / −0.0265 / −0.0360),
which is the precondition `padding_split` prints first and the only thing that licenses splitting at all.

| member                  | fills n=430          | padded n=479         | pooled n=909 |
| `crop160_span_s2026`    | 0.8402, toll −0.0264 | 0.8211, toll −0.0272 | 0.8300, **−0.0265** |
| `fovjitter160_s2026`    | 0.8320, toll −0.0320 | 0.8192, toll −0.0277 | 0.8248, **−0.0297** |
| `band_dense_hold_s2026` | 0.8282, toll −0.0408 | 0.8162, toll −0.0315 | 0.8213, **−0.0360** |

**PADDING BITES is refuted, and it is refuted in the direction nobody predicted.** The branch asked
whether the wide members' padded studies carry a WORSE toll than the 130 mm member's on those same
studies. They carry a BETTER one: `crop160_span` tolls −0.0272 where it pads against the control's
−0.0315. The composition the arm was bought to price — wide field → pad-filled border → pad learned as a
site cue → transfer toll — does not fire on this endpoint. The control's own spread across the two
subsets (−0.0408 vs −0.0315, 0.0093) is LARGER than either wide member's (0.0008 and 0.0043), which says
the fills/padded cut carries a study-difficulty signal of its own that has nothing to do with padding.
Any future split on this cut has to price that baseline before charging a difference to the pad.

**EXTENT SURVIVES was written here for twenty minutes and then REFUTED by the same file.** On the
pre-registered 160 mm cut the wide member's ADVANTAGE over the 130 mm control is +0.0120 foreign AUC
where the field fills and +0.0049 where it does not, against +0.0087 pooled — 2.4x concentrated where
the extra extent is physically present, which is the branch's own text. That reading did not survive
asking the same question at the cuts either side of it. `padding_split --extent` is free once the npz
exists, so all four were taken:

| cut    | fills                | padded               |
| 130 mm | +0.0088 (n=874)      | **−0.0067** (n=35)   |
| 140 mm | +0.0082 (n=762)      | **+0.0163** (n=147)  |
| 150 mm | +0.0088 (n=616)      | +0.0083 (n=293)      |
| 160 mm | **+0.0120** (n=430)  | +0.0049 (n=479)      |

The advantage is **flat at about +0.009 across every cut and both subsets**, and at 140 mm the ordering
REVERSES — the padded studies show twice the advantage of the filled ones. One separation in four cuts
with a sign flip in the neighbouring one is scatter, not structure, and the pre-registered cut being the
one that separated is exactly the coincidence a single pre-registration cannot protect against. So the
+0.0087 pooled advantage of the 160 mm member is **NOT explained by the extra anatomy being present**.
Whatever `crop160_span` has over `band_dense_hold`, it is carried equally by the studies where its extra
field is real pixels and by those where it is zeros — which is the same direction as the padding
refutation above, read from the other side.

The cost of the correction was four minutes of arithmetic and it saves an arm: a 150 mm member (66.6%
fill, the interpolation point between 130 and 160) was queued on the strength of the +0.0120 and would
have spent ~1.4 h of card testing a coverage/extent split that this table says is not there.

**`fovjitter160`'s null is still unexplained, and the retraction above is why.** The reading that looked
like a mechanism — on the 160 mm fills subset the jittered member's advantage over the control is +0.0038
against the fixed member's +0.0120, so jitter appeared to remove the extent benefit exactly where extent
is measurable — rests entirely on the same +0.0120 the four-cut table just dissolved. It is quoted here
so that nobody re-derives it and believes it. The pooled −0.0297 stands; its mechanism does not.

WHAT THIS LEAVES, AND THE ANSWER IS NOTHING. Having lost the extent explanation, the obvious remaining
one is SCALE: a wider physical crop on the same pixel grid shows the joint smaller and coarser, which is
a real transfer variable and was on nobody's list. It is also **already controlled, by the arm itself**.
`crop160_span.sh:54` reads `--image-size 420` under a `# deliberate:` line saying "carried by the flag
above to hold mm/px, not an independent choice". So the wide member samples at **420/160 = 2.625 px/mm**
against the control's **336/130 = 2.585** — 1.5% apart, matched by design. A bead was filed to test this
and closed twenty minutes later against the arm's own header. Third reading of this axis in one hour,
third explanation excluded, and the exclusion was already written down.

So the position on `crop160_span`'s +0.0087 pooled transfer advantage over `band_dense_hold` is now:
**not extent, not padding, not scale, and not distinguishable from run-to-run scatter.** Two single runs
differing by 0.009 on a foreign readout whose per-subset intervals are 0.02-0.03 wide is one draw each,
and every structural explanation offered for it has now been measured out or was controlled before it was
offered. The number should not be carried into another argument as a fact about geometry. What would
settle it is a seed pair on either member — a second `crop160_span` at a different seed, priced on the
same readout — which is banned here for good reasons and would be the only thing that could turn +0.009
into a finding rather than a coincidence.

### The mm-vs-pixel-grid axis is NOT open here — every member is already mm-normalised (2026-09-09)

D266 reports that mm-resampling versus a fixed pixel grid is unpublished on a classifier endpoint
between two real corpora (the spacing literature scores Dice and volume), and called our arm on it a
genuine contribution in both directions. Checked against the eleven arms in the toll table above, **we
do not have that arm and cannot build it out of this pool.**

`crop160_span` is the only one of the eleven that WRITES `--crop-mm`, which reads at a glance like ten
pixel-grid members and one physical one. It is not: `kneemri/training/options.py:102` declares
`crop_mm: float = CROP_MM` and `core/data/corpus/crop_centre.py:25` sets `CROP_MM = 130.0`, so a member
that names no extent is cropped at **130 mm — physically, by default**. The ten silent members are
mm-normalised too. The only axis separating them from `crop160_span` is the EXTENT, 130 vs 160 mm, which
is exactly what the span paragraph above already charges it to. There is no second reading of that cell.

**Consequence for the plan.** Pricing mm-normalisation against a pixel grid needs a member trained with
the physical resampling OFF, and no such member exists — the flag is an extent, not a switch, and
nothing in `Crop` turns the normalisation off. So the D266 axis costs a code change plus a cache build
plus a twelve-epoch arm, not a readout of records on disk. Recorded so it is not planned again as free.

**And the −0.0336 is a POST-normalisation residual, which is why no published toll is comparable to it**
(D268, retracting D266's framing). Every external number D266 offered is one of three other things:
Xie et al. 2025 (eClinicalMedicine 89:103534, [CLF], 13,419 patients / 5 centres, −0.05…−0.07 external)
crops a **256×256 PIXEL** region around a meniscus segmentation, so it is a PRE-normalisation penalty;
Consispace (arXiv:2606.31839) and PVS (arXiv:2411.19564) are [SEG] Dice; CARVE's −0.125 is a CT
protocol/depth shift. What a corpus crossing still costs a model that ALREADY sees a fixed 130 mm
physical field is unmeasured in the literature. Our figure being smaller than Xie's pixel-grid penalty
is directionally consistent with physical normalisation having already removed part of the gap — and
that is exactly the not-comparable comparison, so it is a hypothesis the extent arm can test, never
evidence. Do not quote Xie against our toll without this paragraph attached.

## 2026-09-09 — three audits, and the one number the ledger had wrong (D262, D263, D264)

None of these cost a card. Two are audits of what is already on disk and one is a lever this project has
never measured; they are recorded here because a finding that lives only in a letter is a finding that
will be re-derived.

### D264 — the frozen set is 19, not 9, and every one of them is recoverable

The prose above says nine caches were reclaimed. Over 359 checkpoints against 340 live caches, **19 are
gone**: the nine already named plus `adjacent224`, `cover_labelwise`, `stack224`, `band_full`,
`band_wide`, `crop80_tissue` (x2), `crop80_span`, `extended_ws`, `band140`. The correction that matters
is not the count. **In all 19 cases only the pixel array was reclaimed** — `mask_<key>.npy` and
`index_<key>.json` survive in every case, so a re-decode restores the cache exactly and none of these
members is frozen in the sense the ledger meant. "Frozen" was a statement about a missing file, read as
a statement about an unreachable experiment.

### D263 — the cross-trunk audit is clean, with exactly one defect

26 rows flagged, 74 examined, 8 unresolved. Twenty-four of the twenty-six are declared by the ledger row
itself — the trunk change is stated where it happens — so they are not confounds, they are labels. There
is **one undeclared-trunk defect**, the `latent_adapt` instance already found and retracted, and one
cross-corner comparison (`merged_dense_cf` vs `merged_blend_cf`, README.md:4642, −0.0028) whose two arms
differ on slices AND band (12sl/0.2-0.8 against 20sl/0.1-0.9) and therefore prices two things as one.
The default-resolution table this rests on: `--variant` resolves to `SMALL`/`dinov2-small`
(`pretrain.py:262`); `--slices` 12, `--image-size` 336, band 0.20/0.80 (`core/data/corpus/cache_flags.py`).

### D262 — norm CHOICE is closed; LN-affine test-time adaptation is the open lever

The M&Ms BN-over-IN result that has been quoted at this project is **one borrowed sentence citing Bjorck
2018**; the 2x2 exists in that paper but the interaction is never tested — the evidence is a visual
ordering of four cells. The adjacent number in the same work is the one worth carrying: no-DA B→A 0.1637
against default-DA B→A 0.6126, so **augmentation alone was worth about +0.45 dice before BN entered the
comparison at all.** BN is the tiebreaker, not the mechanism.

Norm choice inside a ViT is structurally closed — LN keeps no running statistics, so there is nothing to
recalibrate. What is open is adapting the LN **affine** parameters at test time: TENT (Wang et al., ICLR
2021, arXiv:2006.10726) by entropy minimisation, with the ViT substitution stated verbatim by the OTTA
survey (Niu et al., IJCV 2024) — *"we replace its BatchNorm updates with a LayerNorm update"*. The line is
crowded (AdMiT CVPR 2025, CELA, MoETTA arXiv:2511.13760, On-the-Fly TTA PMLR v227 2024, InTEnt
arXiv:2402.09604) and **this project has never measured any of it.** It needs no architecture change and
no new cache, it applies to every member on disk, and it attacks the flat −0.0336 decode toll that is a
blind spot every member SHARES rather than a seat. It also changes the SERVED function, so it is gated
on `witness_check` and on whether the adapted forward pass depends on test-batch composition. The recipe
question is out as M264.

Closed by the same letter: decode-time intensity normalisation. With per-volume z-score already at the
flat optimum it is ~0.5% of transfer variance — not a lever, and not worth a slot.

## 2026-09-10 — four noisy-student knobs closed by literature before any of them cost a card (D279)

`noisy_student` had sat written, pre-registered and beaded P1 since 2026-09-07 without running. Nothing
about it was stale: the merged3 cache, `merged3_labels.csv` and the four fold-0-clean twins were all on
disk, and the ONLY missing artefact was `teacher_merged3.npz`. It was step three of
`after_seats_done.sh`, whose watcher gated on a marker in `lr4e-5_ws_df.full.log` and died with the
session that launched it — so the chain never reached the teacher pass that gates the arm. Re-armed
directly by `experiments/run_noisy_student.sh` (`5c26788e`). **This is the failure mode `queue_check`
cannot see** and the third instance of it: a stranded arm looks identical to an arm nobody wanted.

**The recipe we were already running is the one the medical replication measures as BEST, and the four
things we might have added are each measured negative or null.** M284 asked whether we were even running
the method we named — our student trains under the standard `$RECIPE` augmentation while the teacher
infers clean off a predecoded cache, which is NOT Xie et al.'s teacher/student noise asymmetry. D279
answers with primary tables:

| knob | what the medical source measures | decision |
|---|---|---|
| student noise asymmetry | Shak et al. arXiv:2012.09472 Table B.4 (the only medical paper running Xie's full noise ablation): full Xie noise **0.78** vs its own supervised teacher **0.82**; strip augmentation **0.83**; strip stochastic depth too **0.86**; noised teacher **0.78** vs clean **0.86** | **DO NOT ADD.** The inversion of Xie. Adding it is a measured −0.08 there |
| confidence filtering | ACPL arXiv:2111.12918 Table 4, CXR14 @2%: low-information (= what a confidence threshold keeps) **67.76** vs high-information **74.44**. PMC10498222 Table 7: confidence-only 0.707 → uncertainty-gated 0.712 for a THIRD of the pseudo-labels discarded | **DO NOT ADD.** Keeping the confident end is the worst of three measured choices; the refinement is +0.005, knob-sized |
| ramped distill weight | no medical paper ablates flat-vs-ramp on a DISTILL weight. The ramps that exist (UA-MT arXiv:1907.07034, `λ(t)=0.1·e^(−5(1−t/t_max)²)`) belong to a consistency term and top out at **0.1**; the distillation-style medical arm (arXiv:2005.02231) uses a FLAT **0.8** | **KEEP 0.7 FLAT.** Reading a 0.1 consistency ramp across to a 0.7 distill weight is a category error |
| round two self-training | Zhou et al. arXiv:2005.11746 Table 2, per-round on n=490: +0.0052, **+0.0024**, +0.0004, −0.0017, −0.0062 | **DO NOT PRE-REGISTER.** Round two is 46% of round one and inside its own noise; by round five it is back at the teacher |

**Two configuration choices CONFIRMED rather than changed**, from the same appendix: soft pseudo-labels
(Table B.2, soft **0.86** vs hard 0.82; Xie Fig 5 says hard can hurt on out-of-domain unlabeled, and our
merged3 is 1,986/6,393 = **31% foreign**), and no warm-start (Table B.3, warm-started **0.81** vs cold
**0.86** — "the student initialized with the teacher can get stuck in a local optimum"). The live log
reads `"init": "None"`, `"init_scope": "all"`, `"encoder_weights": "None"`, so the student starts from the
stock trunk and the −0.05 configuration is not in play.

**THE CAVEAT THE RESEARCHER RAISED AGAINST THEIR OWN §1, AND IT IS THE SAME DEFECT WE HAVE ALREADY VOIDED
A NUMBER FOR.** Shak's unlabeled pool IS their test set — §4.1.2 draws 2,005 NLST scans as the unannotated
set and §5.1 scores on "2,005 completely independent testing scans", the same 2,005. That is the
`raptor_solo` defect class (98.6% in-sample, 0.8938, voided 2026-08-29). The within-paper ORDERING is
still a fair comparison, but a transductive pool has a mechanism that could manufacture the inversion:
student noise stops the student reproducing the teacher's function on the very scans it is scored on, so
"removing noise helps" may be "memorising the pool helps". **We are the disjoint case** — our
pseudo-labels are inferred on the 5,484 TRAIN studies and the 909 holdout is excluded from the twins'
training — so if the inversion is transductive it does not transfer to us. Out as M285; until it comes
back, §1's recommendation is FOLLOWED but not treated as settled.

**Harness check, passed off the live log** (the arm demanded it in writing): `scheme merged3`,
`labels merged3_labels.csv`, `eval_labels report_labels_v2.csv`, `image_size 336`, `distill_weight 0.7`,
`teacher_targets teacher_merged3.npz`, 6393 studies / 5484 train / 909 holdout. Target coverage prints
`ACL: 1.0` and every other column `0.689` — and 0.689 = 4407/6393 exactly, which is the arm's "no labels
rewrite" argument showing up as a number: the foreign rows carry a REAL ACL label and ZERO label gradient
on the eleven columns they do not supervise.

**A DEFECT IN THE ARM'S OWN WITNESS PARAGRAPH, corrected off the run.** It claimed the twins were fitted
at 336/20 over the 0.1-0.9 band and worried that teaching at 336/12 over 0.2-0.8 made the depth an
argument rather than a measurement. `teacher_clean.sh` fits them at `--slices 12 --band-low 0.2
--band-high 0.8 --image-size 224`: **slices and band match the teacher pass exactly** and the mismatch
the witness existed to catch does not exist. Wrong in the safe direction. The one axis that does differ
is the source array (native 224 decode vs the 336 merged3 cache downsized by `Member.read_size`), a
resample difference. Related trap: `teacher_readings.py:82` logs `reading N training studies at %d px`
from `member.read_size`, the member's OWN trained size, NOT from `--cache-size` — so `224 px` in that
line is correct behaviour, and reading it as a flag that failed to land would kill a healthy run.

## The first ImageNet CNN this project ever fitted reads 0.8527, and the 48-epoch budget question is still open — 2026-09-10

Two owed rows, written together because the second is only readable against the first.

`resnet_224_short_s2026` — resnet50d at 224 px, 2.5D through-plane RGB, max over 20 slices, full-trunk
finetune at 2e-4, twelve epochs — peaked **0.8527 @e8/12** and settled (0.8496, 0.8494, 0.8481). Converged,
not truncated. It is the number that replaces a belief: thirteen encoders are on the registry, twelve of
them transformers or hybrids, and the one convolutional line on the ledger (`radnet121`, 0.6716) was a
reading about RadImageNet's *corpus*, not about convolution. No ImageNet CNN had ever been trained here.

**It is `resnet50d_short_s2026` 0.8393 repaired, not a new lane.** The two arms differ in one flag:
`--unfreeze-last 16`. `--whole-stack` selects the SLICE WINDOW (`run_setup.py:638`) and says nothing about
which blocks carry a gradient, so the earlier arm fitted a CNN inside our usual six-block frozen trunk and
its log read `train mode pins 36 frozen norm layer(s)`. Sixteen is resnet50d's own block count (3+4+6+3) and
`BlockWindow.of` clamps, so it opens every block. **+0.0134 of the gap between those two rows is a flag, not
an architecture** — which is this project's most expensive recurring failure appearing once more, and the
reason the arm's harness check demanded that line read 3 rather than 36.

`resnet_224_long_s2026` — the same recipe at his 48 epochs — was **killed at epoch 9** and has no checkpoint,
only a `.partial`. Best 0.8404 @e6, then 0.8298 and 0.8281. **That is a FLOOR and it must not be read as a
budget result.** Under `one_cycle` at epoch 8 of 48 the rate is still near its peak and the anneal has not
begun; the two arms are different schedules compared at a point only the short one had finished. The
declining tail is what a mid-schedule one_cycle looks like, not evidence that longer overfits. The
48-epoch CNN budget is UNMEASURED, costs ~3.5 h at ~265 s/epoch to measure, and is declined for now on
ratio rather than on a result — the short arm already delivers the thing the long one was gating, which is
an ARCHITECTURE FAMILY the ensemble has no member of.

**What the short arm buys is distance, not quality.** 0.8527 sits inside our own 336/12 family band
(~0.852-0.862), so as a solo it is unremarkable and nothing here claims otherwise. The argument for it was
never quality — the seven board flats were all reseatings WITHIN the ViT family, and this is the first seat
from outside it. That is a claim about the ENSEMBLE and it is priced on the board, not here.

## The external-data axis closes on its own measurement: matched supervision did not stop the foreign block displacing us — `noisy_student` 0.8548 — 2026-09-10

`noisy_student_s2026` = **0.8548 @e10 of 12**, converged (e11 0.8545, not truncated, not undertrained).
Against its pre-registered control `merged3_corpus_s2026` = 0.8521 at the identical geometry: **+0.0027**,
which is the arm's own **0.852-0.856 FLAT branch**, written before the run.

**What was tested.** The third site again, with its SUPERVISION replaced rather than its pixels. One
variable against `merged3_corpus`: `--distill-weight 0.7 --teacher-targets teacher_merged3.npz`, the
teacher being the four `oof_clean_fold[1-4]_s2026` twins that no fold-0 study ever reached. This was the
one untested cell of the corpus x supervision 2x2 — foreign pixels WITH supervision that speaks all twelve
columns — and the cell the whole "the label mismatch is the blocker" argument rested on.

**THE DE-CONFOUNDING READ, which is the reason this arm was worth running.** `merged3_corpus`'s failure
had a shape: a ROTATION, not an addition, with Lateral Meniscus worst of twelve at -0.0217. If matched
supervision were the blocker, that column is where the repair had to show. Per-column, `noisy_student`
against `merged3_corpus`:

| column | merged3_corpus | noisy_student | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Lateral Meniscus** | 0.848 | 0.842 | **-0.006** |
| Fracture | 0.818 | 0.807 | -0.011 |
| Medial Meniscus | 0.898 | 0.895 | -0.003 |
| PF OA | 0.824 | 0.840 | +0.016 |
| Contusion | 0.855 | 0.871 | +0.016 |
| Lateral OA | 0.807 | 0.818 | +0.011 |
| Medial OA | 0.872 | 0.882 | +0.010 |
| Synovitis | 0.854 | 0.860 | +0.006 |
| ACL | 0.886 | 0.891 | +0.005 |

**Lateral Meniscus is still negative.** Matched supervision did not recover the column the corpus argument
was built on, and the gains sit in the OA/Contusion/PF group — the same rotation, not a repair of it.

**The two-delta caveat, and it bites the wrong way.** The arm stated before running that the distill term
alone is worth ~+0.0056 on OUR rows (`seat_clean_distill` 0.8634 vs `band_dense` 0.8578), so a result in
+0.004..+0.013 would be consistent with "the distill term worked and the foreign rows contributed nothing".
+0.0027 is BELOW that. The honest reading is not "the foreign rows did nothing" but "the distill term paid
part of what it normally pays and the foreign block ate the rest".

**CONSEQUENCE — the corpus axis is closed, and it is closed on a measurement rather than on a confound.**
That was the stated value of this branch and it is the whole return on the run. The site-count corner was
already negative (README:332 — second site +0.0043, third site -0.0024; `merged3_corpus` 0.8521 under
`merged_corpus` 0.8545), but every one of those readings carried the same live objection: the foreign rows
supervise one column of twelve, so the corpus was never fairly tested. That objection is now answered. It
also pre-prices fastMRI-as-a-fourth-site, which needs no run: adding sites is not the lever, and neither is
supervising them properly. **Do not re-propose a corpus arm without a mechanism that is neither of these
two.** The corner that still pays is supervision at a FIXED two-site cache (`merged_blend_cf` 0.8597,
`merged_span_cf` 0.8618) and that is untouched by this result.

Four further noisy-student knobs — student noise, confidence filtering, a ramped weight, round two — were
closed by literature before any of them cost a card (D279, section above). None is re-opened by this row.

Recipe confirmed by the arm's own harness check before the number was read: `scheme merged3`,
`merged3_labels.csv`, `eval_labels report_labels_v2.csv`, `image_size 336`, `distill_weight 0.7`,
`teacher_targets teacher_merged3.npz`, 6393 studies / 5484 train / 909 holdout, `init: None`. 223 s/epoch.

## The offline ruler resolves its TOP and not its MIDDLE, and the cut re-draws the order rather than lifting it — rank_stability, 2026-09-10

The question the seven board flats could not answer, asked of our own holdout instead of the board:
**does resampling the 909 studies change which arm is best?** Researcher D281 §3(1) named the method
(Maier-Hein et al., Nat Commun 2018, arXiv:1806.02051, Figs. 3-4 — resample the test set, re-derive the
ranking of unchanged submissions). `python -m kneemri.evaluation.rank_stability` is it, and it costs no
card and no slot: 13 arms of the 0.851-0.863 family, 909 shared studies, 500 resamples, rank-average vote.

**Midpoint ruler (`cut0.5`, the one every ledger number was read at):**

```
arm                                score  rank  first%  mean rk  cols
seat_clean_distill_s2026          0.8634     1   96.8%     1.03    12
band_dense_long_s2026             0.8587     2    2.6%     3.05    12
band_dense_s2026                  0.8578     3    0.2%     4.02    12
grade_ladder_s2026                0.8565     4    0.2%     5.44    12
band_span_s2026                   0.8565     5    0.2%     5.55    12
depth_regions_narrow_s2026        0.8554     6    0.0%     6.78    12
band_wide_s2026                   0.8553     7    0.0%     7.22    12

calib_span_s2026                  0.8545     9    0.0%     7.99    12
resnet_224_short_s2026            0.8527    10    0.0%     9.85    12

res392_ws_s2026                   0.8523    12    0.0%    10.69    12

**READING 1 — the ruler is not noise, and it is not a ranking either. It is both, in different places.**
`seat_clean_distill` holds rank 1 in **96.8%** of resamples, so "everything offline is inside the noise"
is FALSE for the top of the band: the best arm is genuinely the best arm and the holdout can say so. But
read the mean ranks of ranks 4-9 — 5.44, 5.55, 6.78, 7.22, 7.55, 7.99 across a score span of 0.0020. That
cluster is ONE number with error bars. Every keep/kill this project took inside 0.8545-0.8565 was decided
by a difference the holdout cannot resolve, and no appeal to the competition's test set is needed to
explain a flat board result from a reseating inside it. The correct statement of the ruler's power is
therefore neither of the two that have been argued all week: **it resolves first place and does not
resolve the middle of its own leaderboard.**

**READING 2 — D281 §1.1 is CLOSED, with a null.** `LabelScores.mean` is a `nanmean` and
`area_under_curve` returns NaN on a one-class column, so our macro could silently have been a mean over
fewer than the twelve the board always averages. It is not: the `cols` column reads **12 for all thirteen
arms**. There is no denominator difference against the competition on this holdout. Do not re-raise it.

**READING 3, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS — the cut is NOT an offset. Kendall tau +0.6667.**
`ledger75` was known to move the LEVEL by +0.026 (knee-f9aao). Nobody had asked whether it moves the
ORDER. Same predictions, two truths, and the ordering is substantially re-drawn:

```

calib_span_s2026                  0.8895     2   38.6%     2.44          9  <-- +7
band_dense_s2026                  0.8877     3   11.2%     4.05          3
