`calib_span` moves from rank 9 to rank 2 and takes first place in **38.6%** of resamples — more often
than `seat_clean_distill`'s 38.4%. Its own roster line reads *"calib_span_s2026.pt 0.8545 — band_span +
calibrated targets, NEGATIVE at this operating point."* That verdict was written under the midpoint, and
under the cleaner truth the same predictions are co-best in the pool. This is D281 §2.2's inversion
criterion firing on OUR data: a truth change that reweights which cases count is model-DEPENDENT, and it
re-draws rather than shifts.

**Why this points at the ruler and not at the members.** `ledger75.py`'s own docstring records D27:
across ~530 leaderboard pairs `ledger75` leaves **5 inversions where the midpoint leaves 21**, and 0 of
326 above the 0.0053 floor, with R^2 .80 -> .96. So the ordering we have been making decisions from is
the one already measured to be the WORSE predictor of the board. That is a mechanism for "why do the
people ahead of us move while we do not" that needs no new data and no new architecture: some fraction of
our keep/kills were taken with a ruler whose false positives sit in the TRUTH.

**What this does NOT license.** It is one pool of thirteen arms, one holdout, one vote rule, and a single
tau. It does not reprice the ledger, it does not promote `calib_span` to anything, and it is not a claim
that `ledger75` is correct — only that the two rulers disagree about ORDER and that the board has already
sided with one of them. Under `ledger75` the top of the band is itself unresolved (38.4% vs 38.6%, 10 of
13 arms take first place in some resample), so the recut buys a better board correlation and LESS local
resolving power at once. The next question is whether a decision procedure that requires agreement from
both rulers keeps anything at all.

`cols` reads 12 everywhere under both rulers.

### The Zech precondition, measured on merged3 — WEAK. 2026-09-10, no card, no slot

D282 corrected D281 §2.2: prevalence differing ACROSS TRAINING SOURCES is an inversion route, not
"neither" — Zech 2018 introduced a 10x prevalence imbalance between training sites, gained internal AUC
at p<0.001, and that gain transferred at zero externally, with the site readable from the image at
99.95%. `merged3` is three sources, so the mechanism is available to us by construction. It was worth one
`groupby` before anything was built on it.

Sources parse cleanly off the study id: ours `1.2.826.*` n=4,406, MRNet n=1,248, Rijeka `<digits>-<digits>`
n=736 (6,390 rows; the arm header's "1,987 foreign" and "6,393" are both slightly off).

**ACL is the only column all three sources supervise, and its prevalence at the midpoint reads
ours 0.278 / MRNet 0.210 / Rijeka 0.257.** A 1.4x spread between the extremes, against the 10x Zech
engineered. Our own column additionally carries 8.1% UNK, which the foreign ones do not have at all. So
the specific Zech lever is present and small here, and no result of ours should be attributed to it
without a much larger measured gap. Do not plan a de-confounding ablation on this axis.

**The related defect it rules OUT, checked in the same pass.** The eleven non-ACL columns on foreign rows
are `NaN`, not zeros — value, conf and verdict all NaN — so `Targets.pair` weights them at 0 and the
foreign rows carry no label gradient on the columns they cannot speak to. The `noisy_student` header's
claim is correct as written. A first pass that read `>0.5` and `== "UNK"` over NaN reported 0.000 for both
and looked exactly like eleven hard negatives per foreign row; it is not. Anyone re-running this must
count NaN explicitly.

**What is NOT ruled out, and is a different mechanism from Zech's.** 31% of the training rows are
supervised on ONE of twelve columns. That is a SUPERVISION imbalance rather than a prevalence one, it is
readable from the source, and it is still model-dependent — so it remains an inversion route. It happens
to have a corroborating hint: in the rank_stability table above, `noisy_student`, the merged3 arm, is the
single biggest FALLER under the cleaner `ledger75` truth (rank 8 -> 11). One hint is not a finding.

## Case mix moves the LEVEL by 0.030 on one model, and 909 studies cannot resolve ranks 2-13 at all — rank_stability --series, 2026-09-10, no card, no slot

D281 §3(3), the last free diagnostic. The spectrum effect asks whether our ARM ORDERING is case-mix
dependent, which is the inversion mechanism stated in D281 §2.2. It is answerable without a single test
label: partition our own 909 holdout studies on an axis that is NOT the label, re-derive the ordering
inside each part, read the pairwise Kendall tau. `--series` on `rank_stability` is that, plus the control
that makes it readable.

**The axes, after two of the four candidates turned out not to be axes.** `train_series.csv` names
`Fluid_Sensitive`, `Fat_Suppression` and `Anatomical_Plane`. `Fluid_Sensitive` and `Fat_Suppression` are
**byte-identical across all 24,371 series** — one variable wearing two column names, and anybody treating
them as two acquisition axes is double-counting. **All 4,407 studies carry Axial+Coronal+Sagittal**, so
plane-set is constant and not a subgroup axis at all. What is left: series COUNT (3-14, mode 5 at n=2299)
and fat-suppression SHARE (0.23-0.45+). Both split at their own median.

**13 arms, 200 resamples, rank-average vote. Midpoint ruler:**

```
series<=median       n=629  best seat_clean_distill 0.8630
series>median        n=280  best seat_clean_distill 0.8620
suppression<=median  n=669  best seat_clean_distill 0.8537
suppression>median   n=240  best seat_clean_distill 0.8835
tau series<= vs series>            +0.2308
tau suppression<= vs suppression>  +0.0256
tau RANDOM half A vs half B        +0.3590   <- the control
```

**Under `ledger75`:** the same shape with the level lifted — suppression halves 0.8823 / **0.9095**, taus
+0.3077 (series), +0.2308 (suppression), control **+0.4872**. And the cut re-draws the top here too:
`calib_span` is best in three of the four subgroups and in one of the two random halves.

**Reading 1 — the sharp one. The same model reads 0.8537 on the low-suppression half and 0.8835 on the
high-suppression half: +0.030 from ACQUISITION MIX ALONE, no model change, twice the 1.5% bar.** Under
`ledger75` it is +0.027. This is the first LOCAL, mechanism-backed evidence for the branch that says our
board number sits 0.09 above our holdout because the test POPULATION is different, rather than because our
models fail to generalise — and it is measured on us, not borrowed from a table. It does not close the
gap: 0.030 is a third of 0.09, and it only shows that a mix change of the size our own data contains moves
the level by that much. It licenses nothing about the direction of the competition's mix, which is hidden.

**Reading 2 — the control eats most of the ordering claim.** Two RANDOM halves of the same 909 studies,
same distribution, nothing different about them, agree at tau +0.359 (midpoint) / +0.487 (`ledger75`).
So most of the disagreement across the acquisition axes is SAMPLING, not case mix. The acquisition taus
sit at or below that floor (+0.026 and +0.231 against +0.359; +0.231 and +0.308 against +0.487), so case
mix subtracts a little more on top — directional, not a finding. **What IS a finding is the floor itself:
909 studies do not resolve ranks 2-13 even against themselves.** Halve the holdout and the ordering of the
twelve arms below the champion is roughly re-drawn. That is the same verdict the first-rank shares gave
from the other side (rank 1 at 96.8%, ranks 4-9 spanning 0.0020), now with a second independent handle on
it.

**What this does NOT license.** It is not a measurement of the competition's case mix — that needs the
test images and is D281 §3(4), adversarial validation, which costs a kernel run. It does not say the
suppression axis is CAUSAL for difficulty; suppression share correlates with site and with protocol, and
this reading cannot separate them. And the champion is stable in every subgroup on the midpoint ruler, so
none of this is a reason to reseat.

**The consequence for how arms are read.** A keep/kill between two arms inside the 0.851-0.863 band is not
merely below the noise floor of the holdout's own resampling — it is below the floor of WHICH HALF of the
holdout you happened to look at. Stop pricing arms against each other inside that band; price them against
the band's edge, or on a subgroup where the difference is mechanism-predicted.

## Neither the ordering NOR the ensemble margin is resolvable on 909 studies — control_spread, 2026-09-10, no card, no slot

The subgroup reading above left one thing unpriced: a SINGLE random split. Its two halves agreed on the
ensemble margin to four decimals (+0.0066 / +0.0067), which looked like the margin being a far more stable
statistic than the ranking — and would have licensed switching every keep/kill from "which arm ranks
higher" to "what does this arm contribute to the mix". Twenty splits say that was luck.

**13 arms, 20 random halves, the two statistics over the identical splits:**

```
                        min       median      max      spread
midpoint  ordering tau  +0.1282   +0.3205   +0.5641
midpoint  margin        +0.0039   +0.0066   +0.0086   0.0047
ledger75  ordering tau  +0.0000   +0.2436   +0.5385
ledger75  margin        +0.0053   +0.0071   +0.0089   0.0036
```

**Reading. Both statistics are noise at this n, and the margin is the more damning of the two.** The
ordering was already known to be unresolvable — median tau +0.32, and one split in twenty put it at
EXACTLY zero, meaning two halves of our own holdout ranked thirteen arms with no relationship at all.
The new number is the margin: **the whole ensemble buys +0.0066 over its best single member, less than
half our 1.5% significance bar, and known only to within a half-split range of 0.0039-0.0086.** A
statistic whose spread is 70% of its own value is not a lever, it is a reading we cannot take.

**What this retracts.** The per-subgroup margins from the section above — +0.0080 on the low-series half
against +0.0032 on the high-series half, a 2.5x spread that looked like a real acquisition effect — sit
entirely inside the 0.0039-0.0086 random range. Not a finding. **And Klontzas et al. 2024 does not
reproduce locally**: their cross-architecture ensemble margin GREW 2.75x out of distribution (+0.024
internal, +0.066 external), so the local proxy predicted a bigger margin on our harder subgroup. We
measured +0.0069 hard against +0.0054 easy — the right direction, one fifth of the random spread, worth
nothing. That does NOT refute Klontzas; their margins are 4-10x ours to begin with, on n=104/49 with three
architectures that differ far more than thirteen variations of one recipe. It refutes the local PROXY, and
it says our members are nowhere near diverse enough for the mechanism to have anything to work with.

**And the CNN addition, priced honestly.** Adding `resnet_224_short` to the twelve moves the margin by
+0.0009 to +0.0011, uniformly across every subgroup. Inside the noise by a factor of four. `kneemri-cnnseat`
therefore ships as an INSTRUMENT and must be written down as one: it asks whether a family the board has
never held moves the BOARD, which is the only ruler left with the resolving power to answer it. Its
pre-registration is a null offline and it has one.

**The consequence, stated plainly.** This project has spent weeks choosing between arms separated by
0.001-0.010 using a holdout that cannot resolve 0.005. Every one of those decisions was a coin flip
dressed as a measurement, and the seven consecutive board flats are exactly what a correct ruler with no
resolving power produces. **Nothing inside the 0.851-0.863 band is worth another hour of card.** What is
worth it is anything whose mechanism could plausibly deliver 1.5% — a genuinely different architecture
family, more supervised data, or a change to the truth definition — and the ONLY instrument that can
price those is the board itself, five reads a day.

## The margin, priced on the RIGHT interval — margin_interval, 2026-09-10, no card, no slot

The section above priced the ensemble margin by cutting the holdout in two and reading the margin in each
half. That is the wrong interval for this quantity, and I should have said so before quoting a spread off
it. A disjoint half costs BOTH terms half the studies AND throws away the pairing; what a keep/kill
actually consumes is the difference between the ensemble and its best single member **on the same
studies**, and the interval for that comes from resampling those studies once for both terms. 2000 paired
study bootstraps, best single member re-chosen inside every draw:

```
                                        value    95% interval        width
13 arms, midpoint                      +0.0063  [+0.0035, +0.0090]  0.0055
12 arms, midpoint (no resnet_224_short) +0.0054  [+0.0025, +0.0081]  0.0056
```

**The correction does not rescue anything, and that is the finding.** The paired interval is 0.0055 wide
against the split-half spread's 0.0047 — the same size. The construction was wrong and the conclusion it
produced was right anyway: the margin is known only to within its own magnitude, and the retraction above
stands. It now stands on the interval the decision actually consumes rather than on a proxy for one.

**One thing the paired reading can say that the split-half reading could not.** The interval EXCLUDES
ZERO. Thirteen members really do beat the best one of them — by +0.0063, about a quarter of our 1.5%
significance bar. That is not nothing; it is the honest size of every ensembling gain this project has
banked, and it is why ensembling stays in the entry while no longer being a place to spend card.

**And the cnnseat pre-registration, on the right statistic.** Twelve arms buy +0.0054; adding
`resnet_224_short` — the only member from a different architecture family — takes it to +0.0063. A
**+0.0009 move, a sixth of the interval's own width**, with the two intervals overlapping almost entirely.
The pre-registration for `kneemri-cnnseat` is therefore a null offline, and it ships as an INSTRUMENT
asking the board a question our holdout has no power to answer (knee-j07a0).

**What this points the next spend at.** Klontzas et al. report +0.024 internal / +0.066 external for a
cross-architecture ensemble — four to ten times ours — across three architectures that differ far more
than our thirteen variations of one recipe. Two points, no axis. The next free instrument is to put an
axis under them: 228 seed-2026 members sit on disk, pairwise prediction correlation is free to compute,
and the margin can be read for many subsets. That yields a LOCAL slope of margin against member
diversity, which is what turns "train a genuinely different family" from a hunch into an arithmetic
prediction. M289 asks the researcher whether that slope is already published.

## What a unit of member DIVERSITY buys — diversity_slope, 2026-09-10, no card, no slot

The section above ended by pointing at this: two points (ours at +0.006, Klontzas at +0.024) and no axis
between them. `kneemri.evaluation.diversity_slope` puts the axis in, on records already on disk. 300
random subsets of the 216 seed-2026 members that share a split, 4-16 seats, each priced on two things at
once — diversity (1 minus the mean pairwise Spearman over the flattened predictions) and margin (the
subset's score over its OWN best single member) — then regressed.

```
300 random subsets of 216 members, 4-16 seats, over 909 studies, ruler cut0.5, vote RankAverage
diversity (1 - mean pairwise spearman)  min 0.1075  max 0.4864  span 0.3789
margin over best single                 min -0.0172  median +0.0034  max +0.0151
RAW      margin on diversity   slope -0.0314 per unit  p 5.2e-11
CONFOUND margin on best single slope -0.4328 per unit  p 1.5e-11
CONFOUND margin on mean single slope +0.1639 per unit  p 3.8e-20
PARTIAL  margin on diversity   slope +0.1328 per unit  p 2.6e-35   <- the answer
what the whole observed diversity span is worth at the partial slope: +0.0503
but the span reached by the top-25% subsets by mean member quality is only 0.0718, worth +0.0095
```

**Read the raw slope and you get the sign backwards.** It is NEGATIVE (-0.0314): across our full pool,
more diverse subsets have SMALLER margins. That is not a statement about diversity. It is a statement
about which subsets are diverse — at the wide end of this pool, a subset is decorrelated because its
members are bad, and a subset of one good member and five bad ones scores BELOW its own best member
(the minimum margin here is -0.0172, i.e. the vote actively destroying the best member's number).

**Two quality terms are needed, and controlling for the best single alone is not enough.** That was the
construction's first mistake and it is worth writing down because it is subtle: residualising the margin
on the BEST single member fixes a subset's ceiling and leaves its floor completely free. A subset of one
good member and five bad ones has an unremarkable best-single, high diversity and a negative margin, and
it enters the fit as evidence that diversity hurts. Adding the MEAN single score as a second covariate is
what closes it, and the sign flips: the partial slope is **+0.1328 per unit, p 2.6e-35**.

**And it replicates.** The same fit over the thirteen champion-adjacent arms alone — a completely
different, much narrower pool — gives +0.1186 per unit. Two pools, spans differing by a factor of eleven,
the same slope to within 10%. Diversity at fixed quality really does buy margin, and this is the first
number this project has that says so with an axis rather than an anecdote.

**Now the part that decides where the card goes. The slope is real and the REACH is small.** Our pool's
whole diversity span is worth +0.0503 at that slope — three times the significance bar — but that span is
bought with badness. Restricted to the top quarter of subsets by mean member quality, the span the pool
actually reaches is **0.0718 wide, worth +0.0095**. That is the honest ceiling on the entire diversity
lever as this project can currently exercise it: two thirds of the bar, for perfect play. The thirteen
champion-adjacent members span 0.034 of it and have already banked +0.0045, so roughly half the reachable
gain is spent.

**What that licenses and what it forbids.** It forbids what we have been doing: re-seating, re-weighting
and re-lensing inside one recipe family moves along an axis whose remaining length is +0.005 — under the
noise floor, and the board has now flattened on that operation seven times, which is the same fact seen
from the other side. It licenses exactly one thing: a member that is BOTH good AND lands past 0.0718 of
reachable diversity. Nothing in 216 members has done that, so the slope out there is a prediction and not
an observation, and the module prints that line rather than letting the extrapolation hide inside a
coefficient.

**Which makes the next question a QUALITY question, not a diversity one.** A foreign family is worth card
only if it is good; its decorrelation is worthless — worse than worthless, per the raw slope — if it is
merely different. This project has never put a CNN on the board alone. `kneemri-cnnsolo` does that, and
its pre-registration is in the kernel's own docstring: `resnet_224_short_s2026` reads offline 0.8527,
within 0.0003 of `labels_v4hybrid` (board 0.922) and 0.0018 under `calib_span` (board 0.921), so if a CNN
transfers the way our transformers do it lands **0.920-0.923**.

**And it retires `kneemri-cnnseat`, which was built and green and was going to have the 11:14Z slot.**
Grepping the board for the operation is what stopped it: `fleettwo_v1` (2026-08-29) already put a CNN —
`raptor_ft_effv2l480` — into the champion seven and read 0.942 against the champion's 0.944. Same
operation, different CNN, already answered, and the paired offline interval prices this member's addition
at +0.0009. A seat asks about the MIXTURE; the mixture cannot be read until the family's own quality is on
the board. Solo first.

## `resnet_224_long` reads 0.8460 and peaked at epoch 12 OF 48 — the budget was never the binding constraint — 2026-09-10

The 48-epoch CNN arm finished. Read against its own pre-registration on both rulers, all 909 studies,
same split as the short arm:

```
resnet_224_short_s2026   0.8527 midpoint   0.8842 ledger75   best epoch  8 of 12
resnet_224_long_s2026    0.8460 midpoint   0.8764 ledger75   best epoch 12 of 48
```

**The branch it was given was `long - short >= 0.015` says longer is real. It is -0.0067 on the
midpoint and -0.0078 on ledger75.** Both rulers agree in sign and to within a thousandth in size, so
this is not a cut artefact. Longer is not real for this recipe.

**And the shape is the more useful half.** `convergence_check` calls it neither TRUNCATED nor
UNDERTRAINED: the curve turned over and stayed over (e44 0.8321, e45 0.8316, e46 0.8319, e47 0.8309)
against a peak at epoch 12. The arm spent **36 epochs, about 1.9 h of card, after its own best epoch**.
Twelve epochs was already the right budget for this recipe, and quadrupling it bought a slightly worse
number. That is a fact about the BUDGET and it generalises no further than a fixed learning rate — an
arm whose curve is still climbing at its last epoch (`ortho_slow_trunk`) is a different shape and this
does not price it.

The CNN lane's best member therefore remains `resnet_224_short_s2026`, which is the member
`kneemri-cnnsolo` already ships. The entry does not change.

## Five axes read closed in one sitting, on records already on disk, and the flatness IS the finding — 2026-09-10

Chasing the large-trunk question above, five separate axes were checked against their own controls.
Every one had already been run. No card was spent on any of this; all of it is `ledger75` over the
909-study holdout that every row below shares.

```
CONTROL band_dense_s2026            0.8578 midpoint   0.8877 ledger75

LAYER-WISE LR DECAY  (7 arms, 2 factors, 3 rates, 3 trunks)
  decay224_high_s2026               0.8487            0.8820
  band_deep_matched_s2026           0.8487            0.8781
  band_dense_llrd_s2026             0.8483            0.8765
  decay224_low_s2026                0.8454            0.8714
  llrd224_s2026                     0.8453            0.8737
  band_deep224_s2026                0.8446            0.8718
  llrd224_flat_s2026                0.8440            0.8694

OBJECTIVE (AUC-margin surrogate REPLACING cross-entropy)
  margin_seat_s2026                 0.8525            0.8702
  margin_calib_s2026                0.8235            0.8678

SAMPLING (disagreement tilt, against its OWN alpha-zero control)
  disagreed_ramp_s2026              0.8574            0.8827
  disagreed_uniform_s2026  CONTROL  0.8507            0.8819
  disagreed_full_s2026              0.8471            0.8770

CAPACITY (large trunk, and the low-rate leg)
  ortho_solo_v1  board              0.8452 -> board 0.907, worst of five solo anchors
  ortho_slow_trunk_s2026            0.8265            (peaked on its LAST epoch; undertrained)
```

**Not one of the twelve beats the flat control, and the whole population sits in 0.8235-0.8578.** The
best of them, `disagreed_ramp`, is +0.0067 on the midpoint and **+0.0008 on ledger75** — the cut
consumes the entire apparent gain, which is what a noise reading looks like when it is written down
honestly.

**The flatness across the axes is worth more than any single row.** These are not variations of one
knob: they are the trunk's capacity, the trunk's learning rate, its per-depth rate schedule, the LOSS
FUNCTION the network descends, and the SAMPLER that chooses what it sees. Five structurally different
interventions, and the answer is the same number to within the noise floor every time. A search that
returns the same value regardless of which axis it moves along is not under-searched — it is measuring
something that does not depend on those axes.

**What that licenses.** It stops the recipe/capacity/objective/sampling family from taking further card
on momentum: each of those cells now has an occupant and a control, and re-running any of them is a
repeat. It also removes the harness suspects one at a time — a faulty-TRAINING or faulty-PLUMBING
explanation would have to be wrong identically across five independent implementations, which is not
the shape of a plumbing bug.

**What it points at.** Every member above is fitted against the SAME supervision: labels derived from
radiology report text. That is the one term held constant across all five axes, and it is therefore the
only one the flatness cannot rule out. `M294` puts that question to the researcher — how much of the
residual is label noise rather than model capacity, and what has measurably moved a model past its own
label quality at our scale. Pending that, no arm in this family is queued.

**Pricing note, from `D283`.** The board/offline relationship refits at slope **1.098** at the top of
the range (CI95 [0.903, 1.350], n=26), which EXCLUDES the +1.55 this project has been multiplying by.
Every plan priced through `board_transfer` is over-priced by roughly 40%: the 0.010 board gap wants
about **+0.009 offline**, not the +0.006 that 1.55 implied. In our working band the gap is a flat
offset, mean +0.0608, sd 0.0035 — below the paired arm-to-arm noise floor.

## The ruler's uncertain-mention bucket is one hardcoded constant covering 27.3% of every cell, and the corpus is multilingual — 2026-09-10

Two facts about `report_labels_v2.csv`, the file `column_surface.py:50` resolves as `CORPUS_LABELS`
and against which every holdout number in this ledger is computed. Neither was written down anywhere.

**The label ladder has five rungs, not a continuum.** Across the 12 finding columns and 4,406 studies:

```
0.08   22298   42.17%
0.28   14445   27.32%     joins 1:1 to __conf 0.05 and __verdict UNK
0.68    6461   12.22%
0.82    6427   12.16%
0.94    3241    6.13%
__conf  takes exactly three values: 0.05 (14445), 0.85 (22298), 0.95 (16129)
__verdict takes exactly three: UNK, NO, YES
```

The 14,445 is exact on both rows, so every UNK cell carries label 0.28. **The convention for mapping
an uncertain mention is therefore a single undocumented constant applied to more than a quarter of
both the supervision and the ruler.** D292 prices that axis from the literature: on CheXpert, holding
images, architecture, split and labeler fixed and changing only the uncertain-mention mapping moves
weighted AUROC by 0.070 (U-Zeros vs U-Ones) and 0.040 for CheXbert — a larger swing than the choice of
labeler. Our knob is set to 0.28 by nobody's stated argument.

**This is the first mechanism-backed candidate for the five-axis flatness recorded above.** Twelve
members across capacity, trunk LR, per-depth schedule, loss and sampler all landing 0.8235-0.8578 is
what a shared wrong target produces: no rearrangement of the model can move a study whose label is
wrong, and 27.3% of cells carry a label that is not a reading of anything.

**The comparison is not straightforward and that is the open part.** Supervision and ruler are the
same file, so moving 0.28 moves the target and the scorer together. CheXpert could A/B this because
they scored against a radiologist-annotated test set; we have none at scale. Three candidate designs
(hold the ruler at v2 and vary only supervision — conservative, the ruler penalises the arm under
test; score on the UNK-free subcorpus — honest but discards the studies the question is about; score
against a gold reading — `processed/rsna_knee_gold58/` is 58 studies and holds images and a mask, not
an established label table). **No card is queued against this until the design is settled.**

**And the corpus is MULTILINGUAL, which nothing in this repo says.** `raw/train.csv` ships a `Report`
column of free text, mean 1,097 chars, zero nulls, and the finding columns beside it are EMPTY — so
every label file this project owns is somebody's extraction and there is no official table to be
approximated. Marker-token census, crude, denominators given rather than dressed up:

```
en   2019  45.8%      ??   1205  27.3%      es    683  15.5%
de    250   5.7%      nl    169   3.8%      fr     81   1.8%      total 4407
```

Only the total is exact; the `??` bucket is a quarter of the corpus and the classified counts are
biased by which markers were written. What survives: English is the plurality and Spanish is a
minority. One extraction ran over all of it, so the label noise is likely **stratified by language** —
the same shape as the age-stratified labeler error D292 §1 reports, and a reason its symmetric
40%-synthetic-noise evidence does not transfer. Per-language member error rates have never been
measured and would cost no card.

A correction worth recording because it nearly cost the researcher a wasted line of work: the first
report row is Spanish and sectioned `Técnica:/Resultados:/Impresión:`, and M295 generalised the whole
corpus from it. M296 retracts that. The sectioning is one language's convention, which demotes the
Impression-vs-Findings idea from cheap to needing a per-language section grammar.

### 2026-09-10 — the reader itself, measured against radiologists: 121 net wrong vs v2's 140

**Three of the paragraphs above are now wrong and are corrected here rather than edited away.**

**(1) The language stratification was a guess and it does not hold.** "The label noise is likely
stratified by language" was never measured when it was written. It has been: per-language binarised
agreement against the 58 radiologist-annotated studies, eight languages (bg/de/el/en/es/hr/nl/tr),
English 80.0% vs non-English 76.3% — **+0.037, 95% CI [−0.079, +0.145]**. The interval contains zero
and is wider than the effect. Per-language error is not an axis at this sample size, and the analogy
to D292 §1's age-stratified labeler error is withdrawn.

**(2) The 0.28 constant is not the CheXpert knob, because our uncertain bucket is not near even.**
knee-7oep had already priced the six reader levels against the radiologist rows, 696 cells over 58
studies, and the bead was not read before the axis was filed:

```
0.08 -> 0.041 (n=196)    0.28 -> 0.136 (n=177)    0.50 -> 0.417 (n=12)
0.68 -> 0.378 (n=98)     0.82 -> 0.688 (n=141)    0.94 -> 0.958 (n=72)
```

The 0.28 bucket is **13.6% positive**, so binarising it to a negative at the midpoint is right about
86% of the time and D292's +0.040/+0.070 price does not transfer — CheXpert's uncertain bucket sits
near even and ours does not. **What survives is better than what was claimed:** the reader's ENDS are
nearly right and its MIDDLE is broken. The 0.68 level is 98 cells that are 62% NEGATIVE, trained today
as 0.68 positive — a target wrong by ~0.30 on 14% of all cells, always in the direction of inventing a
positive. Mean per-finding rank AUC 0.866 against binarised agreement 0.789 says the same thing from
the other side: the ORDERING is good and the VALUE is broken.

**(3) A card IS now queued, because a better reader arrived and sat four days unscored.** The rebuilt
corpus reader finished 2026-09-06T14:53Z (4407 studies, both census sidecars, `finish_reasons` all
`stop`) and `reader_end_chain.sh` had been written and never run against it. Run 2026-09-10:

```
v2   140 net wrong of 696 cells   108 confident false positives + 32 misses
new  121 net wrong of 696 cells    47 false positives          + 74 misses
```

It passes v2's gate by 19 cells and **the failure mode inverts**: v2 invents positives, the new reader
withholds them (45 of its 74 misses are UNK, 29 an explicit NO) and its silent share rises 27.3% →
32.1%. Synovitis (−13) and Effusion (−14) carry −27 of the −30 net under-call. Installed as
`report_labels_v5reader.csv` — NOT a third file spelled `v3`, which is knee-ibfrw.

**This settles the design the paragraph above left open.** Of its three candidates: scoring on the
UNK-free subcorpus is dead — dropping those cells moves 318 members by mean +0.0229 (sd 0.0063) and
re-ranks 8.8% of member pairs, so it is not a neutral lens but an easier corpus
(`kneemri.evaluation.unk_surface`). The gold reading is the one that works and it **exists**, contrary
to M296: `foreign_gate --gold-auc`, n=58, and it has already carried a decision — the gold-vs-proxy
pair that declined a member is written out in `comp/members.declines`, and is deliberately not
re-quoted here, because that member's own holdout record sits on a ruler that moved with it and the
same file says its number must not be quoted. Read it there with its population attached. So
`reader_through` holds the ruler PINNED at v2 and moves only `--labels`, and
reads gold first. **The asymmetry is pre-registered in the wrong direction**: an arm taught to withhold
positives is scored by a ruler that rewards inventing them, so the proxy should read flat-to-negative
even if the table is better, and a holdout regression inside 0.0062 is not a refutation here.

**A ruler swap on the candidate table is not a gain either.** 116 members, 909 shared studies, 8 seats
deep: all 8 seats moved, churn 0.375, 0.8770 on the recorded ruler against 0.9025 on the candidate.
Same trap as the UNK-free subcorpus — a different ruler reading higher is a different question, not a
better answer.

**Why this is the supervision change worth the card.** D283 measured the board−offline gap at +0.0608:
the board reads our members HIGHER than our own ruler does, which is exactly what a ruler that
over-calls positives produces. The board is scored against real readings; our proxy is scored against a
reader that invents 108 of them in 696 cells. This is the one label-side change with a mechanism
pointed at the board rather than at the proxy.

### `oof_reader_fold[0-4]_s2026` — v5reader does not replace v2. THE ARM ABOVE READ, AND IT READ NEGATIVE.

Five folds, 224/8, seed 2026, `--labels report_labels_v5reader.csv`, against `oof_fold[0-4]_s2026` on
the same folds. So this is a PAIRED gold@58 read, all 58 studies honest by construction, and it is the
first supervision change this project has ever decided on a full out-of-fold stitch rather than on
thirteen studies.

```
PAIRED against oof_fold[0-4]_s2026 — the difference and ITS sd, which is the ruler:
  rankpooled  -0.0112   sd 0.0122      <- the registered internal ruler
  paircount   -0.0120   sd 0.0128
  macro       -0.0170   sd 0.0135      <- the board-comparable row (D298)
```

**Read it as a kill, and say why it is not a refutation.** The pre-registration was ±0.020 on the paired
rankpooled, so −0.0112 lands INSIDE the null band and the honest word for the arm's own gate is null.
But three estimators point the same way at roughly 1σ each, and the board-comparable macro is the one
nearest the "cost real signal" branch — the direction is consistent and the size is not zero. Nothing
here licenses `v5reader` over `v2`, and the 74 reader-miss repairs bought no signal on 58 honest studies.

**The asymmetry pre-registered above did not save it.** The argument was that an arm taught to withhold
positives is scored by a proxy that rewards inventing them, so a flat-to-negative proxy read would be
expected even if the table were better. That argument was about the PROXY. This reading is on gold — 58
radiologist-annotated studies, the only truth in this project not produced by a reader — and gold does
not have the asymmetry the argument invokes. So the escape hatch the arm was given does not apply to the
ruler it was actually read on.

**What it closes and what it does not.** It closes REPAIRING what the reader got wrong: this is the
second label-side route to fail on a measured control, after the UNK-free subcorpus lens. It does not
close the label side. Re-spreading what the reader DECLINED TO ASSERT is a different mechanism on
different cells — the middle rung, 12.22% of the table, which v5reader never touched — and it is on the
card as `oof_band_folds` (knee-27kuj). A route that repairs assertions and a route that resolves
non-assertions are not two attempts at one idea.

**Price paid: 2.1 h of card for a kill.** That is a real result and it is cheaper than the arm would have
been worth had it passed, because a table that reads −0.0112 on gold would otherwise have gone on
supervising members for weeks on the strength of its 19-cell gate margin.

## The middle rung reads NULL, and the honest word is null — `oof_band_folds`, 2026-09-10, 2.1 h of card

Self-training with the reader's bracket kept: `report_labels_v6band50.csv` re-spreads the 6461 cells
sitting on the reader's middle rung (raw 0.68) by their own out-of-fold order, share 0.5, symmetric about
the rung so the band's mean does not move. Five folds at 224/8, one token different from `oof_folds`.

PAIRED gold@58, against `oof_fold[0-4]_s2026`:

| estimator | difference | sd of the difference | resolves at two sd |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rankpooled` (registered) | **−0.0066** | 0.0062 | 0.0122 |
| `paircount` | −0.0071 | 0.0070 | 0.0137 |
| `macro` (board-comparable, D298 §3a) | −0.0076 | 0.0075 | 0.0147 |

Levels for the record: band `rankpooled` 0.8579 / `macro` 0.8852; the two read 0.027 apart on one system,
which is why neither is quoted alone.

**Third branch of the pre-registration, verbatim: "between — NULL AT THIS RESOLUTION, and that is the
honest word."** −0.0066 is 1.06 paired sd. The sign is not readable and must not be reported as a small
harm: at this n the estimator cannot tell −0.0066 from 0. What the arm buys is the CHEAP branch closing.
The mechanism is not refuted — it is priced, and the price is that a 2.1 h instrument on 58 gold studies
is the wrong instrument for an effect this size.

**The 0.6879 rung is not attempted.** The arm reserved that closure for the ≤ −0.020 branch and this is
not that branch, so the reason is different and worth writing down: D301 §4 measured the upper rung as
better TILTED (43.5% of its band mass on our six weakest columns against the middle rung's 35.0%) but
D300 measured the model ordering it WORSE (within-band 0.7002 against 0.7490). Two effects pointing
opposite ways, with a ruler that has just demonstrated it cannot resolve either. `--rung` and
`report_labels_v7upper50.csv` are built and stay on the shelf; arming the second arm of a mechanism whose
first arm read null is the thing this ledger keeps recording as a mistake.

**What this does NOT close.** The band mechanism at FULL recipe strength, and the band mechanism read on
a ruler with more than 58 studies. D301 §6 and D297 §4 arrive at the same sentence from two directions:
the cheapest thing that would settle it is more gold, not a cleverer statistic.

Computed off every `scope: ensemble` row in `comp/board.jsonl`. It is written here so no later
slot is spent rediscovering it, and it is written WITH the era control because the naive
version of this table is misleading and was quoted that way once.

| seats | n | best | mean | worst |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 10 | 0.928 `holdsolo_v1` | 0.9146 | 0.868 `solo_v1` |
| 2 | 4 | 0.936 `onepair_v1` | 0.9238 | 0.919 |

| 4 | 13 | 0.937 `fourseat_v1` | 0.9280 | 0.918 |
| 5 | 7 | 0.941 `fiveship_v1` | 0.9310 | 0.911 |
| **6** | 17 | **0.944 `monotone_v1`** | **0.9378** | 0.925 `maxdiv_v1` |
| 7 | 20 | 0.944 `stackseat_v1` | 0.9365 | 0.908 `weakseven_v1` |
| 8 | 5 | 0.943 `vjepaseat_v1` | 0.9378 | 0.932 `peak8` |
| 9 | 1 | 0.936 `nine_v1` | — | — |
| 11 | 1 | 0.941 `calibmix_v1` | — | — |
| 12 | 1 | 0.937 `honest12` | — | — |
| 14 | 1 | 0.937 `distinct14` | — | — |
| 25 | 1 | 0.894 `fusion25_v2` | — | — |

**THE ERA CONTROL, and it is the whole reason this table needs a caveat.** `fusion25_v2` at
0.894 is dated **2026-08-17** — the oldest row in the file, a pre-improvement generation. Read
without its date it looks like proof that seat count goes negative, and that is an era effect
quoted as a mechanism. The other big-N entries are modern and do not collapse: `calibmix_v1`
11 seats 0.941 (08-27), `honest12` 12 seats 0.937 (08-27), `distinct14` 14 seats 0.937
(09-01), `nine_v1` 9 seats 0.936 (09-08). Restricted to the last 21 days: 6 seats n=17 mean
0.9378 best 0.944; 7 seats n=20 mean 0.9365 best 0.944; 8 seats n=5 mean 0.9378 best 0.943.

**What the record therefore DOES say:** within one era, 6-8 seats reach 0.944 and 9-14 top out
at 0.941. That plateau is not era.

**What it does NOT say, and this is the part that keeps getting lost:** those four modern
big-N entries are all the champion six PLUS progressively worse members drawn from the same
pool, selected by a rule (`honest12` by licence-cleanliness, `distinct14` by max diversity,
`calibmix_v1` by calibration). They test the DILUTION of a good six under unweighted
LogitAverage, where seat 12 carries the same 1/12 as seat 1. They do not test "assemble
twenty-four independently good models", which has never been built here.

**The member-quality curve says the pool is not the constraint.** 273 members with a valid
holdout peak: #2 0.8747, #6 0.8657, #12 0.8635, #24 0.8610, #60 0.8564, #120 0.8503. From #2
to #24 is only -0.0137 and #24 to #60 another -0.0046 — flat, not a cliff. (#1
`recal_holdannot` at 0.8964 is +0.0217 clear of #2 and is a suspect outlier, not a member to
plan around; `hold_annotations` is one of D303's flagged supervision flags, so the gap may be
the flag. The `oof_*` rows are a different eval population D303 said not to pool. All midpoint,
not `@ledger75`.)

**So the binding constraint is CORRELATION, not member quality.** Essentially all 273 are
dinov2/dinov3 variants of one another, which is why `distinct14` — built explicitly for
maximum diversity — still only reached 0.937: its diversity was knob-diversity inside one
family. The untested axis is FAMILY count, not seat count. We own two families (the DINOv2/v3
line, and borrowed raptor whose quality is unmeasurable at `--fold -1`) plus exactly one
all-ours convolutional member, `resnet_224_short_s2026`, trained 2026-09-10.

### The plateau is a property of the POOL, and the board's noise floor on identical members is ±0.001

Computed 2026-09-10 from `comp/board.jsonl`, over every entry at or above 0.943 (n=16). Two facts fall
out, and the second is the one that matters.

**FIRST, THE NOISE FLOOR, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** Five of those sixteen entries have
**byte-identical member sets** — all six of `final_ws_cf`, `calib_span_ff`, `grade_ladder_cf`,
`merged_blend_cf`, `lr4e-5_ws_cf`, `through_dense_cf`:

| entry | date | board | what differs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `champviews_v1` | 2026-08-31 | 0.943 | views |
| `rootmove_v1` | 2026-09-02 | 0.944 | root transform |
| `aucvote_v1` | 2026-09-02 | 0.943 | vote rule |
| `stackvote_v1` | 2026-09-02 | 0.943 | stacked vote |
| `monotone_v1` | 2026-09-02 | 0.944 | monotone calibration |

Same members, four different serving knobs, spread **0.001**. So **±0.001 is what this board returns on
an unchanged entry**, and every 0.943-vs-0.944 comparison written anywhere in this project is noise. It
also measures the SERVING axis dead across four knobs at once, which is four instruments' worth of
answer that nobody has to spend a slot on again.

**SECOND, AND IT IS THE PLATEAU'S ACTUAL DIAGNOSIS: `corpusdose_v1` is the control we did not know we
had.** It scored 0.943 on 2026-09-01 with six seats sharing only **three of six** with the champion —
`merged_span_cf`, `merged_span_ff` and `merged_dense_cf` standing in for `final_ws_cf`, `calib_span_ff`
and `lr4e-5_ws_cf`. A **half-different six lands on the same number.** Taken with the five identical-set
entries above, that says 0.943–0.944 is a property of the POOL and not of any seating of it — which is
exactly what 273 members that are dinov2/dinov3 variants of one another predict, and it is the same
reading the seat-count curve reaches from the other direction.

Member frequency across the sixteen makes the shape explicit. `grade_ladder_cf` 16/16 · `through_dense_cf`
16/16 · `final_ws_cf` 15/16 · `calib_span_ff` 15/16 · `merged_blend_cf` 14/16 · `lr4e-5_ws_cf` 12/16 ·
`raptor_v4_swa` 8/16 · `merged_span_ff` 2/16 — and then **eleven members appearing exactly once**
(`vjepa_warm_s2026`, `calib_dense_hold_ff`, `stack_increments_ff`, `labelwise_dense_s2026`,
`merged_span_cf`, `merged_dense_cf`, `oof_teacher_s2026`, `labelwise_dense_ff`, `warm_calib_dense_s2026`,
`warm_calib_lowlr_s2026`). **Those eleven singletons ARE the member-axis experiment**: one slot each, each
added to the same fixed six, all flat. Pairwise Jaccard over the sixteen: n_pairs 120, mean 0.676, min
0.167, max 1.000.

**AND THE ENSEMBLE BONUS THAT SIZES THE REMAINING PROBLEM.** Best solo on the board is `holdsolo_v1`
0.928 (offline 0.8634); the plateau is 0.944; so the bonus the mixture buys is **+0.016**. Confirmed
independently: `calibsolo` served seat 1 of the champion alone for 0.923 against that seating's 0.941 —
**+0.018**. Two reads, same answer. Running 0.955 off a +0.016–0.018 bonus therefore needs a solo at
**~0.938–0.939**, and board ≈ offline + 0.063 on this board (`cnnsolo` +0.0623, `holdsolo` +0.0646,
`spansolo` +0.0665, `v4solo` +0.0696, `ortho_solo` +0.0618) puts that at **~0.874 offline clean**, against
our best honest member ~0.866. **The whole remaining problem is ~+0.007 offline on ONE member** — below
the house bar, which is why no knob has moved it and why the levers worth arming are the ones that change
what a member IS rather than how the six are seated or served.

Caution on foreign checkpoints, priced: `aprime_solo_v1`, a raptor fine-tune, scored **0.506**. A borrowed
trunk's quality is unmeasurable here until it has been honestly held out.

## D309 §1's pooling claim, answered on arrays already on disk — the sign FLIPS across the frozen/fine-tuned boundary — 2026-09-10

The researcher's D309 §1 cites arXiv 2606.11606 [CLF]: frozen probes of RAD-DINO / DINOv2 / DINOv3-7B /
MedSigLIP where **global (CLS) pooling sits at chance (AUC 0.500–0.524) on small-footprint signal while
patch-local pooling from the same forward pass recovers ≈1.0**, a small-vs-large stratum gap up to +0.243
recovered by region-restricted pooling. Our members pool `cls_mean` and our deficit sits on focal findings,
so the lead read as directly ours. It cost no card to answer, because both halves were already measured.

**THE FINE-TUNED HALF WAS ALREADY CLOSED, and I called this "the strongest lead of the day" before reading
that.** `focal_dense` (`--pool cls_mean_focal`, one flag off `band_dense`, flag verified in the CHECKPOINT
config) read **0.8534, −0.0044**; by structure scale, focal +0.0001 / regional −0.0114. `sided_pool`
(`--pool sided`) read +0.0007 seat value under the ledger's own title, *"the head was given a medial/lateral
axis, and did not use it"*. The family was written closed on all its axes. This is the failure CLAUDE.md
names in as many words, and it is the second time this week that a finding was filed against a number the
ledger already held.

**THE FROZEN HALF IS THE NEW READING, and it is in the ten-trunk probe table above.** `feature_probe.py:58`
maps `@mean` to `..._mean_max` — patch **mean alone, the global vector DROPPED**, which is 2606.11606's own
operation — and `:81` maps `@focal-max` to `..._cls_mean_focal_max`. Slice pooling is `max` in both, the
studies are the same 909, each trunk gets its own ridge penalty. So the pair isolates PATCH pooling:

| trunk (frozen ridge probe) | `mean` (global dropped) | `cls_mean_focal` | delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ortholarge` | 0.8170 | 0.8249 | **+0.0079** |
| `v3large` | 0.7968 | 0.8046 | **+0.0078** |
| `dinov2-large` | 0.7996 | 0.8048 | **+0.0052** |

Three trunks, same sign, +0.0052 to +0.0079, mean +0.0070 — and `focal_dense` reads **−0.0044** for the
same substitution on a FINE-TUNED trunk. **The sign flips across the frozen/fine-tuned boundary**, which is
the mechanism M307 proposed to the researcher before this table was found: a fine-tuned trunk can move
focal signal INTO the global vector and a frozen one cannot, so local pooling is worth something to a probe
and nothing to a member. Our nulls are correct for our regime and 2606.11606 is correct for its own.

**AND THE PAPER'S DIRECTIONAL CLAIM IS REFUTED ON OUR TRUNKS IN ITS OWN SETTING.** `mean` DROPS the global
vector — the operation 2606.11606 says recovers ≈1.0 from a chance-level global — and on all three large
trunks it is the WORST row, by 0.005 to 0.008. Whatever is at chance in their CXR trunks is not at chance
in ours.

**WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY, and it is the one honest hole.** `cls_mean_focal` both restores the class token
AND appends a focal tail, so the +0.0070 cannot be split between the two. `dinov2-small` is the only trunk
cached at `cls_mean_max` and it is the wrong size to compare against. Splitting it costs one encoder pass
per large trunk to write `..._cls_mean_max` caches — no training, no fit, minutes on the card — and that
arm would ALSO settle whether the frozen gain is the CLS token's or the tail's. It is an instrument and is
worth queuing behind current work; it is not worth a fitted arm, because the fitted half already answered.

Seat value is the check that kills any temptation to serve this: `ortholarge@mean` and `ortholarge@focal-max`
seat into `honest12` at **+0.0014 both**, identical to three decimals. The solo gain does not survive into
an ensemble at all — which is the ledger's standing reading that pooling shifts budget and does not create
it, now measured on the frozen side too.


## `ortho_fresh_lowlr` reads 0.8248 — the third branch fires, and `ortho_lpft` now has a different control — 2026-09-10

The initialisation control of the ortho triple. Random head, backbone 1e-5, whole stack, twelve epochs,
`ortholarge` at 224 px / 12 slices, every other flag identical to `ortho_dense`.

| arm | head | backbone lr | score |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ortho_dense` | random | 4e-5 | 0.8452 |
| **`ortho_fresh_lowlr`** | random | 1e-5 | **0.8248** |
| `ortho_lpft` | fitted (LP first) | 1e-5 | **TRUNCATED e4 of 12, floor 0.7937** |

**−0.0204 against `ortho_dense`, which is the pre-registered `s <= ortho_dense - 0.006` branch by more
than three floor-widths.** 1e-5 undertrains this trunk in twelve epochs. Converged and clean —
`convergence_check` does not list it, peak e10 0.8248 with e11 at 0.8247, so the one-cycle anneal ran and
this is the schedule's own answer rather than a killed process. 324-326 s/epoch against the 432 priced,
zero stall lines, 885-903 img/s, peak memory 28.59 GB reserved / 13.48 GB allocated.

Trajectory: 0.7360, 0.7726, 0.7933, 0.7990, 0.8164, 0.8159, 0.8182, 0.8212, 0.8237, 0.8241, 0.8248, 0.8247.
The e3 -> peak gain is +0.0258, above the 12-epoch median (+0.0210) and under p90 (+0.0380), so the arm
was not short-changed by its budget — it climbed normally to a lower ceiling.

**WHAT THIS BUYS, and it is the whole point of running an instrument.** `ortho_lpft` must now be read
against **0.8248**, not against `ortho_dense`'s 0.8452. It cannot be read yet at all — `convergence_check`
calls it `TRUNCATED  best e4 of 5 run, 12 asked`, so its 0.7937 is a FLOOR and the row at :7749 already
says the arm "cannot answer the question it was built for". Completing it costs 1.44 h and its BEST
pre-registered branch (+0.015 on this control) lands at 0.8398, still under `ortho_dense`'s 0.8452 — so
it is a mechanism finding with no path to a better member, and it is not being queued ahead of score work.
The control is banked and keeps: whenever that arm is completed, it is readable, which it was not before
today. Read against the wrong control, any LP-FT result
in the 0.83-0.84 band would have been written as "the warm start costs 0.01" when the rate alone accounts
for 0.02. And a flat between the two 1e-5 arms says the warm start did not rescue an undertrained
schedule — NOT that a fitted head does nothing. That sentence was unwriteable before this arm and is the
reason it was priced as an instrument rather than sold as an improvement.

**WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY.** The top branch did NOT fire: `s >= ortho_dense + 0.015` would have made 4e-5 too
hot for a ViT-L on 4,400 studies and re-opened `radnet121`'s written decline (0.6716 at 4e-4 against
0.8197 frozen) as a RATE finding. It fired the opposite way, so that decline stands as written and every
external trunk this project declined on a fine-tune stays declined. P(that branch) was priced at ~0.3
before the run; it lost.

## The regeneratable-cache sweep took four members and an arm with it, and `roster_check` names only some of them — 2026-09-10

`diversity_curve` was put on the card at 17:59:56Z to fill it after the overwrite guard refused
`disagreed_ramp`. It died twice, both times on a deleted array:

    FileNotFoundError: images_336px_12sl_extended.npy
    FileNotFoundError: images_336px_16sl.npy

Both are casualties of the approved regeneratable-cache deletion. The first killed it after six solo
rows; the second after the same six, one member later. Four of its eleven members cannot be read
without first rebuilding a cache on the card: `extended_ws_s2026`, `res392_ws_s2026`,
`intensity392_ws_s2026` and `slices16_ws_s2026`.

**`roster_check` does not name all four.** Its gone-cache list carries twelve members, and
`slices16_ws_s2026` is not among them — the check reports the arrays a member's own record points at,
and this one was found only by a crash. So the twelve are a floor on the blast radius, not the radius.

**What it costs the question.** The arm asks whether mechanism-ensembling buys what fold-ensembling
bought. `extended_ws` is its ONLY member whose INPUTS differ (line 51 of the arm says so in its own
words); the other ten are different recipes over the same inputs. With `extended_ws` gone the arm can
answer the RECIPE-diversity half and not the input-diversity half, and the withdrawal is written into
the script so no later reading quotes it as the whole answer. The three 392/extended members are a
cache rebuild away, not a re-train — the checkpoints are all on disk.

**A second thing fell out of the six rows it did read.** The arm's own header quotes
`lr5x_d6_s2026` 0.8323, `max12_s2026` 0.8310 and `large_deep_rank24` 0.8304; `member_curve` read them
at 0.8475, 0.8451 and 0.8450 — **+0.0152, +0.0141, +0.0146**, a systematic offset and not scatter.
That is the cut, not the members: a bare number in this repo is midpoint unless it says otherwise, and
the header's numbers and the tool's are two different statistics over the same predictions. Nothing
here is a gain; it is a reminder that a solo score quoted without STATISTIC/POPULATION/CUT is not a
number, and this offset is about three times the board gap.

### The capacity ladder has one rung at the winning geometry, and `band_dense` is standing on it

Priced 2026-09-10 with `vram_need` at the shipped operating point — 336 px / 20 slices / batch 12 /
recompute on, so gradient checkpointing (`encoder_surgery.py:443`) is already IN these numbers —
against a 32,607 MiB card:

| variant | MiB at 336/20/batch 12 |
|---|---|
| small | **28,934** |
| base | 58,700 |
| large | 81,400 |

`band_dense`, the best single member this project owns at **0.8578**, is a `small` trunk (read out of
its own checkpoint config, not out of prose). It holds 28,934 MiB and leaves 3.7 GB, and that is all
the headroom there is. A wider trunk at this geometry needs 1.8x to 2.5x the card.

**So "capacity is the last open suspect" was the wrong sentence.** Capacity at the geometry that wins
is not untested — it is structurally unreachable on this card at an honest batch, and every wider-trunk
number in this ledger is therefore measured through a batch substitution: `base_dense` at batch 2,
`ortho_stack` at batch 1 with a 66-pair memory. `band_pairmem` prices the batch-1 substitution at
**−0.0092** on the small trunk at this same geometry — the same order as the differences being read
from it. `ortho_stack` − `band_dense` = −0.0161 and `base_dense` − `band_dense` = −0.0066 are both
confounded by an effect of their own size.

The one cell that fits and is not the batch-1 corner is `base_honest_batch` (knee-omnzl): base trunk,
`band_dense`'s exact geometry and cache, **batch 5 at 25,207 MiB** with 7.4 GB of headroom, no
accumulation and no pair memory. 66 within-batch pairs at 12, 10 at 5, 1 at 2 — it shrinks the confound
by an order of magnitude rather than removing it, and it lands the first pure BATCH read on the base
trunk at fixed geometry (batch 5 against `base_dense`'s batch 2), which nothing here owns yet.
6 fits too, at 29,992, and was refused: `mae_unitfix_s2026_run1` held 32,024 MiB, reported 51 MiB free
at its first step, and collapsed 510 → 57 img/s the moment epoch 0's holdout eval allocated on top.

### The offline ruler has a measured resolution limit, and every lever of the last week sits under it — 2026-09-10

Fitted on `comp/board.jsonl`, entries from 2026-08-20 on, `scope: excluded` dropped (so `raptor_solo`'s
98.6% in-sample row and `aprime_solo_v1`'s 0.506 are out). Two populations, and they do not share a
constant:

| population | n | mean board − offline | sd | range |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| solo (1 member) | 5 | **+0.0650** | 0.0029 | +0.0618 … +0.0696 |
| ensemble (>1) | 23 | **+0.0614** | 0.0026 | +0.0518 … +0.0649 |

**A solo transfers +0.0036 BETTER than an ensemble.** Part of the ensemble bonus is paid back at the
board, which is a fact the target arithmetic has been quoting a single blended `+0.063` over.

**THE RESOLUTION LIMIT.** Over all 230 ordered pairs of the 23 ensemble anchors, how often does the board
order the pair the opposite way from offline:

| Δ offline | pairs | board order inverted |
|---|---|---|
| 0.000 – 0.002 | 86 | 15 = **17%** |
| 0.002 – 0.005 | 73 | 4 = 5% |
| 0.005 – 0.010 | 49 | **0** |
| ≥ 0.010 | 22 | **0** |

So the ruler is not broken — it is strictly monotone on the board above Δ0.005 offline, zero inversions
in 71 pairs. It is simply BLIND below Δ0.002. The worked case is on the board already: `foldfour_v1`
(offline 0.8711) scored **0.936** while `peak8_v1` (offline 0.8731, the better offline number) scored
**0.932** — 0.002 of offline producing 0.004 of board in the wrong direction.

**WHY THIS IS THE ANSWER TO "WHY ARE WE STUCK AT 0.944".** Every operation this project has priced in the
last week lies under the floor: the marginal seat on the diversity curve **+0.0004**, `sided_pool`
**+0.0007**, LogitAverage over RankAverage **+0.0014**, the seat-oracle headroom **+0.0039**, the
split-half per-label top-4 **+0.0043**. Not one of them is resolvable on the board, which is why they
keep reading as flat there no matter how carefully they are measured offline — `cnnseat_v1` landing on
0.944, the champion's exact number, is the same sentence in board units. The house bar of ~1.5% and this
0.005 floor are the same instruction arriving from two directions.

**AND IT PRICES THE ONE AXIS THAT IS STILL ABOVE THE FLOOR.** Using the ensemble constant rather than the
blended one: 0.955 needs an ensemble at **0.8936** offline; `cnnseat_v1`'s 0.944 implies **0.8826**; so
the ensemble owes **+0.0110** offline. That sits in the ≥0.010 band, 0 of 22 pairs inverted — the board
can see it. Nothing in the seating family can deliver it (the whole oracle headroom is +0.0039). Only a
better MEMBER can, which is the arithmetic that has been quoted as "one member at ~0.874 against our best
honest ~0.866" and is now the only lever measured above its own instrument's noise.

This is a reading of the board record, not an experiment; it cost no card and no slot.

### Correction to `base_honest_batch`'s stated axis: it is effective-batch MATCHED to `base_dense` — 2026-09-10

The arm header reads `base_dense` as "batch 2 / accumulate 3" and treats `base_honest_batch`'s batch 5 as
buying a larger optimizer batch. It does not. `accumulate 3` means `base_dense`'s optimizer saw an
**effective batch of 6**, against this arm's **5**. The two runs are matched on the axis the header
claimed to be moving.

What actually differs is the RANKING LOSS's within-batch pair count, which is drawn inside the physical
batch and not across accumulation steps: **1 pair at batch 2, 10 at batch 5, 66 at batch 12.** So the
comparison this arm lands is cleaner than it was designed to be — a near-pure read on ranking-pair
density at fixed trunk, fixed geometry and fixed effective batch, which nothing in the ledger owns.

It also re-points the branches. `base_honest_batch` − `base_dense` is no longer "what batch buys the base
trunk"; it is "what ranking-pair density buys it", and `band_pairmem`'s −0.0092 (measured on the SMALL
trunk at 336/20) is the only prior we have for that quantity.

Epoch-3 anchors, all three on fold 0 under the same 12-epoch `one_cycle` budget:

| run | trunk | physical batch | effective batch | within-batch pairs | epoch 3 | final |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `band_dense` | small | 12 | 12 | 66 | 0.8330 | 0.8578 |
| `base_dense` | base | 2 / acc 3 | 6 | 1 | 0.8232 | 0.8512 |
| `base_honest_batch` | base | 5 | 5 | 10 | **0.8112** | running |

At epoch 3 the arm sits 0.0120 under `base_dense` and 0.0218 under `band_dense`. `trajectory_check`
declines to truncate it (generous ceiling 0.8641 against a 0.8578 target, so the branch is not yet
unreachable), but the median e3→peak gain over 201 matched runs is +0.0205 and p90 is +0.0325, which
project to 0.8317 and 0.8437 — both under `base_dense`'s own 0.8512. The bottom branch is the live one:
the wider trunk under-performing its own handicapped run would say the batch was never what held it
back, and would retire capacity as the last open suspect at n=4,407.

Read the final number against `base_dense` FIRST, and read it as a ranking-pair result, not a batch one.

### The board holds TWO populations and the champion is in the one that cannot be priced — 2026-09-10

`python -m kneemri.kaggle.entry_offline` returns **0 fillable, 48 declined, of 48 entries missing
offline**. Not a backlog — a structural fact, and it retires the whole "fill the missing offline
numbers" thread.

Split the board on whether a row HAS an honest offline number:

| population | n | best board | offline available |
|---|---|---|---|
| priceable (fold-0 members, real holdout) | 52 | **0.937** (`honest12` 0.8751, `distinct14` 0.8749) | yes |
| unpriceable (a full-data or foreign in-sample member) | 48 | **0.944** | never |

Every entry at 0.936 and above carries either a member fitted at `--fold -1` (so it has seen every
holdout study) or a foreign in-sample one. `stackseat_v1`, the pinned champion, declines in-sample on
`calib_span_ff` and `stack_increments_ff`; `cnnseat_v1` declines foreign-in-sample on `raptor_v4_swa`;
`dark6`/`dark7`/`votefit`/`jitterfit` on `final_ws_e12`, `calib_span_ff`, `grade_ladder_ff`,
`base_dense_ff`, `lr4e-5_ws_ff`, `through_dense_ff`.

**Three consequences, and the third is the lever.**

1. **The +0.0614 ensemble transfer constant may not be applied to an unpriceable entry.** It was fitted
   on fold-0 rows, whose members trained on 79% of the studies (3,498 of 4,407); an `_ff` member trained
   on 100%. An "ensemble debt of +0.0110" computed for `cnnseat_v1` that way earlier in this session is
   **invalid and is retracted here**. `entry_offline`'s own docstring is the rule: *a wrongly filled row
   is worse than a null.*

2. **The two populations answer "why are we stuck at 0.944".** Honest seating tops out at 0.937 and the
   0.005 board resolution floor swallows every operation under it, which is why three DIFFERENT member
   sets — ref 56084691 (8 members), `cnnseat_v1` (7), `stackseat_v1` (6) — all returned exactly 0.944.
   That is not three coincidences, it is one ruler that cannot separate them.

3. **The champion is seated from full-data refits of members that were our best MONTHS ago.** The
   full-data census, taken off the recorded `fold` field rather than off the `_ff` filename (a name glob
   misses `_cf`, `_df` and `_ff_s2026` — it undercounted 28 as 12), is **28 checkpoints**. Against the
   top of the current fold-0 pool, almost none of the good members have a full-data twin:

   | fold-0 member | offline | full-data twin |
   |---|---|---|
   | `foreign_distill_mix07_s2026` | 0.8657 | **none** |
   | `clean_calib_s2026` | 0.8649 | **none** |
   | `chainfour_s2026` | 0.8648 | `chainfour_ff_s2026` |
   | `foreign_distill_calib_s2026` | 0.8641 | **none** |
   | `chaindense_s2026` | 0.8628 | **none** |
   | `labelwise_extended_s2026` | 0.8623 | **none** |
   | `foreign_distill_s2026` | 0.8595 | **none** |

   The champion's own seats `calib_span` (0.8545) and `base_dense` (0.8512) are **+0.011 to +0.014
   offline weaker** than members already on disk. That gap sits in the Δ≥0.010 band where **0 of 22**
   board pairs inverted — the one band the ruler can actually see. Refitting current top members at
   `--fold -1` is MEMBER work, not a seating, so it is not on the closed axis.

**The honest caveat, computed before the queue is priced.** The data slope is concave at +0.009 per
doubling, and 79%→100% is ~0.34 doublings ≈ **+0.003** — under the 0.005 floor. So the extra data alone
does NOT explain 0.937→0.944, and the argument for the refit queue rests on **member quality** (the
+0.011 offline gap), not on the extra studies. A refit queue justified on the data bonus would be a
sub-floor operation wearing a mechanism's clothes.

### The default ruler is the WRONG one: `ledger75` more than halves the board resolution — 2026-09-10

`matchpair_v1` was shipped to measure the board's resolution floor at a matched-offline point. It
measured something better: **the ruler.**

The pair, identical on every recorded recipe key (variant small, 336 px, 20 slices, band 0.1-0.9,
`cls_mean`/attend/max, batch 12, 12 epochs, seed 2026, fold 0, lr 4e-5):

| entry | member | midpoint | **ledger75** | board |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `holdsolo_v1` | `calib_dense_hold_s2026` | 0.8634 | 0.8949 | 0.928 |
| `matchpair_v1` | `stackfit_s2026` | 0.8631 | **0.9039** | **0.933** |

Matched to 0.0003 at midpoint and separated by **+0.0090** at ledger75 — and the board moved +0.005,
in ledger75's direction. So the 0.005 was never floor noise. It was a real difference the midpoint
ruler cannot see.

**Tested against the whole record, not just the pair.** Fitting board from each ruler over every entry
carrying both numbers, dropping `aprime_solo_v1` (board 0.506 — a broken entry, not a ruler failure;
it is the ONLY reason a pooled fit ever favoured midpoint, and pooling solos with ensembles was
Simpson's paradox on top of it):

| ruler | n | resid sd | corr | **2sd board resolution** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| midpoint | 40 | 0.0036 | +0.901 | **0.0071** |
| ledger75 | 40 | **0.0015** | **+0.982** | **0.0031** |

Leave-one-out, so this is out-of-sample rather than a leverage artefact — ensembles only, n=34:
midpoint rmse **0.0029**, ledger75 rmse **0.0017**, and ledger75 is closer on **29 of 34** rows. It
wins on solos too once the broken row is out (0.0014 vs 0.0043).

**WHAT THIS COSTS US, stated plainly.** Every offline number in this repo is midpoint unless it says
otherwise — 47 call sites in 41 files take `MIDPOINT = 0.5` by default and exactly three paths can
produce a recut number. So the ruler behind every seating verdict, every "flat" result and every
member ranking this project has written down has **twice the blur of the one we already had on
disk**. The resolution floor that closed the seating axis five times, that made three different
member sets read as an identical 0.944, and that was used this very session to declare operations
"under the floor" — that floor is 0.0071 on the ruler we used and 0.0031 on the ruler we should have
used. Operations previously dismissed as sub-floor at 0.004-0.007 are NOT sub-floor on ledger75.

**WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY.** It does not say those operations WORK — it says they were dismissed with an
instrument that could not see them, which is a different sentence and the reason none of them may be
re-run on this basis alone. Nor does it make the board's own three-decimal granularity go away: 0.001
is still the smallest difference the board can express, so 0.0031 is a floor on the RULER, not a
licence to read thousandths. And this is a predictive claim about board transfer, not an argument
that ledger75 is a better clinical metric.

Closes knee-f9aao with a measurement rather than a preference. The default should move to ledger75,
and until it does, a bare number in this repo is the blurry one.

### RETRACTED THE FOLLOWING EVENING: ledger75 lost its only out-of-sample test — 2026-09-10

Everything above this line about ledger75's superiority is an IN-SAMPLE fit and none of it survived
contact with a point it had not been fitted on.

`l75seat_v1` (ref 56151868) was built as that test and it was a clean one: the same greedy over the
same 226-member pool as `greedyseat_v1` (board 0.936), with ONE variable moved — the cut the greedy
maximises. The two rulers made DIFFERENT predictions about an entry neither had seen. Midpoint said
+0.0007, dead flat, **~0.936**. Ledger75 said +0.0098, **0.949**.

**The board read 0.939.** Midpoint missed by 0.003; ledger75 missed by 0.010, three times as much,
having looked four times sharper on the record.

**The mechanism of the error, which is the part worth keeping.** Ledger75 was fitted board-from-offline
OVER THIS RECORD, and the residual sd above was measured against the same rows. A recut that reorders
the same members and is then SELECTED BY that recut is not a second observation — it is the fit reading
itself back. The leave-one-out above does not rescue it: LOO resamples rows inside one fitted frame and
cannot see a frame chosen to suit them.

**What now holds.** The repo default cut stays **midpoint**, and the P0 migration bead closes UNBUILT.
knee-f9aao's labelling rule — a scalar carries STATISTIC, POPULATION and CUT, `nn_corr@pool251`,
`solo@ledger75` — stands entirely on its own merits and never licensed a ruler swap; it was, and is,
about ambiguity rather than accuracy. The midpoint target arithmetic that the section above declared
superseded is back in force: **board ≈ offline + 0.063, so 0.955 needs ONE member at ~0.874 offline
against our best honest ~0.866.**

**What it does NOT say.** It does not restore any operation dismissed as sub-floor. The floor is
midpoint's 0.0071 again, which is the wider one, so the dismissals stand and this retraction removes
the licence to re-run them rather than granting one.


### Three knob results the ledger owes, all of them flat or worse — 2026-09-08, written up 2026-09-10

None of these was written down when it landed, which is how a repeated experiment gets ordered. All
three are single-arm reads against an existing control, per the quick-over-matched rule; all three are
recorded to CLOSE their knob rather than to price it.

| arm | control | delta | reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base_honest_batch` 0.8502 | `base_dense` 0.8512 | **−0.0010** | the capacity ladder does not pay |
| `band_lpft` 0.8513 | `band_dense` 0.8578 | **−0.0065** | LP-FT costs more than it protects |
| `ortho_fresh_lowlr` 0.8248 | `ortho_dense` 0.8452 | **−0.0204** | 1e-5 does not converge in 12 epochs |

**The capacity ladder (−0.0010).** Under the 0.0062 holdout floor in the losing direction, so it is a
tie read pessimistically and the knob is closed at this budget. It does not say capacity is worthless —
it says the ladder as specified buys nothing a 12-epoch budget can spend.

**LP-FT (−0.0065).** Linear-probe-then-fine-tune is a published defence of pretrained features against
fine-tuning distortion, and here it lands just past the floor on the LOSING side. The mechanism it
protects against is one our recipe does not suffer: at `backbone_lr` 4e-5 for 12 epochs the trunk is
barely moved, so the probe stage spends budget defending against a distortion that was not going to
happen, and the arm is a shorter fine-tune wearing a longer one's schedule. That is a statement about
OUR budget, not about LP-FT, and it would want re-testing at a rate where the trunk actually moves.

**1e-5 undertrains (−0.0204).** By far the largest of the three and the only one clear of every floor.
**REPLICATED**: `ortho_slow_trunk` read 0.8265, within 0.0017 of `ortho_fresh_lowlr`'s 0.8248, from a
different arm on the same axis. Two arms agree that at 12 epochs a 1e-5 trunk rate is not slow-and-safe,
it is unfinished — the run is still climbing when the budget ends. This is a BUDGET × RATE interaction
and not a rate result: it says nothing about 1e-5 at 48 epochs, and `convergence_check` would call both
of these UNDERTRAINED rather than converged. The practical rule it earns: do not read a low-rate arm at
12 epochs as a verdict on the rate.

**What the three say together.** Every knob on this list is flat or negative, and that is now the third
consecutive sweep to end that way. The pool is not short of recipes; it is short of a DIFFERENT member.

## `ortho_fastmri` reads 0.8475 and the per-finding shape is the INVERSE of the one masking would fix — 2026-09-10, 1.6 h of card

Control `ortho_dense` **0.8452** (peak e8), arm `ortho_fastmri` **0.8475** (peak e5). Delta **+0.0023**,
inside the 0.0062 resolution of this holdout and inside the house bar by a factor of six. The middle
branch fired, and the arm's own pre-registration says the breakdown — not the scalar — decides what it
means. Here it is, best epoch against best epoch:

| finding | fastMRI grades it | `ortho_dense` | `ortho_fastmri` | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|

worth about nothing to this stack at 224/12**, and that is the third time it has been measured. It is
also the branch `slots.FASTMRI_MERGED_SCHEME` names in advance: one filled slot of six is too little
input — and masking does not fix too-little-input, it fixes a supervision prior.

**What this does NOT close.** The corpus was decoded at 224/12 into ONE of six canonical slots; 588 of
its 1,173 studies were dropped at the door for filling only `COR_FLUID_NOFS`. A reading of fastMRI at
336/20 with an extended slot axis is a different experiment and this arm says nothing about it. It is
just no longer worth a card ahead of anything else, because — see the licence finding of the same day —

**`ortho_fastmri_masked` is running behind this on the watcher and its premise is falsified by the table
above.** It is left to finish rather than killed for one reason only: it is the arm that separates

the alternative was not a better arm, it was no arm. Its result is pre-declared here as an **offline
close on fastMRI either way** — a win does not re-open a shippable path, because there is no shippable
path.
