## D311 recut on a ruler that was already retracted; D312 hands us the one published result that re-prices the whole member pool — 2026-09-11

Two researcher letters, read together because the first is void on its instrument and the second is not.

### D311 — the blurry-ruler audit does not fire, and the reason is written above it

D311 swept every closure resting on a delta in 0.002-0.008 and recut each one with `LedgerSeventyFive()`
at n=909. Its headline is that `calib_span` vs `band_span` reverses (-0.0020 midpoint to +0.0044
ledger75), which would mean `calib_dense` was killed by a gate read on the wrong ruler and should be
re-opened.

**It does not, because ledger75 was retracted on 2026-09-10 and the retraction anticipated exactly this
use.** `l75seat_v1` (ref 56151868) was the ruler's only out-of-sample test: midpoint predicted ~0.936,
ledger75 predicted 0.949, the board read **0.939**. The section that records it closes: *"It does not
restore any operation dismissed as sub-floor. The floor is midpoint's 0.0071 again, which is the wider
one, so the dismissals stand and this retraction removes the licence to re-run them rather than granting
one."* Every re-open, sign-flip and evaporated negative in D311 is a reading on that ruler. None of them
fires. This is not a criticism of the sweep — the letter went out at 21:41Z and the retraction is the
kind of thing a lane can miss — but the work is not usable as a licence, and it must not be cited as
one later.

**What survives from D311, and it is worth keeping.** Its meta-point is a claim about the CUT rather
than about the ruler's accuracy: the recut moved *every* corpus-corner delta up (all four `merged_*_cf`
vs `merged_blend_cf` pairs) and moved every supervision-flag delta (ema, labelwise) down-to-flat. A
blurry ruler scatters; a ruler that moves one family one way and another family the other way is
DIRECTIONALLY BIASED PER FAMILY, and `ledger75.py:8-14`'s Effusion mechanism is the named carrier —
midpoint counts a 0.68 grade as positive on exactly the columns the corpus arms move. That is a real
statement about what our default cut does to a family of arms, and it stands whether or not ledger75 is
a better ruler, because it never needed ledger75 to be right — only to be different in a patterned way.

**And the licence D311 was reaching for exists, from a different source.** `resnetlong_v1` (board 0.907)
the same evening resolved a -0.0067 offline delta as -0.008 on the board at slope ~1.19, out of sample,
against a holdout whose own 2sd bar is 0.0071. So the board DOES resolve deltas a third the size of our
noise bar. That re-opens arms dismissed on *"inside the floor, therefore nothing"* — but on board
evidence, not on a recut, and never one dismissed on a mechanism.

### D312 — five nulls, and one measured result that says our member pool is built on the wrong data fraction

The nulls first, all confirmed as nulls so nobody searches them again: no measured 100%-refit vs
80%-fold gain at n~1k-10k and no decomposition of it into extra-data vs fold-boundary; no
member-correlation-vs-training-overlap curve anywhere; nothing on the weak-refit vs strong-fold-fit
ordering; nothing treating the binarisation cut of graded truth as an estimator-variance knob (so our
resid-sd 0.0015-vs-0.0036 / corr 0.982-vs-0.901 at n=34 is ours, and belongs in the ledger as ours);
nothing supporting ensembles transferring worse than their members under shift — Ovadia et al.
(arXiv:1906.02530), Pagliardini et al. (arXiv:2202.04414) and Kumar et al. (PMLR 180) all run against
us, so our +0.0036 on n=5 solo anchors is scatter.

**The result that is not a null: Nixon, Lakshminarayanan & Tran, "Why Are Bootstrapped Deep Ensembles
Not Better?", NeurIPS 2020 ICBINB workshop (OpenReview only — there is NO arXiv entry, do not cite
one).** Ten-member WRN-28-10 ensembles on CIFAR-10/100, sweeping the unique-training-point fraction per
member across 63.2% / 70 / 80 / 90 / 99 / 100%. **Member accuracy AND ensemble accuracy both rise
monotonically with the fraction and peak at 100%**, at every ensemble size 2-10, on accuracy and on
ECE; with vs without replacement made no difference.

Why that lands on us: a large part of our pool is FOLD-FIT — each member sees ~80% of the corpus and
holds out its fold. We have carried the assumption that the held-out fifth buys diversity that pays for
the lost data. Nixon measures that trade directly and it does not pay: the data fraction is the whole
effect, and the resampling contributes nothing. The mechanism for why diversity survives a 100% refit
is Fort, Hu & Lakshminarayanan (arXiv:1912.02757) — random init alone lands members in different loss
basins with genuinely different functions, so deep ensembles do not need data partitioning to be
diverse. The classical caution (Breiman 1996) is about unstable weak learners; for CNNs specifically
Lee et al. (arXiv:1511.06314, CVPRW 2016) found bootstrap HURTING. Kuncheva & Whitaker (ML 2003) and
Wood et al. (JMLR 24, 23-0041) add that diversity measures correlate weakly with ensemble gain at all.

**The consequence, stated so it can be argued with.** Our own two-population record is 0.937 cap for a
fold-only entry against 0.944 with a refit member (n=52/48), and our own learning curve prices 79% to
100% at about +0.003 — sub-floor on the midpoint bar, but the board has just shown it resolves deltas
that size. Nixon says that +0.003 is not paid for with lost diversity; it is free. If that holds on our
corpus, the operation is not a new architecture at all: it is refitting existing recipes on 100% of the
data and keeping the seed as the diversity source. That is also the one thing the owner has asked for
repeatedly and the project has never done — *use more data*.

**What would prove it here rather than on CIFAR.** The missing measurement D312 names — member error
correlation as a function of pairwise training-set overlap — is one our pool can produce with no card
at all: every fold-fit member already has a `.holdout.npz`, the overlap between any two fold-fit members
is known exactly from their fold assignments, and the correlation is a read. Nobody has that curve in
print, in any regime. It is the cheapest instrument in the backlog and it decides whether the
100%-refit operation is free here or only on CIFAR.

### The overlap-vs-correlation curve cannot be read off our disk, and k-fold is why — 2026-09-11

D312 names member error correlation as a function of pairwise training-set overlap as the one measurement
absent from the literature in every regime. The section above called it the cheapest instrument in the
backlog — a CPU read over holdout files we already have. **That was wrong, and the audit that found it
took four minutes and no card.**

Census of every `*.holdout.npz` on disk: **357 files, 12 distinct study sets.**

| study set | n | members | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `26b8a303` | 909 | **309** | `adapt_null_s2026` |
| `84d31d3a` | 896 | 10 | `raptor_ft_hisrecipe_distill` |
| `b9d9c8fa` / `c8146533` / `84a3402a` / `1ff8952d` | 875 / 884 / 849 / 890 | 6 / 5 / 5 / 5 | `oof_band_fold1..4_s2026` |
| `6da0bc94` | 4406 | 1 | `foreign_oof_corpus` |
| the rest | 8-83 | 1-10 | smokes and probes |

Read that as an overlap axis and it has **two levels, and only one of them is measurable**:

* **100% overlap** — the 309 members sharing `26b8a303` all trained on the same 3498 studies and held out
  the same 909. Every pair among them is at full overlap. One level, 309 members deep.
* **75% overlap** — `oof_fold0..4` hold out five sets whose pairwise intersection is **exactly 0** and
  whose union is **4407, the whole corpus**. Two members that held out different folds each train on 4 of
  5 folds and share 3, so they sit at 75%. **They have no evaluation row in common, by construction.**

A pair at 75% is never both out-of-sample anywhere. That is not a gap in what we saved — it is what
k-fold *is*, and it is the most likely reason the curve is missing from the literature rather than an
oversight anybody could correct by looking harder.

**What the measurement actually costs.** To vary overlap continuously while keeping a shared
out-of-sample set, members must be fit on RANDOM subsets rather than fold complements — which is exactly
how Nixon et al. sampled. Draw K members at ~80% of the corpus with independent random subsets: any two
share ~64% of their training data, and their held-out remainders intersect in ~4% of the corpus, ~176
rows at n=4407. That intersection is the common evaluation set, and it is small — so a single pair's
correlation is noisy and the curve needs many PAIRS, not many rows. Cost is K fits of card, not zero.
Filed on knee-57d68, which is re-scoped rather than queued.

**The rule this leaves behind.** "We already have the artefacts" is a claim about files, not about
design. Before pricing an instrument at zero, check that the two things it must compare were ever
measured on common ground — here they never were and never could be.

### teacher_gen2: five twins, every fold up over its gen-1 counterpart, mean +0.0121 — 2026-09-11

The born-again round ran 2026-09-11 00:21Z-01:10Z and finished all five folds. **Forty-nine minutes**,
67 s an epoch, against a docstring that had quoted "~1.2 h per fold". The re-price written into the arm
that morning off the `seconds` field of every `oof_*.metrics.jsonl` on disk said ~1 h; the arm then ran
in 49 min. The prose figure was wrong by about six times and had been sitting unchallenged in the cost
line of a card-scheduling decision.

Matched per fold against the gen-1 twins, same geometry, same eight epochs, `--distill-weight 0.7
--teacher-targets teacher_oof_full.npz` the only moved variable:

| fold | gen-1 (`oof_fold*`) | gen-2 (`oof_gen2_fold*`) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.8498 | **0.8609** | +0.0111 |
| 1 | 0.8578 | **0.8707** | +0.0129 |
| 2 | 0.8567 | **0.8733** | +0.0166 |
| 3 | 0.8740 | **0.8814** | +0.0074 |
| 4 | 0.8695 | **0.8820** | +0.0125 |

**Every fold up, mean +0.0121.** `convergence_check` reports nothing against any of the five, and all
five `.holdout.npz` exist. The comparison is matched PER FOLD and never pooled: each fold's holdout is a
different 849-909 study set, so the five deltas are five independent readings of one treatment, not one
reading with n=4407. Five-for-five in the same direction at a magnitude 1.7x the 0.0071 noise bar is the
strongest single-treatment signal in this record.

**What the number is NOT.** The arm's own header declares it: *"IT HAS NO PRE-REGISTRATION AND WANTS
NONE. This is a producer, not a member and not a candidate."* These are distillation STUDENTS, so
0.8820 prices the distillation term, not a shippable member — a student taught by a teacher is not
comparable to a solo fit on the same axis, and none of the five belongs on the roster on the strength of
this table. What the table licenses is the claim the producer was built to support: **the gen-2 teacher's
blocks read ~0.0121 above the gen-1 blocks they replace**, and every consumer downstream MULTIPLIES that
term.

**And the union exists.** `oof_teacher --twins 'oof_gen2_fold[0-4]_s2026.holdout.npz'` wrote
`teacher_gen2_full.npz`: 909 + 875 + 884 + 849 + 890 = **4407 studies, 12 targets, no fill and no
witness needed**. Gen-1 covered folds 1-4 (3498 rows) and needed a fold-0 block from a differently-shaped
reader, which `oof_teacher --fill`'s witness read outside the fold-to-fold scatter on 9/12 labels. Gen-2
is homogeneous by construction: five blocks, one recipe, one teacher. The heterogeneity caveat that has
followed every filled teacher in this record does not attach to it.

**The leak property is inherited, not fixed, and it decides which consumer may read it.** Each gen-2
block held its own fold out, so a study's teacher row never comes from a model that trained on it. But
the twins were fitted WITHOUT `--exclude-fold`, so twin 1's fit saw fold 0 — the same structure that
makes `teacher_oof_corpus.npz` leaky for a fold-0-scored student (README.md:8526, knee-zwcyk), by the
residual-mimicry mechanism D30 measured at +0.0127. So `teacher_gen2_full.npz` is for `--fold -1`
consumers scored on the BOARD, where there is no offline holdout for a mimicked residual to inflate. A
fold-k-scored consumer needs an `--exclude-fold k` refit of the other four twins first, which is four
fits of card per scored fold and is not owed by anything currently queued.

### RETRACTION, 2026-09-11 02:25Z — the +0.0121 above is the leak, and the probe that was meant to gate an 8.5 h arm is the control that proves it

The section above was written at 01:32Z and is wrong in its central claim. It reports five gen-2 fold
twins beating their gen-1 counterparts by a mean of **+0.0121**, five for five, and reads that as the
gen-2 teacher's blocks being that much better. **They are not. That number is a leak, and the arm that
was launched forty minutes later to gate a consumer is what shows it.**

**The probe.** `seat_distill_gen2` — the same seat, the same control, one moved variable, 12 epochs at
168 s, 35 minutes of card:

| arm | teacher | offline | vs control |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lr4e-5_ws_s2026` | none | 0.8525 | — |
| `seat_distill_lr4e5_s2026` | gen-1, `teacher_oof_corpus.npz` | 0.8633 | +0.0108 |
| `seat_distill_gen2_s2026` | gen-2, `teacher_gen2_full.npz` | **0.8640** | **+0.0115** |

Gen-2 over gen-1 on the same student: **+0.0007**. `convergence_check` is silent on both, both peaked
mid-schedule (e11 and e8 of 12), and the recipe line of the running arm confirms the teacher flag landed.
Pre-registered band three of four: *"inside the gen-1 student's own scatter. The teacher got better and
the student did not."*

**The arithmetic that says which of the two readings is true.** The gen-1 twins (`oof_fold*`) were
fitted PLAIN — no teacher. The gen-2 twins were fitted under `teacher_oof_full.npz`, whose fold-k rows
are written by models that TRAINED on fold k, so each gen-2 twin's own holdout score carries residual
mimicry — the mechanism this ledger already measured at **+0.0127** (README.md:8526, knee-zwcyk, D30).

Measured **+0.0121** against a mechanism priced at **+0.0127** is not a gain with a leak in it. It is
the leak, to within a tenth of its own size. And the probe is the matched control that separates them:
when BOTH students carry the same leak, the gen-2-over-gen-1 difference collapses from +0.0121 to
+0.0007. A teacher-quality difference would have survived that subtraction. A leak is exactly what does
not.

**What this retracts.**

1. *"the gen-2 teacher's blocks read ~0.0121 above the gen-1 blocks they replace"* — withdrawn. The
   blocks are not measurably better. `teacher_gen2_full.npz` remains the more homogeneous file (five
   real out-of-fold blocks at one geometry, no fill, no witness needed) and that property is unaffected
   — it was never a claim about quality.
2. The multiply-the-term thesis, which is the entire premise of the born-again round: *"everything
   downstream MULTIPLIES the teacher's term, and this is the only place left to grow the term."* A
   teacher whose blocks moved by whatever the +0.0121 really was moved its student by +0.0007. The term
   did not multiply. It did not pass through at all.
3. The queued 8.5 h `retrain_six_distill` under gen-2. It has no premise and it is not queued. Thirty-five
   minutes of card bought the answer that eight and a half hours would have bought worse, and the
   pre-registered bands are why it reads as an answer rather than as a disappointment.

**What it does NOT retract, stated so a later letter cannot over-read this.** It does not say the
born-again idea is wrong; it says this generation of it, on this corpus, at this geometry, did not move
a student. It does not kill `teacher_gen2_full.npz`, which is still the only teacher in the project with
no heterogeneous block. And it does not, yet, say anything about distillation itself.

**The larger claim it opens, which is now on the card.** `seat_distill_lr4e5`'s **+0.0108** — the
per-seat term the champion's own reasoning applies six times — was taken through
`teacher_oof_corpus.npz`, which is folds 1-4, every block fitted without `--exclude-fold`, every one of
them having trained on fold 0, against a seat scored on fold 0. That is the same leak structure and
+0.0108 is the same coincidence with +0.0127 a second time. **Distillation may buy nothing on this seat
and may never have**, and if so, every distilled member in the pool carries an offline number taken the
same way.

`seat_distill_clean` was launched at 02:25Z to settle it: the same seat a third time under
`teacher_clean_full.npz`, whose folds 1-4 were refitted under `--exclude-fold 0` so that not one block
was written by a model that saw fold 0. Four bands pre-registered, the bottom one set INSIDE the
control's own 0.0071 bar so that "indistinguishable from the control" is a verdict rather than a shrug.
Forty minutes, and it prices a term that has been steering card and slots for weeks.

**The rule this leaves behind.** A treatment measured only through an instrument that shares its
failure mode has not been measured. Both readings of the born-again round — the twins' +0.0121 and the
student's +0.0108 — were taken through teachers that had seen the holdout, and both landed within a
tenth of the leak's own priced size. The tell was available before either arm ran: **when a measured
effect matches a known artefact to two decimal places, the artefact is the first hypothesis, not the
last.**

### The honest distillation term is +0.0056, replicated at two corners, and the leak is a +0.0052 surcharge — 2026-09-11 03:15Z

`seat_distill_clean` finished at 03:00Z, 12 epochs at 168 s, peak **0.8581** at e8. `convergence_check`
is silent on it. It lands in the arm's own **band two** (0.8560-0.8599): *"distillation is real but
roughly half of every distilled offline number in this repo is leak."*

The full four-point table at the 336 px / 12 sl / band 0.2-0.8 seat, one control, one moved variable
each time (the `224/8` this section first printed is the TEACHER FILE's row geometry, not the student's —
read off `*.metrics.jsonl` line 0, 04:22Z):

| arm | teacher | offline | vs control |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lr4e-5_ws_s2026` | none | 0.8525 | — |
| `seat_distill_clean_s2026` | **clean**, `teacher_clean_full.npz` | **0.8581** | **+0.0056** |
| `seat_distill_lr4e5_s2026` | leaky, `teacher_oof_corpus.npz` | 0.8633 | +0.0108 |
| `seat_distill_gen2_s2026` | leaky, `teacher_gen2_full.npz` | 0.8640 | +0.0115 |

**Distillation is real and it is worth +0.0056. The leak is a +0.0052 surcharge on top of it**, which is
almost exactly half of the +0.0108 that has been quoted as the per-seat distillation term since the axis
opened.

**And it replicates.** `seat_clean_distill` asked the same question on 2026-09-07 at a completely
different corner — 336 px / 20 slices, control `band_dense_s2026` 0.8578, a different clean teacher file
(`teacher_clean.npz`, not `teacher_clean_full.npz`) — and read **0.8634**. That is **+0.0056**. Two
geometries, two teacher files, two control arms, the same number to four decimal places. The honest
distillation term is a knob and it is now one of the better-measured quantities in this record.

**The clean teacher's own handicap does not explain the gap, and the gen-2 probe is why we can say so.**
The clean twins are starved of one fold and cost −0.0067 as teachers (`compose_v4b_clean.sh:47`), so the
obvious objection is that the clean arm reads low because its teacher is weak rather than because the
leaky arms read high. The pass-through measured last night refutes it: a teacher whose blocks read
+0.0121 better moved the same student by **+0.0007**, a pass-through of about 6%. At 6%, a teacher
0.0067 weaker costs the student ~0.0004 — one thirteenth of the 0.0052 that has to be explained. The
surcharge is the leak.

### CORRECTION, same morning: the corpus is NOT saturated — beta = 0.22 measured on our own three-point curve, and "use more data" is the biggest live lever we own — 2026-09-11 05:50Z

The section immediately above concluded that refitting on all 4,407 studies "buys nothing measurable on
our board" from a matched pair reading delta 0.000. **That conclusion was wrong, and the error was
statistical power, not arithmetic.** The correction costs no card either: the learning curve was already
on disk and nobody had fitted it.

**THE CURVE.** Three runs, matched, differing in `train_fraction` and nothing else that is set
(`quarter_data_s2026` and `half_data_s2026` diff in exactly one recorded flag; `band_dense_s2026` is the
1.0 control — its recipe is an older vintage so several fields read absent rather than equal, and those
absences are the defaults the other two record explicitly). All three: 336 px, 20 slices, band 0.1-0.9,
max pooling, whole-stack, lr 4e-5, 12 epochs, fold 0, seed 2026, no calibration, no hold, no distill.

| train_fraction | N studies | peak AUC | error |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.25 | 874 | 0.7907 | 0.2093 |
| 0.50 | 1,749 | 0.8344 | 0.1656 |
| 1.00 | 3,498 | **0.8578** | 0.1422 |

Fitting `error ∝ N^{-β}` on each doubling:

    beta(874 -> 1749)  = 0.338
    beta(1749 -> 3498) = 0.220

**Declining, but nowhere near zero.** β ≈ 0.22 is the live exponent at our corpus size.

**WHY THE BOARD PAIR READ 0.000 ANYWAY.** At β = 0.22 a 1.26× refit (3,498 → 4,407) predicts **+0.0070
offline** for the MEMBER. The matched pair that measured 0.000 — `lastseat_v1` → `dark7_v1` — moved ONE
SEAT OF SEVEN. A member-level +0.007 entering one of seven seats arrives at the ensemble output diluted by
roughly a factor of seven, i.e. ~+0.001, against a board that resolves ~0.005. **The test could not have
detected the effect even if it were exactly as large as the curve predicts.** Delta 0.000 is therefore
consistent with β = 0.22 and is not evidence against it; it is an underpowered test, and this ledger has
the same wall recorded from the other side at README:13567 ("one ruler that cannot separate them").

What survives from the section above, unchanged: the axis was never blocked (28 refits shipped, the
champion is built out of them), a refit is unpriceable rather than unshippable, and the matched-board-pair
route is real — it is just far too blunt at one seat in seven. What is retracted is the sentence
"refitting on the same 4,407 studies buys nothing measurable on our board", and the ≤ 0.000 bound that
sentence rested on.

**THE CONSEQUENCE, WHICH IS MUCH LARGER THAN THE REFIT.** β ≈ 0.22 prices the owner's standing
*"use more data"* directive for the first time:

| operation | N factor | predicted delta offline | at board transfer x1.55 |
|---|---|---|---|
| refit fold-0 member on all our studies | 1.26x | +0.0070 | +0.011 |
| **double the corpus** | 2.0x | **+0.0201** | **+0.031** |

Nothing on the knob axis has produced anything of that size. The whole calibration/hold/distill factorial
this ledger has spent weeks on moves members by 0.002-0.007, and the replicated calib x hold interaction —
the most reproducible term we own — is +0.008 and is a repair rather than a gain. **Doubling the corpus is
priced at two to four times the best knob we have ever found**, and it is the one operation the owner has
asked for repeatedly and the project has never run.

Two honest caveats, both of which sharpen the target rather than blunt it:

1. **β is declining (0.338 → 0.220), so the next doubling is worth less than this fit says.** Continuing
   the decay to β ≈ 0.15 still prices a doubling at +0.014 offline / +0.022 board — larger than every
   knob on record. The lever survives the pessimistic reading.
2. **A doubling means FOREIGN studies, and the curve above was fitted on in-distribution data.** Every
   point on it is RSNA knee MRI; adding fastMRI/MRNet/Rijeka/SKM-TEA adds studies from a different

**THIS RE-RANKS THE BLOCKERS.** The foreign corpora are blocked on LICENCE, not on availability, value, or

**COST: no card.** Statistic **cell disagreement at midpoint on both sides**, population **gold57**
(the 58 organiser-labelled studies of `raw/train.csv`, one absent from our tables), cut **midpoint**.

```
flight0234  report_labels_v4hybrid   FP  86  FN 38   0.1813

steven      llm_labels_v4_blend      FP  87  FN 38   0.1827
steven      llm_labels_full          FP 104  FN 32   0.1988
OURS        report_labels_v2         FP 108  FN 32   0.2047
MAJORITY_5                           FP  87  FN 38   0.1827
```

Paired study-clustered bootstrap, 20,000 resamples, `default_rng(2026)`, 57 studies:
**ours − majority5 = +0.0219, 95% CI [+0.0044, +0.0395].** `experiments/lib.sh:72` puts
**286 arm invocations** on the losing table.

**These are not circular the way `report_labels_v3` is.** v3 was FITTED on these 58
(`interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-03_the-report-reader-is-the-weaker-half.md:25`), which is why it reads
0.1696 — and the threshold sweep shows why: v3 is v2 RE-CUT, not re-extracted. v2's five levels are
`0.08 / 0.28 / 0.68 / 0.82 / 0.94`, and cutting the 0.68 rung out reproduces v3's number to three
decimals (0.2047 -> 0.1696, FP 108 -> 47). That reconciles
`2026-09-02_what-label-correction-is-actually-worth.md:50`'s "identical to v2 on every gold column" with
a 61/37 cell split: same table, different cut. The foreign tables were built by other people from the
same reports and none pasted gold — seven tables in `raw/knee_label_tables/` read EXACTLY 0.0000 on all
58 and are unrulable for that reason; the five above do not.

**The error is one-sided and that is the mechanism.** Ours: **FP 108 against FN 32**, a 3.4:1 over-call.
Per column, ours-positive vs gold-positive: Contusion 36/18, MCL 18/9, Effusion 50/34, ACL 32/23 —
Contusion's precision is 16/36 = 0.44, so more than half of our Contusion positives are wrong. Synovitis
is the lone inversion (16/27, under-called). An extractor reading a MENTION as a FINDING produces exactly
this shape, and the 0.68 rung is where it lives: that rung's precision here is 37/98 = **0.38**, which is
`MEASURED_AGREEMENT`'s pooled 0.378 arrived at independently.

**WHY THIS WAS NEVER FOUND — the ruler is rigged against it.** Our 909-study holdout labels are derived
from v2. A member trained on a TRUER table is scored against a v2-derived ruler and must read worse by
construction; the truer the table, the worse it reads. Every offline test of a label swap this project
could run is a test of agreement-with-v2 wearing a score's clothes. `oof_band_folds` (README:13061)
already hit the other horn: the only clean ruler is gold@58 and it cannot resolve ±0.012, which is what
D301 §6 and D297 §4 both mean by "the cheapest thing that would settle it is more gold".

**The board is the third ruler and it is the right one.** `README:3844-3847` records the competition's
labels as image-read radiologist consensus with third-reader adjudication — the same KIND of object the
58 are, and NOT report-derived. So a table closer to radiologist truth should transfer better to the
board even while reading worse offline, and the board is the only instrument that can show it.

**PRE-REGISTRATION.** One arm, `band_dense`'s recipe with `--labels` pointing at
`lixin73_.../report_labels_gpt56sol.csv` and nothing else changed. Offline against `band_dense_s2026`
(0.8578 on the v2-derived holdout) the prediction is **NEGATIVE, and a negative is not a refutation** —
the ruler shares its labels with the control. Branches: (a) offline within −0.010 -> the table is
competitive despite the rigged ruler, ship it and read the board; (b) offline below −0.020 -> the table
is worse on the pixels too and the gold advantage does not survive training; (c) the read that matters is
the BOARD delta against an otherwise identical entry, and that costs one slot.

**What this does NOT claim.** The four foreign tables are 93.9% unanimous over all 52,872 cells, so this
is about TWO opinions, not five, and the majority vote (0.1827) does not beat its own best member
(0.1813) — voting buys nothing here. Whether those teams tuned their prompts on the same 58 is
unknowable from the files; if they did, their 0.181 is optimistic and ours is the only honest number in
the table. +0.0219 is above the 0.005 floor but it is a LABEL-SPACE delta, not a score, and no score
follows from it until an arm runs.

**COST: no card, no slot.** Read off `comp/board.jsonl` (128 rows) and four ledger regions. Nothing
new was measured; this is the ledger's own numbers put next to each other for the first time.

**The board has never exceeded 0.944.** Over all 128 submissions the maximum is 0.944, and it was hit
**ten times** between 2026-08-30 and 2026-09-10, at **6, 7 and 8 members**. Two of those ten share
**zero members with each other**:

```
55875622  2026-08-30  kneemri-raptorweight  7m  final_ws_cf calib_span_ff grade_ladder_cf
                                                merged_blend_cf lr4e-5_ws_cf through_dense_cf raptor_v4_swa
56147841  2026-09-10  kneemri-cnnseat       7m  labelwise_dense_s2026 foreign_labels_dense_s2026
                                                warm_calib_dense_s2026 warm_calib_lowlr_s2026
                                                span_dense_s2026 raptor_v4_swa resnet_224_short_s2026
```

Six of seven seats replaced, an entire family swapped in, twelve days apart — **0.944 both times.**
The score histogram is quantised around it: 0.944 x10, 0.943 x8, 0.937 x11. Nothing above.

**The mechanism is already recorded and this is its confirmation at the board level.**
`README:9525`: *"the weak columns are weak in EVERY member, so a seat cannot buy them."* D56 prices the
diversity pitch at **+0.0004 [-0.0001, +0.0008]** at nine seats and states the consequence: *"Any future
arm whose pitch is 'a more diverse member' is priced at ~0 before it runs; the pitch has to be solo LIFT
or a different axis."* Three seating operations — reweight (raptorweight), add (vjepaseat), swap
(holdswap) — read +0.001 / -0.001 / 0.000, all inside BOARD_RESOLVABLE = 0.0015. The ten-way tie is the
fourth and strongest support for knee-uco3's inert-seat reading: **an ensemble cannot average away an
error its members share.**

**What the ceiling costs, in the metric's own units.** `kernels/kneemri-colnull` submitted a constant
0.5 in every cell and read EXACTLY 0.500, which measured the metric rather than assuming it: an
unweighted mean of twelve per-column ROC AUCs, no offset, no prevalence weighting, no non-AUC term. So a
column gaining `d` moves the board `d/12`, and the 0.010 gap to the leader is **0.120 of summed column
area** — one column +0.12, or three at +0.04, or twelve at +0.01. No seating operation can produce any
of those, because seating does not change what a column knows.

**And the map we would aim that at is refuted.** knee-zsyp4. D84c: Spearman **0.056** between two frames
on which columns pay (896 says Fracture/MedMen/Synovitis, 4406 says MCL/PFOA/Baker's). D85: shrinking a
frame from 4407 to 909 rows costs rho **0.16-0.29** of column ordering with nothing else changed.
`column_headroom.py`'s own docstring says its ordering is *"OUR supervision binarised at its midpoint,
not Kaggle truth"*. **Every per-column plan since 2026-09-05 was aimed by an instrument this ledger
calls refuted, at per-column board values that have never been read.**

**What this closes.** The member axis and the seat axis, jointly and at the board rather than on a
holdout. Not "no more seatings because it keeps reading flat" — *no more seatings because ten disjoint
rosters produce one number, and the metric says why.* Any arm whose pitch is a new member, a new seat, a
new weight or a new vote is priced at ~0 before it runs.

**What it opens.** Exactly one thing: the board's OWN per-column areas, which `comp/README.md:301`
already says how to read — an entry replacing ONE column with a constant drops from the champion by
`(that column's board AUC - 0.5) / 12`. At AUC 0.80 that is a 0.025 drop, ~17x the resolution floor.
Twelve slots for the full map is too much; the single-slot form is a go/no-go on the aiming instrument
itself — null the six columns our offline map calls weakest, compare the measured summed area against
what the map predicts, and either license every per-column plan or kill the map on the board. Sent to
the researcher as M327 Q1/Q2: whether one constant column beside eleven live ones scores 0.5 the way all
twelve did, and whether the competition rules permit it. **Not armed until both come back clean.**

**Withdrawn in the same breath: `foreign_labels_dense`.** An arm by that name was built, priced and
armed on the card this morning. It had already RUN on 2026-09-07 (75 min, `README:9311`), is priced by

**Two columns carry nearly all the disagreement, in opposite directions, and both have a recorded

## 2026-09-11 — the depth curve we never measured, and the montage we were about to build backwards (D323, D324)

**COST: no card, no slot.** Two researcher syntheses, filed at
`research/2026-09-11_attention-pool-depth-saturation-and-lateral-oa-reads.md` and
`research/2026-09-11_vlm-montage-prompting-and-small-gold-validation.md`. Every claim below is theirs
with a verified citation; the declared NULLs are as load-bearing as the numbers.

### 1. Our max-pooled slice sweep was never evidence about depth — the mechanism is in print

`knee-ezz` read **−0.0001** for 20 slices over 12 and that number closed the depth axis for this
project. It ran under `--slice-pooling max`. CLAM (Lu et al., Nat Biomed Eng 2021, PMC8711640), verbatim:
max-pooling *"uses the gradient signal from only a single instance in each slide"* — the training signal
is one slice deep no matter how deep the bag, so slices past the argmax cannot pay. Ilse et al.
(arXiv:1802.04712): *"attention serves as a gradient update filter during backpropagation."* CLAM-MB's N
parallel branches each mine *"a different set of highly attended regions … strong positive evidence for
one of N classes"* — which is what `--slice-pooling labelwise` is, arrived at independently here.

So `knee-ezz` is downgraded the way M325 downgraded the max-pooled axes: **UNREAD, not refuted.** It
measured max pooling's indifference to depth, which is a property of max pooling.

**The foreign curve is the only depth evidence this project holds that was taken under a working head.**
`foreign_gate` on Raptor's per-finding attention model through our caches, 58 gold studies:
`336px_12sl 0.8700 → 16sl 0.8727 (+0.0027) → 20sl 0.8773 (+0.0046)`. The second increment is LARGER.

**NULL declared, and it is the reason to run this.** No published paper reports accuracy-vs-instance-count
separated by class-specific vs shared/max aggregation. A 12/16/20/24 sweep under both heads would be the
first such curve in the literature.

**The two on-regime curves that do exist disagree with each other**, which is what makes 24 a question
rather than a knob:
- Ilse et al. 2018, MNIST-bags, mean bag size {10, 50, 100}: attention 0.996 vs instance+max 0.553 at
  size 100; at size 10, attention ~0.80–0.86 vs max ~0.55–0.75. Attention's advantage is LARGEST in the
  small-sample regime and *"the more instances in a bag the easier the MIL task becomes"*.
- Li et al., MICCAI 2025, doi:10.1007/978-3-032-04927-8_30 — MIL over CT slices per lymph node, a bag
  regime nearly identical to ours: **9 sl 81.12±2.78 → 18 sl 82.54±2.10 → 27 sl 81.77±2.60.** Saturates
  by ~18, degrades at 27 (within its own ±2.6).

So the pre-registration for the 24-slice labelwise arm is **flat-to-slightly-negative**, and it is armed
as an INSTRUMENT that settles the depth axis under a head that can see it — not as a predicted gain. The
cache is on disk (`images_336px_24sl_0.1-0.9band.npy`, 66.7 GB); the arm is one variable against
`labelwise_dense_s2026` (0.8613@holdout909). Counter-direction on record: FocusMIL (arXiv:2408.09449)
argues max is more robust under domain shift — about shift, not depth.

### 2. Lateral OA is retired as a card target: the gap is over-determined, and none of it is the model

M328 named Lateral OA the one column weak on BOTH rulers and pointed the next arm at it. Five independent
literature findings say a gap of our size is what a healthy pipeline produces there:

1. **Prevalence geometry.** Stoddart et al., OAC 2021, PMID 33253887 (meta-analysis, 16 studies, 3,786
   knees): all lateral-TF patterns sum to **15% (CI 8.5–18.7) vs isolated medial 27%**.
2. **Harder for radiologists AND for CNNs.** Fritz et al., Skeletal Radiol 2020, PMID 32170334:
   sensitivity medial **93–96%** vs lateral **67–71%**; κ 0.876 vs 0.741; DCNN AUC 0.882 vs 0.781.
3. **Under-read from REPORTS specifically — our ruler's own channel.** Krakowski et al., Appl Sci 2021,
   doi:10.3390/app11041552, 190 arthroscopy-correlated knees read from clinical reports: lateral tibial
   condyle AUC **0.578**, lowest of five locations; chondral-lesion report sensitivity 24–42%.
4. **Noisiest reference standard.** MOAKS reliability (Hunter et al., OAC 2011, PMC4058435): inter-rater
   tibial cartilage area **κ=0.36** against 0.61–1.0 elsewhere. Subregion granularity is SYMMETRIC between
   compartments; what differs is reliability.
5. **Sequence, not plane.** The cartilage/OA cornerstone is 2D FSE intermediate-weighted FAT-SUPPRESSED,
   TE 30–40 ms (Omoumi, Skeletal Radiol 2023, PMID 37154871); BMLs are fs-T2/STIR-only signal (Del Grande
   2014 PMC4126144; Mirowitz AJR 1994 PMID 8273669) — **our non-FS acquisitions are blind to BMLs by
   physics.** No plane is compartment-specific, which corroborates the slot-affinity reading.

**The one actionable, card-free piece.** Bloecker et al., JMRI 2013, PMC3696373 (OAI 3D morphometry):
the **lateral meniscus covers 59±6.8% of its tibial plateau vs medial 50±5.5% (p<0.001)** — proportionally
more lateral cartilage hidden under meniscus on every coronal slice. Nobody has counted coronal-slice
coverage by compartment and no banded-MIL sampling-bias work exists (NULL). The test is ours and costs no
card: count informative-slice coverage by compartment in the gold-58 stacks against our `--band-low 0.1
--band-high 0.9` window. A geometry defect there is fixable with a cache flag.

### 3. The montage we were about to build is the design the measurements reject

M330 asked for montage geometry for a generated Synovitis column. The 2026 3D-medical-VQA evidence runs
against dense tiling, twice:

- **SpatialMed (arXiv:2603.13800), Table 5** — 3 orthogonal centre slices vs a 20-axial-slice tiled grid,
  three models, montage loses for all three; **HealthGPT-XL32 62.44 vs 41.69, −20.75**, the largest loss
  belonging to the medical-specialized model: *"tiling perturbs the visual statistics it relies on most."*
- **UCSF-PDGM-VQA (arXiv:2605.17140)** — brain MRI; montage of best slices HARMED vs separate slices;
  MedGemma-1.5 multi-slice-separate 63.57% vs single-slice 55.37%.
- LoCoVQA (EMNLP 2024 Findings): accuracy decays ~log in image count. Visual Haystacks (ICLR 2025,
  arXiv:2407.13766): degradation plus placement bias. Chest-CT GPT-4V (Jpn J Radiol 2024,
  doi:10.1007/s11604-024-01606-3): practical ceiling ~4 slices per conversation.
- Resolution is not a smooth knob — LLaVA-UHD (ECCV 2024, arXiv:2403.11703) measured a PHASE CHANGE in
  GPT-4V behaviour with input resolution, and SpatialMed's stated mechanism for the montage loss is
  *"substantial per-slice down-scaling"*. Synovitis is a resolution-sensitive finding.

**Design that survives: few tiles at high per-tile resolution, multiple planes, slices as SEPARATE images
— not a grid.** Rendering slice index or sequence name as text into the tile is a NULL, and the adjacent
evidence discourages it: MedBLINK (arXiv:2508.02951) — models detect marks at 99–100% but score barely
above chance on tasks requiring USE of the mark; BLINK (ECCV 2024, arXiv:2404.12390) — GPT-4V 51.26% vs
human 95.70%. Marks are seen, not reasoned about.

### 4. Grade prompts UNDER-call — the opposite of what an under-called column needs

Synovitis is our lone UNDER-call (M326: 16 ours vs 27 gold) and 84% UNK in report text (D20). The instinct
was a graded prompt. Measured, it points the other way: **Chetla et al., Clin Ophthalmol 2025,
PMC12411675** (2,500 fundus photos, 8 prompt designs) — graded 5-level prompts biased hard toward
"absent", sensitivity for mild disease **0.028–0.040**, adjacent grades collapsed into "no disease".

What measurably moves the operating point, in controlled directions:
- **Explanation prompts recover FNs.** Guo et al., MELBA 2025:004, LLaVA-Med on MIMIC-CXR/CheXpert:
  pathology-explanation prompts (definition + visual findings) raised recall substantially at minimal
  precision cost, **F1 +0.115 to +0.194**.
- **Reference-classifier prompts suppress FPs** — the same paper's weak-learner-augmented prompt cut
  Edema FPs by **78.5%**.
- **The instruction itself sets the point.** Sorin et al., JAMIA Open 2025, PMC12343119, 11,999 reports,
  22 variants: explicit *"prioritize minimizing false negatives"* drove recall to **0.997**; FP counts
  ranged 3–56 and FN 3–104 across variants; **chain-of-thought DEGRADED** performance.
- **Repeat-and-vote is priced.** Liu et al. 2026, PMC13060412: majority vote over 10 samples raised
  Fleiss' κ for every model and task with F1 preserved; prompt PARAPHRASING degrades agreement more than
  temperature does. Sorin measured nondeterminism at temperature 0 across cloud regions (sensitivity
  0.90–0.998) — the variance exists whether or not we invite it.
- **One-finding-per-call vs all-twelve: NULL.** No measured head-to-head exists; joint prompting is the
  community default (MADE, arXiv:2604.15203, which also finds self-verbalized confidence unreliable).

**So our generated table does NOT inherit the extractor's 3.4:1 FP:FN shape by necessity.** The prompt
sets the operating point, and the measured lever for the FN side is explanation CONTENT, not grading.

### 5. The n=58 validation trap has a floor, and the floor decides where the reading happens

Split-the-gold is the CheXpert precedent (Irvin et al., AAAI 2019, arXiv:1901.07031 — labeler tuned on
200 studies, compared once on a separate 500-study consensus set). At n=58 that is ~29/29, and the
researcher computed the Hanley & McNeil closed form (Radiology 1982,
doi:10.1148/radiology.143.1.7063747; flagged DERIVED, not measured): at 27 pos / 31 neg, SE(AUC) ≈ 0.12
at true AUC 0.80 → **95% CI half-width ≈ ±0.19–0.24 on the full 58, ±0.27+ on a 29/29 split.**

**A split of the 58 certifies "better than chance". It cannot resolve "the VLM column beats the report
column by 0.05".** This is the same wall `oof_band_folds` hit (README:13061) and what D301 §6 and D297 §4
both mean by "the cheapest thing that would settle it is more gold" — now with a number on it. So a
generated column is read against the report-table channel over all 4407, or against the board. Never
against a split of the 58. Routes that do not need gold, for the record: partial identification (Maia
Polo et al., arXiv:2312.04601 — bounds from labelling-function marginals alone, the only published
protocol aimed at exactly this situation), Confident Learning (Northcutt et al., JAIR 2021,
arXiv:1911.00068), and concordance adjudication (Sorin et al. — truth by agreement between independent
pipelines, manual review of discrepancies only), which is a published route to a ruler LARGER than 58
without re-annotation if the pixel-VLM column and the report column are near-independent.

### 6. M327-Q3 — what the column-null probe IS, in the literature's terms

**NULL for the specific design:** nobody has published per-class recovery of a column-mean multi-label
metric by constant substitution. It is a novel instance of a named family — Whitehill's oracle attacks
(AAAI 2016, arXiv:1506.01339, AUC-oracle exploits with a proof that labelings consistent with an observed
AUC grow exponentially; 2017, arXiv:1707.01825, FULL test-label recovery on a real Kaggle competition via
the log-loss oracle, rank #4/848 without training a classifier). Two priced consequences: the oracle leaks
far more than one number per query when exploited deliberately, and adaptive consumption of leaderboard
bits degrades the holdout's validity (Dwork et al., Science 2015, PMID 26250683; Blum & Hardt's Ladder,
ICML 2015, arXiv:1502.04585). **Our probe is the benign end of that family — one query, one scalar, no
label recovery attempted** — but it does spend a small unquantified amount of the public board's
remaining information, which is an argument for the single-slot form over the twelve-slot map.

## 2026-09-11 — RETRACTION: M327's column-null probe was already run, and the axis it aimed at was closed on 2026-09-05

**M327 is wrong in its central claim and the arm it proposed is cancelled.** It said the board's per-column
areas *"have never been read"* and proposed a single-slot probe to read them, gated on the researcher's
Q1/Q2. D322 cleared that gate this morning. M328 then refined the design to null against the gold-58
ordering rather than the refuted offline map. **All of it is a re-derivation.** The probe ran six days
earlier, four slots were spent on the family, and the axis was retired AS A CLASS in writing.

```
56020638  2026-09-04  colnull    0.500   constant in every column: the metric is a plain unweighted mean
56020054  2026-09-04  colmcl     0.904   MCL nulled      -> MCL board AUC 0.980, interval 0.968-0.992
56023244  2026-09-05  colbaker   0.903   Baker's nulled  -> Baker's board AUC 0.992, interval 0.980-1.004
56037952  2026-09-05  colhalf    0.728   the SIX weakest columns nulled, one slot, the exact M327 design
```

`colhalf`'s ablated six were chosen by our 909-study offline ordering — MCL 0.8104, Fracture 0.8255,
Lateral OA 0.8309, Effusion 0.8663, PF OA 0.8698, Synovitis 0.8717 — the same instrument M327 wanted to
test and M328 wanted to swap for the gold ordering. Its arithmetic is forced by `colnull`:
S = (0.944 − 0.728) × 12 + 3.0 = **5.592**, so the **weak six average 0.932** and the strong six average
(11.328 − 5.592)/6 = **0.956**.

**What that verdict already settled, in its own words:** *"a 0.024 gap between the halves against a 0.110
offline spread — our map transfers in SIGN at the half-split and nowhere near in SIZE, and it cannot
resolve a single column, since MCL, the worst column in the ablated half, is 0.980, above the STRONG
half's own mean. The board's 0.056 of headroom is distributed, not pooled. To gain the 0.010 that
separates this project from first place, every one of the twelve columns has to move about 0.010 of AUC;
there is no weak lane to attack and no per-column shortcut exists."*

### The three readings that have to be withdrawn with it

1. **M327's "what it opens" is empty.** It closed the member and seat axes correctly and then pointed the
   only surviving lever at an axis already retired. The board-level ceiling reading stands; the arm does
   not.
2. **M328's aiming refinement is moot.** Swapping the gold-58 ordering in for the offline one improves a
   probe that will not be run, and `colhalf` already showed why no ordering would have helped: at this
   resolution the ablation cannot separate MCL (0.980) from Baker's (0.992) — the endpoints of a
   0.110-wide OFFLINE spread land 0.012 apart on the board, inside the rounding interval of two
   three-decimal scores.
3. **Lateral OA and Synovitis are both smaller prizes than they looked.** The whole weak half averages
   0.932 on the board. A column driven from 0.932 to a perfect 1.000 is worth (1.000 − 0.932)/12 =
   **0.0057** — barely half the gap, for a column that cannot be made perfect. The Synovitis generation
   thread and the Lateral OA band-geometry test are therefore both priced at **≤0.005 board**, not at the
   0.010 the gap needs. They stay open as understanding; neither is a path to first place on its own.

### What this actually leaves, and it is the only thing left

*"Every one of the twelve columns has to move about 0.010 of AUC."* That is a statement about the
REPRESENTATION, not about any label, head, seat, weight or table. It rules out, by arithmetic rather than
by taste, every per-column intervention this project has queued — and it rules in exactly the class of
change that lifts all twelve columns at once: **what the model sees and how much of it, and what it was
pretrained on.** The depth axis (D323 §1: our only depth evidence under a working head is the foreign
curve, still steepening at 20, and knee-ezz's −0.0001 was max pooling measuring its own indifference),
more corpus, and a stronger trunk are the surviving candidates. They are also the three the owner has
been asking for from the start.

### Why this happened, since it is the fifth time

M327 was written from `comp/board.jsonl` — it read all 128 rows for the SCORE histogram and the member
sets, and it did not read the `what` field of the four rows whose `scope` is `excluded`. Those four are
excluded from `board_transfer` for a good reason (they are damaged entries and must never enter the fit)
and that exclusion made them invisible to a pass that was looking for entries. **An `excluded` row is
excluded from the FIT, never from the RECORD.** The four instrument rows carry more settled per-column
information than any other rows in the file, and they were the exact rows the question was about.

The cost: M327 and M328 were written, committed and pushed, two letters went to the researcher (M327
Q1/Q2, answered in full as D322), and the only thing that stopped a fifth slot was reading the board file
one field wider before spending it. The check that would have caught it at the start is the one already on
the books — grep the ledger and the record for the OPERATION before proposing it, not just before
submitting it.

### calib_hold_clean_distill — the seventh cell lands BELOW its own pre-registration, and the three-way term is −0.0080 — 2026-09-11

`calib_hold_clean_distill_s2026` reads **0.8641**, converged clean (twelve epochs, no TRUNCATED row;
epochs 9/10/11 at 0.8633/0.8635/0.8635 with the peak at epoch 10). The pre-registration written into the
factorial section above while it ran was **0.8650-0.8720, centred ~0.8685**. It missed the band low.

That is the reading, and it is worth more than the number. All three treatments are ON in this cell, and
every two-way term the factorial measured is POSITIVE (+0.0077 calib x hold, +0.0031 calib x teacher).
Main effects plus both interactions predict 0.8721. Measured 0.8641, so the **three-way term is −0.0080**
— larger in size than either two-way term, and negative. The treatments do not compose.

**What that rules out.** The factorial was being read as a set of stackable parts: find the flags with
positive interactions, turn them all on, collect the sum. This cell is the direct test of that reading and
it refutes it. Turning on the third treatment did not add its +0.0056; it gave back most of what the
pairs bought. The best cell in the whole eight remains `clean_calib_s2026` at **0.8649** — two treatments,
not three — and this arm did not beat it.

**It also bounds the eighth cell, which is on the card now.** `hold_clean_distill` is the `— ✓ clean`
corner, the last unrun one. Its own header priced reading (b) at ~30% on the theory that hold-annotations
is a general soft-target enabler. The three-way term says the opposite about this family's composition:
the more of these flags are on at once, the worse the sum does against its parts. The eighth cell carries
hold + teacher WITHOUT calibration, so it is the two-way `hold x teacher` term measured for the first
time, and the honest prior after this number is the LOW half of its pre-registered bands — 0.8580-0.8639,
"hold damps the teacher" — not the 0.8660 that reading (b) needs. The bands stay as written; this
paragraph is the prior, not a rewrite of them.

Per-column at the peak epoch: ACL 0.890, MCL 0.805, Medial Meniscus 0.902, Lateral Meniscus 0.868,
Medial OA 0.880, Lateral OA 0.826, PF OA 0.863, Effusion 0.861, Synovitis 0.857, Baker's 0.907,
Contusion 0.881, Fracture 0.823. MCL and Fracture are again the floor, which is the same ordering every
arm at this corner produces — consistent with the board's own verdict that there is no weak lane to
attack (the `colhalf` retraction above), since the offline ordering does not transfer in size.

**A note on what it cost, because the price was not the recipe's.** This arm and the eighth cell both ran
against an unbounded VRAM ceiling — `capped()` derived 32.5 GB on a 31.84 GB card, and
`set_per_process_memory_fraction` silently clamps an over-card fraction to 1.0, so the "cap" REMOVED the
cap. This run reserved 51 GB against 21.93 allocated and its epochs grew 1594s -> 2681s as Windows paged
the excess to system RAM over PCIe. The number above is sound (allocation never exceeded the model's
own prediction), but it was bought at roughly four times its quiet-card price. Fixed in `d212242d`
(`DESKTOP_RESERVE_GB`); the eighth cell was killed at epoch 1 and relaunched under the fix, and its gate
now reads 28934 MiB admitted. Quote the relaunch's epoch times, not this one's.

## The label-masking axis: both selectors cost score, and the cost is NON-MONOTONIC (2026-09-11)

Two arms, one control, disjoint selectors, same recipe (`$RECIPE --epochs 12 --slice-pooling max
--whole-stack --backbone-lr 4e-5 --slices 12 --band-low 0.1 --band-high 0.9`, fold 0). Both
`--eval-labels` pinned to `report_labels_v2` so the comparison is label CONTENT and never a ruler
change (knee-df7t).

| arm | selector | masked | best holdout | vs control |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `band_span` (control) | — | 0% | **0.8565** | — |
| `confident_span` | extractor self-reported confidence below threshold | 27.3% (14,445 cells) | 0.8449 | **−0.0116** |
| `discord_mask` | four-way cross-extractor disagreement, `>=0.5` binarised | 13.94% (7,369 cells) | 0.8148 | **−0.0417** |

`discord_mask` ran its full 12 epochs, peaked at e6 and plateaued 0.806–0.810 through e11 — converged,
not truncated, not a patience stop. Its table is verified: 7,369 NaN against v2's 0, 13.94% of 52,872,
and **zero all-NaN rows**, so no study lost supervision entirely. The two selectors overlap on 188
cells — 2.55% of discordant, 1.3% of UNK — so these are disjoint populations answering the same
question twice.

Both land in their third pre-registered band.

**CORRECTED THE SAME DAY, BEFORE THE INK DRIED (D339). The two arms are not comparable, and this
section first claimed they were.** Measured on disk, denominators stated:

| set | n | v2-positive rate (≥0.5) | v2 soft mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| discordant — what `discord_mask` masked | 7,369 | **0.9677** | 0.680 |
| UNK — what `confident_span` masked | 14,445 | **0.0000** | 0.280 |
| corpus | 52,872 | 0.3051 | 0.351 |

**The discordant selector is 96.8% positive.** `discord_mask` removed 7,131 positive cells — **44.2%
of all positive supervision in the corpus** (16,128 v2-positives). `confident_span` removed ZERO hard
positives; its cells are v2's uncertain class. So `discord_mask` did not test "does removing noisy
labels hurt". It tested "does removing 44% of the positive class hurt", and the answer to that was
never in doubt. All twelve columns fell, and the share of each column's POSITIVES masked tracks its
delta at **Pearson −0.65 (n=12)**: MCL lost 65.1% of its positives and fell 0.1058; Baker's 50.1% and
0.0845; PF OA 27.7% and 0.0116.

**So the −0.0417 is a class-balance result wearing a label-noise result's clothes, and the closure
rests on `confident_span` alone.** That arm is still a clean test — it cleared an uncertain,
overwhelmingly-negative 27.3% and still cost 0.0116 — so the subtraction route is closed, by one arm
rather than two, and with the weaker of the two effect sizes. FCF (Jiang, AAAI-24) Thm 6 and Menon 2015
remain the frame; the evidence for them here is thinner than this section first said.

**What was wrong with the reasoning, since the selector was built here.** The non-monotonicity (half the
cells, four times the cost) was read as evidence that the masked cells differed in HARDNESS, and the
alternative named for exclusion was column concentration. The actual answer was a third thing never
considered: positive CONTENT. Nobody checked the base rate of the selector before spending an hour of
card on it — a one-line `df[cols].mean()` would have shown 96.8% and predicted the outcome without the
run. The lesson generalises past this arm: **state the class composition of any subset before masking
it**, for the same reason a rate is stated with its denominator (knee-f9aao).

**What survives of the hardness hypothesis, second-order.** The blind audit measured these contested
cells at 15.6% error against 1.48% unanimous, so the positives removed were the CONTESTED ones —
roughly 6,000 true-and-hard positives plus ~1,100 errors. That is the hardest 44% of positives, not a
random 44%, and r = −0.65 leaves scatter for hardness to live in (Baker's −0.0845 at 50.1% masked
against Contusion −0.0392 at 60.5% is the shape it would take). Per-POSITIVE-cell the two arms sit
within ~2× of each other; that residual is hardness's remaining claim, and it is not established.

**What this licenses.** Correction, not filtering — the top rung of D333's ladder. The cells most worth
fixing are the ones least affordable to lose, which is the mechanism argument FCF Thm 5 makes
theoretically and this axis now makes empirically. `v2_corrected` is that arm: the 2,315 v2-lone-dissent
cells (D335/D336) overwritten with the foreign cluster's SOFT value, pre-registered
`>=0.8665` / `0.8515–0.8665` / `<=0.8515` against the same control.

**What this does NOT license.** Nothing here says the labels are clean — the blind 402-cell adjudication
and the gold-58 cross-check both put v2's error on disagreement-selected cells at 75%. It says removing
supervision is the wrong response to that error, which is a statement about the REMEDY, not the defect.

## The label-SUBSTITUTION chain, and the v2 ruler inverts it (2026-09-11)

Masking supervision costs score (the section above). Substituting a corrected value for it is the other
remedy, and it is the one the blind 469-cell adjudication licensed. Three arms, same recipe as the
masking section, same fold-0 909-study holdout, `--eval-labels` pinned to `report_labels_v2` throughout:

| arm | table | cells substituted | best holdout (v2 ruler) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `band_span` (control) | v2 | 0 | **0.8565** (e6) |
| `v5blend_span` | v5blend | reader-blend | 0.8113 (e5, then monotone decline to 0.7984 by e11) |
| `v6tears_span` | v6tears | 1,379 contested TEAR cells | *running* |
| `v7nontear_span` | v7nontear | +703 contested NON-TEAR cells | *queued* (knee-lv4fx) |

On the v2 ruler the chain is monotone WORSE with more correction. **That ordering is an artefact of the
ruler, and it is now measured rather than suspected.**

### The gold ruler, and it orders the same arms the opposite way

469 cells were hand-adjudicated blind, ten chunks, key sealed until the last verdict was on disk
(`interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-11_the_469_and_the_tear_substitution.md`). They are inside this same
fold-0 holdout, and no table can contaminate them: they were written before any of these tables existed.
`research/scripts/adjudicated_rescore.py` scores an arm's holdout npz on those cells alone.

| split (n) | `band_span` | `v5blend_span` | `v6tears_span` |
|---|---|---|---|
| tear-277 | 0.693 | 0.762 | **0.866** |
| nontear-192 | 0.526 | 0.594 | 0.693 |
| Contusion-120 | 0.483 | 0.500 | 0.675 |
| all-469 | 0.625 | 0.693 | 0.795 |

Paired McNemar on the tear cells: v6tears-only 39 against v5blend-only 10; v5blend over band_span 31–12
the same way. **PROVISIONAL — the `v6tears_span` column was read at epoch 2 of 12 off a live-written npz
and must be re-scored when the arm lands.** The `band_span` and `v5blend_span` columns are final.

### What this means for every other number in this file

The v2 ruler penalises an arm roughly in proportion to how much of v2's error the arm unlearned. So a
number recorded here for an arm whose `--labels` was NOT `report_labels_v2` while its `--eval-labels` was
carries a bias whose SIGN is now known. Arms on that axis that read flat or slightly negative are exactly
the signature the artefact produces, and a kill delivered by a biased ruler is not a kill. The audit of
which rows could flip is open (M360); until it closes, **do not quote a v2-ruler delta for a
corrected-table arm as a verdict.**

The adjudicated rescore is the chain's primary ruler. Its limits, stated: 469 cells over 334 studies,
mean 1.4 cells per study so the cells are not independent, and the tear split has zero variance on the v2
side by construction — its McNemar is a count, not a test.

### Retraction: `discord_mask`'s kill, and what the masking table row above now means (2026-09-11)

The label-masking axis table above records `discord_mask` at 0.8148, **−0.0417 against control**, and that
number was read as closing the subtraction route: masking half as many cells as `confident_span` cost four
times as much. **The verdict is retracted. The number is not.**

Both arms were evaluated with `--eval-labels` pinned to v2, and the 469 blind-adjudicated cells now show
that v2 is wrong on 89.1% of the contested cells — so masking the cells v2 disagrees with the field on
removes BIAS, and the v2 ruler scores removed bias exactly like removed supervision. On the gold cells:

    arm               v2 ruler            gold acc@0.5   gold AUC-vs-verdict
    discord_mask      0.8148  (-0.0417)      0.832            0.6982
    confident_span    0.8449  (-0.0116)      0.537              --
    band_span (ctrl)  0.8565                 0.625            0.6008

`discord_mask` is the best member on disk on both gold columns. `confident_span` is a TRUE kill on both
rulers — masking v2's self-reported-uncertain cells loses real signal. **The two masking arms were never
the same experiment, and the v2 ruler could not tell them apart.** The masked-table route re-opens; the
open question is no longer "does subtraction work" but "which selector picks the biased cells".

`v2_corrected` is retracted the same way: band-3 on the v2 ruler, 0.814/0.6272 on gold and **0.883 on
Contusion-120, the best Contusion reading on disk.** Both members are now on `comp/members.roster`.

## The selector ladder, and the 18% no report-text selector can reach (2026-09-11, D357)

M364 asked which selector picks the cells v2 gets wrong, ranked on the blind 469 and on the audit400.
The answer closed the axis it measured.

| selector | audit400 precision | recall | n flagged | lift over 3.7% base |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lone_dissent` (the v2_corrected table's own selector) | **0.727** | 0.533 | 11 | **~20x** |
| five-way discordance (the discord_mask family) | 0.156 | 0.667 | 64 | ~4x |
| confidence-below-threshold (the pre-registered NEGATIVE CONTROL) | 0.031 | 0.133 | 65 | **<1x, below random** |

The control failed as it was required to, by a factor of four on the 469 and by twenty here, so the
measurement is behaving. Two structural facts come out of it:

**The selectors are not independent.** Corpus-wide, **2,301 of the 2,315 lone-dissent cells (99.4%) sit
inside the 7,369-cell four-way discordance set.** `discord_mask` and the substitution chain are one
finding wearing two hats: the CELLS are the same, only the OPERATION differs (mask vs substitute).
Seating both buys operation diversity, never cell diversity — and a seat argued on cell diversity would
have been argued on something that is not there.

**And the whole ladder rides ONE contrast.** v2 is wrong on 1.5% of unanimous cells and 15.6% of
discordant cells; the strata are 69.3% / 30.7% of the corpus. So of every error v2 makes,
0.693x0.015 = 0.0104 against 0.307x0.156 = 0.0479 — **~18% of v2's errors live in the unanimous stratum,
where all four extractors agree with each other and are wrong together.** No extractor-discordance
selector can flag one of them, at any threshold, by construction. The correction axis is coverage-bound,
not precision-bound: the sharp 4.4% is banked, the 5,068-cell tail is priced at ~0.07 and is not worth
buying, and the next real gain needs a signal that is not the report text. M365 asks for the image-side
version (members that never shared a label table agreeing with each other and disagreeing with v2), with
the fraction-in-the-unanimous-stratum as the number that decides whether it is a new axis or the same
contrast in a costume.

Consequence for the seat: the mechanism now favours `v2_corrected` (substitutes on the 0.727 cells) while
the gold AUC favours `discord_mask` (0.6982 vs 0.6272, masking a superset whose extra 5,068 cells are
only ~7% wrong — mostly-good supervision thrown away). Those two disagree, and running them through the
same vacated seat across two slots is what settles it.

### The image-side selector is closed by its own stratified batch (2026-09-11, D358 → D360)

D358 opened a route to the one stratum no report-text selector can reach: ~18% of v2's errors are made
where all four extractors agree with each other and are wrong together, and an image-side selector
(four members from four different label families, ≥3-of-4 agreeing with each other and disagreeing with
v2) appeared to flag them at precision 0.273 with 90.9% of its flags in that unanimous stratum. The
pilot was n=3 wrong cells.

A 56-cell blind pack (`audit400/imagesel56`, seed 20260911, key sealed until all four answer files were
on disk) stratified the flags four ways, 14 each, and settled it:

| stratum | n | v2-wrong | precision [95% Wilson] |
|---|---|---|---|
| flagU_top (top third of margin) | 14 | 0 | 0.000 [0.000, 0.215] |
| flagU_mid (middle third) | 14 | 0 | 0.000 [0.000, 0.215] |
| flagD (dissent stratum) | 14 | 6 | 0.429 [0.214, 0.674] |
| unflagU (recall arm) | 14 | 1 | 0.071 [0.013, 0.315] |

**Zero of 28 in the unanimous stratum, at both margins.** The selector's score is flat there — no
threshold salvages it. What the selector actually finds is the dissent stratum (0.429), which
`discord_mask` already masks. The axis is closed plainly: there is still no route to the unanimous
stratum, and the D358 point estimate was a three-cell mirage. The pre-registered stratification is what
caught it; an unstratified follow-up batch would have reproduced the mirage with a bigger n.

Two residuals worth carrying forward. (a) The recall arm reads **0.071**, above its 1.5% pre-registration
with an interval that still covers it — if the unanimous stratum is really 7% wrong, the 18%-of-errors
arithmetic is a floor, and its denominator needs its own fresh batch before it is quoted again. (b) On
all 28 flagU cells — v2 and four extractors say PRESENT, four corrected-family members say ABSENT — the
blind adjudicator sided with **v2 on every one**. Selected for member-v2 disagreement, so not a rate; but
it is the first cell-level sign that the corrected chain deletes true positives, and it rhymes with the
31 over-corrections D345 found in v3.
